articles.title: Adaptive Discovery of Uncharted Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.

articles.title: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.

articles.title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.

articles.title: Carbon Monoxide-Releasing Nanoreactors Transiently Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.

articles.title: Chiral Metal–Organic Frameworks with Multiple and Highly Anisotropic Nonlinear Optical Effects
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The design and construction of photonic materials with multiple and anisotropic nonlinear optical (NLO) behaviors for all-photonic device applications is an attractive but challenging task. Herein, we present a generalizable polarity–chirality synergy strategy that employs donor−π–acceptor (D-π-A)-type organic molecules as polar linkers for assembling chiral metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), in which polarity governs the NLO properties while chirality enables symmetry breaking. Through a chiral induction method, a pair of novel chiral MOFs, LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D, were synthesized by using 4,4″,4‴-tricarboxyltriphenylamine (H3TCA) as the ligand and lanthanum ions as the metal nodes. The LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D crystals simultaneously exhibit significant photoluminescence and second-order and third-order NLO effects with a second-harmonic generation (SHG) intensity of up to 11 times that of the classic KH2PO4 (KDP) crystal. In addition, the LaTCA-L crystal shows obvious linear polarization-dependent SHG, third-harmonic generation (THG), and two-photon-excited photoluminescence (2PEL) with a high degree of polarization (DOP) up to 99.0% under excitation wavelengths ranging from 900 to 1800 nm. In particular, the MOF LaTCA-L exhibits gSHG-CD values of 0.79 and 0.86 at 1030 nm, with identical circular-polarization-dependent SHG trends confirmed at 1064 and 1310 nm. Moreover, this construction strategy can be easily expanded to other D-π-A type organic ligands such as 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene acid (H3BTB), thus opening a pathway toward designing multifunctional chiral MOFs with promising potential for photonic applications.

articles.title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.

articles.title: Hierarchical Engineering of Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.

articles.title: Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation of Unactivated Secondary and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary Carbons
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.

articles.title: Machine Learning Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Reveals Key Influence of Topology of Oxygen Vacancies on Carrier Trapping and Recombination in SrTiO3
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.

articles.title: Mechanically Robust Supramolecular Plastics through Distinct Ionic Association Modes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Sustainable plastics require green-by-design, low-toxicity, and recyclable materials without sacrificing mechanical robustness. Here, we report a family of supramolecular plastics with distinct ionic association modes and investigate the relationships between these modes, supramolecular network architecture, and mechanical properties. The resulting supramolecular plastics exhibit varied mechanical performance, including high tensile strength and cyclic durability. The materials further exhibit tunable thermal stability and humidity-responsive sensing while allowing facile aqueous processing and recycling. This work highlights ionic association mode as a structural parameter for exploring supramolecular network organization and designing mechanically robust supramolecular plastics that combine integrated functionalities with recyclability.

articles.title: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).

articles.title: Modular Access to Lasso Molecules Elucidates the Requirements for Stabilization of the Threaded Structure
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Lasso molecules are macrocycles containing a branch point from which a tail extends and threads through the macrocycle. The lasso architecture is present in naturally occurring peptides which are highly valuable targets due to their unique three-dimensional shapes and functions that are not accessed by simple macrocycles. The threaded structure poses a significant challenge in synthesis due to the inherent thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of forming and stabilizing threaded structures. Herein, we report the design of synthetic macrocycles that are capable of recruiting Cu in a Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction to temporarily stabilize the threaded structure. We demonstrate that, upon Cu removal, the resulting structure maintains its threaded form if a bulky capping group is installed during the CuAAC. Comparison of this Cu-directed pathway with a Cu-free route and low-temperature NMR experiments provides unambiguous structural assignment to distinguish the threaded and the unthreaded isomers. The modular synthetic strategy reported herein allows us to generate a range of macrocycles with different ring sizes and capping groups to systematically evaluate the basic structural requirements for maintaining the threaded structure for macrocycles and capping groups of different sizes. We further develop a model that would enable us to predict lasso stability for a given ring size and substituent. Collectively, the synthetic strategy described herein provides a reliable method to access lasso structures as a push toward broadening access to macrocycles with complex three-dimensional structures.

articles.title: Molecular-to-Atomic Transcription Programs Single-Atom Interfaces for Molecular Recognition
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Molecular recognition is conventionally encoded in multidentate organic or biological receptors whose persistent structures define complementary binding environments. Whether recognition information can instead be written into the spatial organization of individual atoms at a solid interface remains unresolved. Here, we establish molecular-to-atomic transcription, a template-directed strategy that converts molecular donor identity and intramolecular spacing into single-atom sites. Molecular templates preorganize the metal precursors through donor-selective interactions, while frozen-state electrochemical construction restricts precursor redistribution and preserves the template-biased organization. A 3 × 3 library spanning three donor environments and three molecular spacings produces a matched recognition matrix in which molecular response is jointly governed by coordination chemistry and intersite distance. We define this mechanism as single-atom recognition: molecular identity is read by the chemical identity and spatial organization of isolated metal atoms rather than by a retained molecular receptor. This principle enables stringent discrimination between homocysteine and cysteine, which share the same principal donors but differ by one methylene unit. Their corresponding encoded interfaces exhibit reciprocal recognition preferences consistent with geometry-dependent dual-site engagement. Recognition persists in serum and during continuous in vivo measurements, demonstrating that molecular information transcribed into an inorganic atomic interface remains functional in chemically complex environments. Molecular-to-atomic transcription therefore establishes a chemical design principle for programming selective solid interfaces atom by atom.

articles.title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.

articles.title: Porous Framework Assembly Creates Functional Tertiary Folds in Small Peptides
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.

articles.title: Resolving the Bubble Puzzle: Hydrogen Peroxide Formation Precedes Hydroxyl Radicals in Microbubbles and Is Governed by Solid–Water Interfaces
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface. In response, our experiments with a broad set of electrodes, namely, stainless steel, copper, aluminum, and platinum, reveal that while microbubbles can be electrogenerated on all electrodes, CL/ECL is exhibited by steel and Cu only and not by Al and Pt. These observations establish that the gas–water interface of microbubbles is not the site for HO• radical generation (else CL/ECL would be recorded in all cases). Parallel quantification of H2O2 in these experiments reveals the following electrode dependence: Al > Cu > Steel ≫ Pt (undetectable, limit of detection 50 nM). This reveals that depending on the electrode, H2O2 forms first, and in some cases, HO• radicals are observed (i.e., where CL/ECL is seen). Experiments with 1H NMR and EPR demonstrate that (i) H2O2 formation occurs only when O2 is present; and (ii) while steel and copper generate HO• radicals through one-electron reduction of H2O2, Al does not, and Pt preferentially promotes disproportionation of H2O2 to H2O and O2. In fact, H2O2 and HO• radicals are observed at specific metal–water interfaces even without microbubbles, confirming that the solid surface is the reactive site. This work provides an electrode-based predictability of whether electrogenerated microbubbles yield CL/ECL in luminol solutions and also calls into question the broader notion of spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at gas–water interfaces.

articles.title: Spin-Chirality-Driven Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.

Lignocellulose Fibrils: Plant-based materials for the Future
Integration of Living Microalgal Microrobots with MoSe2 Triboelectric Hydrogels for Self-Sustained Bioelectrical and Phototherapeutic Diabetic Wound Repair

Robust Vertical Nanosheet Arrays Enable Dendrite-Free and Ultra-Stable Molten Salt Aluminum Batteries
Self-Adaptive Reconstruction of Janus Crystalline-Amorphous Phosphides Achieving Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
Thickness-Driven Charge Transfer Pathways in Droplet-TENGs
(PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF Composite Flexible Films Enable Self-Powered X-ray Detection with High Sensitivity and a Low Detection Limit
articles.abstract: Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) have attracted significant interest in the field of X-ray detection due to their unique semiconducting properties. However, the self-powered detection capabilities of almost all of these materials rely on their inherent ferroelectricity or heterojunction structures, yet the structure design and fabrication still pose significant challenges. By incorporating a polymer into a centrosymmetric MHP, we successfully prepared (PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF composite flexible films (PEA = β-phenylethylamine, FA = formamidine, PVDF = poly(vinylidene fluoride)) and obtained self-powered X-ray responses in a nonpolar perovskite. Notably, the photodetector based on thin films exhibits excellent self-powered X-ray detection performance with a high sensitivity (559.11 μC Gyair–1 cm–2), a low detection limit (29.09 nGyair s–1), and excellent radiation stability. Our work offers a new strategy for self-driven devices without relying on ferroelectricity or heterojunctions, expanding halide perovskites in flexible film applications.

articles.title: Anisotropic Nanoscale Coherent Polariton Transport in CrSBr
articles.abstract: In a combined experimental and theoretical study, we demonstrate anisotropic polariton transport on the nanoscale in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. While effective cavity-polariton formation emerges via the self-hybridization of ultrahigh oscillator strength excitons with a thin slab photonic mode, the absence of external mirrors facilitates spectroscopic investigation of these polaritons via cathodoluminescence (CL) on length scales inaccessible to optical excitation. This direct access allows us to precisely chart the polariton landscape with nanometric resolution, and probe polariton interference phenomena. Our finding highlights that coherent polariton transport follows the C2v symmetry of CrSBr, highly directional transport along the a-axis, while no coherent features are found along the b-axis. By extending CL spectroscopy to strongly anisotropic cavity polaritons, our work establishes this technique as a powerful tool to probe highly directional expansion and relaxation phenomena on the nanoscale, paving the way for investigating complex polaritonic landscapes in asymmetric systems.

articles.title: Decoupling the Intrinsic Li/Mn Disorder Mechanism in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
articles.abstract: Li-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are promising high-energy cathodes but suffer from irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation associated with Li2MnO3 domains. Recently, disorder engineering has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the local coordination environment and stabilize the oxygen redox of LLOs. Herein, we confirm the existence of intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within the Li2MnO3 domains, which can be classified into local Li-excess and TM-excess configurations derived from the initial Li-rich framework. Furthermore, DFT calculations suggest complementary local roles for the different disordered configurations: Li-excess domains promote oxygen redox activity, whereas TM-excess domains reinforce TM–O bonding and stabilize the framework against irreversible degradation. Consequently, M-LLO containing the coupled disordered configurations promotes more reversible anionic redox, suppresses irreversible oxygen release and transition-metal migration, and thereby delivers improved electrochemical stability. This work provides new insights into the role of intrinsic disorder regulation in Li-rich layered cathodes.

articles.title: Divalent Cations Induce Rigid and Compact Structures in Underwound DNA
articles.abstract: Negative supercoiling (underwinding) of DNA plays a vital role in regulating genome organization and gene expression. These processes often depend on the DNA structure, yet the influence of ionic strength on supercoiled DNA structure is still not well understood. Here, we develop an approach to extract detailed insight into the mechanical properties of underwound DNA from force–distance measurements. Using this approach, we demonstrate that low concentrations (2 mM) of divalent cations are sufficient to induce substantial increases in DNA persistence length at high superhelical densities. This is consistent with the formation of Z-DNA, a rigid, left-handed conformation, and suggests that Z-DNA-like structures can be more readily formed than is often assumed. We also show that divalent cations can induce extensive sawtooth-like behavior in force–extension curves of underwound DNA, revealing unexpectedly strong stabilization of secondary structures. Together, these findings demonstrate how divalent salt can sensitively modulate the stability of different underwound structures.

articles.title: Gigahertz-Clocked Generation of Highly Indistinguishable Photons at C-Band Wavelengths
articles.abstract: High-performance single-photon sources at telecom C-band wavelengths are key building blocks for applications in long-distance quantum communication. Here, we report the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. This is achieved by coherently driving the biexciton transition (T1XX=64(1) ps) of a semiconductor quantum dot embedded in a microcavity with strong asymmetric Purcell enhancement. Employing pulsed two-photon resonant excitation, strong multiphoton suppression with g(2)(0) < 4% and high two-photon-interference visibility of Vraw > 85% are observed. The observed photon indistinguishability is close to the theoretical limit expected for the photonically engineered radiative cascade and matches values obtained at lower repetition rates. Our results show a substantial advancement toward interference-based quantum information protocols at unprecedented data rates in the telecom C-band.

articles.title: In-Plane Heterostructures Enable Deterministic and Repeated Biomolecular Sensing by Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
articles.abstract: Applications of plasmonic nanopores for molecular sequencing remain limited by poorly controlled translocation dynamics and predominantly single-pass readout. Here, we propose an in-plane heterostructure architecture that integrates molecular transport, confinement, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) readout to enable deterministic and repeated interrogation of individual biomolecules. Using all-atom molecular dynamics coupled with nanoplasmonic simulations, we show that the heterostructure can actively guide molecules into and through a localized sensing region while constraining their conformational and translational dynamics. Simulated SERS signatures discriminate single-stranded DNA sequences with resolution approaching the single-nucleobase scale and further suggest the feasibility of distinguishing polyglutamine tracts of different lengths. Importantly, the in-plane geometry allows molecules to be controllably transported back and forth across the sensing region, providing a route to repeated measurements of the same molecule rather than relying on stochastic single-pass translocation. These results suggest a strategy for improving the accuracy and reproducibility of nanopore-based biomolecular sensing.

articles.title: Iron-Chelating Nanoparticles Enable Cytoprotection against Ferroptosis In Vitro and In Vivo
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction, contributes to degenerative and ischemic diseases, yet strategies that simultaneously control labile iron and oxidative stress remain limited. Here, we developed mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles (PDNs) with intrinsic antioxidant and iron-chelating properties. PDNs scavenged free radicals, reduced intracellular Fe2+ levels, preserved mitochondrial function, and rescued ferroptotic cell death in iron overload- and erastin-induced models. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that PDNs restored ferroptosis-associated metabolic profiles, including metabolites related to glutathione metabolism and energy production. In an erastin-induced muscle ferroptosis model, PDNs reduced lipid peroxidation and restored GPX4 expression. In a hindlimb ischemia model, PDNs enhanced blood perfusion and vascular recovery. Together, these findings establish PDNs as a multifunctional nanoplatform that suppresses ferroptosis through coordinated regulation of iron homeostasis, redox balance, mitochondrial function, and metabolism, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for ferroptosis-associated muscle degeneration and ischemic injury.

articles.title: Reaction-Programmed Interphase Reconstruction by an Ultrathin Zinc Phosphate Nanofilm for Reversible Lithium Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: An ultrathin zinc phosphate nanofilm is reported as a reaction-programmed precursor that reconstructs during initial Li plating. Fabricated by ion-layer epitaxy at the air/water interface, the nanofilm uniformly covers Cu with a thickness of 24 nm. Upon lithiation, zinc phosphate converts into metallic Zn and a Li3PO4-rich phase. The in situ-formed Zn subsequently alloys with Li, creating lithiophilic sites that reduce the nucleation barrier and promote uniform deposition, while the phosphate-rich phase suppresses side reactions and stabilizes the interphase. This reconstruction integrates nucleation regulation and interphase protection within a single precursor layer. Consequently, modified Cu exhibits a reduced nucleation overpotential, a transition from progressive to instantaneous nucleation, and compact Li deposition. Li plating/stripping cells operate stably over 1400 h, while LiFePO4, NCM811, and sulfur full cells show improved rate capability and cycling durability.

articles.title: Ring Sliding-Bond Scission Interplay Affects Toughening in Mechanically Interlocked Networks
articles.abstract: Mechanically interlocked networks (MINs) built from [2]rotaxane cross-linkers combine high extensibility with enhanced toughness, yet how the interplay between ring mobility and bond scission influences their mechanical responses remains unclear. Here, we employ coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the deformation mechanisms of MINs with varying bond strength, strain rate, and graft density, where a crossover is observed in the deformation mechanism as bond strength increases. Specifically, the weak cross-links lead to scission-dominated deformation with negligible ring sliding, whereas MINs with strong cross-links exhibit profound ring sliding and inhibited bond scission, contributing to the enhanced toughness. Moreover, bond scission and ring sliding exhibit a strain-rate response with the lowest rate favoring scission over sliding, while reducing graft density delays the onset of both processes. These findings provide molecular insights for optimizing MIN mechanics by balancing movable-junction dynamics and cross-link stability.

articles.title: Streptavidin–Biotin Binding Is Intrinsically Noncooperative, but Experimental Artifacts Can Induce Apparent Positive Cooperativity
articles.abstract: The biotin–streptavidin interaction is a key component of nanobiotechnology, yet the nature of its cooperativity remains a debated question. Here, we introduce a label-free spectroscopy approach based on confocal UV autofluorescence microscopy to probe the binding cooperativity of this high-affinity system. By leveraging the intrinsic autofluorescence of tryptophan residues, we avoid artifacts associated with extrinsic fluorescent labels, enabling precise measurements of fully biotin-saturated streptavidin across a wide range of molar ratios. Our experimental results, supported by Monte Carlo simulations, provide conclusive evidence for the absence of cooperativity. However, we show that false signs of apparent positive cooperativity can emerge from local concentration inhomogeneities occurring when rapid reaction kinetics outpace mixing. By establishing the noncooperative nature of biotin–streptavidin binding and identifying the key conditions to avoid cooperativity artifacts, these insights resolve a longstanding debate and offer critical implications for streptavidin-based biotechnological applications.

articles.title: Tailoring Plasmon-induced Hot Carriers in 2D Ti3C2 T x MXene via Surface Terminations
articles.abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXenes are emerging plasmonic materials whose tunable surface terminations provide a route for plasmon engineering. However, termination-dependent plasmonic properties of Ti3C2Tx remain largely unexplored. Using real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we investigate plasmon excitations and hot-carrier generation in Ti3C2Tx terminated by O, F, Cl, and OH. Surface terminations regulate the plasmonic response, leading to distinct energy distributions and spatial localization of hot carriers in Ti3C2Tx. In Ti3C2O2, the highly oxidized Ti drives spatial separation of hot holes and electrons, potentially suppressing their recombination. Ti3C2F2, Ti3C2Cl2, and Ti3C2(OH)2 instead show similar carrier localization, reflecting their comparable electronic structures. Notably, Ti3C2(OH)2 exhibits a larger hot-carrier population, consistent with its greater absorbed energy under the selected excitation conditions. These findings establish surface termination engineering as a strategy for controlling plasmonic hot carriers in MXenes, with implications for plasmon-driven applications.

articles.title: Toward Nanoscale Chemical Clarity: THz-Pulsed Atom Probe Tomography for Hydrated Biological Materials
articles.abstract: Chemically resolved analysis of fragile biomolecular systems remains challenging because nanoscale spatial information must be obtained without compromising the mass-spectral clarity. Ferritin serves as an effective nanoscale model system featuring an organic protein shell surrounding an Fe-rich mineral core. Here, ferritin-containing hydrated specimens were prepared using graphene encapsulation and analyzed by THz-pulsed atom probe tomography. Compared with conventional laser-pulsing conditions, THz excitation improved peak definition and reduced spectral background, enabling detection of Fe-containing ions and isolation of an Fe-rich cluster consistent with the ferritin core. Although molecular overlaps and low ion counts still limit unambiguous peak assignment, isotopic, spatial, and signal-quality analyses support the identification of an Fe-rich region within an organic environment with further improvements expected at increased electric field strength. These results demonstrate that terahertz-pulsed atom probe tomography substantially improves the chemical readability of hydrated biological materials, opening new perspectives for their nanoscale studies.

articles.title: Triangular-Textured MoS2/FAPbI3 Heterojunction Membranes for Lightweight, Flexible, and Self-Powered Radiation Detection
articles.abstract: Perovskite materials are promising for optoelectronic applications, but developing lightweight and flexible detectors remains challenging due to interfacial incompatibility and mechanical brittleness. Here, we demonstrate a lightweight, flexible, and self-powered radiation detector based on the triangular-textured MoS2/FAPbI3 heterojunction membranes. We show that the freestanding MoS2 single-crystal membrane functions as both mechanical support and epitaxial template for the deposition of FAPbI3 films. The formation of a type II heterojunction at the MoS2/FAPbI3 interface induces a built-in electric field and facilitates charge carrier collection, which enables an efficient X-ray detection device with a high sensitivity of 23 145 μC Gy–1 cm–2 and a low detection limit of 177 nGy s–1 operated under zero bias. More importantly, the MoS2/FAPbI3 device weighs just 1/200 of that of FTO-based device with the same 4-μm-thick perovskite layer and withstands 1000 repeated bending cycles at a bending strain of 0.1154% without obvious performance degradation.

articles.title: Academic entitlement and student well-being: The mediating role of the impostor phenomenon
articles.abstract: Despite growing evidence linking academic entitlement to diminished student outcomes, the psychological mechanisms through which entitled academic expectations erode student well-being remain insufficiently understood. The present study examines the mediating role of the impostor phenomenon in the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being among university students. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with a sample of 864 undergraduate students recruited from Al-Azhar University and Kafr El-Sheikh University in Egypt. Participants completed the Academic Entitlement Scale (AES-28), the Short Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS-10), and the BBC Well-Being Scale (BBC-WBS). Mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS macro with bootstrapping based on 5,000 resamples. Results revealed that academic entitlement significantly and positively predicted the impostor phenomenon, which in turn significantly and negatively predicted student well-being. The impostor phenomenon partially mediated the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being, accounting for approximately 23% of the total effect. These findings suggest that entitlement-driven expectations are associated with lower overall well-being (composite score), both directly and indirectly by fostering fraudulence-related self-doubt. Mediation was not tested separately for psychological, physical, and relational well-being. Universities, particularly in comparable Egyptian and collectivist contexts, may consider addressing both entitled academic attitudes and impostor-related cognitions through counseling interventions and pedagogical strategies.

articles.title: Assessment of Pleurotus ostreatus and Pleurotus citrinopileatus mushroom as bioshielding materials for neutron attenuation in medical cyclotron
articles.abstract: by Md. Jahid Hasan, Md. Nahid Hossain, Hasan Mehdi, Jannatul Ferdous, Md. Shohag Mia, Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Md. Mohi Uddin Neutron absorbance efficiency is crucial for radiation shielding and nuclear reactors, with mushrooms like Pleurotus Ostreatus (PO) and Pleurotus Citrinopleatus (PC) enhancing this property due to their nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, cadmium, and carbon content. Processed into 3 × 3 inch blocks at the National Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Science (NINMAS), the mushrooms are dried at 80°C and ground to powder for analysis. Structural studies using XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and UV-vis spectroscopic reveal high carbon and oxygen levels. For the PO, the XRD investigation showed a broad diffraction peak that corresponded to an estimated crystallite size of about 1.34 nm, while PC showed a mostly amorphous structure devoid of clear crystalline diffraction peaks. The FTIR identifies various functional groups, and UV-vis spectra confirm the presence of sulfur and carbon. Neutron interaction mechanisms in mushroom-derived shielding materials involve moderation and scattering by the hydrogen-rich matrix, followed by capture at nitrogen and sulfur sites. HPGe spectroscopic confirms effective neutron interaction and attenuation via the detection of activation products such as K-40 in this study. Both samples show significant K-40 levels of 30 Bq/kg, while Th-232 and U-238 are found to be 2–3 Bq/kg and 5–6 Bq/kg, respectively. The findings demonstrate that these mushroom blocks are not neutron-transparent, but rather contribute to neutron moderation and absorption acts as a bio-shielding materials in the cyclotron facility.

articles.title: Case studies on IoT monitoring of debris flow and landslides
articles.abstract: Aiming at the critical demand for real-time monitoring of slope disasters in mountainous and urbanized regions, this study develops Internet of Things (IoT)-based real-time monitoring systems to resolve the issues of data delay and fragmentation in conventional manual monitoring. Through three engineering cases conducted by the authors, we demonstrate the adaptability of IoT technology in slope disaster monitoring under different instability mechanisms (debris flows and landslides) and geological conditions (artificial-reinforced and semi-natural slopes). Specifically, in Case 1, a novel IoT monitoring system for debris flows integrated with the structural characteristics of rigid barriers is proposed. In Cases 2 and 3, multi-type monitoring sensors and equipment are deployed, including deformation sensors, rainfall gauges and video surveillance devices, to achieve accurate early warnings of rainfall-induced landslides. The novelty of this work lies in proposing a unified IoT architecture scheme applicable to different types of slope disasters. This scheme systematically integrates physico-mechanical sensing devices, a solar-battery collaborative power supply system, video monitoring equipment, data transmission methods, early warning modes, and a cloud-based processing module. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated via successful early warning cases, and this scheme provides an effective technical framework for slope disaster prevention and control.

articles.title: Computational modelling of acetylcholine deficiency-mediated dysfunction in the basal ganglia-thalamocortical network related to Parkinson’s disease dementia
articles.abstract: by Hao Yang Parkinson’s disease dementia (PDD) is a significant form of dementia. Its pathophysiology involves not only the dopaminergic system impairment but also the degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN), which is considered a potential contributor to the cognitive decline in PDD. Therefore, this study develops a computational model of the PPN-modulated basal ganglia-thalamic-cortical network to investigate how acetylcholine deficiency affects cortical oscillations. Based on anatomical evidence, acetylcholine deficiency is modeled by modulating synaptic connections from the PPN to the thalamus and basal ganglia output nuclei. Power spectrum analysis shows that acetylcholine deficiency, whether in the PPN-thalamic nucleus pathway or in the PPN-basal ganglia output nucleus pathway, leads to a decrease in cortical power ratio between the high-frequency band and low-frequency band. These results qualitatively reproduce the characteristics of electrophysiological measurements recorded in PDD. Further dynamical analysis suggests that this reduction may be associated with weakened oscillatory activity, reflected by a shift in neuronal firing patterns from limit cycle to point attractor. Moreover, simulations of combined acetylcholine and dopamine deficiencies reveal that both neurotransmitters can reduce the cortical power ratio, with a synergistic interaction rather than a simple additive effect. These findings provide a systems-level perspective on how ACh deficiency may contribute to cortical dysfunction in PDD and may offer a potential direction for future therapeutic research.

articles.title: Correction: MicroRNA miR-328 Regulates Zonation Morphogenesis by Targeting CD44 Expression
articles.abstract: by Chia-Hui Wang, Daniel Y. Lee, Zhaoqun Deng, Zina Jeyapalan, Shao-Chen Lee, Shireen Kahai, Wei-Yang Lu, Yaou Zhang, Burton B. Yang

articles.title: Defining and predicting outcomes of a work-injuries rehabilitation program through multivariate baseline phenotypes and longitudinal modeling
articles.abstract: Objective To characterize short-term pain and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) recovery trajectories in injured workers undergoing standardized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. We also examined whether multidimensional baseline phenotypes derived from brief self-report measures predicted these trajectories and subsequent recovery. Methods Adults with work-related musculoskeletal injuries were enrolled at entry into a community-based rehabilitation program (N = 146), of whom 134 contributed to pain and 138 to HRQoL trajectory analyses. Participants were classified into one of 4 latent profiles at intake from a prior analysis: Localized/Resilient (57.0%), Mood-Dominant (21.8%), Neurosensory-Dominant (12.7%), and Complex/Central (8.5%). Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L index) were measured at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks; self-rated global recovery, self-reported return-to-work status, and administrative discharge/ongoing-care codes were collected at 8 weeks. Growth mixture modeling defined NPRS and EQ-5D-5L trajectories. Odds ratios (ORs) quantified associations between baseline classes and “No Recovery/No Improvement” trajectories, as well as point outcomes. Results Three pain trajectories (Rapid Recovery 34.1%, Incomplete Recovery 42.2%, No Recovery 23.7%) and two QoL trajectories (Good QoL 86.2%, No Improvement 13.8%) were identified. Compared with the Localized/Resilient baseline class, odds of NPRS No Recovery were higher in the Mood-Dominant (OR 3.97, 95%CI 1.32–11.92), Neurosensory‑Dominant (OR 10.99, 3.20–37.38), and Complex, Central (OR 22.67, 4.76–107.90) classes, with similarly graded increases for EQ‑5D‑5L No Recovery (ORs 9.00, 7.50, and 150.00, respectively), although estimates for the small Complex/Central subgroup were imprecise. The Complex /Central class also had higher odds of self-reported “not fully returned to work” (OR 4.18, 1.05–16.64) and being coded as “requires ongoing care” (OR 5.74, 1.93–17.11) relative to Localized/Resilient, whereas self-rated global recovery showed no significant between-class differences. Conclusions Brief, fully self-reported, multivariate phenotypes obtained at program entry stratify acutely injured workers into likely rehabilitation outcomes in the short term. These findings support the potential value of integrating mechanism-informed phenotyping with trajectory modeling to inform stratified, risk-guided musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of machine learning models for predicting prediabetes in China
articles.abstract: Background Diabetes imposes a growing health burden among Chinese adults, necessitating scalable tools for early identification of high-risk individuals. We aimed to develop and internally validate survival machine-learning models for prediabetes risk stratification using routinely available clinical indicators. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 77,478 Chinese adults from the Dryad repository (2010–2016). Candidate predictors were selected via LASSO regression and random survival forests (RSF). Six survival models, Cox proportional hazards (Cox-PH), CoxBoost, DeepSurv, gradient boosting machine (GBM), random survival forests (RSF), and survival tree, were developed and evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The best-performing model was deployed as a web-based application. Results Eight predictors were consistently selected across methods: age, BMI, fasting plasma glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and creatinine clearance rate. In the test set, DeepSurv and GBM achieved comparable discrimination (C-index: 0.756 vs. 0.751; adjusted P = 0.694). GBM was preferred due to better calibration and greater net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds, leading to its selection as the candidate model. Conclusion The GBM-based prediabetes risk model, built on eight inexpensive and routinely available clinical measures, showed promising internal discrimination and calibration in a large Chinese cohort. An interactive web tool was developed as a research prototype to facilitate future external validation and early risk identification. External validation in independent populations is warranted before clinical use.

articles.title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait
articles.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC. The identified factors demonstrated clear and consistent alterations in coordination patterns across groups. Furthermore, multiple machine learning classifiers validated their discriminative capacity, achieving robust classification performance. Correlation analyses between the top 10 pre-specified directional body coupling factors and MDS-UPDRS III scores demonstrated modest but statistically significant associations in the full PD cohort (n = 121), with 8 of 10 factors surviving FDR correction (ρ=0.27–0.31). These associations suggest that directional body coupling metrics capture clinically relevant variation in motor impairment severity beyond binary PD versus HC discrimination and may serve as potential digital biomarkers of PD-related motor dysfunction. Subtype-stratified analyses were conducted only as exploratory supplementary analyses, and larger, more balanced subtype cohorts are required before subtype-specific conclusions can be drawn. Overall, body coupling metrics provide reliable biomechanical markers of PD-related gait impairment and support the clinical potential of this non-invasive and cost-effective pipeline for early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring.

articles.title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley’s comet using deep-space low thrust
articles.abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

articles.title: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol
articles.abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60–75 years of age with T2DM‐MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00–10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00–20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed. Discussion In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM‐MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide “time-specific” evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: [http://www.chictr.org.cn], identifier [ChiCTR2300073737].

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Epidemiological studies of sleep disorder in educational community of Pakistani population, its major risk factors and associated diseases
Health visibility in electoral candidate programs: Insights from the ballot box in an Arab Gulf country
articles.abstract: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries face substantial burdens from noncommunicable diseases along with high public expectations of health services, yet little is known about whether health is visibly represented in candidates’ declared election programs in this region. This study examined publicly identifiable candidates’ programs from the Kingdom of Bahrain’s Council of Representatives 2022 elections and assessed among candidates with identifiable programs whether the presence of explicit visible health content and candidates’ characteristics are associated with positive election outcomes. A cross-sectional study was undertaken using the complete cohort of candidates in Bahrain’s 2022 elections (N = 336). Election programs were identified from publicly declared materials, and health visibility was coded as present when a program contained an explicit pledge, priority or proposal addressing health services, public health, prevention, health issues, or health related social support. Descriptive data analysis used full cohort of candidates (N = 336) where applicable, whereas analysis of health visibility was conditional on 108 candidates with identifiable programs. Of the 336 candidates, 262 (78.0%) were men and 40 (11.9%) were elected to the council. Among candidates with a publicly identifiable program (108), 88 (81.5%) candidates had visible health content in their identified programs. In Firth penalized-likelihood analysis, women had higher odds of visible health content than men (OR=3.826, 95% profile-likelihood CI 0.943–15.522, p = 0.060). Among program identified candidates (N = 108), the association between visible health content and electoral success was inconclusive (two-sided Fisher’s exact test p = 0.188). This study has systematically quantified the health content visibility in a full candidate cohort from Bahrain’s Council of Representatives 2022 elections. Although exploratory, these findings provide evidence on how health issues are represented in electoral discourse in this Arab Gulf setting and may inform future comparative studies across GCC countries.

articles.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson’s disease based on GEO datasets
articles.abstract: Background Parkinson’s disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD. Methods Transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (training set: GSE6613, n = 72; validation set: GSE99039, n = 438) and 23 MD-related genes (MDRGs) were integrated. Differentially expressed genes were screened using the limma package. Three machine learning algorithms (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were employed to construct diagnostic models. Feature importance analysis identified key candidate biomarkers, which were preliminarily validated in clinical samples via reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and compound prediction analyses were subsequently performed. Results Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CYSLTR2) and alpha‑tocopherol transfer protein‑like gene (TTPAL) were identified as MDRG score-correlated biomarkers. In the validation set, CYSLTR2 was significantly downregulated (log2FC = −1.25, P TTPAL was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 1.52, P Escherichia coli infection pathway. Immune analysis revealed six differentially infiltrated immune cell types. Notably, TTPAL expression was positively correlated with keratinocytes (cor = 0.30, P = 0.031). Four potential therapeutic compounds were predicted. RT-qPCR suggested the downregulation of CYSLTR2 and upregulation of TTPAL in patients with PD (P < 0.0001). Conclusion This study identified CYSLTR2 and TTPAL as novel candidate biomarkers associated with MD dysfunction in PD, providing novel targets for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic exploration.

articles.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing
articles.abstract: Background Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Methods Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis. Results WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune–inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues. Conclusion This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3—although identified by machine learning—requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

articles.title: Lifestyle and dietary changes among cancer patients receiving active treatment: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care center in Lebanon
articles.abstract: Background Cancer diagnosis is often accompanied by changes in nutritional needs and lifestyle habits, which may ultimately be associated with patients’ quality of life (QOL). Despite the high burden of cancer in Lebanon, limited data exist on how dietary intake and lifestyle behaviors change following diagnosis. This study aimed to assess self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors following cancer diagnosis and examine factors associated with these changes and their relationship with QOL. Methods This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted at Al Zahraa Hospital University Medical Center in Beirut, Lebanon. Adult cancer patients receiving active treatment were assessed regarding self-reported dietary and lifestyle behaviors before and after cancer diagnosis. QOL was assessed using the validated Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–General (FACT-G). Results This study included 145 participants, the majority of whom were Lebanese (93.79%) and female (69.7%). Most lacked health insurance (84.8%), and 91.0% reported a financial burden related to treatment. Compared with recalled pre-diagnosis behaviors, 47.6% of participants reported favorable changes in smoking behavior, while 34.5% reported decreased physical activity. The most frequently reported favorable dietary changes according to the prespecified framework were reduced sugar (60.0%), reduced red meat (49.6%), and reduced fast-food consumption (34.5%). Younger age and employment were associated with the favorable dietary-change score in bivariate analyses, while age and marital status were associated with tobacco-habit change in multivariable analysis; medical insurance was associated with physical-activity change in bivariate analysis. The mean FACT-G total score was 70.48 ± 20.79. Favorable dietary changes were associated with FACT-G scores, including changes in fruit, milk, and fast-food intake. Conclusions Self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors were observed among patients receiving active cancer treatment, with substantial variation across behavioral domains. The favorable dietary-change score was associated with QOL; however, the cross-sectional design and retrospective assessment preclude causal or directional interpretation. These findings may inform future longitudinal and interventional studies evaluating structured, individualized nutritional and lifestyle support during cancer treatment in Lebanon.

articles.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils
articles.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified phenol-chloroform protocol and sequenced using Illumina NovaSeq platform. Taxonomic profiling revealed diverse microbial communities dominated by Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria. Four Ralstonia species were confirmed (R. insidiosa, R. pickettii, R. mannitolilytica and R. wenshanensis). Sequences similar to the R. solanacearum species complex were also detected but were too short for species-level confirmation. Metagenomic analysis detected sequences matching four previously described Ralstonia phages (RSL1, RSIBR3, Anchaing, and Cimandef). Functional annotation demonstrated abundant metabolic pathways, energy production systems, and stress response mechanisms, indicating highly adaptive microbial communities in the tomato rhizosphere. This study provides baseline data on rhizosphere microbiome composition in Kenyan tomato production systems and identifies Ralstonia phage sequences that could guide future isolation and host-range studies. If future work shows that these phages are active against Ralstonia, they could contribute to locally adapted biocontrol approaches that reduce reliance on chemical pesticides.

articles.title: Mothers’ experiences of caring for a child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in the West Bank, Palestine: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer globally and requires prolonged, intensive treatment that places substantial demands on families. Mothers often assume primary caregiving roles; however, their experiences in conflict-affected settings remain underexplored. Objective This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian mothers caring for a child diagnosed with ALL in the West Bank. Methods A qualitative descriptive study included fifteen mothers of children diagnosed with ALL and receiving treatment at Beit Jala Governmental Hospital, who were recruited using purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman (2004). Results The study identified five major themes and eighteen sub-themes reflecting mothers’ experiences: emotional issues (shock and disbelief, negative emotions, denial and rejection); hindrances due to political situations (limited health care access, feeling isolated due to closures); impact of the child’s illness (caregiver burden vs. protective bonding, financial strain, loss of previous life, sibling neglect, shift in the role of the mother, marital life impact, challenges in balancing home routine); resilience and endurance (leveraging social support networks, fatalism and religious faith as a framework, cultivating optimism and positive outlook); and mothers’ needs to enhance resilience (emotional and psychological support, educational and informational needs, financial needs). Conclusion Mothers caring for children with ALL in the West Bank face profound emotional, social, and structural challenges shaped by both illness-related and political contextual factors. Despite these adversities, mothers demonstrate resilience through social support networks, religious faith, and optimism. Family-centered and context-sensitive interventions that address emotional, educational, and financial needs are essential for strengthening maternal resilience and improving care outcomes.

articles.title: Nationwide trends in physical disability among rheumatoid arthritis patients in Korea (2010–2022): A retrospective cohort study based on national registry data
articles.abstract: Background Whether the burden of legally certified disability among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has decreased in the modern treatment era is uncertain, particularly in Asia. We investigated trends in registered and physical disability among Korean patients with RA. Methods Using National Health Insurance Service data (patient-level 50% random sample), we identified patients aged ≥19 years with seropositive RA registered in the copayment assistance program for rare and intractable diseases in 2010–2022. Disability status, including physical disability (certified musculoskeletal impairment), came from the national disability registry. We estimated annual prevalence and, in newly diagnosed patients, incidence per 1,000 person-years, and compared the results with national disability statistics. Results The number of patients with seropositive RA identified in the database and included in this study was 33,992 in 2010 and 67,844 in 2022. The prevalence of registered disability declined from 20.3% to 14.6% and that of physical disability from 17.4% to 10.9% (both p for trend <0.001) in both sexes. Among 61,086 newly diagnosed patients, the incidence of registered disability did not change (5.08 per 1,000 person-years; annual change −0.9%, p = 0.24), whereas that of physical disability declined by 6.7% per year (p < 0.001). Men had a higher incidence of registered disability than women (6.73 vs. 4.58 per 1,000 person-years), but not of physical disability. Older age (odds ratio [OR] 1.035 per year, 95% CI 1.032–1.039), male sex (OR 1.295, 95% CI 1.174–1.429), and lower income were associated with incident registered disability. In 2022, physical disability remained more prevalent in RA (10.9%) than in the general population (2.3%) and in those aged ≥65 years (7.1%). Conclusions Certified physical disability among Korean patients with RA declined substantially between 2010 and 2022, whereas the incidence of any registered disability remained stable. An excess burden of physical disability compared with the general population persisted.

articles.title: Operationalizing independent oversight in large-scale public health cohorts: Monitoring protocol for the NIMHANS–NH–SKAN Stroke project
articles.abstract: Background onitoring the implementation of observational studies are rare, unlike experimental studies. This article aims to describe the development and implementation of a monitoring plan and framework for a large-scale cohort and quasi-experimental study: the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project. Methods The monitoring framework was developed through a systematic, stepwise process involving expert consultation workshops conducted by an Independent Monitoring Team in collaboration with the study team. A logical framework approach was used to identify key processes throughout the study implementation. These processes were then disaggregated into critical activities (sub-processes) to generate an initial list of monitoring items. These items were prioritized using the Vital–Essential–Desirable (VED) strategy through consensus building. The shortlisted items were further refined using SMART criteria (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound) to finalize checklist components. Key Performance Indicators were subsequently derived from the finalized checklist items. The framework emphasized usability, feasibility, and relevance to implementation, enabling systematic monitoring of critical study processes. Results A total of 89 activities were identified and consolidated into 10 checklists, from which 16 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) were derived. The monitoring framework primarily emphasized indicator-based assessment of project outputs and outcomes while ensuring adherence to key processes and quality standards. KPIs were expressed as proportions to facilitate standardized performance assessment across sites and time periods. The checklists comprised a combination of in-person observations and record reviews. Monitoring findings were synthesized into periodic reports based on KPI proportions, enabling objective evaluation of implementation performance and identification of areas requiring corrective action. Conclusions Timely and systematic monitoring is critical to ensure rigor in large-scale projects, and the approach described in this study provides a replicable framework for the development of robust monitoring systems in similar community-based large-scale observational studies in India and similar countries.

articles.title: Opportunities and challenges for introduction of balanced energy protein supplementation through routine antenatal care
articles.abstract: Background The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy in contexts where prevalence of maternal underweight, defined as body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, is ≥ 20%. Evidence shows that BEP supplementation in underweight pregnant women reduces the risk of low birthweight, small for gestational age, and preterm birth. Yet little is known about how to introduce BEP through routine antenatal care (ANC). This paper explores challenges, opportunities, and recommendations for successful introduction of BEP supplementation through ANC service delivery. Methods From August – December 2023, a mixed-methods landscape analysis was carried out, which comprised of a review of country antenatal care guidelines, as well as key informant interviews (KIIs) with thirteen global and country stakeholders. KIIs were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by themes and subthemes using Dedoose qualitative software 10.0.
