articles.title: A Reproducible Decomposed Large Language Model Pipeline for Structured Abstraction of Multimodal Neuroimaging Reports: Development and Independent Validation in 1,669 Emergency Department Encounters for Dizziness and Vertigo
articles.abstract: Objective: To develop and independently validate a decomposed, modality-specific large language model (LLM) pipeline that abstracts structured variables from the free-text neuroimaging reports of a multimodal stroke workup, and to validate the resulting structured dataset for reuse in downstream research. Materials and Methods: A frozen pipeline (temperature 0) extracting 22 variables across CT head, CT angiography, CT perfusion, and MRI brain was applied to 1,669 ED encounters for dizziness or vertigo; 11 variables were pre-specified as primary (Tier 1). Reproducibility used three same-session runs and a nine-week repeat run; three frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.5 Flash) measured cross-model agreement (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa). Accuracy was assessed in an independent 200-encounter cohort (150 random, 50 enriched for rare findings); 100 were double-read by two blinded reviewers with discordances adjudicated. Results: Test-retest reproducibility was high (Tier 1 Fleiss' kappa = 0.993; 99.8% exact) and stable nine weeks later (kappa = 0.992); inter-model agreement was kappa = 0.962. Against the adjudicated reference, pooled Tier 1 accuracy was 0.971 to 0.988 across models (Cohen's kappa 0.959 to 0.982), comparable to inter-reviewer agreement (kappa = 0.932). Accuracy was 0.980 to 0.983 in random and 0.955 to 0.977 in enriched encounters (agreement on model-flagged findings, not sensitivity). Discussion: A decomposed LLM pipeline produced reproducible, model-portable, stable, and accurate multimodal abstraction. Because schema design and validation are up-front costs, such pipelines scale to larger research cohorts. Conclusion: The quantified per-field error rates support reuse of this dataset with field-specific review, and such pipelines offer a practical path to large-scale, reproducible research datasets.

articles.title: A population-based resource for the prioritization of rare variants of unknown significance in clinical genomics
articles.abstract: Rare diseases represent a major public health challenge because they are often associated with severe phenotypes, yet many causal variants remain undiscovered. Founder populations provide a unique opportunity to identify disease-causing variants through the local enrichment of rare alleles. Using whole-genome sequencing data from individuals in the Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean population, enriched variants were identified and their founder status was assessed through identity-by-descent sharing. Variant impact was evaluated using functional prediction tools without relying on prior clinical classification. A total of 131 founder variants of interest were identified, most of which would likely have been overlooked by conventional approaches based on existing clinical annotations. We developed a web-based platform that facilitates clinician access to the latest interpretation of their genetic variants of interest. These findings demonstrate that potentially pathogenic variants can remain undetected even in extensively studied founder populations. More broadly, they highlight the value of population structure-based approaches for uncovering rare disease variants and improving the characterization of genetic disease risk across human populations.

articles.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions
articles.abstract: Background: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. Methods: We applied a pre-trained deep learning model to brightfield images of single cells from malignant effusions of 10 patients with metastatic breast cancer to extract morphological features, quantify tumor cell fraction (TCF), and guide label-free microfluidic enrichment. We profiled copy-number alterations and somatic mutations in enriched tumor cell fractions and compared them with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors. Results: AI-powered single-cell morphological analysis identified putative tumor cells in all 10 patients (median TCF, 5.4%; range, 0.51-15.8%; n = 25 samples). AI estimates of major immune-cell populations varied across patients and samples and correlated with flow cytometry measurements (n = 21 paired samples, Pearson r = 0.69-0.75). Unsupervised analysis identified four tumor cell morphotypes, revealing intra- and inter-patient morphological heterogeneity and longitudinal variation in morphotype composition. Genomic profiling of enriched tumor cell fractions by low-pass whole-genome sequencing (n = 26 samples) and whole-exome sequencing (n = 24 samples) identified copy-number alterations and somatic mutations, with tumor fraction influencing genomic signal strength. Comparisons of genomic profiles from tumor cell-enriched fractions with matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors revealed shared genomic alterations, providing orthogonal support for tumor origin and relatedness, while differences across analytes revealed genomic divergence and tumor heterogeneity. Conclusion: AI-powered analysis leverages single-cell morphology for tumor cell identification and label-free enrichment, while integration with genomic profiling enables simultaneous interrogation of phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. This approach expands the potential of malignant effusions for liquid biopsy applications and biomarker development and discovery.

articles.title: Accuracy and precision of visual acuity tests: A systematic review and meta-analysis across testing strategies
articles.abstract: Purpose: Visual acuity (VA) testing has expanded from examiner-guided to examinee self-guided assessments, yet measurement variability may limit clinical utility. This meta-analysis investigated VA-test's intertest and test-retest accuracy and precision across different testing strategies. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for VA validation studies published between 1 January 1983 to 02 December 2024. Eligible studies reported intertest or test-retest Bland-Altman mean bias and limits of agreement (LoA); objective VA assessments and correlation coefficient only studies were excluded. Testing strategies were classified by test site, optotype sampling methods, response input methods, and level of supervision. Accuracy outcomes were reported as mean biases. Precision outcomes were reported as intertest LoA half-width and test-retest coefficient of repeatability (CoR) for test-retest. Multilevel random-effects models accounted for multiple estimates per study. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results: Across 82 included studies (10,873 participants), pooled intertest and test-retest mean biases were both 0.01 logMAR. Intertest LoA half-width was 0.19 logMAR and test-retest CoR was 0.14 logMAR. Variability showed marginal difference by optotype sampling (adaptive: LoA half-width 0.20 logMAR, CoR 0.15 logMAR; fixed: 0.18, 0.13) or response input method (examiner: 0.19, 0.13; self-run: 0.19, 0.18). Only few studies reported results for test site and level of supervision, hence only intertest was compared (test site, clinic: LoA half-width 0.19 logMAR vs remote 0.27 logMAR and level of supervision, supervised: 0.19 logMAR vs unsupervised 0.26 logMAR). QUADAS-2 identified patient selection as the domain of greatest bias concern. Conclusion: Across testing strategies, VA assessments showed minimal systematic bias but substantial variability. Lack of precision is more notable in remote and unsupervised testing while no difference within optotype sampling and response-input methods. Future development should prioritize on improving precision of visual acuity tests with finer adaptive optotype resolution and remote/unsupervised testings through repeatability studies.

articles.title: An Edge-AI Pose-Estimation Platform for Real-Time Posture and Posture-Transition Monitoring: A Feasibility Study for Pre-Emptive Fall-Risk Alerting in Elderly and Dementia Care
articles.abstract: Falls and unmonitored patient movements remain leading causes of harm in healthcare settings. Current solutions - such as weight-based alarms, remote video monitoring, and in-person sitters - are reactive, labor-intensive, or prone to false alarms, often compromising both care quality and staff efficiency. We developed a machine learning-enabled, proactive-preventive patient monitoring platform that uses 17-keypoint pose estimation to detect changes in patient posture and generate alerts in real time. The Edge-AI device integrates a Raspberry Pi 5, Hailo-8L neural processing unit (NPU), and Raspberry Pi camera module 3, and runs Hailo-YOLOv8-Pose at 30 frames per second to classify postures (i.e., lying, Fowlers, sitting, standing). Alerts are transmitted via Bluetooth to caregivers through earphones or speakers. System performance was evaluated across multiple scenarios, including bed and chair monitoring, free limb movement, partial body occlusion (e.g., blankets), and varying lighting and care environments. The platform maintained accurate monitoring under varying lighting conditions, including lights-off scenarios, and because all processing occurs locally without network dependence, it is designed to continue operating during network outages - an important resilience feature for care environments where connectivity may be interrupted. By abstracting images into skeletal keypoints without recording video, the system preserves privacy while potentially enabling earlier intervention and reducing false alarms and caregiver workload. This cost-effective, scalable system supports future enhancements such as dual alerting, multi-device full-room coverage, and continuous monitoring for dementia patients.

articles.title: Applying Diagnostic Network Optimisation analysis to inform the introduction of G6PD testing into Indonesia for improved treatment of relapsing malaria
articles.abstract: Background: Radical cure for P. vivax and P. ovale malaria using 8-aminoquinoline drugs primaquine or tafenoquine can prevent relapse, but requires glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) screening due to the risk of haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals. This study aimed to provide an evidence-based framework to inform the optimal allocation and referral networks for G6PD testing devices in Indonesia. Methods: A diagnostic network optimisation (DNO) analysis using OptiDx was conducted across eight districts in Sumba, North Sumatra, and Central Java, representing high-, moderate-, and low-transmission settings. The maximum annual number of malaria cases from surveillance data between 2019 and 2022 was used as a proxy for testing demand. In baseline scenario, all public health facilities were equipped with G6PD testing devices. In referral scenario, devices were allocated only to selected facilities, with a maximum sample transport distance of 15 kilometres and sample delivery scheduled three times per week. Model outputs were reviewed with the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) to identify the optimal scenario, considering factors including implementation cost and accessibility. Results: Equipping 39% (30/76) of facilities in Sumba with G6PD testing devices could reduce total costs by nearly 30% in the first year and approximately 20% in subsequent years compared with the baseline, although the average referral distance increased from 4.48 kilometres to 9.8 kilometres. In North Sumatra, deploying 15 of 68 devices (19%) could reduce total costs by almost 60% in the first year and approximately 15% thereafter. Two health facilities (Puskesmas Padewatu in Sumba and Abdul Manan Hospital in North Sumatra) could experience workload increase exceeding 400 hours annually as referral facilities. In Purworejo, a single device placed at Puskesmas Mranti could enable on-site diagnosis for 56% of patients. Interpretation: The findings demonstrated that DNO can identify cost-efficient and equitable G6PD testing strategies to support safe radical cure and accelerate malaria elimination.

articles.title: Balancing Analgesic Effects and Abuse Liability in Older Adults: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Oral and Vaporized Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol
articles.abstract: Cannabis use is rising fastest among older adults in the U.S., and pain is among the most common reasons they use it. No trial, however, has measured the trade-off between the analgesic and abuse-related effects of {Delta}9-tetrahydrocannabinol ({Delta}9-THC) in this population. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 20 adults aged 65 and older were assigned to oral {Delta}9-THC (placebo, 5, 10 mg) or vaporized {Delta}9-THC (placebo, 2, 4 mg) across three eight-hour sessions in counterbalanced order. We assessed laboratory-evoked pain sensitivity using quantitative sensory testing, abuse liability using subjective drug effects and reinforcement value, and also sampled plasma {Delta}9-THC and 11-OH-THC. Analgesia and abuse liability outcomes were measured repeatedly within each session. On a pain sensitivity index, oral 5 mg relieved pain relative to placebo (p=.040), although the oral arm's overall dose effect was not significant (p=.108); oral 10 mg and both vaporized doses did not differ from placebo. Subjective effects increased with dose and were greatest after vaporization, whereas reinforcement value increased only after vaporized 4 mg. After oral 5 mg, analgesia exceeded placebo at every assessment (60-360 min), while its pleasurable effects peaked at 150 min. Vaporized {Delta}9-THC produced pleasurable effects within 30 min but did not significantly change thermal pain sensitivity. While abuse liability tracked {Delta}9-THC exposure, analgesia showed no significant association, and all adverse events occurred at vaporized 4 mg. These findings suggest dose and route selection may help maximize {Delta}9-THC analgesia while minimizing abuse liability, a strategy that warrants evaluation in clinical populations.

articles.title: Before AI tells patients what to eat, it needs to know where they live: a cross-sectional ecological study of diabetes and food access in California and Michigan census tracts, with a spotlight on Metro Detroit and Metro Los Angeles
articles.abstract: Background: AI chatbots now give people with diabetes diet advice, but whether those foods can be bought near home is rarely checked. Methods: In a cross-sectional ecological study of 11,974 California and Michigan census tracts, I linked diabetes prevalence (CDC PLACES 2025) with two USDA food-access maps: all SNAP-authorized stores (2025) and large grocery stores only (2019). I identified double-burden tracts (high diabetes and low income/low access) and hidden food deserts (low access to large grocery stores, but not to any SNAP store). In a pilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude generated meal plans for the same person across 20 high-diabetes tracts in Metro Los Angeles and Metro Detroit; I scored whether advice was healthy and whether foods were sold at nearby store types. Results: Double-burden tracts were few (71 in California, 19 in Michigan), almost none in the two metros. Food-desert tracts had a 1.5 percentage-point higher diabetes prevalence (95% CI, 1.0-2.0). Counting all SNAP stores hid 567 Californian and 329 Michigan food deserts; in Metro Detroit, all 97 disappeared, including 51 high-diabetes tracts with about 19,500 adults with diabetes. Chatbot advice was healthy, but in hidden tracts 30% of recommended foods were not reliably sold nearby; the chatbots barely adjusted. Of 55 places they named, 13% had errors, and most were over a mile away. Conclusions: The current USDA map obscures food deserts, especially in Detroit, and AI diet advice barely adjusts for them. AI nutrition tools for diabetes should include a place-aware check built on public food-access data.

articles.title: Biomarkers of ageing and lung function trajectory: a multi-omics study in a UK birth cohort
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accelerated biological ageing and cellular senescence are pathogenically implicated in COPD and may represent therapeutic targets. Adverse early-life lung function trajectories offer opportunities to prevent COPD but their relationship with epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers remains unexplored. We investigated using conventional epidemiological and Mendelian randomisation (MR) methods. METHODS: Outcomes were the two lowest of five FEV1 trajectories (Persistently Low and Below Average) previously identified using latent profile analysis (ages 8-30) in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children. Exposures included nine measures of blood-derived epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and thirteen senescence-associated plasma proteins (ages 7-9). We used logistic regression to estimate odds of lower trajectory membership by exposure and bidirectional one-sample MR to investigate causation. RESULTS: Higher plasma CXCL10 (OR 1.29 per SD; 95% CI 1.03, 1.57), IL6 (OR 1.29; 1.03, 1.57) and IL33 (OR 1.23; 1.04, 1.44) were associated with Persistently Low lung function trajectory, with little evidence for associations between EAA and lower trajectories. MR provided little evidence that genetically predicted plasma proteins influenced risk of lower trajectories, but lower genetically proxied childhood FEV1 predicted higher plasma CXCL10 at ages 9 ({beta} -0.34; -0.65, -0.03) and 24 ({beta} -0.38; -0.67, -0.08). INTERPRETATION: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, predict low lung function trajectory into early adulthood. Lower childhood lung function may causally relate to persistently increased plasma CXCL10. Future research should investigate IL33 as a potential therapeutic target in low lung function trajectory and persistent systemic inflammation as a mechanism for associated multimorbidity.

articles.title: CSF PrP-amyloid seeding predicts clinical onset in inherited prion disease
articles.abstract: Silent proteopathic seed propagation is hypothesised to precede neurodegenerative disease, but direct evidence that it signals near-term clinical conversion in humans is lacking. In prion disease, a prototypic disorder of proteopathic seeding, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) offers a direct measure of prion protein amyloid seeding activity. We analysed longitudinal CSF RT-QuIC data from 94 PRNP E200K mutation carriers across international natural history cohorts to determine whether seeding status predicts clinical conversion. Eleven carriers developed inherited prion disease; all showed at least one positive RT-QuIC result before onset. First positivity appeared a median of 2.0 years prior to symptoms (IQR 1.3-3.3; range 0.2-4.8). Landmark analyses showed RT-QuIC positivity identified a markedly increased short-term conversion risk, whereas persistently asymptomatic carriers remained negative throughout follow-up. These findings establish CSF RT-QuIC positivity as a biomarker-defined state of incipient conversion in E200K carriers, informing risk stratification and preventive trial design.

articles.title: Career development awards are associated with lower career-long research attrition risk in Veterans Affairs investigators.
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate research attrition and the associated factors among US Department of Veterans Affairs investigators with and without a prior Career Development Award (CDA) from fiscal year 2008 to 2026. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Methods : Investigators whose CDA ended between October 2008 and March 2026 were identified from the Research Analysis and Forecasting Tool (RAFT) database and compared to non-CDA peers. Extracted descriptive variables included sex, investigator type, doctoral degree, salary source, specialty, and research area. Attrition, derived from the electronic Project Management and Information System, was defined when an investigator ceased serving as a principal or coinvestigator on VA-funded research. Analysis utilized attrition percentages, crude count ratios (CR), chi-squared statistics, and multivariable binomial regression to assess adjusted odds ratios (ORadj). Results: Investigators with a prior CDA were 42% less likely to attrite from VA research engagement compared to non-CDA counterparts (CR 95% CI, 0.50-0.67, p<.001). They maintained high engagement regardless of demographic or professional variables (engagement ranges: 66.7%-93.8%). Clinician-scientists were 34% less likely to attrite from science (ORadj 0.54) compared to non-clinician scientists. The 1.68-times higher crude attrition risk for non-VA salaried investigators became non-significant after adjusting for other factors. Attrition was significantly higher in basic science and engineering (ORadj 3.90), endocrinology, metabolism, and nutrition (ORadj 4.24), infectious disease (ORadj 3.80), aging and geriatrics (ORadj 3.56), and cardiopulmonary and vascular research (ORadj 2.70) compared to health services and epidemiology. Conclusion: Prior CDA recipients demonstrate significantly lower research attrition in VA research.

articles.title: Clinical and Social Determinants of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Optimization in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
articles.abstract: Background: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF has been shown to improve outcomes, with higher GDMT scores at hospital discharge being associated with lower mortality, fewer rehospitalizations and reduced healthcare costs. Yet, disparities in the utilization of GDMT remain. In this study, we examined the effect of various clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic factors on the utilization of GDMT in HFrEF patients referred to Cardiology in a tertiary care safety net hospital, using a standardized GDMT scoring system. Methods: We conducted a single-center cross-sectional retrospective analysis of patients who had an index HFrEF 40% diagnosis between January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024, and who were referred to Cardiology at a tertiary care safety net hospital. Baseline characteristics, laboratory investigations, health care utilization, and GDMT score data were extracted at the ambulatory care visit nearest to 90 days from the index HF diagnosis. GDMT score ranges from 0 to 9 factored in doses of beta-blocker (BB), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker (ACEi/ARB), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (ISDN/HYD). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations between low GDMT scores (0-4) nearest to 90 days from new onset HFrEF diagnosis and several clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic variables. Results: In 200 patients meeting entry criteria, mean age was 62.7 years, 64.0% were male, 47.5% were classified as white and 42.0% as Black. 39.5% had a low GDTM score (<5). The following were less likely to be associated with low GDMT score: diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR: 0.41, 95%CI=0.18-0.91) and frequent medical appointments (adjusted OR: 0.37, 95% CI=0.25-0.54), while higher serum eGFR was more likely to be associated with low GDMT score (adjusted OR: 1.02, 95%CI=1.00-1.03). There was no significant association between GDMT score and age, sex, race, or payer status. Conclusion: In patients with HFrEF referred to Cardiology in our safety net tertiary care center, higher utilization of GDMT at 90 days was achieved in those who have diabetes mellitus, more frequent medical appointments, or lower serum eGFR. There was no difference in GDMT utilization according to age, sex, race, or payer status predictive of lower GDMT scores. Contrary to findings from previous studies, no significant differences were observed across demographic or payer groups, emphasizing the role of healthcare access and utilization.

articles.title: Combined Use of Topic-Analysis and LLMs on Online Peer-to-Peer Medicaid Discussions to Detect the Impact of HR1 on Individuals Medicaid Experience Across The US
articles.abstract: Medicaid is a government program providing benefits to 1 in 5 people in the US, including medical care for children and adults, long-term care for the elderly, and home/community-based services for the disabled[1]. Effective January 1st 2027, HR1 (One Big Beautiful Bill) passed by Congress will implement new administrative requirements to Medicaid expected to strip benefits from 1.8 million adults, children, and seniors[2]. As each US state administers Medicaid independently, the timing, frequency, and severity of those losses may vary across states. Monitoring that human impact requires an detailed ongoing view of affected individuals and their families. To monitor the human-impact of HR1, this work develops a proof-of-concept using topic analysis and LLMs to generate detailed categorization of individuals' Medicaid experiences across multiple states and over time.

articles.title: Consumer continuous glucose monitoring uncovers hidden metabolic risk in free-living adults without diabetes
articles.abstract: Whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides actionable information in adults without diabetes is contested, as its metrics were designed for diabetes and screening relies on HbA1c. In this cross-sectional study of 62,122 free-living adults on the Levels digital-health platform, average glucose was the most reliable measure across weeks (intraclass correlation 0.747). Among 7,930 participants without diabetes with laboratory data, it tracked insulin resistance, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, uric acid, and C-reactive protein more closely than HbA1c, explaining nearly three times more variance in fasting insulin (R2 0.131 vs 0.048). With a normal HbA1c, occult hyperinsulinemia (fasting insulin [≥]10 {micro}IU/mL) was twice as common at average glucose [≥]110 mg/dL (27.5% vs 12.6%). Counterintuitively, at the same average glucose, spike width, not height or frequency, tracked insulin resistance, triglycerides, and C-reactive protein; carbohydrate sensitivity, although reliable, did not track insulin resistance. This analysis suggests a framework for interpreting CGM in adults without diabetes.

articles.title: Cross-reactive antibody and functional T-cell responses to Bundibugyo virus induced by Zaire ebolavirus vaccination and infection
articles.abstract: Background There is no licensed specific vaccine against the current Ebola Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbeak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo. However, clinical evaluations of a licensed Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) vaccine have just launched. It remains unclear whether EBOV infection or vaccination generate cross-reactive immunity against BDBV. Methods We quantified CD4 and CD8 T-cell magnitude, polyfunctionality, and cytotoxicity after 8-day expansion with EBOV, BDBV, Sudan (SUDV), or Marburg (MARV) GP peptide pools, and measured GP-binding antibodies by multiplex assay, in recipients of Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (n=10), single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=10), or two-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=8) ( NCT02876328 ), and in EVD survivors sampled approximately 3 years after infection (n=10). Findings Fourteen days after completion of each licensed vaccine regimen, median BDBV-reactive CD4 responses were 9.8% [IQR:8.9-14.0] after single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (D14) and 8.0% [5.5-9.9] after Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (D70). The highest BDBV-reactive CD8response was observed in survivors (24.7% [20.3-33.1]), together with a prominent cytotoxic CD8 response (14.4% [10.4-19.7]) ; corresponding vaccine-group medians ranged from 0.9% to 17.7% and from 0.6% to 6.7%, respectively. SUDV responses were also detected, whereas MARV recognition was limited. BDBV-binding antibodies were detected following both vaccine regimens, with the highest levels observed in survivors (491 [330-1261] net MFI). Among vaccinees, EBOV- and BDBV-reactive cellular and humoral responses were positively correlated after adjustment for multiple testing. Interpretation EBOV infection and vaccination elicited BDBV-cross-reactive T-cell responses and binding antibodies. These findings support further evaluation of existing EBOV vaccines in the context of BDBV outbreaks. Funding INSERM, Vaccine Research Institute (ANR-10-LABX-77-01), and Institut de Recherche pour le Developpement (IRD).

articles.title: Determinants of Binge Drinking Among Current Alcohol Drinkers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2013 Health and Welfare Survey
articles.abstract: This cross sectional analytical study examined the prevalence and determinants of binge drinking (BD) among current alcohol drinkers (CAD) aged 20 years and older in Thailand (N = 52,847). Data from the Health and Welfare Surveys (HWS) were analyzed using chi square tests and multiple logistic regression. In 2013, nearly 69% of the 5,445 current drinkers reported BD. Multivariable analyses indicated significantly higher odds of BD among men (AOR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.90-2.66; p < 0.001), younger adults (AOR range: 1.50-1.90; p < 0.001), individuals with household housing expenses (AOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39; p < 0.05), and those with secondary/vocational or tertiary education (AOR range: 1.35-1.36; p < 0.05). Smoking was also associated with elevated odds of BD (AOR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.23-1.62; p < 0.001). In contrast, respondents in high income groups had lower odds (AOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.54-0.87; p < 0.01), as did residents of non metropolitan areas compared with Bangkok (AOR range: 0.44-0.59; p < 0.01). In conclusion, binge drinking affected over half of Thai drinkers and was strongly linked to demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. The frequent co-occurrence of alcohol use and smoking underscores the clustering of non-communicable disease risks, highlighting the need for integrated dual-cessation programs. While cross-sectional design and 2013 data limitations apply, these findings provide actionable evidence for public health agencies to implement targeted screening and intervention strategies for high-risk populations.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a single-reaction, pan-lineage Lassa virus RT-PCR at two Nigerian laboratories: a retrospective and prospective cohort study
articles.abstract: Background Lassa virus (LASV) intra- and inter-lineage nucleotide diversity has made it challenging to develop a single-reaction RT-PCR assay that can detect all viral variants with equal sensitivity. We evaluated PANDAA(R) LASV, a single-reaction pan-lineage RT-PCR assay, at two Nigerian Lassa fever laboratories against the RealStar(R) Lassa Virus RT-PCR Kit 2.0, the current diagnostic standard in Nigeria, which requires two separate reactions per patient sample to mitigate against false negative results. Methodology and Principal Findings We conducted a diagnostic accuracy study using retrospectively (n = 200) and prospectively (n = 100) plasma samples that had been collected from patients meeting the standard case definition of suspected Lassa fever for testing by real-time PCR at Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital in Bauchi and Federal Medical Centre in Owo. PANDAA LASV(R) sensitivity was 98.6% (138/140; 95% CI 94.9-99.8%), specificity 99.4% (155/156; 96.5-100%), and accuracy 99.0% (293/296; 97.1-99.8%). The positive likelihood ratio was 153.8 (21.8-1084.9) and the negative likelihood ratio 0.01 (0.00-0.06). PANDAA Ct values correlated significantly with the reference assay L gene target (Spearman's {rho} = 0.80; p < 0.0001) and GPC target ({rho} = 0.69; p < 0.0001). Three confirmed discordant results occurred at high Ct values near assay detection limits. Performance was consistent across sites with overlapping confidence intervals for sensitivity and specificity and no difference in median Ct values for any assay target between laboratories. Ct values were significantly lower in patients [≥] 45 years (p = 0.008). Conclusions and Significance PANDAA(R) LASV demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy to detect Lassa virus RNA compared to the dual-reaction reference assay. Reducing the operational burden from two PCR reactions per sample to a single PANDAA(R) LASV reaction while maintaining equivalent sensitivity and specificity could have a direct impact on labour and reagent costs, and turnaround time. Clinical validation against additional LASV lineages is an immediate priority.

articles.title: Effect of protocolized MAGNesium replacement in critically ill patients On mortaLIty and Atrial fibrillation: protocol for the MAGNOLIA randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Background: Measurement of serum magnesium levels, and administration of supplemental magnesium when levels are below target, is a common element of routine care for critically ill patients. However, targets for replacement vary, and the targets that lead to the best outcomes are unknown. Methods: Multi-center open-label parallel group randomized controlled superiority trial of adult critically ill patients receiving protocolized magnesium replacement, comparing a higher target (>0.95mmol/L) to a lower target (>0.7mmol/L). The trial will be embedded into the electronic health record (EHR) at 6 hospitals across 2 health networks in Ontario, Canada, with a shared EHR. We will include patients aged 16 years or older who have ICU admission orders, including an order for the magnesium replacement protocol. Patients with pre-eclampsia, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or neuromuscular junction disease will be excluded. Because both targets lie within the standard of care, we will use an opt-out consent approach. Screening will be integrated with the EHR, such that when a patient meets inclusion criteria, a pop-up will appear to allow the ordering clinician to confirm eligibility or indicate the relevant exclusion. After the clinician confirms eligibility, patients will be randomly assigned to a magnesium target. The primary outcome will be an ordinal composite, evaluated at 30 days, composed of death and the number of days free of atrial fibrillation or flutter in ICU. Secondary outcomes will include ventricular arrhythmia and antiarrhythmics administered; receipt of vasopressors, ventilation, and new renal replacement therapy in ICU; lengths of ICU and hospital stay; hospital mortality at 60 and 90 days, magnesium levels, and magnesium supplementation. For analyses, we will use Bayesian regression with weakly skeptical priors and an intention-to-treat approach. Outcome ascertainment will occur within the EHR. Discussion: This randomized controlled trial addresses an important uncertainty regarding routine care in the ICU with an EHR-embedded design. The innovative EHR-embedded design facilitates the large sample sizes and comprehensive, equitable recruitment needed for a trial evaluating a routine care intervention, and will lead to seamless integration with routine care upon trial completion. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07173855 . Registered 12 September 2025, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/ NCT07173855 .

articles.title: Effects of Weighted Seated Core Exercises on Immediate Postural Stability in Healthy Young Adults: An Exploratory Study
articles.abstract: Objectives: This exploratory study investigated whether low-load, seated core exercises could produce immediate improvements in standing balance among healthy young adults, aiming to provide a foundation for safe, early-stage rehabilitation protocols. Methods: Ten healthy males performed seated core exercises consisted of alternating hip flexion 5 times per side while seated and maintaining bilateral shoulder flexion at 120-degree shoulder flexion under four load conditions: upper-limb weight only, a 400-g empty box, a 1-kg ball, and a 2-kg ball. Immediately following the exercise, participants performed a 10-s single-leg stance. Transversus abdominis (TrA) thickness was measured via wireless ultrasound at baseline, post-exercise, and during the stance. Center of pressure (CoP) sway was recorded concurrently to evaluate postural stability. Results: Left-side TrA thickness during stance increased significantly under the 1-kg and 2-kg load conditions compared to baseline (p < 0.05), although substantial missing data for the left-side measurements limited the robustness of this finding. No significant load-dependent effects were observed for CoP sway parameters (p > 0.05). A moderate positive correlation (rho = 0.43, p = 0.002) was found between right-side TrA thickness and CoP sway velocity during the single-leg stance. Conclusions: Low-load, seated core exercises do not yield immediate enhancements in standing stability in healthy populations. The results suggest that increased TrA thickness during a balance task may correlate with heightened postural instability rather than improved balance control. Further research is needed to determine whether these findings translate to clinical populations with impaired physical fitness.

articles.title: Epilepsy Lateralization by Elastic Net Regularization of a Diffusion Tensor Imaging Biomarker using Machine Learning
articles.abstract: Objective: Accurate lateralization of the epileptogenic focus is essential for presurgical evaluation of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. This study examined whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) measures of white matter microstructure, combined with clinical and demographic variables, could classify epilepsy lateralization using machine learning. Methods: We present a retrospective analysis of 334 adult patients undergoing presurgical epilepsy evaluation at the University of Kansas Health System. Fractional anisotropy (FD) and mean diffusivity (MD) were extracted from 36 bilateral white matter tracts and combined with clinical and demographic variables. Several supervised machine learning approaches were evaluated, with elastic net logistic regression selected for detailed analysis. Models classified right-sided, left-sided, and bilateral or generalized epilepsy. Performance was evaluated with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity as performance metrics. Results: Elastic net models demonstrated good discrimination across classification tasks, with AUC values ranging from 0.76 to 0.88. The strongest performance distinguished left-sided epilepsy from bilateral or generalized epilepsy (AUC = 0.88; accuracy = 0.90; sensitivity = 0.90; specificity = 0.89). Discrimination between unilateral epilepsy and bilateral or generalized epilepsy was also good (AUC = 0.83). Classification of right-sided versus left-sided epilepsy demonstrated lower performance (AUC = 0.76). Significance: DTI-derived white matter features analyzed using a machine learning approach may provide complementary information for epilepsy lateralization during presurgical evaluation. Further studies incorporating other pre-surgical evaluation data into the machine learning model are needed to establish the clinical utility of this approach.

articles.title: Estimating duration in sex work from cross-sectional studies: a Bayesian global synthesis suggests shorter durations
articles.abstract: Durations selling sex are key determinants of HIV/STI transmission dynamics and service coverage. Such durations are usually estimated from cross-sectional surveys of people actively selling sex. However, cross-sectional surveys are more likely to include individuals selling sex for longer, and survey-reported durations will be right-censored. Prior works have not adequately addressed these two competing biases. In this paper, we derive the mathematical relationship between the distribution of durations reported in cross-sectional surveys and the distribution of true durations in the population overall. These distributions will be identical if true durations are exponentially distributed; otherwise, reported durations will typically underestimate the variance in true durations. We develop a parametric Bayesian model of this relationship, and apply it to re-analyze aggregate data from a global systematic review. Our model-estimated average true durations selling sex are significantly shorter than previously published for all regions - e.g. in Africa: 2.1 (95% CI: 1.8-2.5) versus 5.5 years; in Asia: 1.4 (1.2-1.5) versus 2.8-4.0 years. Shorter average durations then suggest that HIV incidence in sex work could be higher than previously thought, to match the same HIV prevalence data. Our approach can be applied beyond sex work, to characterize duration distributions for any transient risk/disease state.

articles.title: Evaluating uncertainty for detecting performance loss and guiding deferral after model transfer between hospital systems
articles.abstract: Clinical prediction models often perform worse after transfer between hospital systems, but deterioration becomes apparent only once outcomes are known. We investigated whether uncertainty measures available at prediction time warn of performance loss and can help identify individual predictions requiring review. Three neural network architectures were trained on MIMIC-IV for in-hospital mortality prediction and evaluated on eICU-CRD. Measures included predictive entropy, mutual information from Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles, and representation density. After transfer, AUROC fell from 0.86-0.87 to 0.76-0.77 and calibration worsened, while entropy and mutual information were lower. None of the measures reliably indicated the reduced performance. Deferring the 20% with the highest entropy reduced the remaining error rate from 17.5-20.1% to 6.3-8.0%; the deferred patients included 91-99% of false alarms but only 2-7% of missed deaths, which carried low uncertainty. Uncertainty therefore supported selective review but failed to reveal performance loss.

articles.title: Evolution-guided association mapping using long-read genomes from a self-identified Black or African American cohort in All of Us
articles.abstract: Background: Identifying functional variants that influence human health remains a challenge in human genetics. Conventional genotype-phenotype association studies test millions of variants, imposing a substantial multiple-testing burden as genomic and biobank datasets expand in size and variant diversity. Additionally, the contribution of structural variation, which is a substantial driver of genetic diversity, remains underexplored in these studies. Signatures of recent positive selection offer a powerful biological basis for prioritizing potentially functional variation, although demographic history can confound their detection and interpretation in these analyses. Results: We performed evolution-guided association mapping using long-read genomes from 1,027 self-identified Black or African American participants in the All of Us Research Program and short-read genomes from an additional 38,552 matched participants of African-ancestry. Using demography-calibrated inferences, we identified 228 genomic regions with local ancestry enrichment or depletion and 1,616 candidate loci showing putative recent positive selection signals. These loci were enriched for genic and regulatory sequences, as well as previously reported eQTL, sQTL, and GWAS associations. Leveraging the resolution of the long-read data, we mapped 15 structural variants to these candidate loci, including 10 located within 1,000 base pairs of putative cis-regulatory enhancers. Admixture- and selection-based phenome-wide association testing identified 13 and 446 nominal associations, respectively, 17 of which remained significant following replication and meta-analysis. Conclusions: Our results support the use of evolutionary signatures as a robust framework for uncovering clinically relevant variation, including structural variants, in underrepresented populations.

articles.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands
articles.abstract: Objective: To measure how often published electroencephalographic analyses for covert command-following call patients positive without commands, and their detection of genuine responses. Methods: This cross-sectional study applied 11 reimplemented published analyses to electroencephalograms without commands: 974 clinical electroencephalography patients and, with rules fixed, 730 new patients; 38 with prolonged disorders of consciousness; and 544 comatose patients after cardiac arrest. Outcomes: false calls (share called positive) against a 5% benchmark, and genuine-response detection. Results: Three of 10 command-following analyses called significantly more than 5% of clinical electroencephalography patients positive, replicated in new patients: Goldfine 2011, a spectral test, 23.3% (95% CI, 20.2%-26.6%), above its stated 5%; du Bois 2026, a criterion for entry to brain-computer interface training, 22.2% (95% CI, 19.2%-25.5%); and Guger 2018, a P300 accuracy threshold, 13.8% (95% CI, 11.5%-16.3%), near its approximate 12% chance rate (24.5% over 2 runs). The other 7 called 0.0% to 6.9%. After cardiac arrest: 11.5% to 27.3%. All 3 detected genuine responses. Identified contributors: a variance ignoring within-command dependence (Goldfine 2011), selection over configurations and times (du Bois 2026) and a permissive threshold (Guger 2018). Goldfine 2011's command-level correction, fixed before testing, called 0.8% of new patients and 2.4% after arrest, detecting 93.4% of stroke imagery-versus-rest sessions but few between imagery types. Interpretation: Reimplemented published analyses called up to 27% of patients positive without commands, more with repeated runs. A positive result needs its complete call rule's false-call rate and detection at that rate; imagery-versus-rest detection may reflect task engagement, not imagery. Funding: A.G. and E.K. were supported by the Clinical and Translational Science Awards (CTSA) Grant UL1TR002541 from the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, through the Harvard Catalyst - The Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center Pilot Award Program. The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Feasibility and Acceptability of a Prospective Remote Pilot Study for Assessment of Airborne Environmental Exposures and Male Fertility
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of serial biosampling and environmental exposure assessment in reproductive-aged men and compare participant experiences with in-person versus remote sample collection. Design: Prospective cohort pilot study. Subjects: Eighteen healthy men aged 21 to 44 years with no history of infertility, medical conditions or medications known to cause infertility, or prior scrotal or testicular surgery. Exposure: Indoor and personal environmental exposure monitoring using PurpleAir monitors and Fresh Air wristbands, respectively. Main Outcome Measures: Feasibility of repeated remote semen and blood collection, evaluated by participant retention and number of samples returned, and participant-reported acceptability, ease of use, discomfort, preference for at-home versus in-clinic sampling, and willingness to participate in longitudinal studies. Results: 18 participants completed the initial in-person and scheduled at-home sampling, and 16 (89%) completed subsequent remote sampling. Participants successfully collected and shipped serial capillary blood samples using homeRNA and semen samples using the Fellow Semen Analysis Kit. Participants rated both collection methods as easy to use and reported minimal discomfort with blood collection. At-home participation was preferred over in-clinic sampling, particularly for semen collection. All 16 participants completing the final survey reported willingness to participate in a similar study again. Participants were willing to provide a median of 18 semen samples (range, 2-40) and 18 blood samples (range, 5-40) over a future hypothetical study. Both home-based environmental monitoring approaches were well accepted. Conclusion: Serial remote semen and blood collection paired with environmental exposure monitoring was feasible and acceptable among reproductive-aged men. High retention, preference for at-home sampling, and willingness to provide repeated samples support this approach for larger longitudinal studies investigating environmental exposures and male reproductive health.

articles.title: From telling to receiving: the disclosure-and-services cascade after childhood sexual abuse across 15 low- and middle-income countries
articles.abstract: Most children who experience sexual abuse in low- and middle-income countries never receive formal help, but few studies have followed survivors through the steps from telling someone to receiving services. In this pooled cross-sectional analysis, we combined 15 nationally representative Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS) fielded between 2013 and 2024 in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe to describe this disclosure-and-services cascade and the factors associated with each step. The analytic sample comprised 3,608 respondents aged 18-24 years who reported sexual abuse before age 18 (2,852 female, 756 male). We estimated survey-weighted proportions for four steps: told anyone, knew where to seek formal help, sought help (among those who knew), and received help (among those who sought it). Design-based logistic regression with country fixed effects estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for individual, family, and community factors. Overall, 47.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 44.4-49.7) of survivors had told anyone and 34.8% (32.2-37.5) knew where to seek formal help. Of those who knew (n = 1,208), 24.8% (20.9-29.1) sought help, and of those who sought help (n = 339), 81.9% (75.9-86.7) received it. In total, 7.0% (5.7-8.5) of survivors received formal help; this proportion ranged from 0.9% to 26.3% across countries. Compared with male survivors, female survivors were more likely to tell anyone (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.73-3.05) and less likely to know where to seek help (aOR 0.68, 0.50-0.93); among survivors who knew where to go, female survivors were more likely to seek help (aOR 2.66, 1.39-5.09). Knowing where to seek help was more likely with older age, more schooling, and a living mother. Survivors who had ever married or cohabited were less likely to have told anyone (aOR 0.75, 0.58-0.96). No factor other than sex was associated with seeking help among those who knew where to go. Most survivors are lost before they reach a service: two in three do not know where to go, and three in four of those who know ultimately do not seek help. Once survivors seek help, most receive it. Interventions should make services known to young people, particularly those with less schooling, and address the barriers that keep survivors, especially young men, from using services they know about.

articles.title: Functional Heritability Partitioning, Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Colocalization, and Pharmacogenomic Target Deconvolution Across 127 Alzheimer's Disease Susceptibility Loci
articles.abstract: Background: The landmark genome-wide association meta-analysis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-by-proxy across N = 2,815,127 individuals (Uffelmann et al., Nature, 2026) expanded the known susceptibility landscape to 127 independent genomic risk loci (160 association signals) and established an autosomal common-variant SNP heritability of h2_SNP = 16.0% on the liability scale. Translating these 127 static statistical signals into pathway-stratified clinical trials requires resolving three quantitative gaps: how the non-APOE polygenic architecture partitions across distinct cellular programs, which effector genes operate via cortical parenchymal versus peripheral myeloid gene expression, and which targets possess nanomolar human bioactivity suitable for genetically stratified trials. Methods: Operating entirely on individual-genotype-free summary statistics structured along a previously established tridimensional diagnostic framework (Axis 1: Etiology and Genetic Architecture; Axis 2: Molecular Pathophysiology and Biomarker Programs; Axis 3: Neuroanatomical-Cognitive Topography; Menendez-Gonzalez, Alzheimers Dement, 2025), we ingested the complete NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog build GCST90695466 (8,159,496 autosomal and 160,704 X-chromosome variants). First, we performed functional heritability partitioning via stratified excess chi-square inflation and additive genetic variance (sum 2pq*beta^2) across +/-50 kb cis-regulatory windows of 50 fine-mapped effector genes organized into five mechanistic Axis 2 programs (MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE, PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY, ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR, SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM, and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE). Second, we conducted Summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) and Approximate Bayes Factor colocalization (PP.H4) across 54 human tissues in GTEx v10 (4,415 matched cis-eQTLs) alongside Open Targets v4 SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets spanning ROS/MAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), BrainSeq, primary human monocytes, and UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) plasma pQTLs. Third, we queried EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 across 2,785 human bioactivity assays (IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50) and Open Targets tractability matrices to construct an empirical pharmacogenomic target atlas. Results: Across 8,159,496 autosomal variants, the genome-wide mean test statistic was chi2_GW = 1.5099. Outside the APOE/TOMM40 super-locus (max chi2 = 3,267.15; 2pq*beta^2 = 0.0882, accounting for 74.82% of top-locus additive variance), 89,589 cis-regulatory SNPs across 48 non-APOE effector genes exhibited a 12.88-fold heritability enrichment over the autosomal background. Normalized across the 16.0% polygenic liability scale, non-APOE functional heritability concentrated in MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE (39.22% share; h2_SNP = 6.28%; 13.02x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.64) and PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY (36.34% share; h2_SNP = 5.81%; 14.98x enrichment; mean chi2 = 8.64), followed by ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR (16.71% share; h2_SNP = 2.67%; 12.69x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.47), SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM (5.40% share; h2_SNP = 0.86%; 10.05x enrichment; mean chi2 = 6.13), and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE (2.33% share; h2_SNP = 0.37%; 5.24x enrichment; mean chi2 = 3.67). Multi-tissue SMR and colocalization resolved a striking divergence between Axis 3 cortical parenchyma and myeloid compartments: QPCT (rs2300880; Z_SMR = -4.62, p_SMR = 3.93e-6, PP.H4_cis = 0.919, PP.H4_local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex; PP.H4_local = 0.979 in Brain_Frontal_Cortex_BA9) and AXL (rs12979764; p_SMR = 2.13e-4, PP.H4_cis = 0.902, PP.H4_local = 0.924 in Brain_Cortex) colocalized directly within human cerebral cortex and ROS/MAP DLPFC. Conversely, canonical myeloid and endocytic drivers (BIN1, CD33, TREM2, INPP5D, SYK) exhibited near-zero bulk cortical eQTL colocalization (PP.H4_cis <= 0.025 in Brain_Cortex) despite high SuSiE Locus-to-Gene scores (L2G = 0.875-0.968) and robust colocalization in primary monocytes and spleen (INPP5D PP.H4_local = 0.992; BIN1 PP.H4_local = 0.999).…

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction - real world outcomes
articles.abstract: Aims: To evaluate the effectiveness of GLP-1 RAs on clinical outcomes in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods and results: In this retrospective observational cohort study, all adults with diabetes mellitus and HFrEF between 2014 and 2025 were identified. Patients treated with GLP-1 RAs were matched to controls using stratified exact matching. The primary outcome was a composite of heart failure hospitalization or all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were estimated using nonparametric bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations) to derive risk ratios, NNT estimates, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Time-to-event analyses using Cox proportional hazards models were performed as a validation analysis. Among 7,878 patients with HFrEF, 793 (10.1%) patients who initiated GLP-1 RA therapy after HF diagnosis were matched to 1,825 controls. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization or death, with risk ratios of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.42-0.77) at 12 months and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.61-0.85) at 36 months. The combination of high baseline event rates and substantial relative risk reduction translated into remarkably low NNT values in the overall population, with an NNT of 17 (95% CI: 11-33) at 1 year and 13 (95% CI: 8-25) at 3 years. Post hoc subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent effects across clinical subgroups, with no significant heterogeneity observed. Conclusion: In this large real-world cohort of diabetic patients with HFrEF, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy, in addition to guideline-directed medical therapy, was associated with a lower risk of death or heart failure hospitalization.

articles.title: High vaccine coverage and non-pharmaceutical interventions decreased hospitalizations and deaths due to the Omicron variant in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
articles.abstract: The Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) had high vaccination coverage, and few infections were reported prior to the establishment of the Omicron variant. We investigated whether changes in the timing and rate of booster dose administration could have reduced severe disease outcome and reliance on non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the Omicron wave in NL. We used a vaccination-stratified epidemiological model calibrated to serology data to investigate the impact of vaccination relative to counterfactual vaccination strategies under actual, strict and no NPI scenarios. Compared with a Canadian vaccination rate scenario, the actual vaccination rollout in NL was estimated to have prevented approximately 519 hospitalizations and 122 deaths from December 15, 2021 to December 15, 2022, corresponding to reductions of 25.9\% and 30.9\%, respectively. These reductions reflected contributions from NL's higher initial primary series coverage (81.3\%), higher final booster dose coverage (57.3\%), and the implementation of various NPIs for 89 days after the Omicron BA.1 variant became established. Earlier and faster administration of booster doses reduced the duration of strict NPIs required to achieve hospitalization targets. Our findings show how the timing and rate of vaccination rollout can complement NPIs to reduce severe disease and the duration for which strict NPIs are required.

articles.title: Himalayan Tartary Buckwheat Sprout Powder, Perceived Cognitive Abilities, and Objective Processing Speed: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
articles.abstract: Subjective cognitive difficulties are common in midlife and later life, and flavonoid-rich foods may support everyday cognitive function. Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) sprouts are rich in rutin and other flavonoids, but their cognitive effects have not been tested in humans. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, US adults with self-reported cognitive difficulties received 18 g per day of Himalayan Tartary buckwheat (HTB) sprout powder or matched placebo for 12 weeks. Of 848 randomized participants, 662 were analyzed. While the rate of change in the primary outcome, PROMIS Cognitive Function, did not differ between arms (contrast = 0.03, 95% CI -0.07 to 0.13; p = .59),PROMIS Cognitive Abilities improved nominally faster with HTB (contrast = 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.24; p = .046), but not after Bonferroni adjustment. Among participants with final-week data (n = 296), more HTB than placebo participants achieved a meaningful ([≥]0.5 SD) improvement in Cognitive Abilities (68.7% vs 52.5%; RR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.59; p = .003). Fatigue, sleep-related impairment and depressive symptoms did not differ between arms. In exploratory computerized testing (n = 512), HTB participants had faster reaction times on the Flanker and Stroop tasks, without loss of accuracy. Exploratory epigenetic analyses (n = 34) identified hypothesis-generating signals in epigenetic age and immune-cell composition, none surviving multiple-testing correction. Side-effect rates were similar between arms. HTB sprout powder did not improve the primary outcome, but findings for perceived cognitive abilities and processing speed warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials. Trial registration: NCT07245784.

articles.title: Interpretable ECG manifolds link longitudinal electrical phenotypes to heart-failure risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) produces heterogeneous electrical phenotypes whose continuous organization, longitudinal evolution and clinical relevance remain poorly defined. We developed complementary variational-autoencoder representations to map HCM ECG morphology relative to physiological variation and characterize within-subject change. Using 5,194 normal-reference ECGs and 2,594 longitudinal visits from 650 individuals with HCM, we found that HCM overlapped the physiological manifold but extended towards its periphery, while an HCM-oriented manifold largely reorganized shared electrical modes. Mixed-effects models identified longitudinal drift in selected phenotypic axes. A lateral/frontal QRS-force coordinate remained time-dependent after censoring septal reduction therapy, atrial fibrillation and pacing, and lower values were associated with subsequent heart-failure risk in baseline and time-updated analyses. A time-conditioned change VAE identified four interpretable within-subject modes aligned with longer-term trajectories. Sarcomeric genotype was associated with phenotype position but not trajectory rate.

articles.title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
articles.abstract: Objective: We aimed to 1) evaluate whether AI algorithms could identify a very low-risk sub-population Lung-RADS 1/2 cases suitable for a safe switch to biennial screening, and 2) externally validate Sybil, an imaging-based deep learning lung cancer risk prediction tool. Materials and methods: We gathered all lung cancer screenings (LCSs) from a tertiary safety-net hospital (n=3120, up to September 2024), manually extracted relevant clinical data, and analyzed Sybil's performance across various subgroups, with a specific focus on Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases. We simulated LCS interval extension using Sybil and the Brock model risk scores calibrated on a subset of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). Confidence intervals were obtained through bootstrapping. Results: The median follow-up was 2.3 years (interquartile range 1.5-3.1), with a total 6-year cancer incidence rate of 2.3% (72/3120). Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases comprised 90.5% of our scans. Sybil's overall area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.819 to 0.912; while its 2-year AUC for Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases was 0.746. In the screening interval extension simulation, calibrating for a 30% shift to biennial screening translated into 33.8% of negative screens in our data being safely extended using Sybil, with no delayed cancers. The Brock model demonstrated an AUC of 0.513 on our data, with a sensitivity of 18.2% using the 1.5% threshold. Conclusion: Sybil has the potential to safely extend LCS intervals for low-risk individuals, reducing radiology workload and opening spots for life-saving new screenings.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to tick awareness and prevention among users of urban green spaces: insights from stakeholder focus groups
articles.abstract: Background: Ticks in the UK can transmit pathogens that lead to diseases in humans, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Expanding tick populations and increasing human use of urban green spaces may elevate exposure risk. Public health advice exists, but little is known about how this guidance is understood and applied by users of urban environments. Methods: Four stakeholder focus groups were conducted with professionals involved in tick fieldwork in urban green spaces. Discussions explored interactions with the public, perceived awareness, behaviours, and views on communication. Data were analysed thematically using an approach informed by the Framework Method. Results: Stakeholders reported substantial variation in public awareness of ticks, influenced by prior exposure to rural environments and local knowledge. Misinformation, particularly around tick removal, was common. Signage was rarely observed in urban green spaces, and views on its effectiveness were mixed. Participants emphasised the need to balance risk communication with reassurance and highlighted the importance of age-appropriate education. Conclusions: Insights from stakeholders underline the importance of targeted, context specific public health messaging in urban settings. Priorities include identifying groups with lower awareness, addressing misinformation, designing balanced communication materials, evaluating the effectiveness of signage, and integrating education for children and families.

articles.title: Medication history, not clinical profiles, predicts antihypertensive treatment persistence across health systems
articles.abstract: Background. Hypertension control remains poor worldwide, in large part because patients discontinue antihypertensive treatment. Machine-learning (ML) prediction models for medication persistence are typically single-country and cross-sectional, rarely compared with simple clinical information, and lack external validation across health systems. Methods. We harmonized three prospective aging cohorts -- the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), and the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) -- including adults aged >=50 years with doctor-diagnosed hypertension at baseline and known medication status at follow-up. We used baseline plus two prior waves to predict non-use of any antihypertensive medication at the next wave (treatment non-persistence), with 21 harmonized cross-sectional features, 11 longitudinal history features (including the prior non-use ratio), and a 3-feature parsimonious medication-history score (baseline non-use, prior non-use ratio, prior discontinuation). Models were L2-regularized logistic regression and random forest, evaluated by 5-fold x 5-repeat nested cross-validation and by direct transport of a CHARLS-trained model to SHARE and HRS without retraining. Three simple rule-based comparators were prespecified: baseline carry-forward (T0), prior non-use count (T1), and the 3-feature score (T2). Non-inferiority of T2 versus the full 32-feature logistic model was tested at delta=0.03 AUC. Country-level external validation across 18 SHARE countries used random-effects meta-analysis and inverse-variance meta-regression on World Bank indicators. Results. The analytic samples comprised 4,532 (CHARLS), 26,128 (SHARE) and 9,495 (HRS) participants, with non-persistence of 22.8%, 19.1% and 12.6%. Within each cohort, adding medication history raised AUC from 0.59-0.67 to 0.78-0.85 (Delta AUC 0.17-0.20; all 95% CIs >0). On direct transport, history models retained AUC 0.73-0.76 in SHARE and 0.83-0.85 in HRS, whereas cross-sectional models collapsed to near chance in SHARE (AUC 0.55-0.57). The baseline carry-forward rule alone achieved AUC 0.70-0.80; the 3-feature score achieved 0.75-0.83 and was non-inferior to the full logistic model (Delta AUC <=0.027; upper CI bounds <0.03) in all three within-cohort comparisons and both transport targets. Across 18 European countries, cross-sectional models pooled at 0.55 (I^2=30%) while history models pooled at 0.74-0.76 (I^2=82-88%); transported AUC increased with national wealth (r=0.58, P=0.011), and calibration slope declined with non-persistence burden (r=-0.69, P=0.002) and out-of-pocket expenditure share (r=-0.51, P=0.032). Conclusions. A parsimonious medication-history core transfers across health systems, whereas cross-sectional clinical profiles do not. Complex ML adds little beyond a one-question or three-variable medication-history rule. Discrimination is strongest in high-resource, low-burden systems, but probability calibration degrades where non-persistence is common, requiring local recalibration before individual-level use.

articles.title: Modulating Amygdala Responses in Major Depressive Disorder using Naturalistic Neurofeedback with Emotional Faces
articles.abstract: Emotion regulation is critical to mental health, and its disruption can lead to psychiatric conditions such as major depressive disorder (MDD). MDD encompasses diverse symptoms, including anhedonia and anxiety, which may be associated with distinct patterns of altered neural activity. Interventions that address the neural mechanisms underlying these symptom dimensions may improve treatment efficacy. We investigated an adaptive, naturalistic real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging neurofeedback paradigm designed to differentially target anhedonia and anxiety through bidirectional amygdala regulation. Unlike conventional abstract feedback, our approach used emotional faces whose expressions changed dynamically according to ongoing amygdala activity, embedding neural self-regulation within a socially relevant emotional context. In this parallel-group study, 21 patients with MDD received one of two neurofeedback conditions. In the Happy-up group, patients attempted to increase amygdala activity by making a neutral face happier to enhance positive emotional responding. In the Fear-down group, patients attempted to decrease amygdala activity by making a fearful face less fearful to reduce negative emotional reactivity. Both groups showed the expected pattern of neural regulation during neurofeedback, with greater amygdala activity during Happy upregulation and decreasing amygdala activity during Fear downregulation. Following the intervention, patients showed reductions in depression severity, anxiety, and anhedonia, and more positive evaluations of neutral and happy faces. However, improvements in anhedonia and anxiety did not differ significantly between groups. These findings show bidirectional amygdala regulation through naturalistic neurofeedback in MDD. Although symptom-specific clinical effects were not established, the observed clinical improvements underscore the therapeutic potential of this approach.

articles.title: Nicotine and Cannabis Co-Use are Associated with Higher Symptom Burden than Use of Either Drug Alone in Early Psychosis: Results from a Multisite Study
articles.abstract: Background: Despite their high usage rates and associations with risk for psychosis and earlier age of symptom onset, few studies have examined relationships between nicotine and cannabis co-use and symptoms. Here we examined associations between symptom burden and cannabis/nicotine use/co-use in individuals with early psychosis (EP). Methods: This cross-sectional, multisite cohort study used data from 738 individuals (mean age 22 years, 62% male) from the Early Psychosis Intervention Network (EPI-NET). Relationships between cannabis and/or nicotine use and frequency (over the prior 30 day period) and Modified Colorado Symptom Index (MCSI) scores were examined using mixed effects models, with site as a random factor and age, sex, and cannabis/nicotine use (none, nicotine only, cannabis only, or both) as fixed factors. Exploratory analyses also examined effects of frequency of use (daily vs. less than daily). Results: 59% of the sample used neither nicotine nor cannabis, 17% only nicotine, 9% only cannabis, and 16% both. Significant effects of use were observed on total MCSI score (F = 6.69, p < .001) driven by greater symptoms in individuals who used both cannabis and nicotine relative to neither, only nicotine, or only cannabis. More frequent use, furthermore, was associated with higher total score. Conclusions: These results suggest that co-use of cannabis and nicotine is associated with greater symptom burden in EP, which may have implications for treatment strategies. Neuropharmacological mechanisms that may underlie this association are discussed.

articles.title: Olfactory Function in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: A Multi-Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Introduction: Olfactory impairment is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, it is unclear if olfactory performance reflects early pathological changes during preclinical AD and/or predicts subsequent clinical progression among characterized cognitively normal (CN) individuals. We aimed to determine whether odor identification differs by amyloid status, relates to medial temporal lobe (MTL) tau burden and morphometry, and predicts longitudinal conversion to mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Methods: We analyzed data from 257 cognitively normal (CN) older adults enrolled in PREVENT-AD (n = 217) and UCLouvain (n = 40), including 76 amyloid-positive (CN A+) and 181 amyloid-negative participants (CN A-). Participants completed olfactory testing, underwent tau-PET imaging, and structural MRI. Results: CN A+ participants had significantly lower odor identification performance than CN A- participants, with no evidence of cohort heterogeneity. Tau-PET associations with odor identification differed by cohort. After whole-brain FDR correction and exclusion of extreme values, parahippocampal tau burden was negatively associated with odor identification score in UCLouvain ([18F]MK-6240), an association that was not found in PREVENT-AD ([18F]flortaucipir). No morphometric association survived multiple comparison correction. In 250 participants with longitudinal follow-up, each 10-percentage-point higher odor identification score was associated with a 16% lower hazard of incident MCI, independent of baseline global cognition and APOE {epsilon}4-carrier status. Discussion: Odor identification was lower in preclinical AD and associated with incident MCI independently of baseline global cognition and APOE {epsilon}4-carrier status. Its association with parahippocampal tau burden differed between cohorts, supporting further investigation using harmonized imaging methods.

articles.title: PRISM-AD quantifies clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive risk prediction
articles.abstract: Background: Older adults with high inherited Alzheimer's disease (AD) susceptibility can still be cognitively normal (CN). An overall risk estimate alone does not show the cognitive and genetic contributions within a forecast. Objective: To quantify clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive prognosis. Methods: PRISM-AD combined nonlinear clinical functions and a polygenic risk score (PRS) term in 4,435 European-ancestry participants. Participant-level internal validation evaluated first recorded mild cognitive impairment (MCI) after CN in 908 participants and AD dementia after MCI in 714, within three or five years. Separately fitted comparators used identical inputs. Post hoc clinical-course comparisons used regression with robust standard errors and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction. Results: PRISM-AD using current assessments achieved average precision of 0.2996 and 0.4094 for three- and five-year CN-to-MCI, with estimates close to logistic regression. No PRISM-AD PRS increment met BH q < 0.05. Three-year first-MCI forecasts characterized risk contributions in 893 initially CN participants. A retrospective comparison over available follow-up included 95 participants with later AD and 701 with CN at their last diagnostic assessment. Modeled genetic factors were higher in later AD in nine of ten shared cognitive-risk deciles. After adjustment for modeled cognitive risk and fold, the genetic-factor ratio was 1.135 (nominal 95% CI, 1.073 to 1.201, BH q < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher genetic contributions were associated with later AD at comparable modeled cognitive risk. These exploratory profiles require independent validation before use in cognitive follow-up or prevention research.

articles.title: Pandemic-Driven Shifts in RSV Diversity, Evolution, and Global Spread
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically disrupted the seasonal circulation of RSV, with subsequent heterogeneous global resurgence. We aimed to characterize how pandemic-era disruptions restructured global RSV transmission dynamics, evolutionary patterns, and drivers of reemergence. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes.

articles.title: Pediatric Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against Emergency Visits and Hospitalization in Canada: 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons
articles.abstract: Importance: Influenza causes substantial morbidity in children, yet Canadian data on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in preventing emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations are limited. Objective: To estimate VE against influenza-associated ED visits and hospitalizations among children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Design: Test negative case control design. Setting: Fourteen Canadian pediatric tertiary-care hospitals participating in the Surveillance Program for the Rapid IdeNtification and TracKing of Infectious Diseases in kidS (SPRINT KIDS) network. Participants: Symptomatic children aged 6 months to <18 years tested for influenza from October 27, 2024, to June 7, 2025, and from November 2, 2025, to June 13, 2026.
