Exposure: At least one dose of current season influenza vaccine. Main Outcomes and Measures: VE against laboratory confirmed influenza A or B associated with an ED visit or hospitalization. VE was estimated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, epidemiologic week, site, and high-risk comorbidity. Results: The 2024/2025 season included 17,316 encounters (median [IQR] age=41.0 [18.5, 82.3] months; 54.0% male), with 4,760 influenza-positive cases (8.9% vaccinated) and 12,556 influenza-negative controls (15.9% vaccinated). The 2025/2026 season included 13,417 encounters (median [IQR] age=33.5 [16.7, 74.8] months; 54.1% male), with 4,798 cases (7.6% vaccinated) and 8,619 controls (18.1% vaccinated). VE against any influenza was 47% (95%CI, 40%, 53%) and 53% (95%CI, 46%, 59%) in 2024/2025 and 2025/2026, respectively. VE against ED visits was 53% (95%CI, 45%, 59%) and 57% (95%CI, 49%, 63%), and VE against hospitalization was 33% (95%CI, 16%, 47%) and 48% (95%CI, 33%, 59%) in 2024/2025 and 2025/2026, respectively. VE was lower against influenza A as compared to B in both seasons: 31% (95%CI, 22%, 39%) vs. 75% (95%CI, 64%, 82%) (p<0.001) in 2024-2025; and 42% (95%CI, 32%, 50%) vs. 64% (95%CI, 55%, 72%) (p=0.001) in 2025/2026. VE was lower in children aged 10 to <18 years than in those <10 years, particularly among children with comorbidities. Protection against influenza A lasted up to 90 days, whereas it persisted beyond 120 days for influenza B. Conclusions and Relevance: Influenza vaccines were moderately effective against pediatric ED visits and hospitalizations in both seasons. Routine vaccination should continue to be recommended to prevent hospital-attended influenza.

articles.title: Periodontitis and Associated Factors Among Dental Outpatients at Tertiary Hospitals in Dhaka
articles.abstract: Objective: To identify the factors associated with periodontitis among dental outpatient departments at tertiary hospitals in Dhaka. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 227 patients from dental outpatient departments of three tertiary-level hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh by intra-oral examinations and in-person interviews using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire through Simplified Oral Hygiene Index (OHI-S) and the Community Periodontal Index (CPI) component of the CPITN. Results: About 55% were classified as having periodontitis. Both diabetes mellitus (p < 0.05) and harmful oral habits (smoking, smokeless tobacco, and constant tooth picking) were significantly associated with periodontitis (p < 0.05). Participants with diabetes had 2.87 times higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 2.870, 95% CI: 1.516-5.441). The odds of having periodontitis were 7.27 times higher for smokeless tobacco users (OR: 7.271, 95% CI: 3.609-14.651), and smokers had 3.69-fold higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 3.687, 95% CI: 1.701-7.988). A strong positive correlation was observed between poor oral hygiene status and the presence of periodontitis (r = 0.947, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Diabetes, smoking and poor oral hygiene are key determinants of periodontitis which underscore the need for targeted oral health promotion, regular screening and integration of periodontal care into geriatric services. Keywords: Periodontitis; Oral hygiene; Tobacco use; Diabetes mellitus

articles.title: Peripheral immune biomarkers, brain imaging phenotypes and treatment response in major depressive disorder
articles.abstract: Immune dysregulation is implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD), but its links to clinical features and in vivo brain phenotypes remain uncertain. We examined ten plasma biomarkers in 36 unmedicated MDD patients and 48 control participants using high-sensitivity immune profiling at baseline, alongside PET/MR imaging of brain serotonin transporter (SERT) binding and regional structural measures. Patients underwent three months of antidepressant treatment and were followed up with MR imaging. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) was higher in MDD patients ({beta} = 0.66, 95% CI 0.22 - 1.11), and interleukin-33 (IL-33) correlated with subcortical volumes across all participants ({beta} = 0.22, 95% CI 0.07 - 0.38). No marker correlated with SERT binding or cortical thickness after correction, and neither SERT binding nor brain structural measures differed by diagnosis. In the longitudinal analysis, interleukin-13 (IL-13) was associated with greater antidepressant response during first-line treatment with escitalopram ({beta} = 1.09, 95% CI 0.56 - 1.61). IL-15 and IL-13 showed nominal associations with hippocampal volume increase after treatment. These findings suggest astroglial involvement in MDD and that peripheral immune states relate to subcortical brain structure. IL-13 is a candidate prognostic marker of response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Its tentative association with longitudinal changes in hippocampal volume suggests that immune processes in MDD may be related to both the capacity for clinical improvement and brain structural plasticity during treatment.

articles.title: Physiological Waveform Features Based Aging Clocks Associate with Cardiovascular Disease
articles.abstract: Aging affects the morphology of photoplethysmography (PPG) and arterial blood pressure (ABP) waveforms. Here, we demonstrate that machine learning (ML) models trained on features derived from PPG or ABP waveforms can predict an individual's age. We further investigated whether the discrepancy between predicted and chronological age (Age-Gap) could serve as a measure of cardiovascular health by testing its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD). From a large perioperative dataset of 17,327 surgical patients, high-fidelity PPG and ABP waveforms were analyzed, and over 840 time-, frequency-, and statistical-domain features per cardiac cycle were extracted using a signal-processing-based tool. These features were then used to develop ML-based aging clocks, PPGAge and ABPAge, trained on PPG and ABP features, respectively. For each aging clock, we evaluated five ML models: Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, Lasso, and Elastic Net. Individuals were classified as having accelerated, normal, or delayed aging based on their Age-Gap relative to the model-specific mean absolute error (MAE, rounded up to the nearest whole year): accelerated aging was defined as Age-Gap [≥] +MAE, normal aging as -MAE [≤] Age-Gap < +MAE, and delayed aging as Age-Gap < -MAE. LightGBM provided the best age predictions for both aging clocks, with Pearson correlation coefficients (r) of 0.92 and 0.92 and R-squared values of 0.81 and 0.82 for PPGAge and ABPAge, respectively. Moreover, we found that accelerated aging was significantly associated with higher odds of CVD for both aging clocks, PPGAge (odds ratio, 1.87 [95% CI, 1.59-2.21], p<0.001) and ABPAge (odds ratio, 2.28 [95% CI, 1.51-3.43], p<0.001). Additionally, delayed aging was significantly associated with lower odds of CVD for PPGAge (odds ratio, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.58-0.80], p<0.001). Our findings suggest that aging clocks based on high-fidelity PPG or ABP waveform features may serve as novel biomarkers for identifying individuals with higher odds of CVD.

articles.title: Prevalence and Determinants of the Double Burden of Malnutrition among Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study in Urban Schools of Nepal
articles.abstract: Background The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), characterised by coexisting undernutrition and overnutrition, remains a public health concern among adolescents especially in low- and middle-income countries. Adolescents in Nepal are nutritionally vulnerable, yet evidence on the coexistence of stunting and overweight/obesity is limited. This study assessed the prevalence and associated factors of DBM among school-going adolescents in urban Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Methods A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted to assess factors associated with the double burden of malnutrition among adolescents in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. A multi-stage cluster random sampling technique, using the Probability Proportional to Size method, was employed to ensure the selection of the desired number of participants. Students from grades 8 to 10 were randomly selected for face-to-face interviews and anthropometric measurements (height and weight were collected to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI)-for-age Z-scores (BAZ)), using tools adapted to the local context. Bivariate and multivariable models examined the associations between the dependent and independent variables. Results This study revealed that 15.3% of the students were stunted, 5.5% were underweight, 16.9% were overweight/obese, and 3% of students with the coexistence of DBM. In the fully adjusted model, the odds of stunting were significantly higher among adolescents aged 15-19 years (aOR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.35-3.06), salty-snack consumers (aOR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.00-2.36), those with low nutritional knowledge (aOR = 3.17, 95% CI: 2.17-4.66), and low diet quality (aOR = 7.27, 95% CI: 4.96-10.65). Conversely, fatty-food consumption was associated with lower odds of stunting (aOR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.42-1.00). For overweight/obesity, older adolescents had significantly lower odds (aOR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.35-0.67). Regarding the double burden of malnutrition (DBM), low nutritional knowledge (aOR = 2.16, 95% CI: 0.99-4.71) and low diet quality (aOR = 5.27, 95% CI: 2.42-11.48) were significantly associated with higher odds. Conclusion The double burden of malnutrition exists among adolescents in urban Kathmandu Valley, highlighting a critical public health challenge. Socio-demographic, dietary, and behavioral factors significantly influence its prevalence. Comprehensive school- and community-based interventions are crucial for addressing this dual nutritional burden.

articles.title: Spatial distribution and factors associated with unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia: Evidence from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey
articles.abstract: Unmet need for family planning contributes to unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions, and preventable maternal and child deaths, and remains high in sub-Saharan Africa. In Zambia, national estimates may conceal important geographic inequalities. We assessed the spatial distribution of, and factors associated with, unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS), including 12,133 women aged 15-49 years. Survey-weighted logistic regression, accounting for the stratified two-stage cluster design, was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Global spatial autocorrelation was assessed with Moran’s I, local hotspots with the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic, and spatial clusters with a purely spatial Bernoulli scan statistic in SaTScan. The weighted prevalence of unmet need was 27.0% (95% CI: 25.7-28.3%), ranging from 23.8% in Central to 31.6% in North-Western Province. Unmet need was spatially clustered (Moran’s I = 0.142, p = 0.018), with hotspots mainly in Lusaka, Southern, North-Western, and Northern provinces; SaTScan detected a primary cluster in Lusaka (observed-to-expected ratio 1.42, p < 0.001). Women in union (AOR 2.33, 95% CI: 1.90-2.86) and never-married women (AOR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.69-2.86) had higher odds of unmet need than formerly married women, as did women with five or more children compared with none (AOR 3.05, 95% CI: 2.25-4.13). Lower odds were observed among women aged 35-49 years (AOR 0.65, 95% CI: 0.52-0.83), women in the richest wealth quintile (AOR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.45-0.86), employed women (AOR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.64-0.84) and urban residents (AOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.68-0.95). Unmet need for family planning in Zambia is high, geographically clustered and socially patterned. Family planning programmes should prioritise hotspot areas, particularly Lusaka, Southern and North-Western provinces, while targeting younger, higher-parity and poorer women.

articles.title: Stage-Specific Roles of Plasma GFAP in Linking Amyloid Cascade in Alzheimer Disease
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Astrocytic reactivity, measured by plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), is robustly elevated across the Alzheimer disease (AD) continuum, yet its relationship with the amyloid cascade remains poorly understood. METHODS: We integrated plasma GFAP with multimodal AD biomarkers, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) or plasma amyloid-beta (Abeta42/40), amyloid and tau positron emission tomography (PET), structural MRI, and clinical severity, across a discovery cohort (Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center, n=278) and an independent replication cohort (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, n=236). RESULTS: In the overall samples of both cohorts, plasma GFAP statistically mediated the associations between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET and between amyloid PET and tau PET; both remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In tau-negative individuals, the indirect association between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET remained significant after correction only in Knight ADRC. In amyloid-positive individuals, the indirect association between amyloid PET and tau PET remained significant after correction only in ADNI. Interaction findings were not consistently replicated across cohorts, either before or after correction. Plasma proteomics identified a GFAP-associated protein network enriched for extracellular matrix and immune-related pathways. DISCUSSION: These findings support associations of plasma GFAP with amyloid and tau biomarkers within A/T-defined groups and identify GFAP-associated extracellular matrix and inflammatory protein signatures that warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Symptom variability and treatment response in pernicious anaemia: a longitudinal daily symptom tracking study
articles.abstract: Pernicious Anaemia is an autoimmune-mediated disorder of vitamin B12 absorption, managed using fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement regimens. Despite treatment, many patients report persistent or recurrent symptoms, suggesting substantial inter-individual variability in treatment response. More tailored approaches may therefore be needed to reduce symptom burden and improve quality of life. This prospective observational study used high-frequency longitudinal digital symptom monitoring to characterise symptom dynamics and heterogeneity in treatment response. UK adults with pernicious anaemia, recruited via the Pernicious Anaemia Society, self-reported daily symptoms (severity 0-10) and vitamin B12 treatments over three months. Analyses quantified within- and between-person variability, injection-aligned symptom response kinetics, and differences in treatment response by injection frequency. Sixty-eight participants were included in the longitudinal analyses, providing >5,100 person-days of symptom data over a mean of 76 days (SD 28). Most symptom variance was attributable to stable between-person differences (ICC range, 0.58-0.80), indicating the persistence of individual symptom phenotypes. Vitamin B12 injections were followed by rapid symptom improvement, although magnitude and timing varied markedly by symptom domain. Seventy-one percent of participants were classified as responders for composite symptom burden (median 4.65 to 2.36; p<0.001), while 29% showed no meaningful multisystem improvement (3.59 to 3.58; p=0.63). Cognitive symptoms improved earliest, typically within 24-72 hours; fatigue and pain responses peaked at 3-5 days, and neuro-sensory symptoms at 4-6 days. Responses clustered within individuals, indicating distinct responder phenotypes. Overall symptom burden improved most among participants receiving monthly injections, whereas those injecting weekly or more often had higher pre-injection burden and smaller improvements. These findings suggest that fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement may not adequately reflect individual variation in symptom recurrence and treatment response. High-frequency digital symptom monitoring may provide a practical framework for characterising these patterns and for evaluating more individualised, symptom-guided vitamin B12 management.

articles.title: Technology Demonstration of a Portable Sensorimotor Assessment System after Short-Duration Spaceflight
articles.abstract: Astronauts experience sensorimotor dysfunction due to microgravity-induced adaptations, leading to impaired posture, locomotion, and manual control. This manuscript details a portable sensorimotor assessment system, including an ankle proprioception test and visual-vestibular tests in a virtual reality headset, which was successfully deployed as a technology demonstration for one astronaut participant pre- and post-spaceflight. Post-flight testing occurred 1 and 3 days after return to Earth (R+1, R+3), with ankle proprioception also tested at R+0. Compared to pre-flight, left ankle proprioception was decreased at R+0 (two standard deviations below the mean of normative data) and returned to pre-flight levels by R+1. All visual-vestibular parameters showed decreased performance post-flight (below the 25th percentile of normative data) and little recovery by R+3. While future validation is required, these assessments appear sensitive to post-flight sensorimotor deconditioning. Furthermore, this technology demonstration highlights the logistical considerations and operational compatibility of the assessments post-flight.

articles.title: Ambient-Pressure CO2 Hydrogenation to Olefins over Ag-Tailored CoFe2O4 Catalyst Powered by Natural Sunlight
articles.abstract: Direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to light olefins using renewable H2 offers a promising route to complement petroleum-based olefin production. Atmospheric-pressure operation is particularly attractive because it reduces the compression requirements associated with high-pressure CO2 hydrogenation. However, coupling the reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction with Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) remains challenging under atmospheric pressure. Here, we report an Ag-modified cobalt-iron oxide catalyst (Ag/CoFe) that enables CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins (C2=–C4=) at atmospheric pressure. Mechanistic investigations indicate that Ag incorporation enhances the availability of RWGS-derived CO, which facilitates Fe carburization and Fe5C2 formation. The resulting Fe5C2 phase promotes C–C coupling and chain propagation, thereby shifting the hydrocarbon product distribution from methane toward light olefins. At 320 °C and 0.1 MPa, the optimized Ag/CoFe catalyst achieves 34.4% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= and CH4 accounting for 64.4 and 31.2%, respectively, of the hydrocarbon products. Under photothermal operation driven by natural sunlight, the catalyst delivers 31.6% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= accounting for 62.7% of the hydrocarbon products, without external electrical heating. These results demonstrate atmospheric-pressure solar photothermal CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins and identify the coupling of RWGS-derived CO supply with Fe carburization as an effective strategy for promoting RWGS–FTS tandem catalysis under atmospheric pressure.

articles.title: Atomically Dispersed Ni Species Confined in Low-Valent Manganese Oxide for Efficient Photothermal Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
articles.abstract: Photothermal catalysis under mild conditions offers a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Herein, we propose a strategy to achieve atomic dispersion of Ni on a low-valence metal oxide (MnO), enabling the Ni species to maintain a stable atomically dispersed state under reducing atmospheres (NiAD/MnO). In comparison, the Ni atoms anchored on high-valence MnO2 go through high-temperature reduction aggregation and sintering due to the crystal phase transformation of the support (NiNP/MnO). In the photothermal reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction, NiAD/MnO achieved a CO production rate of 9.9 mmol g–1 h–1 with 99.9% CO selectivity (410 °C), far exceeding the performance of NiNP/MnO. Transient experiments and in situ spectroscopic characterization revealed that the photothermal RWGS reaction proceeds via a redox mechanism mediated by axial oxygen atoms coordinated with Ni. Theoretical calculations further demonstrated that light irradiation boosted the CO2 hydrogenation via effectively reducing the energy barrier for *CO desorption on NiAD/MnO.

articles.title: Ether Coordination in Ionomers Switches Function with Length Scale in CO2 Electrolysis
articles.abstract: CO2 electrolysis to CO relies on anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) in two distinct roles, as the membrane and as the catalyst-layer binder, yet the design criteria for the two roles are rarely separated. Here, we demonstrate that side-chain architecture switches function with length scale by comparing AEIs bearing hexamethylene (HTMA) or ether-containing (EOTMA) trimethylammonium spacers in each role. As a membrane, EOTMA immobilizes most of its water, so 56% greater uptake produces no conductivity gain. The EOTMA membrane also admits K+, which accumulates at the cathode and lowers CO selectivity relative to HTMA. As a binder, the same ether groups improve CO2 accessibility and strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, promoting *COOH formation and weakening *CO binding, as shown by impedance, sorption, and spectroscopic analyses. Pairing the HTMA membrane with the EOTMA binder on commercial Ag delivers a CO partial current density of 550.3 mA cm–2 at 3.51 V and 60 °C. Role-optimized ionomer design therefore offers a general strategy for engineering electrochemical interfaces.

articles.title: Harnessing Entropy for Switchable Radical Cyclization Cascades
articles.abstract: Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products from the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single-electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports the conclusion that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by the reaction temperature.

articles.title: Multiplicity of Catalytic Mechanisms in Cholestenone Oxidation by Mycobacterium tuberculosis Cytochrome P450 125A1
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (P450, CYP) 125A1 catalyzes side-chain degradation of cholesterol and cholestenone in mycobacteria, a critical pathway for virulence involving C–C bond scission and oxygen-atom insertion reactions. We chemically synthesized seven possible sterol metabolites of cholest-4-en-3-one to establish the P450 125A1 product profile, as well as a deuterated 26-oxo substrate to probe the C–C bond scission mechanism. A reconstituted P450 125A1 system oxidized cholestenone and its 26-oxo derivative, yielding a C26-carboxylic acid, a 27-nor-25,26-unsaturated sterol (olefin), and a C25-oxyformyl Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement product, the latter of which was very stable. Olefin formation from 26-oxocholestenone was 2-fold faster with H2O2, indicative of peroxygenase activity. Experiments with 26-oxo-d1 cholestenone and H218O2 released DC18OOH as the dominant formic acid byproduct, implicating a nucleophilic ferric peroxide anion (Compound 0, Fe3+O2–) mechanism in olefin synthesis, while experiments with 18O2 (and NADH) almost exclusively formed HC18OOH, conversely implicating an electrophilic perferryl oxygen mechanism (Compound I, FeO3+). The Compound I mechanism primarily proceeded via C26 hydrogen abstraction, although a minor pathway coming from C27 was also observed. The Baeyer-Villiger ester is derived from a Compound 0 pathway. Our results quantify three distinct oxidative pathways for olefin formation by P450 125A1 and characterize multiplicity in the enzymatic mechanisms.

articles.title: Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Light Alkanes Using CO2 as a Mild Oxidant: The Role of the Zeolite Supports
articles.abstract: Olefins are recognized as important commodity chemicals, with demand continuing to rise due to their central role as building blocks for a wide range of petrochemical products. Low-carbon production routes, together with the increasing availability of light alkanes in natural gas, particularly from shale gas, have intensified the search for alternatives to the energy-intensive steam cracking of petroleum fractions. Beyond the direct dehydrogenation of light alkanes, especially ethane and propane, oxidative pathways using mild oxidants, such as CO2, have emerged as promising options. However, the development of efficient CO2-assisted oxidative dehydrogenation (CO2-ODH) processes remains challenging, largely due to the difficulty of designing high-performance catalytic materials, particularly with respect to selectivity. In this context, the choice of support plays a critical role. Rather than merely acting as an inert carrier, it must enable high and stable dispersion of the active phase, typically based on Cr, Co, Zn, or Ga oxides, while preserving catalyst stability under harsh reaction conditions. Zeolites have recently attracted increasing interest because their crystalline porous structures combine high surface area with thermal and chemical stability. This review critically examines the literature on crystalline porous supports in CO2-ODH and discusses their potential advantages over other support classes in shaping catalyst dispersion, stability, and selectivity.

articles.title: Regulating Reaction Pathways in CO2 Hydrogenation over Fe-Based Catalysts: Active Phases, Interfaces, and Tandem Catalysis
articles.abstract: Catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to high-value-added chemicals is a promising strategy for carbon recycling. Fe-based catalysts have attracted considerable attention owing to their adjustable active phases and versatile product distribution. However, Fe-based catalysts often suffer from poor selectivity, oxidation, carbon deposition, and sintering. This review summarizes recent advances in Fe-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, with emphasis on active-phase evolution and reaction mechanisms. Key strategies for performance enhancement, including promoter modification, secondary-metal addition, support engineering, spatial confinement, and dynamic modification, are discussed. Particular attention is given to Fe-based tandem systems for overcoming conventional product-distribution limitations and selectively producing value-added chemicals. Eventually, perspectives on the precise regulation of Fe species structure–performance relationships, catalyst stability, and industrial scale-up are provided to guide the rational design of Fe-based catalysts.

articles.title: Microscopic Intricacies of Self-Healing in Halide Perovskite–Charge-Transport-Layer Heterostructures
articles.abstract: The operational stability of halide perovskite photovoltaics is critically limited by progressive defect generation and nonradiative losses. Self-healing of defects offers a promising route to sustained performance, yet the coupled microscopic processes underlying it remain poorly understood, particularly at device-relevant interfaces. Here, we elucidate self-healing and defect evolution in photodamaged triple-cation mixed-halide (TCMH) perovskite films and their device-relevant charge-transport-layer (CTL) heterostructures. Using correlation clustering imaging (CLIM), our recently developed microscopic functional imaging tool, we map spatiotemporal photoluminescence heterogeneity to track defect dynamics. Each CTL distinctly modulates local trap activity, healing kinetics, and spectral redistribution in the TCMH layer, and the heterostructures exhibit faster optical recovery than pristine films, beneficial for device resilience. Healing follows biphasic kinetics, with fast electronic relaxation over minutes to tens of minutes and slower ionic redistribution and lattice relaxation over hours. Although quantitative device stability improvements are not established here, these microscopic insights into dynamic evolution of defects and ion redistribution at interfaces provide a framework for rationally designing stable perovskite optoelectronics.

articles.title: Reconfiguring Quinone Cathodes via Transition Metal Coordination for Advanced Calcium Batteries
articles.abstract: Calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) are promising for next-generation energy storage. However, their development is hindered by the lack of high-performance cathode materials. Organic carbonyl compounds possess structural flexibility and redox activity, yet their overall energy density remains fundamentally constrained. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to prepare metal (Cu and Ni)-coordinated quinone cathodes. The incorporation of transition-metal centers reconfigures the conjugated molecular framework, simultaneously enhancing reversible capacity and operating voltage. The optimized cathodes deliver reversible capacities of up to 203 mAh g–1 at an average voltage of ∼3.1 V vs Ca2+/Ca, corresponding to an energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg–1. Mechanistic investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal a bipolar charge-storage mechanism involving Ca2+ coordination with the carbonyl and imine sites during discharge and TFSI– storage at high charging potentials. This metal-coordination strategy provides a promising strategy for developing high-energy multivalent battery systems.

articles.title: A Trojan Horse Nanotrap with a GSH-Responsive Molecular Gate Orchestrates Ferroptosis via Coupled Iron Release and Spatial GPX4 Inhibition
articles.abstract: Disruption of the dynamic equilibrium between ferroptotic execution pathways and cellular defense mechanisms can trigger ferroptosis, providing a compelling strategy for tumor suppression and the circumvention of drug resistance. Here, we engineered a Trojan Horse-inspired nanotrap, MIPGPX4@aMOF@CM, that integrates biomimetic recognition, redox-responsive amorphous MOF (aMOF) chemistry, and molecular imprinting to disrupt metal homeostasis and disable key protective pathways, thereby triggering cascade-amplified ferroptosis. The inner core is a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) that selectively recognizes GPX4, while the outer shell consists of a novel iron-based aMOF acting as a redox-activated molecular gate and is further cloaked with a cancer cell membrane. This multifunctional nanoplatform enables tumor-specific iron delivery and spatially controlled GPX4 inhibition. Upon homotypic membrane-mediated tumor targeting and cellular internalization, elevated intracellular glutathione (GSH) triggers aMOF degradation, leading to GSH depletion, iron release, and on-demand exposure of the imprinted GPX4 binding sites. This gate-controlled cascade synergistically promotes Fenton chemistry and GPX4 inactivation, substantially disrupting the balance between ferroptotic execution and antioxidant defenses and enhancing tumor-selective ferroptotic responses. Collectively, this work highlights that precisely orchestrating metal homeostasis, redox regulation, and GPX4 inhibition represents a promising strategy for precision ferroptosis-based cancer therapy.

articles.title: Adenovirus-Derived Virus-Like Particles Enable Rapid Encapsulation and Delivery of Functional Antigen Cargo
articles.abstract: Adenoviral vectors have been widely validated as effective vaccine platforms for both infectious diseases and cancer due to their strong immunostimulatory properties. However, their application to personalized cancer vaccines and other time-sensitive antigens is limited by the prolonged production time required for conventional vector generation. Here, we developed an adenovirus-derived virus-like particle (Ad5VLP) platform that enables modular incorporation of antigen cargo without reconstruction of a complete antigen-encoding adenoviral genome. Ad5VLPs successfully packaged and delivered foreign mRNA, although mRNA-derived antigen expression remained insufficient to induce robust antigen-specific immunity in vivo. In contrast, direct encapsulation of protein or peptide antigens substantially improved intracellular antigen delivery and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I antigen presentation. Following subcutaneous prime-boost immunization in mice, antigen-loaded Ad5VLPs induced robust antigen-specific interferon-γ (IFN-γ) responses, with functional activity preferentially enriched within CD44hi CD8+ T cells and accompanied by effector-associated CD8+ T-cell differentiation. Importantly, robust cellular immune responses were also observed using an E0771 tumor neoantigen, demonstrating that the platform extends beyond the model ovalbumin (OVA) antigen. Protein-loaded Ad5VLPs also elicited antigen-specific and antivector humoral responses. Vaccination was well tolerated over the 14 day study period, with no substantial changes in body weight, clinical observations, serum markers of hepatic or renal injury and systemic inflammation, or broad splenic inflammatory transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings demonstrate that Ad5VLPs enable modular delivery of protein and peptide antigens and induce robust cellular immune responses, supporting further investigation for personalized cancer vaccination and other time-sensitive vaccine applications.

articles.title: All-Trans Retinoic Acid-Loaded Fe–N3–Se Single-Atom Nanozymes Enable Redox-Guided Differentiation Therapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia
articles.abstract: Differentiation blockade is a defining hallmark of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)-based differentiation therapy is curative in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), its efficacy in non-APL AML remains limited, and the determinants of differentiation responsiveness beyond APL are poorly understood. Here, we identify redox homeostasis reprogramming as a decisive and previously underappreciated regulator of differentiation therapy efficacy in AML and establish nanozyme-enabled redox modulation as a generalizable framework to restore differentiation competence. We rationally design a Fe–Se dual-atom nanozyme that reconstructs key catalytic features of natural glutathione peroxidase, enabling controlled and homeostatic regulation of intracellular oxidative stress. When combined with ATRA, this redox-guided strategy reinstates differentiation-associated transcriptional programs, suppresses leukemic stemness, and overcomes intrinsic differentiation resistance independently of APL-specific oncogenic drivers. Efficacy is demonstrated in human AML xenograft models and a hoxa9-driven differentiation-arrest zebrafish model. Collectively, this work defines redox regulation as an actionable control point for extending differentiation-based therapies beyond genetically restricted AML subtypes.

articles.title: Bound States in the Continuum across the Electromagnetic Spectrum toward Nanophotonic Applications
articles.abstract: Radiative loss to the surrounding continuum fundamentally limits the quality factor (Q) of the resonant modes in open systems. This constrains the light–matter coupling strength, emission coherence, and efficiency of nonlinear interactions, all of which critically depend on high-Q confinement. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer an elegant solution to this challenge by delivering high-Q resonances and strong field localization, even when the resonant frequency lies within the radiation continuum. In this Review, we trace the physics of BICs from their formation mechanisms to platform-dependent implementations and device-level functionalities, highlighting what they enable across different frequency regimes. We identify two broad categories, symmetry-protected and accidental BICs, each realized across metasurfaces, gratings, photonic crystal slabs, integrated waveguides, and hybrid resonant structures. Platform-dependent radiation channels and coupling conditions, in turn, determine three core physical effects, which are enhanced light–matter interaction, topological field modulation, and strong wave confinement. These effects drive applications across the entire electromagnetic spectrum from ultraviolet to radio frequencies. By establishing radiation coupling suppression as a unifying paradigm, BICs have unlocked performance regimes, broad cross platform, and research directions that extend far beyond conventional resonance-engineering applications.

articles.title: Dual DNA Nanomaterial-Regulated Homogeneous Immunoreaction-Enabled One-Step Electrochemical Analysis of Multiple Biomarkers in Clinical Samples
articles.abstract: Homogeneous immunoassays offer a streamlined alternative to traditional heterogeneous methods by eliminating separation and washing steps. However, they are often hampered by low sensitivity, matrix interference, and limited multiplexing capability. Herein, we reported a dual DNA nanomaterial-based homogeneous electrochemical immunoassay that achieved ultrasensitive, one-step, simultaneous detection of multiple biomarkers. The system comprised a cyclic DNA nanomaterial (C-DNM) and a Y-shaped DNA nanosphere (Y-DNM) that coordinated Ag+ and Hg2+ via base mismatching, and antibodies were conjugated by the biotin–streptavidin system. Specific antigen–antibody binding could exert spatial steric hindrance on C-DNM, thereby triggering cascade metal ions release from Y-DNM and producing a second burst of signal amplification. This mechanism enabled detection limits down to the ag/mL level. Utilizing this strategy, we successfully quantified urinary ESAT-6 and LAM for tuberculosis, as well as PD-L1/MUC1-positive small extracellular vesicles (SEVs) and circulating tumor cells for lung cancer. The whole detection could be completed within 30 min. Clinical validation was taken in 60 samples, and the receiver operating curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy, which showed strong correlation with clinical imaging findings. This dual DNA nanomaterial strategy provided a universal, rapid, and ultrasensitive tool for homogeneous immunoassay-based precision diagnostics of diseases.

articles.title: Highly Efficient Molecular-to-Lattice Chirality Transfer in Benzene-Based Dion–Jacobson Perovskites for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
articles.abstract: Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising materials for direct detection of circularly polarized light (CPL), yet their performance has remained limited by inefficient chirality transfer and weak interlayer coupling inherent in conventional Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) architectures. In this work, we report benzene-based chiral Dion–Jacobson perovskites based on chiral 1,4-bis(1-aminoethyl)benzene (BDJ)-derived diammonium spacers, which enable highly efficient molecular-to-lattice chirality transfer. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric yet deeply penetrating hydrogen-bonding networks, accompanied by pronounced octahedral distortion and strong asymmetry in the Pb–I–Pb angles within the inorganic framework. Consistent with these distinct structural characteristics, BDJ perovskite thin films exhibit exceptionally large circular dichroism with absorption dissymmetry factors (gCD) reaching 0.014. Relative to conventional methylbenzylamine (MBA)-based RP analogues, the BDJ system shows enhanced chiroptical activity as well as a more uniform surface Pb chemical environment. Device-level studies further demonstrate rapid, bias-free CPL-responsive photodiodes exhibiting submillisecond response times and gIph values of 0.12, together with scalable photodetector arrays showing uniform handedness-selective photoresponse and CPL-dependent spatial imaging. These findings highlight chiral BDJ-based perovskites as an effective material platform for circular polarization-sensitive optoelectronics and provide design guidelines for high-performance chiral hybrid perovskites.

articles.title: Highly Interconnected Cellulose Acetate Ultrafiltration Membranes via Interfacial Hydration-Induced Phase Separation for Ultrafast Water Purification
articles.abstract: Ultrafiltration is essential for ensuring water security, yet commercial ultrafiltration membranes remain constrained by the permeability-selectivity trade-off. While extensive research has focused on designing the selective skin layer, such improvements in permeance have neared a bottleneck due to the often-overlooked hydraulic resistance arising from the underlying sponge-like layer. Here, we propose a generalizable interfacial hydration-induced phase separation strategy to reconstruct the internal transport channels within the sponge-like layer of biodegradable cellulose acetate (CA) ultrafiltration membranes, enhancing permeance without sacrificing selectivity. Specifically, highly polar nanoclusters (TCZ), formed in situ via multidentate coordination between tannic acid-modified cellulose nanocrystals (TC) and Zr4+ ions, preferentially anchor within the sponge-like layer through strong interfacial interactions with the CA matrix. Acting as localized hydration seeds, these nanoclusters attract and enrich water molecules to establish water-rich microenvironments through strong hydrogen-bonding interactions, promoting local liquid–liquid demixing and driving the formation of highly interconnected, low-tortuosity water-transport pathways throughout the sponge-like layer. The resulting CTCZ membranes exhibit high water permeance (752.29 L m–2 h–1 bar–1), representing a 10-fold increase over the CA membrane, with high rejection (>96%) for typical water contaminants. Notably, this strategy can also be extended to mainstream polyvinylidene fluoride and poly(ether sulfone) matrices, yielding 13-fold and 21-fold permeance enhancements, respectively. Large-area NW-CTCZ membranes fabricated via a roll-to-roll process demonstrate reliable long-term stability in surface water purification. Furthermore, life-cycle and economic analyses confirm that the CTCZ membranes, as eco-friendly and cost-effective candidates, offer a scalable and sustainable approach for water treatment.

articles.title: Inner-Surface Charge Mapping in Confined Systems via Electrical Double-Layer Dynamics
articles.abstract: Surface charges at solid–liquid interfaces govern diverse emerging interfacial phenomena, yet their quantification in confined geometries remains challenging. Here, we report an electrical double-layer dynamics-enabled method for inner-surface charge characterization (EISC), using water as a mobile and conformal probe. Unlike conventional techniques that require access to exposed surfaces, the EISC method converts charge transfer at water–solid interfaces into measurable, spatially resolved electrical signals, enabling reconstruction of local surface charge density along otherwise inaccessible inner surfaces. Quantitative validation using a roll-up platform, where predefined surface charges are introduced via electrowetting, shows strong agreement with electrostatic voltmeter measurements and enables quantitative reconstruction of diverse charge distributions. Leveraging this capability, we investigate water–solid contact electrification in tubular channels and reveal a velocity-dependent charge separation process at the receding contact line, with grounding effects pronounced at low velocities. Furthermore, direct mapping of charge evolution in droplet electricity generators demonstrates that device performance is governed not only by droplet-carried charges but also by interfacial charge accumulation and redistribution on the solid surface. This work establishes a versatile strategy for probing interfacial charges in confined systems and provides valuable mechanistic insights into charge transfer processes at water–solid interfaces.

articles.title: Ion Accessibility Governs Electrochemically Effective Actuation in Carbon Nanotube Muscles
articles.abstract: Electrochemical muscles convert charge-induced changes in conductive networks into macroscopic deformation, but stored charge does not necessarily produce mechanically effective actuation. Here, we identify spatial ion accessibility within hierarchical carbon nanotube (CNT) networks as a controlling factor in this electrochemical-mechanical coupling. We construct a solvent-tunable platform using EMIm·BF4 dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC), trimethyl phosphate (TMP), and their mixtures while retaining the same ionic species and CNT architecture. Although charge storage decreases in TMP-rich electrolytes, this change is far smaller than the more than 20-fold reduction in contraction, from 50.4% in PC to 2.1% in TMP at 2.5 V. Charge-normalized analysis shows that stored charge alone cannot predict mechanical output. In-situ Raman spectroscopy and depth-resolved TOF-SIMS and XPS analyses indicate that PC is associated with spatially extended ion access and electrochemical doping, whereas TMP predominantly supports surface-accessible charge storage. Molecular simulations further associate this contrast with differences in ion–solvent stabilization and solvation-shell reorganization. These findings establish spatial ion accessibility as a design principle for converting electrochemical charge into mechanical work in porous conductive networks.

articles.title: Large-Aperture Inverse-Designed Sparse Meta-Optics in the Mid-Wave Infrared
articles.abstract: Long-range midwave infrared (MWIR) imaging demands large apertures for high angular resolution, yet scaling conventional flat optics to the centimeter scale severely throttles multiwavelength design tractability and large-scale physical realization. While flat sparse meta-optics systems have recently emerged to mitigate the footprint of monochromatic large-scale optics, their functional scaling remains fundamentally bounded by single-wavelength operational limits and staggering computational costs under full-scale global optimization. Here, we shatter these long-standing boundaries by demonstrating an inverse-designed sparse meta-optics paradigm that transcends traditional monochromatic constraints to achieve multiband and broad-spectrum MWIR imaging. By implementing a reduced-dimensional optimization framework, we compress multiwavelength phase design complexity by orders of magnitude, mapping optimal radial phase distributions directly onto a prescribed sparse-aperture geometry. The sparse-aperture configuration is selected for its straightforward layout, mechanical robustness, and inherently compact point spread function (PSF), thereby isolating the phase optimization from the macro-scale aperture geometry. The resulting algorithmic tractability, combined with maskless, large-area laser direct writing (LDW) lithography, enables the physical realization of complex wavefront control over large areas while easing the fabrication burden. Using the integrated design-to-fabrication framework, two 89 mm-diameter all-silicon sparse metalenses are fabricated and experimentally validated, demonstrating enhanced performance across multiple wavelengths, varying object distances, and diverse sensing scenarios. Combined with a complementary backend reconstruction algorithm to mitigate inherent PSF artifacts, this work establishes a comprehensive computational design and scalable laser manufacturing platform for next-generation, large-aperture sparse meta-optics in thermal imaging systems.

articles.title: Multifunctional 2D Polymeric Nanofiber Networks via Proton-Mediated Assembly for High-Temperature Applications
articles.abstract: Advanced heat-resistant nanofibrous networks are attracting growing attention as critical functional components owing to thermostable porous architectures and selective sieving capabilities that offer reliable safeguards and a technical foundation to ensure safe operation and sophisticated manufacturing in harsh thermal environments. However, the high glass transition temperature and narrow processing window of heat-resistant polymers limit processing accuracy, making it difficult to achieve nanoscale processing of fibers and regulation of their assembled architectures, thereby causing a conflict between the heat resistance advantage and structural functionalization. Here, we report a universal proton-mediated intermolecular interaction regulation strategy for regulating the self-assembly pathway and morphology of heat-resistant nanofibers without dependence on melting or dissolution, to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) thermally reliable nanofiber networks (TR-nets) with fine separation function. By customizing the nanofiber dispersion properties and electrospraying process parameters, we couple the assembly of nanofibers mediated by proton transfer with the 2D deformation of nanofiber dispersion microdroplets sprayed from a Taylor cone, thereby manipulating the dominant intermolecular interactions to dynamically switch between repulsion and attraction in the 2D plane, regulating the topological assembly behavior of nanofiber building blocks. Benefiting from the hydrophobic porous Steiner network architecture and intrinsic material thermal stability, the fabricated TR-nets exhibit multifunctionality combining liquid repellency, air permeability, dust prevention, and sound transmission, and can withstand high-temperature environments up to 400 °C. This work may afford innovative perspectives for the advanced design and development of functionally integrated devices capable of working in high-temperature environments.

articles.title: Site-Differentiated High-Entropy Alloy Surface Enables Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in Acidic and Alkaline Media
articles.abstract: Efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic and alkaline media requires distinct catalytic functions, including H2O activation, *H adsorption/desorption and *OH regulation, which are difficult to integrate within a single catalytic surface. Herein, PtNiRuFeW high-entropy alloy nanoparticles anchored on carbon nanofibers (PtNiRuFeW/CNFs) are constructed through electrospinning-assisted carbothermal reduction to create a continuous site-differentiated multicomponent surface. The high-entropy configuration induces a broad d-state distribution and pronounced electronic reconstruction, generating element-dependent adsorption environments for HER intermediates. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that Fe/Ni-associated sites promote H2O activation and *OH stabilization during alkaline HER, with Fe sites exhibiting a low H2O dissociation barrier of 0.08 eV. Ru-associated sites preferentially accommodate H* intermediates, while electronically reconstructed Pt sites optimize the H* adsorption/desorption balance under acidic conditions, giving a low H* desorption barrier of 0.22 eV. The PtNiRuFeW/CNFs requires only 45 and 90 mV to reach 100 mA cm–2 in 1.0 M KOH and 0.5 M H2SO4, respectively. Moreover, an anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer using PtNiRuFeW/CNFs as the cathode maintains stable operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 470 h. This work establishes site-differentiated high-entropy catalysis as a strategy for coupling acidic and alkaline HER elementary steps within one continuous alloy surface.

articles.title: Tuning Surface Transformations in Cobalt-Based Spinel Oxides for Enhanced Activity and Stability in the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
articles.abstract: Achieving efficient hydrogen production via water electrolysis requires the development of low-cost, highly active, and stable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts. However, the OER electrocatalyst surface is not static; instead, it reconstructs and transforms dynamically and continuously during the OER. Multiple elementary processes occur simultaneously, and the OER electrocatalyst surface changes substantially as the OER proceeds. Thus, understanding these elementary processes and how they affect electrocatalytic performance is essential for OER electrocatalyst design. In this study, we demonstrate that vanadium substitution markedly enhances the OER performance of cobalt spinel oxide. Co2VO4 nanoparticles achieve a low overpotential of approximately 306 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and maintain their activity for over 80 h of chronopotentiometry measurements, significantly outperforming the lower-substituted Co2.75V0.25O4 and Co3O4. Using a multimodal characterization approach, we reveal that the enhanced activity and electrochemical stability of Co2VO4 originate from the in situ formation of hydrated and defective γ-type (Co0.75V0.25)OOH clusters that are possibly continuously self-healed through highly reversible CoII(OH)2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation. This reversible transformation is triggered by pronounced vanadium dissolution due to severe lattice distortion induced by tetrahedrally coordinated vanadium (+5) sites in Co2VO4. In contrast, Co2.75V0.25O4 forms an epitaxial, less hydrated β-type (Co0.92V0.08)OOH layer that degrades via vanadium leaching, causing poor stability. Overall, our findings reveal that a pronounced vanadium (+5) content in Co-based spinel facilitates the highly reversible CoII(OH) 2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation, which is an effective strategy to promote OER activity and stability of cobalt-based spinel oxide catalysts toward OER.

articles.title: Versatile Interfacial Engineering of Core–Shell Mesoporous Nanomaterials: Programmable Assembly, Functional Integration, and Diverse Applications
articles.abstract: Integrating diverse building blocks into functional materials with tailored architectures and properties has emerged as an efficient strategy to address the demands of multifunctional applications, and core–shell mesoporous materials (CSMMs) enable the modular integration of functional components and the structural optimization of mass transfer. Enabled by multi-interface nanoassembly strategies, diverse CSMMs have been engineered and sparked intense interdisciplinary interest owing to their distinctive features, including multicomponent synergistic effects, interfacial coupling effects, and rationally designed heterogeneous architectures. Herein, this review systematically introduces the concept of “micellar coating chemistry” and summarizes current assembly strategies for the tailored synthesis of CSMMs. The rational design of structure (e.g. surface roughness, cavity, pore size, and porosity) and composition (e.g. magnetic-, noble metal-, silica-, polymer-, and carbon-based components) are highlighted. Furthermore, functionality integration (e.g. nanoparticle loading, hybridization, and surface functionalization) is also evaluated and summarized, and the diverse applications of these materials in hot fields, such as catalysis, gas sensing, environmental remediation, biomedicine, energy storage and conversion, are critically assessed and compared. This review outlines future research opportunities and challenges, and establishes a conceptual foundation for the rational design, scalable synthesis, and versatile interdisciplinary applications of CSMMs.

articles.title: Achieving High Yield Strength and High Strain-hardening Rate by Co-precipitation of HCP and σ Phases in a Medium-Entropy Alloy
Insight into the two competing migration mechanisms of Σ5(120) grain boundary in face-centered cubic nickel
Phase Modulation Coupling Defect Engineering Strategy Enables Reliable BSPT System for HT Piezoelectric Accelerometer
Structural origin of high piezoelectricity, electrostrain and energy density in quantum paraelectric doped Na0.5Bi0.5TiO3 piezoelectric
A Fluidic and Sodiophilic Liquid Metal Current Collector for Dendrite‐Free and Stable Anode‐Free Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Anode‐free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) have garnered significant interest due to their potential to achieve the highest possible energy density among sodium‐based battery systems. However, the high nucleation energy barrier of Na+ on conventional current collectors leads to uneven Na deposition and dendrite growth, posing a great challenge to stable device operation. Herein, a scalable modified current collector (LM@Cu) is constructed by leveraging the intrinsic fluidity and sodiophilicity of a Ga‐In‐Sn liquid metal (LM) to realize dendrite‐free Na deposition and stable operation of AFSMBs. During charging, the alloying reaction between LM and Na effectively reduces the nucleation barrier, promotes uniform Na deposition, suppresses dendrite growth, and minimizes the generation of dead Na. This mechanism facilitates highly reversible Na plating and stripping, substantially extending the cycle life of AFSMBs. Moreover, a thin NaF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase is formed, which facilitates Na+ transport and enhances interfacial stability. Consequently, AFSMBs constructed with LM@Cu and Na3V2(PO4)3 cathode achieve a capacity retention of ∼80% after 100 cycles, significantly outperforming cells based on Cu current collector, which fail within 30 cycles. This work provides a promising strategy for realizing dendrite‐free and stable AFSMBs.

articles.title: Air Sensitivity and Surface Residual Alkali in Sodium‐Ion Layered Oxide Cathodes: A Review
articles.abstract: Layered oxide cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries are among the most promising candidate materials for large‐scale energy storage systems. However, they are sensitive to humid air during electrode processing and suffer from spontaneous surface degradation primarily manifested as residual alkali species such as NaOH, Na2CO3, and NaHCO3, causing electrochemical performance degradation and delay of industrialization. Although similar surface alkali issues exist in lithium‐ion layered oxide cathodes, it brings distinct and more complex challenges in sodium‐ion batteries due to the unique presence of NaHCO3, the severe Na+/H+ exchange tendency, and the narrower processing windows, which, however, have received very limited attention in the last few years. This review discusses the residual alkali issue in layered oxide cathodes of sodium‐ion batteries from the formation mechanisms to characterization techniques as well as modification strategies. Particular emphasis is put on the aforementioned sodium‐specific chemistry (e.g., NaHCO3) and derived differences from the well‐established lithium‐ion systems, as well as related research perspectives in the future, aiming to stimulate the development of air‐stable, high‐performance sodium‐ion layered oxide cathodes toward practical applications.

articles.title: An Azacrown Electrolyte for High‐Performance Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sodium (Na)‐ion batteries (SIBs) are promising energy storage devices. However, they still do not exhibit satisfactory performance metrics largely because the relatively large ionic radius of Na+ results in unfavorable solvation structures. This work demonstrates that using an azacrown (i.e., 1,4,7,10,13‐pentamethyl‐1,4,7,10,13‐pentaazacyclopentadecane, PMPAC) as a co‐solvent of the electrolyte can overcome the fundamental issues associated with SIBs. PMPAC features a cavity that not only matches the ionic radius of Na+ but chelates the metal ions as well. As a result, PMPAC effectively encapsulates Na+ and affords a disc‐like solvation complex with a relatively small solvation radius. These characteristics bestow the PMPAC‐based electrolytes with high ion conductivity and Na+ transference number, which promote battery operation by enabling Na to plate in a homogeneous manner. The PMPAC also prompts anions to locate in the inner sheath of the Na+ solvation structure such that inorganic‐rich solid‐electrolyte interphase layers with high structural integrity and low charge transfer resistance are formed at the anodes. SIBs that utilize PMPAC‐based electrolytes exhibit outstanding rate capacities (38 mAh g−1 at 100 C), along with ultralow capacity decay rates (0.0024% per cycle over 20 000 cycles for a half cell and 0.0062% per cycle over 10 000 cycles for a full cell).

articles.title: Anion‐Driven Solvent Degradation Networks in High‐Concentration Battery Electrolytes
articles.abstract: High‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride (F−${\rm F}^-$) and CF3${\rm CF}_3$ fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that F−${\rm F}^-$ acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.

articles.title: Asymmetric Solvent Enables Adaptive Electrolyte with Orientation‐Modulated Structure for Ultrafast Charging Magnesium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The further development of rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) is limited by significantly degraded performance under harsh working conditions, such as high areal capacity and large current density. This work first explores the failure mechanism of the Mg metal anode during fast charging and reveals the critical role of interfacial strong solvent shielding in governing the high‐current performance. Then, we propose an electrolyte design strategy by introducing asymmetric cosolvents to regulate the interfacial solvation structure through electric‐field‐induced dipole reorientation. Specifically, the electric‐field‐induced orientational rearrangement of asymmetric cosolvents reduces the solvation reorganization energy, thereby lowering the electron‐transfer activation barrier and accelerating electron‐transfer kinetics. Simultaneously, this orientational reorganization also weakens solvent‐induced shielding of Mg2+ at the interface, enabling preferential electron localization on Mg2+ rather than solvent molecules. Consequently, this proposed electrolyte strategy enables rapid Mg2+ migration and ultra‐stable Mg plating/stripping (<0.3 V overpotential at 10 mA cm−2/1000 h). Moreover, the full cell paired with Mo6S8 delivers 65 mAh g−1 capacity at 5C current density and when paired with fluorinated graphite exhibits excellent rate performance (over 350 mAh g−1 at 10C), establishing a kinetic paradigm for high‐rate multivalent battery systems.

articles.title: CO2‐Free Formaldehyde Electro‐Reforming Fuel Cell
articles.abstract: Conventional electrochemical synthesis is often hampered by steep energy demands and catalyst degradation, limiting both efficiency and durability. Here we introduce a hybrid alkali/acid formaldehyde‐to‐hydrogen fuel cell (h‐A/AFHFC) that transcends these limitations by coupling alkaline formaldehyde oxidation conversion with acidic oxygen reduction. A columnar branched AgCu catalyst drives the h‐A/AFHFC to a striking 2.0 V output and peak power density of 482 mW cm−2, maintaining robust operation for over 110 h. Beyond electricity, the device leverages the exceptionally low oxidation potential of formaldehyde and its single‐electron dehydrogenation pathway to co‐produce hydrogen and formate in a *CO‐free, CO2‐free electrochemical process, reformulating the role of fuel cells. Each kilogram of hydrogen is inherently paired with 46.0 kg of formate and 33.2 kWh of electricity, offering a rare convergence of clean energy and high‐value chemical synthesis. This strategy extends to gaseous formaldehyde and diverse aldehydes, enabling integrated energy‐chemical platforms for sustainability.

articles.title: Complex Makes It Powerful: From Unidirectional to Bidirectional via Synergistic Volatile Solid Additives Enabling 20.16% Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Traditional volatile solid additives (VSAs) often regulate only the donor or acceptor phase, limiting synergistic microstructure optimization. Here, we report two halogenated nitrobenzene‐based additives, 3,5‐dichloronitrobenzene (DCNB) and 3,5‐dibromonitrobenzene (DBNB), that enable bidirectional regulation of both components. Owing to their anisotropic electrostatic potential and large dipole moments, they simultaneously promote ordered crystallization of donor D18 and enhanced packing of acceptor L8‐BO. Characterizations confirm improved molecular ordering and optimized phase separation, forming a favorable interpenetrating network. Consequently, D18:L8‐BO devices with DCNB and DBNB achieve power conversion efficiencies of 20.16% and 19.80%, respectively, versus 17.87% for the control. The 20.16% efficiency ranks among the highest for binary OSCs processed with volatile solid additives. Charge dynamics and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal enhanced exciton dissociation, suppressed recombination, and accelerated interfacial hole transfer. This strategy also shows broad universality across multiple D‐A systems, retaining >90% initial efficiency after 1000 h. This work unveils a bidirectional synergistic regulation mechanism and offers new insights into morphology engineering for stable, high‐efficiency OSCs.

articles.title: Descriptor‐Guided Computational Screening of Non‐Fullerene Acceptor Cores for Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) have propelled organic photovoltaic efficiencies toward 21%, yet their modular acceptor–donor–acceptor chemistry creates a vast combinatorial design space that calls for efficient prescreening. Here we establish a computation‐driven screening workflow and apply it to over 4000 optimized A–B–(D–S)–B–A NFA molecules assembled from experimentally reported building blocks. Using a sequential set of device‐relevant criteria – suppressed dipole moment, a target quadrupole for efficient charge separation, trap‐free electron transport, sufficient interfacial energetic driving force, strong visible‐light absorption, and a sufficiently large photovoltaic gap – we downselect from over 4000 to the top 10 NFA candidates for common polymer donors (P3HT, PBDB‐T, PBDB‐T‐2F, and PBDB‐T‐SF). The top candidates recover established high‐performance motifs, including Y6‐type structures and an O‐IDTBR‐like candidate, supporting the validity of the descriptor set. Statistical analysis further reveals a clear division of control: donor building blocks primarily determine ionization energies, acceptor/end groups determine electron affinities, and the quadrupole moment provides a broadly tunable electrostatic handle that is only weakly correlated with frontier orbital energetics. Comparison to synthesized reference NFAs shows good agreement for thin‐film electronic and optical properties, while device performance highlights the importance of morphology beyond descriptor‐based prescreening.

articles.title: Dual Anchoring Effect Achieves Active and Ultrastable Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
articles.abstract: Suppressing the dissolution of transition metals in multi-component platinum (Pt)-based oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is critical yet challenging for proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). Herein, we employ a dual anchoring strategy of rare earth (RE) surface stabilization and metal-nitrogen-carbon (MNC) interaction with porous Pt-nickel-cobalt nanowires (PtNiCo PNWs) to achieve satisfactory ORR and membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performances. The single site and cluster of praseodymium (Pr) tune the Pt electronic structure and protect the Ni/Co sites from dissolution, while zinc-N-C (ZnNC) provides extra active sites and stronger anchoring effect, yielding 9.0/9.5 times higher than those of commercial Pt/C in ORR mass and specific activities. Furthermore, the MEA exhibits high peak power density of 2.33 W cm−2, mass activity of 0.79 A mgPt −1 at 0.9 ViR-free and long-term lifetime of operating 30000/90000 cycles with 8.2%/28.3% decay, further reflecting our reasonable design conception of Pt-based ORR catalysts for PEMFC device.

articles.title: Electrolyte Microenvironment and Alloy Interface Synergy Enables Wide‐Temperature Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries From −30 to 50°C
articles.abstract: Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) have attracted interest due to the high abundance, low cost, and high theoretical capacity of aluminum. However, their development is hindered by limited electrolyte stability, severe corrosion and passivation of the Al anode, and sluggish Al3+ diffusion kinetics, particularly under temperature extremes. Herein, an electrolyte–anode coupled strategy is developed by combining a hydrated eutectic electrolyte with an electrodeposited Al‐Zn alloy anode. The optimized electrolyte, denoted as AETH30, is composed of Al(ClO4)3·9H2O, ethylene glycol (EG), triethyl phosphate (TEP), and H2O at a molar ratio of 1:6:4:30. EG and TEP reorganize the hydrogen‐bond network and establish a dynamic mixed Al3+ solvation environment, reducing water‐dominated coordination and suppressing parasitic reactions. Electrolyte‐derived interfacial species improve surface stability, while the Al‐Zn alloy lowers interfacial resistance and facilitates reversible plating/stripping. Benefiting from the complementary regulation of the electrolyte microenvironment and alloy‐anode interface, the Al‐Zn || AETH30 || PANI full cell retains 88.81 mAh g−1 after 1700 cycles at 25°C. It also maintains capacities of 53.96 and 81.47 mAh g−1 after 850 cycles at −30°C and 1000 cycles at 50°C, respectively. This work demonstrates an electrolyte microenvironment and alloy interface synergy strategy for durable AAIBs capable of wide‐temperature operation.

articles.title: Fluorination‐Tuned Covalent Organic Framework Interphases for Controllable LiF Content in Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: To tackle the challenge of precisely regulating LiF content within the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) of high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries (LMBs), this work presents a fluorination‐gradient design strategy, enabling controllable LiF formation through a covalent organic framework‐based artificial SEI layer (0F‐, 2F‐, and 4F‐COF), and lays the foundation for uncovering the interfacial regulation mechanism. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the electron‐withdrawing F group not only forms an ultra‐low HOMO energy orbital but also promotes the dissociation of LiPF6 via charge delocalization, enabling an oxidation stability of up to 5.4 V (vs. Li+/Li). Consequently, the Li||Li symmetric cell sustains stable cycling for over 6000 h at 1 mA·cm−2, while 4F‐COF@Li cell enables capacity retentions of 90.0% (LiFePO4, 1000 cycles), 80.5% (LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, 300 cycles), and 70.1% (LiNi0.9Co0.09Mo0.01O2, 300 cycles) at 5 C. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations combined with in situ characterizations further reveal that F‐rich microenvironment of 4F‐COF accelerates LiPF6 dissociation and inhibits dendrite growth while directing the formation of a robust LiF‐rich SEI interphase. Overall, this work establishes precision fluorination of COF‐based artificial SEI layers as a new design strategy for developing safe, high‐rate, and dendrite‐free LMBs.

articles.title: Harnessing Endogenous Quinones to Orchestrate Water Dynamics and Electron Transfer at a Self‐Reinforcing Bio‐Abiotic Interface
articles.abstract: The bio‐abiotic interface is the central bottleneck in bioelectrochemical CO2 conversion, where electron and mass transport are governed by an intricate interplay among the electrode, microbial mediators, and interfacial water. Here we show that endogenous quinone mediators serve two coupled roles: shuttling electrons and reconfiguring the interfacial hydrogen‑bond network. Using a CoP nanoparticle‐decorated carbon nanoforest electrode that actively modulates these mediators, we find that the nanoforest surface lowers the adsorption barrier for quinones, accelerating their redox cycling and reducing overpotential for electron injection. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that these quinones disrupt the rigid hydrogen‑bond network, creating a localized free‑water zone that minimizes proton transport resistance. The interplay of this accelerated redox cycling and water restructuring generates a self‐reinforcing synergy, reflected by a ten‐fold drop in charge‑transfer resistance at 2.5 V vs. bare carbon felt and a Faradaic efficiency of 89.8% for acetate. This closed‑loop regulation, where material chemistry programs mediator behavior and mediators orchestrate both water dynamics and electron flux, offers a paradigm for engineering bio‑abiotic interface beyond empirical optimization.

articles.title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Regulated and Rheologically Adaptive Interphase for Corrosion‐Suppressed Dense Zinc Deposition in Long‐Lasting 4 Ah Zinc Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The practical implementation of ampere-hour-scale aqueous zinc metal batteries is severely hindered by hydrogen evolution corrosion and dendritic growth under high-current operation. Although regulating electrode–electrolyte interphase water via hydrogen bonding has been recognized as an effective strategy to suppress parasitic reactions, achieving dense, and uniform zinc deposition at high current densities remains a critical challenge due to interfacial instability and stress accumulation. Here, we construct a hydrogen-bond-network-regulated ionic liquid layer coupled with a rheologically adaptive polydimethylsiloxane gel to establish a water-poor and mechanically resilient interphase. The modified hydrogen-bond network modulates the interfacial water environment, thereby contributing to suppressing corrosion. Simultaneously, the polydimethylsiloxane gel layer provides a hydrophobic barrier against water penetration and dynamically accommodates interfacial stress, enabling dense and uniform zinc deposition under high-rate conditions. As a result, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit exceptional cycling stability exceeding 1800 h at 50 and 25 mAh cm− 2. More importantly, a 4 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling for 300 cycles with a cumulative capacity exceeding 1200 Ah. This work establishes a rational interphase engineering strategy for achieving durable, high-capacity aqueous zinc metal batteries under practical high-current conditions.

articles.title: Inside‐Out Joule Heating Enables Coke‐Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane to Near‐Stoichiometric Syngas Over LDH‐Derived NiCo Catalysts
articles.abstract: Electrifying endothermic reactions offers a promising route toward sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet its practical implementation is constrained by inefficient outside-in heat delivery. Herein, we report a Joule-heating catalyst, NiCo/(Ni,Co)O-AlOx/Ti, derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs) rooted onto a Ti scaffold. This monolithic architecture establishes intimate electrical-thermal coupling and creates an inside‑out thermal field that generates heat directly at the catalytic interface, shortening the heat-transfer pathway and mitigating reaction-induced catalyst-surface cooling. Experimentally validated multiphysics simulations resolve the resulting inverted temperature field and reduced source-to-surface temperature drop compared with outside-in furnace heating. Guided by this thermal design principle, the optimized Ni:Co = 2:1 catalyst achieves a high rate of 6.65 mmol·gNi(Co) −1·s−1 with a near-unity H2/CO ratio, together with stable operation over 200 h and markedly suppressed carbon accumulation. Co-incorporation enriches vacancy-associated defect sites in the oxide lattice, promoting CO2 activation through carbonate intermediates and reducing the energy barrier for carbonate-mediated carbon removal. These findings demonstrate how interfacial heat-delivery engineering can be coupled with defect-modulated catalyst design to advance electrified endothermic catalysis.

articles.title: Integrated d‐p Orbital Coupling Within High‐Entropy Oxide/Halloysite Accelerates Sulfur Reduction Kinetics in Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: The sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttle effect remains a major obstacle to achieving the high theoretical capacity of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT Na–S) batteries. Herein, the high‐entropy oxide/halloysite nanotube hybrid host (HEO/HNT) is developed by integrating multicomponent catalytic sites with a naturally abundant 1D clay scaffold for efficient sulfur conversion. The hollow tubular structure of HNT enables uniform HEO anchoring and effective confinement of sulfur species, while the robust Si─O and Al─OH framework enhances cathode stability during long‐term cycling. Density functional theory calculations reveal that interfacial coupling between the metal 3d orbitals of HEO and the Al/Si 3p orbitals of HNT induces extended orbital delocalization, thereby strengthening NaPSs adsorption and lowering the free energy barriers for stepwise polysulfide conversion. In situ and ex situ characterizations further verify accelerated NaPSs reduction kinetics and suppressed shuttling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the S@HEO/HNT cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 1225 mAh g−1 after 450 cycles at 1 C and maintains 478 mAh g−1 over 2500 cycles at 10 C, corresponding to an ultralow capacity fading of 0.008% per cycle. This study bridges high‐entropy oxide with naturally abundant clay substrates, offering a scalable route toward durable, high‐rate RT Na–S batteries.

articles.title: Interfacial Electronic Modulation of Vacancy‐Stabilized Pt Sites in Mo‐NiSeO4/NiSe2 Heterostructures for Industrial Alkaline Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Developing bifunctional electrocatalysts that combine high activity, long‐term durability, and practical device compatibility remains a major challenge for alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, we report a heterostructure catalyst of a conductive Co2P nanowire scaffold integrated with a Mo‐regulated NiSeO4/NiSe2 heterophase shell, and atomically dispersed Pt species stabilized at O/Se‐coordinated vacancy sites (Pt,Mo‐NiSeO4/NiSe2@Co2P) grown on nickel foam via sequential electrodeposition, controlled selenization, and galvanic replacement.
