Benefiting from synergistic electronic modulation and heterointerface engineering, the catalyst requires only 24 and 98 mV to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm−2 for the hydrogen evolution reaction, and 242 and 330 mV for the oxygen evolution reaction, in 1.0 M KOH, with excellent durability. Operando Raman spectroscopy and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy reveal dynamic surface evolution during electrocatalysis and confirm the atomic dispersion of Pt. When assembled in a two‐electrode electrolyzer, the catalyst achieves cell voltages of 1.47 V at 10 mA cm−2 and 1.65 V at 100 mA cm−2 in 30 wt.% KOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer delivers 1.55 V at 0.3 A cm−2 and 1.76 V at 1.0 A cm−2 at 70 °C, demonstrating its promise for practical alkaline hydrogen production.

articles.title: Local Atomic Disorder‐Driven Deep Relaxor State for Ultrahigh Dielectric Energy Storage With High Thermal Stability
articles.abstract: Lead-free dielectric ceramic capacitors are indispensable for advanced high-power electronic pulse systems owing to their exceptional power density and rapid charge-discharge kinetics. However, the simultaneous realization of ultrahigh recoverable energy density (W rec) and high efficiency (η), especially with robust thermal stability, remains challenging. Here, we propose a local structural design strategy focused on implementing atomic-scale disorder within relaxor ferroelectrics to achieve a deep relaxor state across a wide temperature window. Atomic-scale structure characterizations reveal that this local chemical/structural disorder induces ultrafine, highly active polar nanoregions, fostering an optimized polarization response while remaining resilient against thermal fluctuations. Consequently, the designed ceramics exhibit superior energy-storage performance, characterized by a large W rec of 13.1 J cm−3 and ultrahigh η of 93%, leading to a high figure of merit up to 187.1. Notably, exceptional performance stability across diverse operating conditions is bestowed, with η remaining above 90% at temperatures up to 200°C. This study thus provides a robust paradigm for designing dielectric capacitors that deliver both high energy-storage performance and reliability in harsh working environments.

articles.title: Materials‐Property Classification of Interlayers for Stabilizing Lithium Metal Interfaces in Sulfide‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: Sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs) promise high energy density by using lithium metal anodes, but their practical implementation is limited by severe interfacial instability. At the lithium metal/sulfide electrolyte interface, coupled chemical, electrochemical, and mechanical degradation accelerates impedance growth and cell failure. Interlayer strategies are promising for stabilizing sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state batteries because they can mitigate interfacial degradation, improve contact stability, and regulate ion/electron transport at critical electrode–electrolyte interfaces. However, their mechanisms have largely been interpreted based on phenomenological observations and empirical performance improvements, rather than through intrinsic material property–mechanism relationships, highlighting the need for a material property‐driven design framework. Here, we categorize interlayer strategies into metal, polymer, ceramic, and composite systems and reinterpret their functions from an electro‐chemo‐mechanical perspective. We discuss how stiffness, ductility, fracture toughness, electronic conductivity, electrochemical stability, chemical stability, lithiophilicity, and Li‐ion transport govern interfacial behavior during assembly, plating, stripping, and long‐term cycling. By correlating representative interlayer systems with their electro‐chemo‐mechanical properties, this perspective clarifies the relationship between material characteristics and interfacial stabilization behavior in sulfide‐based ASSLMBs. This property‐driven framework is expected to provide practical criteria for screening unexplored interlayer materials and guiding the rational design of stable lithium metal/sulfide electrolyte interfaces.

articles.title: Maximum Stability Point Tracking Stabilizes Wide‐Bandgap Mixed‐Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Mixed‐halide wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites with bandgaps above 1.65 eV are essential top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, bromide‐rich WBG perovskites suffer from photo‐induced halide segregation, while its origin under operating conditions remains unclear. Here, we identify trapped‐charge accumulation as a key factor triggering phase segregation during operation and develop a practical operational strategy to mitigate this process. Time‐evolving photoluminescence and depth‐profiling x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal that trapped‐charge accumulation accelerates ionic redistribution and halide segregation under illumination. Based on this insight, we introduce a maximum stability point tracking (MSPT) strategy that periodically relieves charge accumulation during device operation. WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) operated under MSPT retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation, whereas devices operated under conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) rapidly degrade during the early stages of operation. Post‐operational analyses further reveal that MSPT preserves the alloyed perovskite phase, whereas MPPT induces pronounced phase segregation. As an operation‐stage strategy that mitigates charge accumulation without altering material composition, MSPT is compatible with existing material approaches and offers a route toward more stable perovskite photovoltaics. These findings provide an operational guideline for stabilizing WBG PSCs and advancing tandem photovoltaic technologies.

articles.title: Maximum Stability Point Tracking Stabilizes Wide‐Bandgap Mixed‐Halide Perovskite Solar Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
articles.abstract: Perovskite Solar Cells In article number e71358, Mansoo Choi, Yun Seog Lee, Namyoung Ahn, and co‐workers report maximum stability point tracking (MSPT) for wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskite solar cells. Trapped‐charge accumulation is identified as a key factor driving halide segregation during operation. By mitigating charge accumulation, MSPT enables devices to retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation.

articles.title: Moist‐Electric Wallpaper With Engineered Unidirectional Moisture Transport for Indoor Energy Harvesting and Humidity Management
articles.abstract: Moist‐electric generators (MEGs) convert ambient humidity into electricity, but their inherently low power output makes outdoor deployment as a general energy source impractical. Indoor environments, where humidity is stable and low‐power electronics demand only microwatt‐to‐milliwatt supplies, present a more realistic opportunity—and wallpaper, with its large continuously exposed surface area and seamless architectural integration, is the most compelling platform to realize it. Here we report the first wallpaper‐type MEG, enabled by a peripheral‐absorption, center‐evaporation architecture that achieves engineered unidirectional moisture transport on a single paper sheet. Glycerol at the periphery captures atmospheric moisture; polyvinylpyrrolidone in the intermediate region acts as a bound‐water sink whose reduced porosity and lowered water activity drive inward transport through Laplace pressure and chemical potential gradients; and a wax‐treated center exploits the phase‐selective behavior of hydrophobic pores—blocking liquid while transmitting vapor—to confine evaporation without a solid seal. A concealed through‐hole interconnection strategy enables modular scaling with no visible wiring. A single unit delivers ∼0.34 V and ∼2.2 µW/cm2 at 80% RH with stable output over 90 min. A 1596‐unit array powers a wireless keyboard and simultaneously reduces indoor humidity from 38% to 32%, transforming passive wall surfaces into self‐powered, climate‐responsive interfaces.

articles.title: Multifunctional Matrix‐Activated Electrodes Enabling Efficient Proton Transport and Durable Low‐Pt Operation for High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: Phosphoric acid (PA)‐related challenges, including PA loss, redistribution, and flooding, critically limit the performance and long‐term durability of high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs) based on PA‐doped membrane electrode assemblies. Although these issues can be partially mitigated using proton‐conducting additives and hydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene, practical commercialization remains impeded by restricted high‐temperature operability and the requirement for high Pt loadings. To address these challenges, here we report a cerium hydrogen phosphate (CeHP)‐integrated multifunctional matrix‐activated electrode (MME) that stabilizes PA‐containing electrode microenvironments and preserve electrochemical pathways under severe high‐temperature operation above 200°C, where acid evaporation, dehydration, and migration become increasingly pronounced. This integrated matrix combines high‐temperature proton‐conduction, radical scavenging, and structural reinforcement of the porous catalyst layer, consequently alleviating the degradation at such high temperature. As a result, the optimized MME delivers a 38% increase in peak power density and a 62% reduction in voltage decay rate at 240°C, while requiring only 40% of the Pt loading of a Celtec commercial HT‐PEMFC electrode (0.4 vs. 1.0 mgPt cm−2 per electrode). These results establish multifunctional catalyst‐layer matrix engineering as an effective strategy for enabling durable, low‐Pt HT‐PEMFC operation in acid‐doped polymer electrochemical systems under harsh high‐temperature conditions.

articles.title: Multifunctional Matrix‐Activated Electrodes Enabling Efficient Proton Transport and Durable Low‐Pt Operation for High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
articles.abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells In article number e71438, Hansung Kim, Katie Heeyum Lim, So Young Lee, and co‐workers introduce a cerium hydrogen phosphate‐integrated multifunctional matrix‐activated electrode that transforms the catalyst‐layer microenvironment in high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The matrix strengthens proton‐conduction networks, suppresses radical‐driven degradation, and fortifies the porous catalyst‐layer architecture, enabling remarkably durable, high‐performance operation at reduced Pt loading.

articles.title: Novel UV‐Shielding Ionic Liquid Enables All‐Air‐Processed Flexible Perovskite Solar Cell
articles.abstract: Flexible perovskite solar cells (f-PSCs) are highly susceptible to ultraviolet (UV) degradation and mechanical brittleness during ambient-air fabrication, hindering their commercialization. Herein, we engineer an anti-UV ionic liquid (1-vinyl-3-[3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl]imidazolium chloride, IL-SiO-2) featuring a tailored C═C-imidazolium hybrid architecture to address these challenges. The conjugated C═C bonds effectively enable UV shielding to suppress precursor degradation while retarding PbI2 segregation and I3 − generation in perovskite film, thereby preventing f-PSC device deterioration. Simultaneously, the ionic liquid IL-SiO-2's adaptive molecular structure enhances mechanical compliance, enabling robust integration with flexible substrates under bending stress. Ultimately, IL-SiO-2 synergistically enables UV-resistant fabrication of defect-suppressed perovskite films and stabilized f-PSC in air, reducing Young's modulus to 2.58 GPa and grain boundary density by ∼10%, achieving exceptional mechanical durability with 92% power conversion efficiency (PCE) retention after 3,000 bends at R = 2 mm. Remarkable ambient-air stability and humidity resistance are also attained. The fully air-processed f-PSC delivers a negligible hysteresis (0.004) and retains 80.0 ± 1.1% PCE after 360 h in a damp heat test. This work pioneers a multifunctional ionic liquid strategy to concurrently boost UV tolerance, mechanical resilience, and efficiency of f-PSC, charting new pathways for air-compatible fabrication of durable flexible photovoltaics.

articles.title: Oxygen Atoms in Pd Single‐Atom Loaded Cs2SnCl6 Perovskite as Electron–Hole Separated Channel for Efficient Photo‐Assisted Electrocatalytic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
articles.abstract: Studies on halide perovskites for electrocatalysis remain in their infancy, largely limited to preliminary attempts at inducing oxygen atoms and improving stability. A key challenge lies in the lack of effective strategies for controlled oxygen atom introduction. Herein, we design a facile method to generate oxygen atoms in Pd single‐atom‐loaded Cs2SnCl6 (O‐Cs2SnCl6@Pd) by using hydrogen peroxide. Under Xe light irradiation, it exhibits a low overpotential (135 mV at 10 mA cm−2) during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with long stability for 100 h. DFT calculations illustrate that the incorporation of oxygen atoms in O‐Cs2SnCl6@Pd modulates the electronic structure, as evidenced by a lowered overpotential for key intermediate species. This modulation further increases electron density, promoting the adsorption and activation of OER intermediates, as well as enabling the population of a new excited state. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further evidences that O atoms reduce the recombination of electron–hole, thereby significantly facilitating charge‐transfer to active sites that promote electrocatalytic reactions. This study introduces a novel strategy for the rational design and synthesis of high‐performance photo‐assisted electrocatalytic materials, offering a pathway to enhanced catalytic efficiency and functionality.

articles.title: Physics‐Informed Machine Learning for Solid Oxide Cell Materials and Microstructures Under Operando Constraints
articles.abstract: Solid oxide cells (SOCs) operate at high temperature under dual atmospheres and electrochemical polarization. Their performance depends not only on composition and instantaneous operating conditions, but also on operating history, because defect populations, transport pathways, and microstructures evolve during service. This behavior limits conventional machine‐learning models trained on static or steady‐state data, because high interpolation accuracy rarely guarantees reliable extrapolation to operando or aging conditions. In this review, physics‐informed machine learning (PIML) encompasses physical knowledge introduced through descriptors, model architectures, generative constraints, and experimental feedback, rather than only neural networks constrained by partial differential equations. We organize representative SOC studies using a four‐level hierarchy of physics embedding and relate it to data fidelity, while tracing descriptors from elemental attributes to dynamic operando‐state variables. We then examine how connectivity, conservation laws, and thermodynamic stability can constrain microstructure inverse design and reject physically inadmissible outputs. Further progress requires closer links among defect chemistry, microstructure physics, service‐relevant data, and experimental feedback, enabling models that remain valid under realistic conditions and support closed‐loop design.

articles.title: Pre‐Sodiation Strategies for Sodium‐Ion Batteries: From Mechanisms to a Multidimensional Evaluation Framework
articles.abstract: The irreversible consumption of sodium ions during the initial cycle, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity decay, poses a fundamental bottleneck to the commercialization of sodium‐ion batteries. While pre‐sodiation has emerged as a pivotal strategy to compensate for this sodium deficit, the field currently lacks a systematic methodology to critically assess and rationally select among diverse pre‐sodiation tactics beyond mere electrochemical metrics. This review addresses this need by synthesizing existing evaluation criteria into a structured multidimensional assessment paradigm. We first delineate the mechanistic underpinnings of physical, electrochemical, chemical, and additive‐based pre‐sodiation strategies. We then introduce a systematic framework that integrates electrochemical performance, interfacial physicochemical properties, and electrode structural evolution to provide a holistic assessment of pre‐sodiation efficacy. Furthermore, we highlight how advanced operando and ex situ characterization techniques decode underlying compensation mechanisms and quantify kinetic improvements. Finally, a comparative analysis based on controllability, scalability, and manufacturing compatibility is presented, offering strategic guidelines for protocol selection. Ultimately, this work provides a foundational reference and a practical decision‐making guide, facilitating the rational design of efficient pre‐sodiation technologies for practical sodium‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Programming Structural Disorder in MOFs for a Stable Bifunctional Water‐Splitting Electrocatalyst
articles.abstract: For practical water electrolysis, electrocatalysts must deliver both high activity and stability. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a programmable platform for constructing tailored active sites and coordination environments, offering considerable potential for high activity. However, MOF electrocatalysts typically undergo activation‐induced reconstruction, during which their ordered frameworks transform into disordered active states, generating reconstruction‐induced strain. Poor accommodation of this strain can lead to morphological collapse, metal‐site leaching, and ultimately compromised stability. To address these issues, we leveraged the programmability of MOFs to restrict the long‐range extension of their secondary building units, thereby pre‐introducing disorder into the framework to facilitate strain accommodation during reconstruction. Consequently, activation increased the electrochemically active surface area of the disordered structure, in contrast to the decrease observed for the ordered counterpart, suggesting that destructive reconstruction was effectively mitigated. The resulting active phase retained M–O–M bridging vibrational features even at 1.9 V (vs. RHE), whereas the corresponding features in the ordered MOF were markedly weakened at 1.4 V (vs. RHE), indicating better structural integrity after reconstruction. These advantages enabled stable operation for up to 500 h in an electrolyzer and 1500 h at 1 A cm−2 in a two‐electrode cell, demonstrating excellent durability for overall water splitting.

articles.title: Resolving the Electro‐Mechanical Trade‐Off at the Buried Interface of Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are essential in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) due to superior electrical properties, yet their inherent rigidity imposes severe mechanical stress on the perovskite layer. Herein, we construct an interfacial architecture featuring discontinuous metal‐oxide islands to circumvent this fundamental electro‐mechanical trade‐off at the buried contact. Specifically, this discontinuous topography imparts macroscopic structural flexibility to the interface by functioning as localized strain‑relaxation zones, enabling strain‐relaxed perovskite films with reduced defect density. Meanwhile, the modified interface maintains unimpeded hole‐selective pathways and optimal energy level alignment. Consequently, the corresponding PSC yields a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.92% (certified 26.60%) with enhanced long‐term stability. This strategy establishes a rational design principle for synergistic electro‐mechanical management, paving the way for high‐efficiency and stable photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: Siloxane‐Mediated Dual Cross‐Linking for Thermally Resilient and Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The practical application of perovskite solar cells (PerSCs) is still limited by their intrinsic instability, particularly under dynamic temperature fluctuations in outdoor conditions. In this study, we present a series of dual cross‐linking agents to improve the efficiency and temperature endurance of PerSCs. Specifically, 3‐(trichlorosilyl)propyl methacrylate (MPTCl) with multiple functional groups is applied to modify the upper interface of the perovskite. The ─C═O group exhibits strong interactions with the undercoordinated Pb2+ on the perovskite surface, helping to stabilize structures and reduce interfacial charge recombination. The C═C bond of the methacrylate group undergoes in situ polymerization/cross‐linking, while the trichlorosilyl group undergoes hydrolysis and subsequent condensation under humid conditions, enabling MPTCl to form a Si─O─Si cross‐linked network. This cross‐linked interfacial layer improves interfacial structural stability and enhances resistance to moisture‐ and heat‐induced degradation. Consequently, the optimal PerSCs achieved a high power conversion efficiency of 26.22% and demonstrated enhanced thermal durability under simulated thermal cycling conditions, retaining 82.4% of their initial efficiency after 250 cycles. This work proposes a dual cross‐linking strategy that provides an effective route for simultaneously improving the efficiency and thermal resilience of PerSCs, offering valuable insights into the development of durable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.

articles.title: Synergetic Regulation of Enthalpy‐Entropy via Dipole Interactions Enabling Textured and Low‐Temperature Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) suffer from severe H2O‐induced parasitic reactions and uneven Zn deposition, especially at sub‐zero temperatures. Herein, we propose a hydrated eutectic high‐entropy electrolyte based on Zn(ClO4)2, ethylene glycol, 1,5‐pentanediol, and H2O, which couples a configurationally diverse bulk solvation environment with spatially differentiated interfacial regulation through synergistic enthalpy–entropy effects. Diversified solvation configurations promote the formation of an organic‐rich gradient hybrid solid electrolyte interphase, while enriched dipole–dipole interactions suppress H2O activity and strengthened ion‐dipole interactions provide kinetic buffering for Zn2+ supply. Such coupled solvation and interfacial regulation enables interfacial deposition kinetics to be balanced with bulk ion migration, thereby homogenizing interfacial Zn2+ flux, alleviating concentration polarization, and inhibiting dendritic growth. Moreover, preferential interfacial adsorption of organic species promotes the exposure of the Zn(002) plane, inducing thermodynamically favorable Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells operate for over 2000 h at 25°C and over 3000 h at −20°C. Zn||PANI pouch cells achieve capacity retentions of 91.32% after 1200 cycles at 25°C and 98.65% after 2000 cycles at −20°C, while full cells cycle stably for 500 cycles at −50°C with negligible capacity decay. These findings highlight synergistic enthalpic‐entropic regulation as an effective strategy for developing durable wide‐temperature AZIBs.

articles.title: Tunneling‐Gated Metalized Plastic Current Collectors Enabling Autonomous and Reversible Thermal Shutdown in Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Thermal runaway has constrained the application of high‑energy‑density batteries. Metalized plastic current collectors (MPCCs) offer a promising approach to reducing inactive mass and improving mechanical safety, yet they remain intrinsically passive and provide no active response to thermal abuse. Here, we propose tunneling‑gated thermoresponsive MPCCs (TTMP), which transforms conventional MPCCs from passive conductors into autonomous, self‑protecting components. The TTMP integrates a polyethylene matrix and embedded spiky carbon conductive particles, sandwiched between ultrathin aluminum layers on both surfaces. Upon heating above 100°C, thermal expansion of the polymer disrupts electron tunneling between adjacent spiky carbon particles, sharply suppressing electrical conduction through the TTMP, thereby interrupting current flow and delaying thermally accelerated electrochemical reactions under abuse conditions. When returns to room temperature, electron transport is fully restored, and the battery resumes normal operation. During thermal triggering, the resistance of the TTMP increases from 6.3 Ω to 2.1 × 105 Ω within a response time of 4 s. Cells equipped with this collector show a reversible reduction in discharge current of up to 92.5%. Furthermore, 1 Ah pouch cells achieve up to 6 cycles of reversible thermal shutdown with complete performance recovery, while the onset of thermal runaway is delayed by up to 30°C.

articles.title: Water‐Mediated Proton Facilitation for Stable Acidic CO2 Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 conversion in acid can, in principle, maximize carbon efficiency but is typically undermined by facile hydrogen evolution. Moreover, operating at high current density often triggers a sharp local pH increase that propagates into the bulk electrolyte, causing an overall pH shift that erodes nominally “acidic CO2 reduction” toward neutral/alkaline conditions. To address these limitations, we incorporated Ce species with high proton affinity into the surface of porous Cu nanosheet, constructing proton‐mitigating Cu─O─Ce active sites. Beyond conventional C─C coupling driven by local *CO accumulation, Cu─O─Ce motifs accelerate *CO formation and its protonation, thereby enabling downhill proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) toward and beyond *CO─*CHO dimerization. This strategy demonstrates efficient multi‐carbon generation under retentive pH conditions minimizing the collateral deficiencies of acidic CO2 reduction. Facilitating kinetically suppressed C─C coupling at a relatively low current density offers a strategic catalyst design that maintains a stable bulk pH compared to high current density operations, thereby maximizing the in situ generation of CO2 within the acidic media.

articles.title: “Lithium‐Free” Anode Solid‐State Batteries Enabled by 3D Structured Miec Garnet
articles.abstract: Inhomogeneous lithium nucleation at the current collector‐solid electrolyte interface leads to unstable lithium growth and poor reversibility in “lithium‐free” solid‐state batteries. Here we show that stable lithium formation occurs within a mixed ionic and electronic conducting (MIEC) garnet scaffold. The intrinsic electronic conductivity of the porous framework enables lithium to nucleate uniformly along internal pore surfaces, rapidly forming a conformal lithium coating, thus establishing electronic connectivity at very low lithium volume fraction. This uniform lithium formation dramatically lowers anode impedance, enabling reversible lithium plating and stripping with Coulombic efficiencies of a previously unheard‐of 99.95%. When paired with NMC811 cathodes, bilayer (MIEC(P)‐LLZ(D)) “lithium‐free” full cells exhibit stable, highly reversible cycling at practical current densities, all at room temperature with no applied pressure. The interplay between lithium volume fraction and impedance is quantitatively modeled, transforming the understanding of lithium nucleation in a “lithium‐free” cell from an empirical interface problem to a percolation‐governed transport process, guiding the design of electronically percolating scaffolds for next‐generation solid‐state batteries.

articles.title: A Water‐Repellent‐Zincophilic Molecular Strategy for Concurrent Solvation and Interfacial Regulation toward Highly Reversible Zinc Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries are promising for grid‐scale energy storage but suffer from severe anode issues, including dendrite growth and water‐induced side reactions. Herein, an organic molecule, N,N,N’,N’‐Tetrakis(2‐hydroxyethyl)adipamide (THEA), is used to implement a “water‐repellent‐zincophilic” strategy for synergistically regulating both the electrolyte and the electrode interface. Its flexible hydrophobic backbone and multiple zincophilic hydroxyl groups enable multi‐site functionality. In the electrolyte, THEA coordinates with Zn2+ to reconstruct the primary solvation sheath, displacing water, and reducing its activity. At the anode interface, it chemically adsorbs to form an organic interfacial layer. This layer effectively repels water to mitigate parasitic reactions while guiding Zn2+ flux toward the dense (002) plane deposition. Consequently, cells employing THEA achieve exceptional stability: Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 5550 h (0.5 mA cm−2, 0.5 mAh cm−2); Zn||β‐MnO2 cells retain 81.3% capacity after 1000 cycles (1 A g−1) and 60.5% capacity after 3000 cycles at 2 A g−1. Furthermore, THEA effectively suppresses ice crystallization at subzero temperatures, enabling stable Zn anode operation at −8°C. This work integrates solvation control with interfacial engineering, offering an effective pathway toward durable, high‐performance aqueous zinc batteries.

articles.title: Applications of Atomic Catalyst Platforms in Electrochemical Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: The electrochemical oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is cornerstone reaction used for sustainable energy‐related devices. However, its sluggish reaction kinetics, stemming from the complex four‐electron transfer mechanism, pose a critical bottleneck, which drives the pursuit of high‑efficiency catalytic materials. Atomic catalysts are currently regarded as highly compelling electrocatalytic platforms for tackling this challenge, garnering tremendous research attention originating from their definite active sites, high metal‑atom usage, and exceptional selectivity. This review outlines the recent advances of atomic catalysts for OER electrocatalysis. To begin with, the microstructure regulation of atomic catalysts is systematically presented from three aspects: metal centers, support carriers, and metal‐support interaction. Furthermore, OER mechanisms are summarized, and the electrocatalytic OER behaviors of atom‑dispersed systems, namely single‐atom catalysts (SACs), dual‐atom catalysts (DACs), multi‐atom catalysts (MACs), and atomic array catalysts (AACs), are elaborated. The intrinsic structure‐activity correlation is comprehensively analyzed with illustrative examples. Following that, the application potentials of atomic catalysts in OER‐relevant electrochemical energy devices exemplified by water electrolyzers and metal‐air batteries are discussed. In the final section, the existing bottlenecks and prospective research orientations for atomic catalysts toward OER are proposed.

articles.title: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase‐Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
articles.abstract: Coupling phase‐change buffering with passive radiative cooling offers complementary continuous and transient regulation for personal thermal management (PTM). In fibrous systems, however, repeated phase transitions drive molecular rearrangement and thermomechanical stress accumulation, causing fiber deformation, pore collapse, and irreversible deterioration of radiative cooling performance. Herein, inspired by graded stress transfer in mussel byssus, we develop a homologous gradient interphase strategy to construct a core–gradient interphase–shell fibrous membrane (Ho‐GIFM) for durable PTM. During coaxial electrospinning, homologous polyethylene glycol‐based polyurethanes interdiffuse and entangle across the interface, while in situ UV crosslinking stabilizes the interphase. This structure redistributes phase‐change‐induced strain and constrains long‐range chain rearrangement, preserving phase‐change functionality and porous fiber networks. Ho‐GIFM exhibits a broad solid‐solid phase‐transition window (30.2–51.5°C) with a competitive melting enthalpy (60.2 J g−1). Notably, after 100 alternating thermal shocks between −40 and 80°C, Ho‐GIFM retains 99.0% of its initial solar reflectance versus only 74.5% for the heterogeneous counterpart, together with 99.9% mid‐infrared emissivity retention. Furthermore, it delivers a calculated daytime net radiative cooling power of 101.9 W m−2 and achieves an average synthetic‐skin temperature reduction of 14.9°C. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for durable PTM and multicomponent functional fibers.

articles.title: Biomimetic Hybrid‐Membrane Nanoreactor for Deep‐Seated Photodynamic Immunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Dual Catalysis‐Enhanced ROS Amplification and cGAS‐STING Activation
articles.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is promising against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its efficacy against deep-seated HCC is severely restricted by limited light penetration, intratumoral hypoxia, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity. Here, we developed a highly integrated biomimetic self-oxygenating nanoreactor UCNP@MnOx-Hyp@HRM (denoted UMHM). Coated with a Hepa1-6 tumor cell/red blood cell fused hybrid membrane, UMHM achieves homologous tumor targeting and immune evasion, ensuring effective nanoparticle accumulation in deep-seated tumors. The manganese oxide shell catalyzes H2O2 decomposition for in situ oxygen generation to mitigate hypoxia and improve upconversion nanoparticle-mediated PDT outcomes, while PDT/CDT synergistically amplifies oxidative stress and induces immunogenic cell death (ICD). Crucially, cytoplasmic double-stranded DNA released by ICD acts synergistically with Mn2 + to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. In concert with ICD, this signaling pathway facilitates dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte recruitment, as well as remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In vivo, UMHM achieved an 86.4% tumor growth inhibition rate in a large-volume subcutaneous HCC model and effectively suppressed tumor progression in an orthotopic HCC model. Furthermore, UMHM induced a marked abscopal effect, inhibiting the growth of distant tumors and lung metastases. This study provides a novel and multifunctional synergistic strategy for photodynamic immunotherapy of deep-seated solid tumors.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Rigid‐Flexible Synergistic Nanofibrous Textiles for Mechanically Robust Radiative Cooling
articles.abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) textiles offer an efficient pathway for personal thermal management. However, the inherent conflict between optical performance and mechanical robustness remains a formidable challenge. Although elastomer-based electrospun nonwovens serve as a potential solution, they typically necessitate high nano-filler loading for sufficient reflectance, which inevitably weakens interfacial bonding, leading to performance degradation and even structural failure during cyclic deformation. Herein, inspired by spider silk, we propose a filler-free biomimetic rigid-flexible synergy strategy regulated by dynamic hydrogen bonding. Via coaxial electrospinning, a robust TPU@PVDF-HFP film (RTPF) comprising a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) core and a polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene (PVDF-HFP) sheath is engineered. The RTPF demonstrates outstanding mechanical strength (10.17 MPa) and elongation (301.34%), exhibiting superior mechanical and spectral stability with a mere 10.53% residual strain and 1.58% degradation after 1000 cycles at 30% strain. Attributed to high solar reflectance (96.2%) and long-wave infrared emittance (92.5%), the RTPF achieves an average/maximum temperature reduction of 21.3/25.4°C on uncovered heated-pad under 950 W·m− 2 irradiation. Remarkably, it exhibits exceptional stability against rigorous washing and extreme environments (high/low temperatures and acid/alkali conditions). This bioinspired design achieves a synergistic enhancement of optical performance and mechanical robustness, paving the way for long-term wearable cooling materials.

articles.title: Challenge‐Routed Reconfiguration in Multidimensional Black Phosphorus Physical Unclonable Functions for Replay‐Resistant Hardware Authentication
articles.abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) provide hardware‐level authentication by converting uncontrollable physical variations into device‐specific challenge‐response pairs. However, conventional PUFs often rely on fixed responses, making exposed responses vulnerable to reuse and replay, while expansion of the challenge space may require additional devices or increased readout complexity. Here, roll‐printed black phosphorus (BP) is introduced as a self‐active multimodal entropy source that intrinsically combines infrared emission, electrical conduction, and strong in‐plane anisotropy. Random variations in layered position, thickness, orientation, overlap, and connectivity generate spatial, spectral, orientation, and percolation disorder. Four polarization‐resolved photoluminescence (PL) intensities and the PL full width at half maximum (FWHM) form a 125‐bit optical authentication response pool, while the electrical PUF provides conductance‐rank‐based routing rules for challenge‐dependent response assembly. Across the optical response channels, the mean inter‐Hamming distance (HD) reaches 0.500 for FWHM, the mean intra‐HD reaches 0 for PL‐YY, the mean bit uniformity reaches 0.500 for PL‐XX, and the mean Shannon entropy reaches 0.985 for PL‐YX. Challenge‐routed responses exhibit a mean inter‐challenge Hamming distance of 0.472, which has been unattainable in conventional PUFs with fixed responses. Server‐issued electrical challenges generate session‐specific response arrangements, enabling replayed responses from previous sessions to be rejected and establishing replay‐resistant, multi‐session hardware authentication.

articles.title: Closed‑Loop Recycling of Gallium‑Based Liquid Metals for Sustainable Soft Electronics
articles.abstract: Gallium‐based room‐temperature liquid metals (RTLMs) are widely used in soft electronics, yet their high fluidity and oxide‐mediated adhesion can generate persistent residues, complicating recovery and reuse. Here, we establish a Stage‐State‐guided closed‐loop recycling framework for externally accessible Ga‐based RTLM residues, in which contamination morphology (Stage) and LM–substrate interfacial condition (State) are independently classified to guide cleaning and recovery. A carbonate–surfactant cleanser (CSC) provides complementary interfacial regulation: the alkaline component promotes oxide‐regulated LM retraction, whereas the surfactant enhances interfacial mobility and de‐adhesion; strongly oxidized residues are further addressed through a particle‐assisted removal mode. The same CSC chemical system and Stage–State decision framework were validated for both EGaIn and Galinstan across representative substrate‐interface states without alloy‐specific chemical reformulation. A single CSC batch retained comparable functional performance over 20 consecutive reuse cycles, while recovered EGaIn maintained electrical functionality under strains up to 500% and continuous electrical responses over 5000 deformation cycles. A YOLOv11‐based vision module provides stage recognition, with true‐positive rates of 0.96, 0.97, and 0.83 for Stages I‐III, respectively, and practical recognition under variable illumination. Recovered LM was demonstrated in a soft‐electronic device, supporting a practical material‐level framework for cleaning, recovery, and reuse of externally accessible Ga‐based liquid metals.

articles.title: Dichloro‐Functionalized Urea Additive for Crystal Regulation in Stable Perovskite Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Developing passivators that deliver multi‐mechanistic synergistic effects constitutes a highly efficacious strategy for crystallization regulation, while simultaneously serving as a critical approach to bolster the long‐term operational stability of perovskite solar cells. In this work, a series of amine‐derived functional additives was rationally engineered and systematically evaluated via molecular design strategy to precisely regulate both the substitution pattern and the chlorine atoms count. Notably, the dichloro‐substituted derivative 1‐(3,4‐dichlorophenyl)‐3‐(pyridin‐4‐yl)urea (DCLPU) demonstrates exceptional coordination passivation capability, an effect predominantly ascribed to the significantly enhanced electronegativity of its carbonyl group. This modification markedly reduces the perovskite crystallization rate and directs the preferential orientation of the perovskite (100) crystal facet. Furthermore, DCLPU suppresses non‑radiative recombination losses and weakens electron‑phonon coupling via energy level modulation. Consequently, the inverted device incorporating DCLPU attained a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.32% (certified: 26.91%), alongside a corresponding module efficiency of 22.50%. These devices further exhibited outstanding thermal stability, ultraviolet resistance, and sustained operational durability. This work delineates a robust and practicable paradigm for advancing high‐efficiency, stable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.

articles.title: Domain‐Pinned Ferroelectric‐Like Fields Drive Deep Zn2+ Intercalation in Bi2TeO5
articles.abstract: Traditional MnO2‐ and V2O5‐based frameworks remain among the most widely studied cathode systems for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs), yet persistent structural instability and sluggish Zn2+ transport often result in severe polarization and capacity degradation during cycling. Herein, we report a domain‐pinned cathode platform based on Cr‐doped oxygen‐vacancy Bi2TeO5 (Cr‐OvBTO). The synergistic combination of Cr/Ov engineering and the stereochemically active lone‐pair electrons of Bi3+ and Te4+ reconstructs localized ferroelectric‐like fields associated with electrostatic heterogeneity and built‐in potential gradients. Consequently, a more stabilized local electrostatic environment is established, thereby enhancing lattice stability during cycling. Contact potential difference mapping and migration‐barrier calculations reveal a 77 mV built‐in potential gradient and a substantially reduced Zn2+ migration barrier from 0.75 to 0.34 eV, consistent with improved Zn2+ transport kinetics. As a result, Cr‐OvBTO delivers reversible deep‐intercalation behavior (∼360 mA h g−1) together with stable high‐rate cycling performance, retaining ∼77% capacity over 2000 cycles at 2 A g−1. More importantly, this work demonstrates that domain‐pinned ferroelectric‐like fields can transform deep Zn2+ intercalation from a kinetically constrained process into a reversible and sustainable transport pathway.

articles.title: Efficient Magnetization Switching Driven by Orbital Torque in Light 3d Transition‐Metal Nitrides
articles.abstract: The orbital Hall effect (OHE) in light transition metals offers a promising route to generate orbital torques for efficient magnetization control, providing an alternative to the conventional spin Hall effect approaches that rely on heavy metals. We demonstrate perpendicular magnetization switching in [Co/Pt] multilayers driven by the OHE in a light 3d transition metal nitride, VN, with a (111)‐textured face‐centered cubic structure. Second harmonic Hall measurements reveal a large torque efficiency of ~ –0.41 in the VN(7.5 nm)/[Co(0.35 nm)/Pt(0.3 nm)]3$_3$, which significantly surpasses those in the control samples with Co, Py, and CoFeB ferromagnets, suggesting strong conversion of orbital current originating from VN into spin current in the [Co/Pt]3$_3$ ferromagnet. Full switching by an in‐plane charge current is achieved in the presence of an in‐plane magnetic field, while partial field‐free switching occurs without it. The critical current density for switching is found to be comparable to that of a W‐based spin–orbit torque device. First‐principles calculations predict a large orbital Hall conductivity in VN, with a small spin Hall conductivity around the Fermi energy. Our results highlight the potential of combining light 3d transition metal nitrides and Co/Pt ferromagnetic multilayers with (111)‐texture to maximize the magnetization switching efficiency of orbitronic devices.

articles.title: Functional Siloxane Cross‐Linking Nodes in Thermoset Polymer Networks Enhance Mechanical Robustness and High‐Temperature Electrical Insulation
articles.abstract: In next‐generation power electronics and electrical systems, thermoset insulating polymers are required to simultaneously provide mechanical support and electrical insulation under extreme electrothermal conditions. However, conventional epoxy resins suffer from an inherent trade‐off between mechanical robustness and high‐temperature insulation. Herein, a nodal engineering strategy is proposed to construct multifunctional thermoset networks based on cyclic siloxane cross‐linking nodes. The siloxane nodes facilitate localized stress relaxation and homogenize the cross‐linked network, thereby enabling efficient energy dissipation while maintaining structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Meanwhile, the intensified local network constraints and homogenized chain distribution effectively decouple inter‐chain charge transport from thermally activated segmental motion. In addition, the nodal platform is further functionalized via highly efficient hydrosilylation. Fluorinated moieties are grafted onto the siloxane nodes to create localized energetic traps that suppress intra‐chain charge transport. Consequently, the resulting network simultaneously improves mechanical robustness and electrical insulation, significantly improving breakdown strength (295.09 kV mm−1 at 120°C, 92.27% increase), tensile strength (75.61 MPa, 29.85% increase), and fracture toughness (2.82 MPa m1/2, 57.54% increase). This study provides a new route for constructing high‐performance multifunctional polymer networks, showcasing the immense potential of functional siloxane cross‐linking nodes for high‐reliability insulation in extreme environments.

articles.title: Glutamine‐Modified Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles Deliver FGF18‐mRNA to Alleviate Cartilage Degeneration in Osteoarthritis
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by articular cartilage breakdown, metabolic disorder, and pain. Current therapies provide only symptomatic relief, while cartilage has limited intrinsic repair capacity. Here, we developed glutamine‐modified ionizable lipid nanoparticles (GLNP) for intra‐articular delivery of FGF18 mRNA. GLNP showed uniform particle size and a favorable polydispersity index, enabling complete RNA encapsulation and protection against degradation. Compared with unmodified lipid nanoparticles (LNP), GLNP achieved efficient lysosomal escape, deep cartilage penetration, and enhanced chondrocyte uptake. In vitro, GLNP‐mediated FGF18 mRNA delivery increased anabolic marker expression and reduced catabolic and senescence markers in chondrocytes, while glutamine release further enhanced metabolic synergy. In a surgically induced OA mouse model, intra‐articular GLNP‐FGF18 improved gait parameters and attenuated cartilage degeneration. It also suppressed synovial inflammation, reduced osteophyte formation, and preserved cartilage matrix integrity in both early and delayed intervention settings. Mechanistically, the therapeutic effect was associated with PRG4 upregulation, PI3K‐Akt‐mTOR signaling modulation, and autophagy restoration. Overall, GLNP‐FGF18 mRNA reversed chondrocyte catabolic and senescent phenotypes and restored joint homeostasis by combining cartilage penetration, chondrocyte affinity, and metabolic regulation, offering a promising synergistic gene therapy for OA.

articles.title: High‐Contrast, Dynamic Visible‐Infrared Regulator for Adaptive Multispectral and Multipixelated Camouflage
articles.abstract: Dynamic regulation of optical properties in visible (VIS) and infrared (IR) simultaneously is vital for camouflage, energy harvesting, information display, and thermal management. However, current approaches cannot achieve high-contrast, versatile modulation of visible colors and infrared emissivity concurrently, essential for emerging applications like adaptive camouflage in multiple scenarios. To address this challenge, here we develop a novel dynamic VIS-IR regulator based on the reversible metal electrodeposition (RMED) technology, whose reconfigurable nanoscale metallic layer, combined with judiciously designed photonic electrodes, permits real-time, precise control of excitation/annihilation of asymmetric lossy Fabry–Pérot resonances. As a result of this strategy, our regulator shows unprecedented performance, which can not only generate diverse structural colors with a large color gamut (∼33% sRGB area) and high color switching contrast (up to 83%), but also realize broadband, large-contrast IR emissivity modulation of Δε 3-14 µm∼0.68. We further demonstrate a highly-programmable multipixelated device, where each pixel can be controlled independently, enabling spatially adaptive multispectral camouflage and information display for the first time. This work offers a remarkably designable, exactly controllable, and highly scalable platform for multispectral dynamic optical regulation, with wide-ranging applications in adaptive camouflage systems, information encryption and optical skin.

articles.title: In Situ X‐Ray Scattering Reveals the Nucleation, Growth, and Self‐Assembly of CsBr Nanocrystals in a Heterogeneous Medium
articles.abstract: Understanding how nanocrystals form is central to the rational synthesis of nanomaterials, yet the formation mechanisms of ionic nanocrystals remain poorly resolved. Here, we use synchrotron‐based in situ small‐ and wide‐angle X‐ray scattering to track the formation and assembly of CsBr nanocrystals in solution. We find that the precursors spontaneously organize into dense clusters before reaction, generating a heterogeneous reaction medium that dictates the subsequent formation pathway. Following injection of Cs‐oleate, these clusters act as metastable precursor reservoirs that regulate precursor availability, thereby sustaining extended nucleation and promoting effective size focusing. At later stages, the same clusters function as depletants that drive the self‐assembly of CsBr nanocrystals into face‐centered cubic superlattices. These superlattices then undergo partial disassembly through Ostwald ripening, governed by the interplay between structural ordering and kinetic evolution. Together, our results identify multiple roles of precursor clusters during nanocrystal formation and assembly and provide mechanistic insights into ionic nanocrystal synthesis in heterogeneous media.

articles.title: Laminar Boundary Layer Mass Transport‐Guided Machine Learning for Precision Density Regulation of Horizontal Carbon Nanotube Arrays
articles.abstract: Horizontally aligned carbon nanotube (HACNT) arrays are essential building blocks for next-generation carbon electronics. However, precise control over the density of HACNT remains a formidable bottleneck due to the complex, nonlinear coupling of multi-physical parameters. To address this challenge, we propose a machine learning (ML) workflow that incorporates boundary layer fluid dynamics (BLFD). Conventional high-dimensional growth parameters are condensed into a concise feature space dominated by two physics-informed descriptors: mass transfer coefficient (Km ) and residence time (t). This kinetics-informed feature set significantly improves HACNT density prediction, increasing the coefficient of determination (R²) from 0.68 to 0.84. Consequently, 4200 virtual screenings map a global kinetic phase diagram, revealing an extremely narrow growth window for high-density HACNT that demands sufficient yet moderate carbon precursor supply combined with appropriate t. Subsequent validation experiments confirm the reliability of BLFD-informed ML model in HACNT density prediction and identifies the failure mechanisms, and demonstrates the capability to guide targeted growth of array with 120 tubes/µm. By uncovering the underlying kinetic mechanisms rather than merely fitting data, this BLFD-ML fusion framework would contribute to the HACNT synthetic paradigm shifting from empirical trial-and-error to a rational design process governed by fluid dynamics and reaction kinetics.

articles.title: Low‐Temperature Construction of Self‑Strengthening, Reusable, Ultralight Mullite Fiber Composites with Fish‑Scale‑Like Adaptive Boron‑Rich Layers
articles.abstract: Reusable thermal protection materials are prone to structural damage accumulation and performance degradation under cyclic thermomechanical loading. Overcoming the conventional “cycling equals damage” paradigm is a critical challenge for long‐term service. Here, we exploit low‐temperature ceramization of a boron‐rich precursor at 600°C to in situ construct a fish‐scale‐like adaptive ceramic reinforcement layer (ACRL) on mullite fiber surfaces and junctions. The composite exhibits remarkable thermomechanical‐cycling‐induced strengthening (TMCIS) during cyclic compression at 420°C, with the average modulus nearly tripling after 100 cycles. In situ SEM reveals that thermomechanical coupling drives local displacement of adjacent fiber segments and node reconstruction; the ACRL of viscous softening acts as a dynamic “high‐temperature solder” that bridges fiber contacts and reconfigures the load‐transfer network, enabling a service‐induced strengthening mechanism. After 50 cycles (totaling 25 h) at 420°C, the mass loss per cycle is only 0.07%. Furthermore, the material simultaneously achieves a low density (0.29–0.35 g/cm3), high compressive strength (1.60 MPa), and low thermal conductivity (0.062 W/(m·K)), realizing a synergy of lightweight, load‐bearing, and thermal insulation. This work converts cyclic loading from a damage source into a driving force for structural strengthening, establishing a new adaptive paradigm for long‐life reusable thermal protection materials.

articles.title: Manganese Nanoparticles Coupled with Adjacent Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Concerted Synergistic Amplification of the cGAS‐STING Pathway and Glioblastoma Immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma is a highly aggressive brain tumor whose profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) compromises the efficacy of conventional therapies and immunotherapy, while insufficient activation and inefficient agonist delivery limit antitumor potential of the cGAS‐STING pathway. Herein, we design a manganese nanoparticle/adjacent single‐atom nanozyme loaded with potent STING agonist diABZI, which is further camouflaged with homologous glioma cell membranes (MnAC/SA‐D@M) to enable efficient blood‐brain barrier penetration and precise GBM targeting. The electronic coupling between Mn10 ACs and neighboring Mn single‐atom sites optimizes the d‐electron density and charge distribution of Mn‐N4 catalytic centers, thereby drastically enhancing peroxidase‐like activity and facilitating tumor‐specific hydroxyl radical generation and glutathione depletion. Such robust catalytic oxidative stress triggers ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, accompanied by mitochondrial damage and subsequent cytoplasmic release of mitochondrial DNA, which potently activates the cGAS‐STING pathway. Meanwhile, released manganese ions (Mn2+) and co‐delivered diABZI sustain and amplify STING signaling, boosting the secretion of type I interferons and proinflammatory cytokines. This integrated cascade promotes dendritic cell maturation, repolarizes tumor‐associated macrophages to antitumor M1 phenotype, and augments cytotoxic T‐cell infiltration. Consequently, the immunosuppressive TME of glioblastoma is reversed, leading to enhanced antitumor immunotherapy in orthotopic tumor models, patient‐derived organoids, and postoperative tumor recurrence settings.

articles.title: Mechanism‐Guided Inverse Electrolyte Design for Advanced Metal‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The development of new electrolytes for metal‐ion batteries is currently constrained by the inefficiency of trial‐and‐error exploration across vast chemical spaces. Here, we establish a comprehensive framework for chemical descriptor‐based inverse electrolyte design that maps target electrolyte properties back to molecular, polymeric, and lattice‐level building blocks. By extracting fundamental chemical descriptors, we decompose electrolyte performance into electrochemical stability, ionic transport, electronic leakage, thermal safety, and lifecycle constraints, challenging classical frontier‐orbital (highest occupied molecular orbital/lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) criteria for electrochemical stability by accounting for the electron/hole addition perturbations and the critical role of interfacial effects. Addressing ion transport, we unify optimization strategies across phases, linking solvation structures in liquids and lattice defects in solids to minimize impedance via atomic‐level ion transport control. We decouple the origins of electronic leakage, distinguishing between structural‐defect‐induced pathways and parasitic redox transport. On safety, we trace thermal runaway to molecular thermodynamics. Integrating lifecycle constraints, we analyse how manufacturing defects and abuse conditions compromise these theoretical designs. Furthermore, to address the data‐scarcity bottleneck in data‐driven discovery, we propose the “Minimum Information for Electrolyte Studies and Cells” (MIESC) checklist and advocate systematic reporting of negative results to establish robust decision boundaries. This work thus provides a roadmap for rationally designing next‐generation electrolytes.

articles.title: Molecular Confinement‐Driven Programmable Multicolor Metal‐AIEgen Frameworks Combined With Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Sensitivity of Lateral Flow Immunoassay
articles.abstract: Fluorescent metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based sensing platforms have emerged as promising tools for bioanalysis. However, their limited optical outputs and insufficient information encoding capacity remain major challenges in complex matrices detection. Here, we develop an artificial intelligence (AI)‐interpretable sensing platform by integrating programmable multicolor aggregation‐induced emission metal frameworks (MAFs) with dual‐hue lateral flow immunoassay (DH‐LFIA) for intelligent detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa). A highly emissive MAF was constructed using an AIE‐active ligand (TCPE) and Hf4+ nodes. Additionally, donor‐acceptor interactions between TCPE and incorporated rhodamine B (RhB) enabled programmable multicolor emission through the Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) mechanism. The optimized MAFR‐6 probe was subsequently incorporated into the LFIA, achieving a detection limit of 10 CFU/mL for P. aeruginosa. Moreover, an inner filter effect (IFE)‐driven DH‐LFIA platform was established to convert bacterial concentrations into visible color transitions, providing a highly sensitive with a 100‐fold improvement over conventional gold nanoparticles‐based lateral flow immunoassay (AuNPs‐LFIA). Furthermore, integration with a convolutional neural network (CNN) enabled autonomous interpretation of color‐coded signals and achieved 100% classification accuracy for P. aeruginosa in human blood, overcoming the limitations of subjective visual analysis. Collectively, this study provides a new strategy for advancing pathogen detection toward automation, precision, and intelligence.

articles.title: Programming Film‐Formation Kinetics via Photoinduced Acceptor Oligomerization for Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Precise control over the solution-to-solid transition is essential for high-performance organic solar cells (OSCs), yet the rapid crystallization of Y-series acceptors severely narrows the morphology-optimization window. Here, we develop a photoresponsive thioctic acid-functionalized acceptor, L8-TA, whose photoinduced pre-oligomerization was systematically optimized to generate Oli-L8-TA prior to film formation. When used as a low-content third component in D18:L8-BO, Oli-L8-TA regulates host crystallization through favorable compatibility with L8-BO and steric confinement from the oligomeric structure, extending the crystallization window from 152 to 273 ms while enhancing molecular ordering. The optimized blend microstructure exhibits a favorable vertical phase distribution, contributing to improved charge transport and reduced recombination. Consequently, ternary devices achieve a PCE of 20.12% with a fill factor (FF) of 81.31%. Device stability is also enhanced, with extrapolated T 80 lifetimes extended from 490 to 905 h under continuous illumination and from 448 to 750 h at 65°C. These results demonstrate that photoinduced pre-oligomerization provides a direct molecular-state handle for programming host crystallization kinetics and optimizing active-layer morphology during the solution-to-solid transition in OSCs.

articles.title: Rational Design of Non‐Centrosymmetric Sn(II)‐Based Chalcogenides Exhibiting Superior Infrared Nonlinear Optical Performances
articles.abstract: Non‐centrosymmetric Sn(II)‐based chalcogenides hold great promise as infrared (IR) nonlinear optical (NLO) materials; however, their rational design and synthesis remain a substantial challenge due to the facile oxidation of Sn(II) to Sn(IV). Herein, by synergistically assembling Sn(II)/Pb(II) cations with GeS4 tetrahedra and MX6 (M═Pb, Sn, Na; X═Cl, Br) octahedral groups, two new Sn(II)‐chalcogenide IR NLO crystals, [Sn0.5Br3][Sn3GeS4] and [Na0.5Sn0.25Br3][Sn3GeS4], were successfully synthesized using a unique quenching‐reannealing method. Notably, they achieved 10‐ and 2–4‐fold enhancements in the SHG effect and birefringence, respectively, compared with their isostructural homolog, [Pb0.5Cl3][Pb3GeS4] (0.6 × AgGaS2, ∆n = 0.030). This unusual property disparity originates from the difference in stereochemical activity of lone pair electrons between Sn and Pb cations. Furthermore, owing to the property‐modulating effect of strongly electropositive Na+ cations, [Na0.5Sn0.25Br3][Sn3GeS4] exhibits a well‐balanced set of optical properties, including strong SHG effect (6.4 × AgGaS2), moderate birefringence (0.074), wide optical transparency range (0.47–12.5 µm), indicating it is a potential IR NLO materials. This work opens an avenue for the design of Sn (II)‐based IR NLO materials and the synthesis of metastable chalcogenides.

articles.title: Supramolecularly Anchored Skeleton‐Intrinsic Phase‐Change Monoliths Enabling Passive Thermal Homeostasis of Outdoor Electronics
articles.abstract: Mitigating extreme temperature fluctuations is critical for maintaining data integrity and preventing failure in outdoor electronics. However, durable passive thermal homeostasis for such electronics under fluctuating outdoor conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a skeleton‐intrinsic phase‐change monolith (SPCM) fabricated through supramolecular anchoring. A noncovalent supramolecular network robustly confines molten phase‐change domains within a load‐bearing skeleton, combining a high latent‐heat capacity of 125 J g−1 with an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.027 W m−1 K−1. The monolith retains 99% of its mass after 100 thermal cycles and remains leak‐free under 50% compressive strain. By integrating thermal insulation, latent‐heat buffering, and radiative heat dissipation, SPCM protects electronic devices against external thermal shocks. An SPCM‐packaged electronic device exhibits a temperature variation of less than 1.5°C when exposed to a 120°C heat source, compared with approximately 25°C for an unprotected device. The monolith also largely retains its phase‐change behavior, thermal insulation performance, and spectral selectivity after thermal cycling and environmental exposure, demonstrating stability under the tested harsh conditions. This work establishes a supramolecular skeleton‐engineering strategy for passive thermal management of electronics in fluctuating outdoor environments.

articles.title: Synergistic Modulation of Interfacial Energetics and Crystallization Kinetics for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long‐term stability of polycrystalline perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are fundamentally limited by bulk non‐radiative recombination and mismatched interfacial energy levels. To address these bottlenecks, we introduced 4,4’‐(2,1,3‐benzothiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)dibenzoic acid (BTBA) as a twisted molecular additive for regulating crystallization kinetics and interfacial energetics. With dual carboxylic acid groups and a rigid, non‐coplanar benzothiadiazole‐based backbone, BTBA coordinates with Pb‐based precursor during film formation, which retards the crystallization kinetics and yields films with enlarged grains. In addition, residual BTBA at the perovskite surface passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ defects and regulates the surface work function, which improves the energy‐level alignment with C60 and facilitates charge extraction. The resulting PSCs achieved a champion PCE of 27.16% (certified 27.14%) with a fill factor (FF) of 86.73%. Furthermore, the unencapsulated devices exhibited improved stability, retaining over 90% of their initial PCEs after 1200 h of maximum‐power‐point tracking (MPPT) under continuous 1‐sun illumination and after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C.

articles.title: Ultrasonically Engineered Low‐Coordination Mn Sites in Fe‐MOF Promote Charge Separation for Sacrificial‐Agent‐Free Photocatalytic N2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction involves complex proton‐coupled multi‐electron transfer processes, which bring about abundant reaction pathways and thus result in poorly controllable product selectivity. Benefiting from their unique electronic configuration and unsaturated coordination environment, single‐atom photocatalysts can effectively regulate the reaction pathways of photoreductive N2 activation and reduction, thereby improving the selectivity and NH3 productivity of target ammonia products. Herein, an acetate‐modified ultrasonication method is developed to construct atomically dispersed, coordinatively unsaturated Mn–N sites on Fe‐based metal–organic frameworks (FeMOFs). Distinct from traditional carbon‐based single‐atom catalysts, these Mn─N sites are fabricated via a mild wet‐chemistry approach without high‐temperature treatment. The optimized U‐FeMnMOF(Fe:Mn = 1:3) achieves a high NH3 productivity of 1823.1 µmol·g−1·h−1, 21.2 times that of pure FeMOF. Characterizations and DFT results verify that Mn─N sites not only activate N2 and optimize hydrogen adsorption, but also work as a charge transfer mediator to form a direct Z‐scheme heterojunction. This study presents a feasible strategy to synthesize non‐carbon M─N single‐atom catalysts for efficient PNRR.

articles.title: Water Rolls Off, Current Flows: The Rise of Conductive Superhydrophobic Textiles
articles.abstract: Conductive superhydrophobic textiles uniquely combine electrical conductivity with extreme water repellency, enabling humidity‐resistant wearable electronics, smart protective clothing, and self‐powered systems. This review systematically examines the design principles, fabrication strategies, and multifunctional applications of these materials, with a focus on the core interfacial coupling mechanism—water rolls off, current flows—that governs their performance. Key application domains are critically analyzed, with emphasis on how superhydrophobic protection enhances device stability under humid, sweaty, or rainy conditions. The review identifies fundamental bottlenecks—conductive network failure under deformation, poor durability of hydrophobic interfaces, and inherent trade‐offs between conductivity and water repellency—that currently limit practical deployment. A structured translation roadmap from laboratory design to scalable manufacturing is presented, incorporating the development workflow of discovery, design, fabrication, testing, validation, qualification, scaling, deployment, impact, and sustainability. Future directions, including stretchable self‐healing architectures, artificial intelligence (AI)‐guided inverse design, fluorine‐free sustainable manufacturing, and self‐powered wireless textile systems, are discussed with technical specificity. This review provides a unified framework connecting materials chemistry, textile engineering, and device physics, guiding researchers and engineers toward transforming these materials from laboratory prototypes to real‐world products that enhance human safety, comfort, and connectivity.

articles.title: Additives and Relaxation Fluidize Molecular Transport Within Covalent Adaptable Networks
articles.abstract: Incorporating dynamic covalent bonds into polymer networks could offer stimuli‐responsive control over molecular transport, often requiring additives to facilitate bond rearrangement. Here super‐resolution localization microscopy was employed to examine fluorescent probe transport in unhydrated, elastic networks containing thiol‐thioester dynamic covalent chemistry (DCC). In static, DCC‐free networks, displacement distributions revealed frequent trapping and slow, anomalous, and heterogeneous diffusion. Introducing a dynamic catalyst additive markedly increased mobile fraction and produced diffusivity that was more fluid‐like. These effects were observed with several classes of fluorescent probes, two distinct additives, and for networks with or without DCC. Experiments with a photo‐releasable catalyst (NPPOC‐TMG) separated additive effects from those of activated exchange. Catalyst release conferred additional fluidization of the network. Importantly, these changes were not accompanied by macroscopic plasticization, suggesting that small additive concentrations can strongly affect transport in confining environments. Spatial analysis further indicated that transport enhancement was primarily due to restructuring of an initially heterogeneous network rather than local bond exchange near the diffusing probes. Additive incorporation and post‐cure exchange likely reduced defects and homogenized the crosslink density. In sum, these results demonstrate how DCC modulates transport, emphasize the importance of the activation method, and highlight its potential in separation and controlled‐release systems.

articles.title: Crystallinity‐Governed Liquid Wettability and Mobility on Solid Surface
articles.abstract: Control over liquid wettability and droplet mobility is essential for several emerging applications including open microfluidics, anti-icing, self-cleaning, and heat transfer. Existing strategies generally rely on permanent chemical modification or continuous external stimuli to regulate droplet spreading, pinning, and sliding. Here, we report a unified approach for reconfiguring wettability states and droplet mobility by regulating crystalline packing of a semicrystalline polymer. A phase-transitioning polymer, poly(octadecyl acrylate) (PODAc), was incorporated into a porous polymeric coating, where melting and subsequent cooling pathways determine the extent of alkyl-chain crystallization and interfacial polar functionality. Cooling in air or underwater generates reversibly switchable hydrophilic (θ W ∼ 85°), hydrophobic (θ W ∼ 104°), and amphiphobic slippery states across liquids with surface tensions of 22–72 mN m−1. These distinct regimes enable programmable droplet spreading, pinning, and low-friction transport without post-synthetic chemical treatment or sustained external stimulation. Furthermore, reconfigurable wettability patterns enable guided liquid transport through spatially selective complete wetting or customized contact line frictional force.

articles.title: Engineering Topological Phases in Two‐Dimensional Materials: A Path from Preparation to Device Applications
articles.abstract: Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two‐dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase‐engineered material platforms.

articles.title: Flexible High‐Speed Low‐Noise Organic Photodiode Arrays for Dynamic Near‐Infrared Imaging
articles.abstract: Organic photodiodes (OPDs) hold significant promise for next‐generation IoT optical sensing and low‐power imaging applications. However, widespread application of OPD in flexible and dynamic imaging has been constrained by high dark current, poor stability, and the lack of a cost‐effective imaging system. In this work, we present an integrated solution through tailoring pseudo‐planar heterojunction (PPHJ) OPD arrays and a customized, rapidly accessible imaging system, the dynamic organic photonics imaging system (DOIS). The resulting PPHJ OPD exhibited a high responsivity (0.6 A W−1 at 868 nm), low dark current (1.5 × 10−8 A cm−2 at −1 V) and fast response time (480 ns), benefiting from optimal vertical phase separation and donor‐acceptor interface morphology. Moreover, flexible photodetector exhibits superior mechanical stability, photostability and storage stability. Crucially, a pixel‐shifting strategy was incorporated into conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) based machine learning algorithms to capture dynamic images and enhance resolution by leveraging sub‐pixel information sampling. This work demonstrates a significant potential for the extensive application of organic photovoltaic materials in image sensing and flexible electronics.

articles.title: Hydro‐Gated Photonic Actuators With Programmable Color and Shape
articles.abstract: Structural color actuators integrating visual readout with motion are prized for biomimicry, yet typically operate in a coupled, color‐gradient mode with limited freedom. Here we report a photonic liquid crystal network that decouples these responses via a scattering‐gated mechanism. The material hides its structural color in the dry state but, upon water uptake, simultaneously switches on vivid coloration and executes programmable three‐dimensional deformation. Crucially, we achieve stimulus‐selective control: ethanol turns on color without motion, while heat induces motion without color. This independent, on‐demand manipulation of optical and mechanical outputs offers a transformative platform for multi‐responsive soft robotics, adaptive camouflage, and smart displays.

articles.title: Lignin‐Based Supramolecular Dynamic Networks: A General Platform for Energy Harvesting and Sensing
articles.abstract: Lignin‐ based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio‐based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self‐healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.

articles.title: Nanoscale Thermal Imaging of Dislocation‐Mediated Heat Transport
articles.abstract: Dislocations are widely used to tailor lattice thermal conductivity in semiconductors and thermoelectrics, yet the local thermal resistance of individual buried dislocations and their spatial extent remain experimentally unresolved. Here, operando scanning transmission electron microscopy–electron energy-loss spectroscopy thermometry, atomic-resolution imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics are combined to map heat transport across a dislocation array within a 5°SrTiO3 low-angle grain boundary. The effective thermal conductance of the dislocation array is estimated to be ∼35.4 MW m− 2 K− 1 using the bulk reference conductivity, corresponding to a Kapitza length of ∼339 nm. Nanoscale temperature maps reveal a spatially heterogeneous resistance landscape: reconstructed dislocation cores act as sharp thermal bottlenecks over ∼2.14–5.17 nm, with steeper local temperature gradients than inter-core regions, whereas inter-core regions show weaker but more extended modulation over ∼8.34–11.57 nm. Correlative structural and vibrational analyses show that Ti─O bond distortion, Ti valence change, P4 optical-phonon blueshift, and reduced local–bulk phonon density-of-states overlap create a core-specific vibrational environment. These results uncover the underlying mechanism whereby atomic-scale core reconstruction generates nanoscale localized thermal resistance, and offer quantitative descriptors for defect-structure-guided thermal design.

articles.title: Orthogonal Passivation of Polar Facets for Efficient InSb Quantum Dot SWIR Photodetectors
articles.abstract: Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) offer a heavy‐metal‐free route to short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetection, but their performance still lags behind lead‐ and mercury‐based CQD systems, and the surface chemistry that limits their performance is not well understood. Here, we identify two independent oxide‐derived trap pathways on the polar terminations of zincblende InSb: oxidation of the In‐terminated {111}A and Sb‐terminated {111}B facets creates chemically distinct mid‐gap states, each of which degrades carrier transport. Density functional theory calculations show that metal halides bind strongly to Sb‐terminated facets, but weakly to In‐terminated facets, while thiolates show the opposite preference; this asymmetry leaves single‐ligand passivation incomplete.
