Resum Els vincles entre els elementomes de les plantes (és a dir, la concentració d'elements químics en els teixits vegetals) i els trets funcionals poden millorar les prediccions sobre el rendiment fisiològic de les plantes i els processos ecosistèmics, i com aquests responen als canvis ambientals. Els elementomes d'alta dimensionalitat, que inclouen no només macronutrients, sinó també micronutrients i elements traça, s'han associat amb diversos trets morfològics i fisiològics vegetals, però no amb trets fotosintètics. Hem determinat els elementomes (incloent 21 elements i les proporcions isotòpiques de C i N) de 26 espècies de briòfits higròfits (16 molses i 10 hepàtiques) presents a fonts mediterrànies, i n'hem analitzat la relació amb quatre trets de resposta fotosintètica a la llum: taxes fotosintètiques màximes, rendiment quàntic aparent, punt de compensació de la llum i taxes de respiració. Els resultats dels models lineals d'efectes mixtos mostren que els elementomes d'alta dimensionalitat estan fortament associats amb els trets fotosintètics i expliquen una proporció substancialment més gran de la variància (R 2 = 38%–61%; 72%–85% quan també s'hi inclou la informació taxonòmica) que els models basats únicament en C, N i P (R 2 = 6%–45% i 35%–72%, respectivament). La selecció de models i la mitjana ponderada de les estimacions revelen que cada tret fotosintètic es pot modelitzar de manera òptima mitjançant un conjunt de 8–13 variables elementals, que inclouen diversos macronutrients (p. ex., N, S, K), micronutrients (p. ex., Zn, Cu), elements traça (p. ex., Ni, Co) i proporcions isotòpiques (δ13C i δ15N). Demostrem que els elementomes vegetals permeten identificar factors clau de variació fotosintètica, la qual cosa se suma a l'evidència creixent de l'existència de vincles estrets entre els elementomes i diversos trets funcionals que sustenten el funcionament dels organismes i dels ecosistemes.…

articles.title: Invasive insects outperform their native counterparts
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Invasive alien species cause substantial ecological damage worldwide, driving biodiversity loss and negatively impacting human livelihoods. Although invasive insects have some of the most severe impacts, the traits associated with their invasiveness remain unclear. We conducted a meta‐analysis comparing phenotypic traits of matched, co‐occurring invasive and native insect pairs (sympatric congeners or confamilials) in the invaded range. In total, we compared 922 invasive‐native pairs using 1327 effect sizes from 182 studies. These pairs comprised 144 unique invasive insect species and 403 unique native species. We found that invasive insects generally have greater fecundity, shorter development times, faster population growth rates and enhanced foraging and competitive capabilities compared with their native counterparts. However, some of these patterns changed after excluding the two most data‐rich families (i.e. Coccinellidae and Formicidae), likely due to divergent evolutionary histories, life history strategies and selection pressures. This study represents the most comprehensive systematic comparison of trait differences between co‐occurring native and invasive insect species and highlights that a diverse array of traits can contribute to invasiveness. Moreover, our open‐access database of insect trait data will facilitate further research into the causes and consequences of insect invasions. articles.title: Out of the fire and into the frying pan: Hostile post‐fire thermal conditions reduce activity windows for reptiles
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Climate change and intensified fire regimes are reshaping ecosystems globally. Reptiles, as ectotherms, rely on microhabitat shelters to buffer against thermal extremes, yet the capacity of these shelters to persist or function following fire remains poorly understood. As heatwaves and fire regimes intensify under climate change, effective thermal buffering will become increasingly vital for reptile persistence. This study quantifies how fire alters the structure and thermal offset of key reptile refugia: spinifex (Triodia) tussocks, chenopod shrubs, and leaf‐litter mats, in the dune and swale habitats of South Australia's Murray Mallee. Using iButton data loggers deployed across four fire histories, we measured hourly microhabitat and adjacent ground temperatures, modelling thermal offset (Toffset) via mixed‐effects models. More recent fire histories were associated with less spinifex and leaf‐litter cover and more bare ground, although evidence for changes in individual shelter dimensions was mixed. Thermal buffering declined markedly in recently burnt sites, with long‐unburnt spinifex providing the greatest daytime protection from extreme ground temperatures. Structural properties such as tussock height and litter depth were associated with Toffset, supporting a relationship between shelter structure and thermal‐refuge quality. Comparisons with the thermal tolerance of spinifex‐obligate reptiles indicate that burnt habitats often exceed critical thermal limits, effectively eliminating usable refugia during heatwaves. These results demonstrate that fire‐driven structural simplification translates to weakened thermal refugia, with implications for species persistence under increasing heat extremes. Effective fire management in arid systems should, therefore, prioritise the protection and regeneration of long‐unburnt spinifex and litter habitats as critical microclimatic refuges. articles.title: Plant‐derived compounds to improve soil inoculation for restoration
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Restoring the soil microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important requirement for the success of ecosystem restoration. Soil inoculation can reintroduce the missing taxa, but its application is limited by the large amount of donor soil that is needed and by the poor persistence of the inoculants, because of habitat filtering, priority effects and the loss of plant–microbe feedbacks. Here we propose the metabolite‐inoculum approach, a framework that combines the chemical diversity of plants with soil inoculation, in order to improve the establishment, persistence and effectiveness of introduced microbial communities. In this framework, the chemical input is delivered as fresh and dead plant material, as extracts of this material or as purified compounds that are applied together with the inoculum, and not by adding or manipulating the living plant community. We first synthesize the evidence that plant metabolites, from both above‐ and below‐ground tissues, act as selective regulators of soil microbial composition and diversity. Building on this, we propose a framework for the selection of plant materials and metabolites at the species, tissue and compound levels, and we introduce the parallel concepts of core and keystone metabolites that are matched to their corresponding microbial groups. We then identify the main challenges of the approach, the mismatch in timescale, the non‐target effects and the feasibility, and we translate them into testable hypotheses. Finally, we discuss the contexts in which the approach is likely to work and the contexts in which it is not. In this way, we frame the metabolite‐inoculum approach as a research agenda through bridging chemical ecology and microbial ecology, offering a potential solution to reduce dependency on donor soil, improve inoculant effectiveness and accelerate the recovery of degraded soils toward desired ecosystem states. articles.title: Precipitation‐mediated asymmetric fitness consequences of nectar robbing in distylous Primula florindae
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Flowers with deep corollas are frequently associated with nectar robbing, a behaviour that often reduces pollen transfer and seed production. Robbing scars, however, may further affect plant reproductive success through rainwater entry into corolla tubes. In distylous species, the reciprocal positioning of stigmas and anthers in long‐ and short‐styled morphs may create unequal exposure to incoming water and thereby impose morph‐specific precipitation‐mediated fitness costs. We used 2‐year field manipulations in one focal population of distylous Primula florindae, manipulating nectar robbing in both years and additionally manipulating pollination success in a full‐factorial design in 2024, to investigate how robbing associated with rainwater affects female fitness and interacts with legitimate visitation to shape phenotypic selection on floral traits. We further combined precipitation data, floral trait measurements and behavioural observations of the dominant visitor Bombus kashmirensis to explore the ecological context associated with the observed shift from legitimate visitation to nectar robbing. Our manipulations revealed that robbing significantly reduced seed production independently of pollen limitation. This reduction was stronger in long‐styled plants, and the contrast between morphs was more pronounced in the wetter year, consistent with differential water exposure in pendant flowers: the long‐styled stigma lies below upward‐facing robbing holes, where water may accumulate and submerge it, whereas the short‐styled stigma lies deeper within the corolla tube but spatially above this accumulation zone. Furthermore, legitimate visitation and nectar robbing exerted complex, interactive selective pressures across floral traits, with illegitimate visitation driving accentuated, morph‐specific divergent selection on corolla length. However, neither type of visitation alone, nor both types combined, fully explained the net selection on this trait, suggesting additional selective agents. Observational evidence indicated that robbing onset was associated with elevated pre‐onset rainfall, unusually long corollas and greater foraging efficiency during secondary robbing, although these relationships remain inferential. In summary, our study provides experimental evidence that nectar robbing can turn floral damage into a precipitation‐mediated fitness cost, offering new insights into how nectar robbing affects plant fitness. More broadly, our results suggest that climatic factors can mediate plant–visitor interactions along the mutualism–antagonism continuum and contribute to context‐dependent adaptive trajectories. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 花冠筒较长的花往往更易发生盗蜜，而盗蜜通常会降低花粉转移效率和种子产量。然而，盗蜜留下的伤痕还可能通过使雨水进入花冠筒，进一步影响植物的繁殖成功。在二型花柱植物中，长、短花柱型的柱头和花药呈交互式雌雄异位排列，这种繁殖器官位置差异可能导致两种花型不同程度地暴露于进入花内的雨水中，进而产生花型特异性的降水介导适合度代价。 本研究以一个二型花柱巨伞钟报春(Primula florindae)群体为对象，开展了连续两年的野外操控实验:两年均操控盗蜜，2024年进一步采用全因子设计同时操控盗蜜和授粉成功，以检验与雨水进入相关的盗蜜如何影响雌性适合度，以及盗蜜如何与合法访花相互作用，共同塑造对花部性状的表型选择。我们还结合降水数据、花部性状测量以及优势访花者克什米尔熊蜂(Bombus kashmirensis)的行为观察，探讨所观察到的合法访花向盗蜜转变的生态背景。 操控实验表明，盗蜜显著降低了种子产量，且这一效应独立于花粉限制。种子产量的下降在长花柱型中更为显著，而且两种花型之间的差异在较湿年份更加明显，这与下垂花朵中两种花型对雨水的暴露差异一致:长花柱型的柱头位于朝上的盗蜜孔下方，雨水可能在此积聚并淹没柱头；短花柱型的柱头虽然位于花冠筒更深处，但在空间位置上高于这一积水区域。 此外，合法访花和盗蜜对多个花部性状施加了复杂且相互作用的选择压力，其中盗蜜进一步强化了针对花冠长度的花型特异性分化选择。然而，无论合法访花或盗蜜单独作用，还是二者共同作用，都不能完全解释该性状的净选择格局，表明可能还存在其他选择因子。 观察性证据表明，盗蜜的开始与盗蜜发生前较高的降雨量、异常偏长的花冠以及次级盗蜜过程中较高的觅食效率相关，但这些关系仍属于推断性证据。 总之，本研究提供了实验证据，表明盗蜜可将花部损伤转化为降水介导的适合度代价，从而为理解盗蜜如何影响植物适合度提供了新的视角。更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，气候因子能够介导植物—访花者相互作用在互利—拮抗连续谱上的表现，并可能影响情境依赖的适应性演化轨迹。

articles.title: Scaling temperature‐dependent dispersal rates to metacommunity dynamics: An experimental test
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Changes in community structure under shifting thermal regimes depend on how both local population dynamics and regional dispersal respond to temperature. Processes underlying dispersal, such as movement speed and demographic density dependence, are constrained by temperature‐dependent metabolic rates; however, the temperature dependence of population dispersal rate, and effects of this relationship on local and regional diversity patterns, have received little attention in the metabolic scaling literature. Here, we propose and experimentally test a framework that relates temperature effects on individual dispersal probability, to thermal performance curves (TPCs) for population dispersal rates, to colonization dynamics in metacommunities. Using multi‐patch well plate microcosms, we measured TPCs for dispersal rate in several naturally co‐occurring ciliate species at different monoculture densities and in polyculture metacommunities. In monoculture metapopulations, the functional form of dispersal thermal responses differed at low (a few individuals) versus high (carrying capacity) population densities, and the strength of density‐dependent effects on dispersal rates varied unimodally with temperature. This may suggest distinct temperature effects on the density‐independent (individual movement speed and dispersal probability) and density‐dependent (quorum‐sensing and resource competition) components of population dispersal rate. In polyculture metacommunities, interspecific variation in dispersal TPCs explained differences in colonization dynamics and diversity patterns across temperature treatments. Species' dispersal rate TPCs differed from their growth rate TPCs; as a result, species with higher dispersal thermal optima had higher‐than‐expected per capita population growth at the regional scale compared with predictions from standard growth TPCs measured in single‐patch monoculture. Together, these results suggest that ignoring temperature‐dependent dispersal can yield an incomplete understanding of biodiversity change in spatially structured systems exposed to warming. articles.title: The oxygen uptake capacity of freshwater fish evolves to favour hypoxia tolerance in lentic species but locomotion capacity in lotic species
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Oxygen supply capacity (α) is a physiological trait hypothesized to shape the metabolic niche and biogeography of aquatic breathers, yet how natural selection targets α remains unclear. Two key fitness‐related traits—locomotor ability and hypoxia tolerance—both depend on α, yet whether this shared physiological basis leads to a functional coupling between these traits, or instead allows them to evolve independently under habitat‐specific selection, remains an open question. We therefore hypothesized that divergent selection pressures across flow regimes decouple these two traits, leading to habitat‐specific associations between α and each trait. To test this hypothesis, we measured α, hypoxia tolerance and swimming performance in 32 freshwater fish species from lentic and lotic habitats. Our results showed that the relationship between α and each trait varied with habitat type: in lotic species, α was strongly associated with enhanced swimming performance, reflecting selection for supporting the high metabolic demands of prolonged locomotion; in lentic species, α was linked to improved hypoxia tolerance, driven by adaptations to function effectively under low oxygen tensions. Overall, these findings provide insights into the evolutionary lability of α and validate it as a highly flexible, fitness‐related trait shaped by habitat‐specific selection. This highlights the role of interactions between shared physiological foundations and habitat‐specific selection in driving trait divergence, thereby offering a broader framework for understanding how physiological flexibility promotes biodiversity across heterogeneous environments. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 供氧能力(α)被认为是塑造水生生物代谢生态位与生物地理格局的核心生理指标，但自然选择如何作用于该性状尚不明确。运动能力和低氧耐受能力作为两类关键的适应性功能性状，均依赖于α这一共同的生理基础。然而，这一共同生理基础究竟是促成两性状的功能耦合，还是在生境特异性选择压力下各自独立演化，目前仍缺乏清晰的认识。 本研究基于不同水流条件所施加的分异选择压力，提出假说:运动能力与低氧耐受能力可发生功能解耦，并预测α与两性状之间将呈现出生境依赖性的关联模式。为验证该假说，我们选取静水与流水生境中32种淡水鱼类为研究对象，系统测定了其运动能力、低氧耐受能力及供氧能力。 结果显示，α与两性状的关联模式具有明确的生境依赖性。在流水物种中，α与运动能力紧密关联，表现为支持其持续运动所需的高代谢输出；而在静水物种中，α则与提升低氧耐受能力密切关联，表现为其在低氧分压环境下仍维持生理稳态。 本研究揭示了α作为生理性状的进化可塑性，证明α是一高度灵活、受生境特异性选择所塑造的适应性性状。研究进一步阐明α与环境选择压力之间的交互作用驱动功能性状分化的演化机制，并为理解生理灵活性在异质环境背景下促进生物多样性的机制提供了理论框架。

articles.title: Tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐mediated feedbacks in subtropical forests
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The rhizosphere microbiome is critical for forest ecological functions, yet the mechanisms through which tree species identity and neighbour tree interactions are associated with its assembly remain poorly understood. Using Illumina MiSeq and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), we investigated how tree species (pine vs. liquidambar) and forest composition (pure vs. mixed) shape rhizosphere microbial communities and root metabolites in subtropical forests. Rhizosphere fungal community structure differed significantly across rhizosphere types, whereas bacterial community and metabolite profiles differed primarily between the pure pine forest and other forest types. Predicted functional shifts included a decline in cellulolytic bacteria (−27%) and an increase in denitrifying groups (+54%), with ectomycorrhizal fungi enriched in mixed than pure forests (p < 0.05). Metabolite profiling revealed that lipids, organic acids and sugars were the most abundant compound classes, with 55 metabolites differentially abundant between pure pine and mixed forest rhizospheres. Rhizosphere metabolite profiles were significantly correlated with microbial community structure (p < 0.05). Specific microbe–metabolite associations were identified; fatty acids positively correlated with oligotrophic bacteria (WPS‐2), sugars with denitrifiers (Reyranella) and dipeptides with the beneficial fungus Penicillium. These results demonstrate that tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐associated feedbacks, which correlate with soil nutrient cycling. This provides a mechanistic, function‐oriented framework for understanding plant–microbiome interaction and harnessing them to enhance ecosystem resilience. articles.title: When is the bait worth the risk? A mechanistic model of a compensatory ecological trap in seabirds
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Ecological traps occur when organisms preferentially select habitats that reduce fitness. In seabird–fishery systems, fishery‐derived trophic subsidies can increase foraging success, reinforce habitat preference and indirectly enhance reproductive output or recruitment, while bycatch simultaneously reduces survival. This subsidy–mortality coupling can generate a compensatory ecological trap when short‐term demographic benefits partly offset survival costs and obscure negative long‐term population consequences. We developed a spatially explicit, individual‐based model to evaluate how compensatory ecological traps emerge from the interplay among trophic subsidies, bycatch mortality and life‐history strategy. The model represented three seabird life‐history strategies—slow, intermediate and fast—and a trade‐off in which trophic subsidies increased energy intake and indirectly enhanced reproductive performance, whereas repeated use of subsidised risky cells increased mortality. Population responses were non‐linear and reflected the joint effects of subsidy level, mortality risk and life history. When mortality risk in subsidised cells was low, trophic subsidies increased population size, particularly in faster life‐history strategies. However, once mortality exceeded life‐history‐specific thresholds, subsidies continued to promote the use of risky areas, increasing exposure to trap mortality and shifting population responses from growth to decline or extinction. Short‐term improvements in reproductive performance sometimes produced transient population growth. Under equivalent behavioural, energetic and subsidy–mortality conditions, slow, albatross‐like life‐history strategies were most vulnerable in terms of long‐term persistence, whereas faster strategies were more resilient and better able to translate additional food intake into positive demographic responses. Trap configuration further modulated these outcomes: negative responses intensified when subsidised risky areas were larger or located in high‐energy habitat. Our results extend ecological‐trap theory by showing how immediate habitat benefits, such as enhanced foraging success, can generate trade‐offs among fitness components and alter trap outcomes across the slow–fast life‐history continuum. They also highlight the need to manage bycatch and trophic subsidies jointly, because their combined effects can reinforce maladaptive habitat selection, increase exposure to mortality and elevate extinction risk.
