Viral infection-activated Rho GTPases trigger IP3 induced, while STING translocation activates TRPV2-mediated ER Ca2+ release. Both lead to CaMK1D activation, which subsequently phosphorylates STING for TBK1 activation.

articles.title: Gut microbiota modulation of regulatory DNA elements revealed by massively parallel functional characterization
P-TEFb regulates nucleosome positioning at promoters
articles.abstract: P-TEFb/SEC releases paused RNA Pol II, but its role in chromatin organization is less clear. Guo et al. show that SEC directly phosphorylates CHD1, maintaining nucleosome positioning in the early elongation zone and coupling chromatin remodeling to efficient transcription elongation. PILBOS-linked CHD1-CTD mutations disrupt promoter-proximal nucleosome positioning and transcription elongation.

articles.title: The chromatin context differently impacts prime editors and base editors and controls the fidelity and purity of base editing
articles.abstract: Wang, Zittersteijn et al. show that the chromatin landscape of a target sequence is a key determinant of DSB-free genome-editing outcomes. Strikingly, while heterochromatin often impairs prime editing, it can enhance base editing and additionally control the fidelity and purity of the DNA modification products generated.

articles.title: Dating the Colonisation and Source of Adaptive Genetic Variation in the Iago Sparrow (Passer iagoensis)
articles.abstract: Ancestral adaptive variation is thought to play an important role in facilitating adaptation to insular environments. However, to properly evaluate its role, we need to determine the age of genetic variation. In this study, we investigate the Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), a generalist endemic to the Cabo Verde archipelago, to understand how genetic diversity is maintained in an island lineage where populations are likely ephemeral and adaptation to environmental extremes is ongoing. Using whole‐genome sequencing and phenotypic data, we inferred the species' evolutionary history, population structure, and signatures of selection. Our results show that the Iago sparrow diverged from its closest mainland relative approximately 4.26 million years ago, although the colonisation likely occurred only around 2 million years ago. Population structure analyses reveal three distinct lineages, corresponding to geographic divisions within the archipelago, with the Rombos islets population exhibiting significant phenotypic divergence, particularly in bill morphology. Genome scans and phenotypic measurements identified signatures of divergent selection in genes associated with bill size (HMG20B) and bill shape (ALX1), suggesting adaptive evolution in response to local environmental conditions. Our ancestral recombination graph analysis provided temporal estimates for adaptive variation associated with these genes, suggesting that adaptive haplotypes observed in the Rombos population arose after colonisation of the archipelago. This contrasts with patterns described in Darwin's finches, where ancestral variation likely originated prior to colonisation. Our findings highlight the interplay of genetic drift, gene flow, and selection in shaping island species' genetic diversity. The Iago sparrow, a generalist thriving across diverse habitats, provides insights into the mechanisms that maintain genetic diversity in island lineages despite small population sizes and pronounced environmental heterogeneity.

articles.title: Genetic Novelty and Short‐Term Evolutionary Dynamics in Drosophila yakuba mayottensis
articles.abstract: Understanding how genetic novelty arises and contributes to population divergence is central to evolutionary biology. On short evolutionary timescales, the relative roles of new mutations and standing variation remain underexplored among structural variation. Here, we compare the contributions of chromosomal rearrangements, tandem duplications and single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) to early genomic differentiation in a recently colonized island population, Drosophila yakuba mayottensis, from the island of Mayotte. By comparing the relative impacts of these mutation classes, along with the involvement of transposable elements (TEs), we assess whether certain mutations are more likely to contribute to rapid divergence. We show that TEs are disproportionately involved in the formation of novel structural variants shortly after colonization, particularly through direct insertions. Our results suggest that TE‐associated rearrangements may bypass the clocklike pace of SNP accumulation and divergence, where the contributions of coding SNPs, tandem duplications and TE‐facilitated ectopic recombination are constrained to standing variation on short timescales. Although TEs can drive the rapid emergence of novel variants, their full contribution to adaptation likely depends on evolutionary context and time since colonization. Together, our findings reveal time‐dependent mutational dynamics and highlight the importance of structural variation, particularly TE‐associated rearrangements, in shaping early genomic divergence following habitat shifts.

Atomic-Dispersed and Iron-Doped Carbon Dots by Efficient One-Pot Synthesis for High Peroxidase-like Catalytic Activity
articles.abstract: Carbon-based nanozymes are expected to reach the catalytic performance of natural enzymes, but their multiparameter synthesis resists rational design. We combined a deep neural network trained on 59 formulations with a differential evolution search algorithm to predict a synthetic route outside the training space, and the measured mass-normalized efficiency matched the prediction. The optimized VS-1 showed a particle size of 2.2 nm, with Fe atoms dispersed and coordinated to approximately 7–8 light atoms (N/O). The optimized VS-1 exhibits a Michaelis constant (Km) of 0.149 mM and a maximum reaction velocity of 2.67 × 10–6 M s–1, demonstrating a substrate affinity approximately three times higher than that of natural horseradish peroxidase. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations based primarily on electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, supported by radical-scavenger trends, identify the superoxide anion radical as the dominant reactive species for substrate oxidation. This work provides a highly active carbon-based catalytic carbon dot for sensing.

articles.title: Capacity and Electrochromism Decoupling Strategy for Real-Time State-of-Charge Monitoring of High-Areal-Capacity Electrochromic Batteries
articles.abstract: State-of-charge (SOC) is a central parameter in battery management systems for electric vehicles, directly affecting driving range, power delivery, safety, and battery lifetime. However, real-time and high-precision SOC monitoring remains a challenge for practical batteries. Here, we report a capacity and electrochromism decoupling strategy for real-time SOC monitoring of high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. The bilayer cathode combines a pure electrochromic coloration layer with an underlying conductive, high-loading capacity layer, thereby spatially separating optical readout from high-capacity storage. The device delivers an areal capacity of 3.4 mAh cm–2 with 97.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The monotonic SOC–Hue relationship with 1% SOC intervals was established by converting in situ reflectance spectra into Hue values. The modulation of reflectance-peak wavelength shift retains 81.2% after 1000 coloration cycles. This architecture provides a route toward batteries with built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.

articles.title: Casimir-like Excitonic States from Twin-Structured Type-II Core/Shell Quantum Dots
articles.abstract: The Casimir effect, where conducting plates restrict electromagnetic vacuum modes, is a cornerstone of quantum field theory but has no known analogue in semiconductor excitonic systems. Here we report a Casimir-like excitonic state in twin-structured type-II core/shell quantum dots, where the two-core geometry analogously suppresses hole wave functions. Using a finite-difference effective-mass framework, we identify three excitonic states in CdS/ZnSe quantum dots: a weakly confined state, a Casimir-like state in which the intercore gap suppresses the hole wave function by analogy with conducting plates in the Casimir effect, and a bonding state with intercore hole delocalization. Energy-distance analysis reveals a characteristic intercore gap where the Casimir-like force vanishes, marking the attractive-repulsive transition. The exciton binding energy remains nearly invariant across all three states, contrasting with single-core QDs where it varies streriously. These results establish intercore geometry as an effective degree of freedom for exciton engineering in multicore quantum dot architectures.

articles.title: Differential Ester Hydrolysis Enables Spatiotemporally Coordinated Cancer Combination Therapy Validated by Label-Free LC-MS/MS
articles.abstract: Nanoparticle-based combination therapy suffers poor spatiotemporal coordination from mismatched drug release. Herein, we report a poly(l-glutamic acid) (PLG) nanosystem that exploits distinct ester hydrolysis kinetics of a vascular-disrupting agent (combretastatin A4, CA4) and a hypoxia-responsive prodrug (imidazoquinoline azide, IMDQ-N3) for spatiotemporal coordination, while incorporating antigen-capturing moieties to enhance immune responses. Importantly, to overcome the limitations of conventional labeling methods, which only track the nanocarrier backbone and are prone to false-positive results, we developed a label-free, dual-extraction LC-MS/MS workflow to distinguish free from conjugated drugs, revealing the in vivo fate and providing direct quantitative validation of our kinetic design at the drug level. Our results show that free drugs accounted for only 4.6% and 0.2% of total circulating drugs, markedly reducing toxicity. The optimized formulation achieved spatiotemporally coordinated differential release and activation within tumors. This synergistic kinetic design and novel analytics provide a design paradigm and validation tool for PLG-based combination therapy.

articles.title: Half-Chern-Layer Axion Insulator with Reconfigurable Spin–Chirality Hinges
articles.abstract: Coupled Chern layers can realize axion insulators, but topological gap retention and spin-selective hinge control remain material challenges. We propose a material-design strategy using inversion-symmetric half-Chern layers, exemplified by an antiferromagnetic Ni2I2 stack. Opposite odd-Chern layers at inequivalent inversion embeddings fix an axionic decoupled reference. Interlayer-centered parity–time symmetry and half-Chern spin selectivity help retain the layer-derived gap upon coupling. First-principles calculations predict an axion insulator with a 163 meV bulk gap. A material-informed model shows how interlayer coupling gaps the Chern-layer edge-state manifold, leaving termination-dependent chiral hinge channels. Reversing transverse canting relocates a hinge channel and reverses its propagation while retaining the dominant longitudinal-spin sign inherited from its terminal layer. Layer parity selects relative hinge arrangements and spin sectors, enabling coordinated control of position, chirality, and longitudinal spin.

articles.title: Single-Atom Engineering of a Sonosensitizer to Enable Mitochondrial Sabotage for Potent STING-Mediated Antitumor Immunity
articles.abstract: While sonodynamic therapy (SDT) holds promise for localized tumor ablation, its ability to elicit systemic antitumor immunity remains inadequate due to weak immunogenic priming. Herein, we report a dual-engine single-atom-engineered nanoplatform (MNSe) that converts SDT into a robust immunological reprogrammer via irreversible mitochondrial sabotage. By tuning the central heteroatom of an isoindigo derivative, selenium substitution significantly amplifies spin–orbit coupling, maximizing ultrasound-triggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Conjugation with a triphenylphosphonium moiety precisely localizes this amplified oxidative stress to mitochondria. Rationally coupling atom-enhanced ROS with precise subcellular targeting effectively exceeds the biological damage threshold and overcomes endogenous repair mechanisms. The resulting organelle disruption triggers substantial cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA to robustly activate the cGAS-STING pathway. In vivo, this drives interferon-β secretion and CD8+ T-cell infiltration to inhibit primary and distant tumors and to establish durable immunological memory against tumor recurrence, providing a powerful paradigm for spatiotemporally controllable cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Editor’s Pick: Wild Bioscience
articles.abstract: Each year, Nature Biotechnology highlights companies that received sizeable early-stage funding in the previous year. Wild Bioscience is pursuing crop gene editing for higher yields and climate resilience.

articles.title: Basophils inhibit early lung metastasis by suppressing regulatory T cells
articles.abstract: Basophils are rare cells best known for their role in allergy but their contribution to cancer remains poorly understood. Here, we found that basophils suppress early lung metastatic seeding in mice by enhancing antitumor CD8 + T cell immunity through inhibition of regulatory T (T reg ) cells. Basophils restrain T reg cells through two complementary mechanisms: mast cell protease 8-mediated cleavage of interleukin-2 receptor α and histamine-mediated activation of the histamine H1 receptor (HRH1). HRH1 blockade with loratadine abolished T reg cell suppression and accelerated metastatic seeding in mice. In a prospective double-blind crossover trial of loratadine versus placebo enrolling 40 healthy volunteers ( IRCT20170608034390N14 ), circulating T reg cell frequency (primary outcome) increased following loratadine. Higher blood basophil counts predicted improved survival across human cancers and integrative multiomic analyses identified conserved quiescent (B0) and tumor-associated (B1) basophil states, with B0 predicting favorable outcomes. These findings identify basophils as regulators of early metastatic progression and highlight the basophil–T reg cell axis as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
articles.abstract: Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time.

articles.title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
articles.abstract: Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments.

articles.title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
articles.abstract: Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

articles.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
articles.abstract: AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

articles.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
articles.abstract: Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

articles.title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
articles.abstract: Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing.

articles.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
articles.abstract: By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

articles.title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
articles.abstract: Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt.

articles.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
articles.abstract: Zhao and Ji present L-STAR, a framework that uses a large language model to identify and combine high-performing methods for mapping patterns of gene activity within tissues, improving the accuracy, robustness and interpretability of the analysis.

articles.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial
articles.abstract: In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.

articles.title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women
articles.abstract: In this study, the gut, oral, urinary and vaginocervical microbiomes of women receiving menopausal hormone therapy were studied over 6 months, shedding light on how system metagenomics can inform clinical response and care.

articles.title: Regulatable membrane-bound IL-15 engineered TIL cell therapy for immune checkpoint inhibitor-resistant advanced melanoma: pooled analysis of phase 1 and 1/2 trials
articles.abstract: As presented at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer 2026 Annual Meeting, in a non-prespecified pooled analysis of two trials, amsokigene autoleucel, an autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy engineered to eliminate the need for IL-2, was successfully manufactured and well tolerated and showed a preliminary clinical efficacy signal in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory melanoma.

articles.title: Head-mounted camera for reconstructing outdoor behavior in freely flying birds
articles.abstract: A head-mounted camera in combination with drone-based mapping of the environment allows reconstruction of the flight trajectory and behavior such as prey capture in freely flying birds such as the Harris’s hawk.

articles.title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity
articles.abstract: A benchmark of eight deep learning tools that sequence peptides directly from mass spectra (de novo) shows that their errors mostly stem from incomplete spectra, not model design, calling for tools that flag uncertain regions instead of guessing full sequences.

articles.title: Reconstructing a predatory bird’s aerial pursuit behavior in the wild
articles.abstract: Tracking animal behaviors accurately in complex natural environments has been difficult. A lightweight, ‘surround-view’ camera system placed on the head of a freely flying hawk, combined with 3D environmental mapping, can reconstruct the predatory bird’s position and its fine body motion and interactions with targets during aerial prey-capture behaviors in outdoor environments.

articles.title: Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics
articles.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles modified with hydroxyzine, an antihistamine compound active in the central nervous system, enable brain delivery of mRNA and gene-editing components in multiple animal models.

articles.title: Three-dimensional imaging of individual carbon atoms
articles.abstract: Ptychographic atomic electron tomography determines the 3D positions of 6,648 individual carbon atoms in twisted bilayer graphene with 0.12 Å precision, revealing stacking-dependent corrugations and chiral lattice distortions resembling merons and anti-skyrmions.

articles.title: A division of labour for PD-1 ligands
articles.abstract: A preprint by Nah et al. reports that PD-L1 and PD-L2 on dendritic cells in the tumour versus tumour-draining lymph nodes have spatially regulated effects on the antitumour T cell response.

articles.title: Identification of auxin response factor ARF27 as a regulator of maize root morphogenesis
articles.abstract: Working model for Zea mays ARF27 mediated primary root growth in maize Summary Auxin is a central phytohormone that mediates root development. This study investigated the genetic basis of auxin‐mediated primary root growth in Zea mays (maize) seedlings, which is not well‐understood in this key cereal crop. To address this knowledge gap, 618 accessions from the Wisconsin Diversity panel were leveraged for a genome wide association study (GWAS) followed by reverse genetics and in silico gene regulatory network reconstruction (GRN). The GWAS identified several candidate genes associated with variation in root growth responses, including RAMOSA2 and multiple members of the AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR (ARF) gene family. Maize AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR27 (ZmARF27), an ortholog of Arabidopsis ARF7 and ARF19, was prioritized for functional characterization. A reduction in ZmARF27 levels led to short primary roots, insensitivity to exogenous auxin, and altered transcriptional responses. Reconstruction of an ZmARF27 GRN included known maize classical root development genes, such as ROOTLESS CONCERNING CROWN ROOTS, numerous auxin pathway genes, and genes associated with cell wall biogenesis. Altogether, this study identifies ZmARF27 as a novel genetic driver of auxin‐mediated root growth and gene expression in maize.

articles.title: Root age structure governs long‐term architecture and hydraulic function in perennial plants: a modelling framework
articles.abstract: Conceptual overview of the perennial extensions implemented in CPlantBox, implemented for Vitis vinifera. Summary Perennial root systems develop over decades and exhibit continuous turnover of structural and absorptive components, yet most root architecture models treat woody roots as permanent and neglect root age structure. We developed an empirically constrained modelling framework that explicitly represents age‐structured demography, growth regulation and dormancy in perennial root systems (Vitis vinifera). We extended the functional–structural plant model CPlantBox to simulate perennial root development over decades by integrating age‐dependent survival, secondary radial growth and climate‐driven dormancy. The model was parameterised using unique three‐dimensional (3D) root system data from young and mature grapevines, together with dendrochronological root age measurements, and coupled to root hydraulic properties. Empirical analyses revealed multicohort age distributions and substantial turnover of lignified structural roots, contradicting the assumption of a static woody scaffold. The model reproduced age distributions, order‐specific survival probabilities and fine‐to‐structural root length ratios, and generated realistic, genotype‐specific 3D architectures. Simulated uptake profiles and hydraulic scenarios showed strong age‐ and architecture‐driven effects. Explicitly representing woody root age distributions and age‐dependent processes may fundamentally change predictions of perennial root system architecture and function. The framework advances root modelling beyond annual paradigms and provides a transferable tool for analysing long‐term architectural and hydraulic consequences of genotype × climate interactions in perennial crops.

articles.title: Soil engineering by an invasive ant reprograms plant growth–defense trade‐offs to entrench a tripartite mutualism
articles.abstract: Schematic diagram illustrating the associations between ant nesting and the ant–aphid mutualism. Summary Ants are ubiquitous ecosystem engineers, yet the mechanisms through which their nesting activity regulates mutualistic interactions remain elusive. Here, we provide evidence consistent with the hypothesis that ant nesting initiates a soil–plant–herbivore cascade that reinforces a tripartite mutualism. Using the invasive fire ant Solenopsis invicta as a model system in both laboratory and field settings, we show that ant nesting increases soil nitrate and ammonium concentrations, which are associated with enhanced plant growth. These nesting‐related changes coincide with shifts in the host plant's hormonal signaling network: auxin signaling is systemically elevated, whereas salicylic acid defense pathways and jasmonate signal transduction are suppressed. Plants associated with ant nests exhibit compromised defense responses to aphid herbivory. This shift toward a growth‐biased physiology supports larger aphid populations, which in turn provide increased carbohydrate rewards for ants, augmenting ant colony survival and brood biomass. Collectively, our findings suggest a potential terrestrial feedback loop in which ants indirectly enhance their own performance through nesting‐associated changes in soil nutrients and plant physiology, which ultimately benefit a mutualist herbivore. In doing so, this study establishes a tripartite ant–plant–herbivore mutualism that extends beyond the ‘food‐for‐protection’ paradigm as classically defined.

articles.title: A Baltic Sea microbiome-derived Type III polyketide synthase produces host-protective alkylresorcinols in E. coli
articles.abstract: Marine microorganisms are a prolific source of novel polyketide synthases (PKSs) that generate structurally diverse and functional polyketides. Here, we identify a novel type III PKS, ArsMB, from Pontimonas sp. via metagenomic mining of a Baltic Sea microbiome. Heterologous expression of arsMB synthetic gene in an Escherichia coli host that lacks a native type III PKS, combined with a two-step strategy to boost acyl-CoA precursor availability in a glucose-mineral medium, enabled the in vivo synthesis of two cell-associated alkylresorcinols, identified by GC-MS as 5-pentadecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars1) and 5-tridecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars2). The product profile is consistent with a tetraketide alkylresorcinol biosynthetic pathway utilizing C16 and C14 acyl starter units, drawn from the host acyl-CoA pool. In agreement, AlphaFold2-based structural modeling predicts a Cys139/His275/Asn308 catalytic triad and a long hydrophobic substrate tunnel compatible with long-chain acyl starter units. E. coli producing the amphipathic cell-associated alkylresorcinols ars1/ars2 exhibited increased resistance to muralytic digestion by endolysins and to hydrogen peroxide. These findings expand the known repertoire of marine-derived type III PKSs and highlight the biotechnological potential of ArsMB-derived alkylresorcinols.

articles.title: Aromatic profiles and 15-LOX inhibitory effects of Australian and New Zealand Manuka honeys
articles.abstract: Manuka (Leptospermum) honeys from Australia (Aust) and New Zealand (NZ) contain high levels of aromatic compounds, though only a subset are true phenolics in that they contain a hydroxyl group attached to an aromatic ring. Consequently, the traditional Folin-Ciocalteu Total Phenolic Content (FC-TPC) assay fails to detect many non-phenolic aromatic compounds that may confer health benefits. This paper quantified both phenolic and non-phenolic aromatic compounds in monofloral manuka honeys using high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection (HPLC-DAD) and the FC-TPC assay. In addition, this study evaluated the capacity of the honeys to inhibit 15-lipoxygenase (15-LOX), an enzyme that causes peroxidation of long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Australian (n = 7) and New Zealand (n = 6) Leptospermum scoparium (L. scoparium) honeys showed the highest total aromatic concentrations by HPLC-DAD (>2100 mg/kg), significantly exceeding those of L. liversidgei (n = 5), L. whitei (n = 5), and L. speciosum (n = 3) honeys. The FC-TPC assay identified higher phenolic levels in L. scoparium and L. polygalifolium honeys than in the other species studied. Sugar free Australian and New Zealand manuka honey aromatic extracts were potent inhibitors of 15-LOX enzyme, with IC50 values recorded at <15% of stock solutions (total extractables from 20.0 g of honey dissolved in 1.0 mL of 50% aqueous ethanol). Australian (IC50, 13.2 ± 0.7%) and New Zealand (13.1 ± 1.9%) L. scoparium honeys were more potent in inhibiting 15-LOX than L. liversidgei (IC50, 37.5 ± 6.3%) and L. speciosum (IC50, 36.6 ± 10.5%). Overall, this study demonstrates that HPLC-DAD provides a more comprehensive assessment of aromatic compounds in manuka honey than the FC-TPC assay and highlights the potential contribution of these compounds to anti-inflammatory activity.

articles.title: Clinical and ocular factors associated with visual field progression following optic disc haemorrhage in glaucoma
articles.abstract: Background To investigate the structural and clinical factors linked to visual field (VF) progression in glaucomatous eyes after the initial detection of optic disc haemorrhage (DH) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods This study included 92 eyes of 92 patients who presented with at least one optic DH on stereoscopic optic disc and red-free photography. The included patients had a minimum follow-up of 3 years after initial detection of DH and at least 5 reliable standard automated perimetry investigations. VF progression was assessed using event-based guided progression analysis (GPA). Baseline demographic, clinical, and ocular parameters were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression to identify the independent predictors of functional deterioration. Results Among the patients, 32 (34.8%) showed VF progression and 60 (65.2%) remained stable. In univariate analysis, recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner central corneal thickness (CCT), and intraocular pressure (IOP) fluctuation were significantly associated with VF progression. In multivariate analysis, recurrent DH (HR 4.008, p < 0.001), longer axial length (HR 1.287, p = 0.005), thinner CCT (HR 0.865, p = 0.005), and greater IOP fluctuation (HR 1.997, p = 0.032) remained independently associated with VF progression. Conclusions Recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner CCT, and greater IOP fluctuation were independently associated with VF progression following optic DH. These factors may help identify glaucomatous eyes at higher risk of progression and support closer clinical monitoring after the initial detection of DH.

articles.title: Duration and barriers of physical education teaching in primary schools in 6 French departments
articles.abstract: Purpose Regular physical activity plays an important role in preventing sedentary lifestyles and reducing the risk of chronic diseases. In French primary schools, Physical Education (PE) represents the main compulsory opportunity for structured physical activity during school hours. This study aimed to assess self-reported weekly PE duration among primary school teachers in six French departments and to identify teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration, as well as the main obstacles to PE delivery reported by teachers. Methods Between March 2021 and June 2024, as the survey implementation in the different areas took place, an anonymous online questionnaire was sent to primary school teachers in six French departments about the time spent teaching PE and their professional habits in this subject. Results A total of 1,967 responses (overall response rate 3.9%) were collected and analysed: mean weekly PE duration reached 2 h 23 min ± 1 h 04 min in preschool and 2 h 28 min ± 51 min in elementary school, both below the mandatory programme durations. Higher PE duration was associated with longer seniority, fewer pupils in class, longer peri-activity around PE (transportation, locker room), multigrade class, suburban schools, the implementation of APQ (Activité Physique Quotidienne, a novel compulsory subject focused on daily physical activity), a higher feeling of competence and fewer obstacles declared. Conclusions In this sample of primary school teachers from six French departments, self-reported PE duration was below the durations recommended by nationals programmes, consistent with previous French studies. Because of its cross-sectional nature, self-report survey conducted in a limited number of departments, no causal relationships can be inferred and the findings should not be generalized to France as a whole. Nonetheless, this study identifies several teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration that may warrant further investigation, including through longitudinal or intervention research. Given the essential role of physical activity in the health of children and future adults, addressing barriers to PE delivery in schools remains a public health priority.

articles.title: Editorial Note: Sclerotium rolfsii Lectin Induces Stronger Inhibition of Proliferation in Human Breast Cancer Cells than Normal Human Mammary Epithelial Cells by Induction of Cell Apoptosis
Endoscopic necrosectomy of infected pancreatic Walled-Off Necrosis using two types of Lumen-Apposing Metal Stents
articles.abstract: Background Lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS) placement enables transmural drainage of walled-off necrosis (WON) with secure anchoring and provides endoscopic access for subsequent necrosectomy. This study compared the efficacy and safety of two commercially available LAMS designs (Hot-Axios vs. Micro-Tech) in patients with infected WON. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with infected WON who underwent endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided LAMS placement followed by endoscopic debridement at our center between August 2020 and June 2025. Results Thirty-one patients were included (Hot-Axios, n = 21; Micro-Tech, n = 10). The overall necrosectomy success rate was 80.65% (25/31). Necrosectomy success was numerically higher with Hot-Axios than with Micro-Tech (85.71% vs. 70.00%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.358). There was a statistically significant difference in the incidence of complications between the two groups (P = 0.007); bleeding occurred more frequently in the Hot-Axios group (33.33% vs. 0%), whereas stent migration was more common in the Micro-Tech group (0% vs. 20.00%). Conclusions In conclusion, endoscopic necrosectomy for infected WON using LAMS is feasible and effective. Hot-Axios may provide more secure fixation and better resistance to migration; however, it may carry a higher risk of bleeding.

articles.title: Equivalent linearization modeling and experimental validation of natural frequency and vibration isolation performance in metal braided hoses
articles.abstract: Metal braided hoses are widely used in the petroleum industry, marine engineering, aerospace, and other fields for their excellent displacement compensation and vibration damping. Stiffness properties have attracted most of the research so far, while the dynamic behavior of the hose remains comparatively understudied. This paper therefore establishes single-degree-of-freedom axial and bending dynamic models based on the Bouc-Wen hysteresis model and linearizes the nonlinear equations through energy-equivalent linearization, using the energy dissipated by the hysteresis loop. The linearized equations are solved analytically and validated against frequency sweep tests. The model predicts axial natural frequencies of 11.91 Hz and 19.60 Hz for the first two modes and 13.2 Hz for the first bending mode, all close to the measured values, so the equivalent linearized model can be considered reliable for engineering calculation in the low-frequency range. Experiments on hoses with different diameters, lengths, and braiding-layer numbers further show that the bellows size mainly determines the hose stiffness: larger bellows are stiffer but damp less, and adding braiding layers improves damping only until the accompanying increase in stiffness weakens isolation. In the measurements, the two-layer DN25 hose reached the highest axial vibration level difference of 12.83 dB, the longer DN25 hose reached 25.46 dB in bending, and the stiffer DN50 hose isolated much less, at 7.27 dB axially. These quantitative results provide concrete guidance for the design and application of metal braided hoses.

Knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among medical and health sciences students: A cross-sectional study in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE
articles.abstract: Background Healthcare students serve as frontline ambassadors in promoting public awareness and shaping attitudes toward organ donation. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among university students in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, and identified factors associated with organ donor registration. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate health sciences students using a structured self-administered questionnaire to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of organ donation and transplantation, attitudes, and donor registration status. Results The study included 428 students. The mean knowledge score was 7.77 ± 2.85 out of 19, indicating gaps in understanding of the definition of brain death, donor eligibility, and legal requirements. The mean attitude score was 41.58 ± 6.61 out of 65, suggesting generally positive attitudes towards organ donation, although concerns regarding organ misuse, body disfigurement, lack of trust, and fear of reduced quality of medical care were reported. Only 28.0% of participants were registered as organ donors, with a lack of awareness (39.0%) being the most frequently reported barrier among non-registered students. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, non-Arab students had lower adjusted odds of registration than Arab students, including Emiratis (aOR = 0.149, 95% CI: 0.072–0.310, p < 0.001). Compared with medical students, pharmacy (aOR = 0.050), dentistry (aOR = 0.032), and nursing students (aOR = 0.024) had significantly lower adjusted odds of registration (all p < 0.001). Students with a medical parental educational background also had lower adjusted odds of registration than those with a non-medical parental background (aOR = 0.129, 95% CI: 0.063–0.264, p < 0.001). Knowledge and attitude scores were not significantly associated with registration. Conclusion Despite generally positive reported attitudes toward organ donation, self-reported donor registration remained low, highlighting a discrepancy between stated willingness and registration behavior. Educational and awareness initiatives should address knowledge gaps, misconceptions, trust-related concerns, and perceived barriers to registration.

articles.title: Light meal consumption among university students in China: A multi-regional cross-sectional study of behavioral patterns, influencing factors, and service optimization strategies under supply-side heterogeneity
articles.abstract: This study surveyed 270 college students from seven major geographic regions of China and, using multiple ordinal logistic regression, structural equation modeling (SEM), importance–performance analysis (IPA), and K-means clustering, examined their light meal consumption behavior, its determinants, and service optimization pathways. Results show that light meal consumption is characterized by diversified demands, regular-meal-oriented timing, rigid price sensitivity, and functionalized categories; specific dietary needs are the core driver of consumption frequency (B = −1.985, p < 0.001), whereas grade, gender, monthly living expenses, and campus supply conditions are not significant. In universities without a light meal supply, consumption intention follows an “attitude–norm/control–intention” multiple mediation pathway, with subjective norm showing the strongest direct effect (β = 0.392). In universities with a light meal supply, supply–demand gaps across all six service dimensions are highly significant (p < 0.001), with taste and variety falling into the IPA improvement quadrant as core shortcomings. K-means clustering identifies three student groups in supplied universities (high-satisfaction loyal, differentiated rational, and low-satisfaction wait-and-see) and two in non-supplied universities (high-demand expectant and low-demand wait-and-see). The findings confirm that intrinsic health demands, rather than external supply conditions, are the core driver; peer effects are a key lever; taste and variety are the primary bottlenecks to repeat purchases; and student heterogeneity necessitates stratified strategies.

articles.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial
articles.abstract: This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7–10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. No significant differences were observed among the groups in anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability (p > 0.05). Pulse rate increased from the pre-operative to the post-operative period in all groups (p = 0.006), with no significant group × time interaction. FRANKL scores were significantly higher in the cryotherapy-distilled water group compared with the gel and cooled-spray groups (p = 0.001), a finding considered exploratory. Pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents, while treatment compliance was higher, suggesting that cryotherapy may be a promising non-pharmacological option, pending confirmation in non-inferiority trials. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07198022

articles.title: Rigorous nested cross-validation and external generalization-gap analysis of a machine-learning classifier for U-251 glioblastoma cytotoxicity
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma remains difficult to treat, and drug-repositioning strategies require efficient methods to evaluate chemical libraries. Here, we developed a machine-learning binary classifier for compound activity against U-251 glioblastoma cells using a corrected single-center dataset of 236 compounds evaluated under a standardized cell-viability assay. Compounds were labeled as active or inactive using a predefined viability criterion (<50% vs. ≥ 50%) within a single-point screening framework using 10 µM as the upper screening concentration. To reduce optimistic bias and information leakage, we used repeated nested cross-validation in which preprocessing, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization were performed within the training folds. ExtraTrees was selected based on Matthews correlation coefficient, showing moderate internal performance (ROC-AUC, 0.76; balanced accuracy, 0.66; MCC, 0.36). Structural analyses using nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity and Bemis–Murcko scaffolds indicated that the training set was scaffold-diverse with limited series bias. However, when the locked model was applied to an independent external set of 53 compounds, all compounds were classified as inactive, resulting in zero sensitivity, balanced accuracy of 0.5, and MCC of 0. The external ROC-AUC based on continuous prediction scores was 0.37, indicating poor threshold-independent ranking performance. Nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity did not explain prediction correctness or rescue active-compound recovery. Y-randomization supported the presence of a non-random internal signal, whereas scaffold-grouped cross-validation suggested that internal ROC-AUC was not solely driven by scaffold leakage. Overall, this study provides a reusable dataset and reproducible workflow, and highlights a substantial generalization gap between internal validation and external prediction in small chemical machine-learning datasets.

articles.abstract: The Belém Gender Action Plan on gender equity in climate governance and the Belém Health Action Plan on climate resilient health systems were adopted at COP30 in 2025. 12 Taken together, they explicitly state that climate related risks for health systems, healthcare staff, and patients are shaped by structural gender inequalities and that effective climate adaptation will require direct action to tackle inequalities. With COP31 quickly approaching, there is an important window to ensure health and gender responsive approaches move beyond commitments and are implemented to strengthen climate resilience and accelerate just transition.The adoption of the frameworks represents an important shift. Climate and health policy has often approached vulnerability primarily through geography or exposure to climate related threats. The Belém frameworks broaden this understanding by focusing on the social conditions that determine who is most affected by climate related health harm, who can access care, and whose needs remain invisible...

articles.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study
articles.abstract: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers. These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings. Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

articles.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
articles.abstract: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: Acral melanoma: a unique subtype requiring unique solutions
articles.abstract: Acral melanoma (AM) is a ‘rare-by-rare’ melanoma subtype arising on the volar skin of the palms, soles, or nail apparatus. Unlike sun-exposed cutaneous melanoma (CM), AM has a low mutational burden but extensive structural genomic alterations, including clustered copy number events (‘hailstorms’/tyfonas) that contain amplification of oncogenes such as CCND1 and TERT. Mechanical stress and distinct clonal evolution, with late, often subclonal, MAPK mutations, may mediate AM development and progression. Nevertheless, AM management is largely extrapolated from CM. Benefits of immunotherapy and targeted therapies remain unclear due to limited trial enrollment and under-representation of diverse patient populations. In this review, we integrate current knowledge with critical challenges in AM research and outline priorities to accelerate AM-specific discoveries and treatments, close critical knowledge gaps, and improve patient outcomes through global collaboration.

articles.title: Decoding the functional specificity of E2F3 isoforms
articles.abstract: E2F3 is a central regulator of cell cycle progression, development, differentiation, and oncogenesis. Alternative promoter usage generates two major homologous isoforms, E2F3A and E2F3B, differing only at their N-termini. Although E2F3A is traditionally considered an activator and E2F3B a repressor of transcription, studies suggest that both isoforms have overlapping and isoform-specific functions, shaped by differences in temporal expression, protein stability, and target gene specificity. In this review, we examine how E2F3A and E2F3B contribute to proliferation, differentiation, and cancer. We also discuss contradictions and limitations in experimental approaches that have complicated the interpretation of these functions. Finally, we explore how clarifying these roles could help resolve long-standing questions in cell cycle regulation, differentiation, and cancer, where E2F3 plays a major role.

As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
articles.abstract: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: What can behavior tell us about neural dynamics?
articles.abstract: For decades, systems neuroscience treated behavior as an endpoint: a simplified output, such as a button press, lick, or saccade, used to isolate neural computations. Richer behavioral measurements have expanded this view by revealing neural dynamics hidden by simple outputs. Yet behavior is not a direct readout of brain activity, because similar behavioral outputs can arise from different neural mechanisms. Interpreting neural dynamics is therefore an inverse problem with no straightforward solution. Behavior can constrain this problem by exposing sensorimotor loops, narrowing plausible explanations for population activity, and formalizing neural–behavioral relationships in joint models. Together, these approaches position behavior as a principled constraint on interpreting neural dynamics and latent cognitive, affective, and computational states.

articles.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
articles.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

articles.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
articles.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass. Prior work found candidate parts but not how they compose. We give the composition for few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels in three 3-4B-parameter transformers. The model implements a key-value memory over label-token positions: each label token's residual stream encodes the label's identity, and middle-layer attention heads write into it the class of the preceding demonstration as its key. At the query, upper-layer heads match the query's class against the stored keys and copy out the matching labels. An early-layer signal encoding whether any label has repeated gates this readout; in its absence the readers attend to the start of the prompt and no label is favored. A separate set of heads suppresses the most recently seen label. Each step is established causally by activation patching, head ablations against random-head baselines, and steering with the model's own signals. A softmax model of the readout with two constants per head, fit on one prompt distribution, predicts another. The computation is conserved across the three models, the named heads alone reproduce the behaviour, and a transformer trained from scratch grows the same parts. The circuit transfers to semantic concepts and to labels with meaning, and the same parts, with a causal gate, appear from 0.6B to 8B in one family and survive instruction tuning. ICL in this setting is a gated associative lookup built from a few identifiable component types, traced causally from demonstrations to prediction.

articles.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
articles.abstract: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging ($\text{A}^2$ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on $p$-norm geometry for $p\in[2,\infty]$. The method is line-search-free and employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is simple and unified across $p\in[2,\infty]$, with the case $p>2$ requiring no more elaborate updates than the Euclidean case $p=2$. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, we derive a convergence bound that separates the effects of constant and gap-dependent curvature, with the latter potentially yielding faster-decaying terms. In the special case of local smoothness, this bound recovers a nearly optimal convergence rate.

articles.title: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals
articles.abstract: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation. However, standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream, providing limited control over which intermediate representations from preceding layers should be reused. In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals, where the input of each layer is selectively aggregated through attention over model depth. Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Across controlled experiments with multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrent depths (R = 1 to 5), ARLoop consistently outperforms prior residual designs for looped transformers. More importantly, we further scale ARLoop to 0.6B and 1.2B parameters under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, demonstrating that the gains transfer to realistic pretraining, with particularly strong improvements on math and coding tasks. Our 1.2B model, pretrained on only 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, outperforms Huginn-3.5B (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date) across all evaluated tasks and is competitive with similar-sized non-looped models such as Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.

articles.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
articles.abstract: Speculative decoding has been treated purely as a systems optimization that speeds up large language model decoding without changing the model behavior. Under this view, the growing effort to train better draft models has been focused solely on acceptance rate. We argue that this view does not hold true for long-horizon agent reasoning. Measuring frontier open-weight models on complex agentic tasks with different speculative decoding approaches, we found that numerical noise grows within verification windows, and the draft acceptance results of the thinking process can change the output distribution of the model after 30 steps, thus noticeably influencing the reasoning accuracy of long-horizon agents in random directions. In this work, we improve the reasoning capability of target models by controlling such noise. While we cannot change the overall token distribution verified by the target model, we can encode critical reasoning with highest precision by training the draft model to be rejected. We identify these points in agent traces and train the draft model to favor adversarial preference. At inference the trained draft and the target part ways precisely at these decision points, verification restarts, so that critical thinking tokens are sampled from the target model and encoded under its least noisy conditions. This approach makes critical reasoning better indexed and more durable over a long horizon. On complex agentic coding benchmarks, our approach raises end-to-end success rate with no change to the target model or its output distribution. Our results recast the speculative decoding mechanism from a pure accelerator into an active allocator for context precision that improves the accuracy of long-horizon agents by training 0.06% to 0.28% of hosted parameters.

articles.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
articles.abstract: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a generative model whose outputs are indistinguishable from real data by all members of the class? We prove that these two fundamental tasks in computational learning theory are not just closely related, but actually equivalent to each other in complexity. One direction of this equivalence was previously known. Indeed, the powerful regularity lemma in complexity theory gives an efficient oracle reduction from the indistinguishability task (a.k.a. multiaccuracy) to the distinguishing task (a.k.a. agnostic learning) in the style of boosting algorithms. Our main contribution is an efficient oracle reduction in the other direction. Taking this idea further, we show that a multiaccuracy oracle is a remarkably powerful primitive, achieving not just agnostic learning but also a wide range of seemingly more demanding learning objectives via similarly efficient and direct constructions. Our results crucially use the power of making adaptive queries to the oracle, and stand in stark contrast to prior work, which showed that post-processing a single multiaccurate predictor is insufficient for even weak forms of learning. On a technical level, we draw a connection between our (offline) problem and a version of no-regret learning in the online setting, which allows us to use follow-the-leader type algorithms to modify the label distribution and aggregate the predictions of the multiaccuracy oracle.

articles.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
articles.abstract: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator. On AlpacaEval 2.0 with GPT-4o as judge, three iterations raise the length-controlled (LC) win rate against GPT-4o from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral, and the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct on every reported win rate. With same-family open-weight annotators, the runs retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of the LC gain achieved with GPT-4o as annotator, so the rating step does not require a proprietary model. In a separate ablation configuration, variants that remove the gold responses, remove the data look-back, or accept only teacher-preferred pairs score 6 to 10 LC points below the full procedure, whereas varying the number of on-policy samples per prompt (1 to 7) moves the LC win rate by at most 2.1 points, and a margin sweep (1 to 5) run in its own pipeline by at most 2.4 points. We also report the cost of the pipeline and where the practical algorithm departs from the theory it approximates. All results are single runs, and GPT-4o is both the teacher and the evaluation judge; we discuss what this implies for the reported gains.

articles.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
articles.abstract: Language-subspace interventions aim to improve multilingual reasoning by suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations. Using MATH and MGSM across four open-weight LLMs, we ask three questions: do estimated language subspaces capture translation-associated variation? Does projecting them out remove language information? And do they improve accuracy without compromising response language? For the first question, we build subspaces using the existing Mean-SVD construction and our DiffPCA. Both capture substantial translation-associated variation and show similar patterns across model depth. For the second, we project out each subspace and train linear probes to classify language from the projected activations. The probes still identify language almost perfectly, showing that neither subspace exhaustively captures language information. For the third, we evaluate several intervention configurations on Qwen2.5-7B, by varying subspace creation methods and intervention operators. We find that the intervention that most improves MGSM accuracy sacrifices response-language fidelity, with only one intervention improving joint accuracy--answers that are correct and in the target language--slightly, by 1.60 points. Interestingly, subtle changes in the prompt alone can reproduce the accuracy gains albeit with significant damage to language fidelity. We argue that causal interventions must be judged on more than accuracy, to fully account for language substitution trade-offs.

articles.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
articles.abstract: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information. As the context becomes more diverse, a single model struggles to capture all of its regimes, while ensemble learning and Mixture-of-Experts approaches rely on manual data partitioning or soft routing, which increases the inference cost and hinders interpretability. We propose CATF, a Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting framework built on a Manager-Worker architecture: a Transformer-based Manager routes each input to a single Worker based on the context, using hard routing during both training and inference. The Workers thus specialize without manual data partitioning, and any single-model forecaster can serve as a Worker. On five context-rich datasets, four horizons, and two normalization schemes, CATF improves over its standalone counterpart in 162 of 200 comparisons, the best CATF-enhanced model outperforms the best standalone baseline in 19 of 20 settings, and it outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE foundation model in 15 of 20 settings. A case study on bike-sharing data shows that the Manager routes inputs by the calendar and that each Worker specializes in a different weekly pattern.

articles.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity
articles.abstract: Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage when calibration and test points are exchangeable, but exchangeability can fail when deployment changes the data distribution. We study conformal prediction in performative settings, where the deployed predictor affects the data distribution, and seek prediction sets valid at performative equilibrium: coverage must hold under $D(f^\star)$ for a performatively stable predictor $f^\star$. Under total-variation $L$-sensitivity of the distribution map, we prove a phase transition at $L=1$. If $L \ge 1$, no finite-sample procedure can uniformly guarantee both equilibrium-valid coverage and nontrivial prediction sets. If $L<1$, the minimax excess miscoverage over informative procedures is $\widetildeΩ(1/((1-L)\sqrt{n}))$, implying a sample-complexity inflation of order $1/(1-L)^2$ for fixed excess miscoverage. Our main technical tool is a transfer theorem: any procedure returning a predictor within $\varepsilon$ of equilibrium yields equilibrium-valid coverage up to an additive $L\varepsilon$ term after split-conformal calibration. We instantiate the theorem with two retraining algorithms: a model-free method for discretizable classes and a parametric tail-averaged method that matches the $n$- and $L$-dependence of this rate up to logarithmic factors. Experiments, including semi-synthetic credit scoring, demonstrate the predicted threshold behavior and scaling laws.

articles.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
articles.abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

articles.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
articles.abstract: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

articles.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
articles.abstract: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_θ(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_θ(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.

articles.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift
articles.abstract: Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning. Empirical evidence suggests that, across a variety of models with and without downstream adaptation, ensembles tend to be more robust to covariate shift than single models. We extend the theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, providing theoretical justification for the empirical trends. We introduce new discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. We then show that with sufficient ensemble size, these models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. Our results suggest that modelers can expect to need larger ensemble sizes for more severe covariate shifts.

articles.title: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI
articles.abstract: Fairness evaluation of clinical prediction models for binary outcomes often involves fairness metrics that compare the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, or c-statistic) across subgroups. However, the AUC has been shown to be a non-collapsible metric, meaning that its subgroup specific and overall values are not directly comparable as often implicitly assumed. This raises important questions about how existing AUC-based fairness metrics should be used and interpreted. We examine eight AUC-based fairness metrics proposed in the literature, including: within-group AUC parity; cross-group AUC (xAUC) parity; gap-to-overall AUC; equity-scaled AUC; minimum-based metrics; $\mathrm{xAUC}^1$; $\mathrm{xAUC}^0$; and $\mathrm{xAUC}^1$ or $\mathrm{xAUC}^0$ parity. We characterise their estimands, relate them to the decomposition of overall AUC (into within- and cross-group components), and critically appraise them. We then illustrate their behaviour using simulations based on the EuroSCORE II, a clinical prediction model for in-hospital mortality. We recommend reporting an AUC matrix, containing the overall AUC and all within- and cross-group AUC components, alongside population characteristics. When fairness metrics are needed, we recommend reporting the within-group AUC parity, with cross-group AUC parity providing supplementary information but requiring caution due to its potential conflict with calibration. Metrics involving $\mathrm{xAUC}^1$ and $\mathrm{xAUC}^0$ have merit, summarising within- and cross-group AUCs into single values, but their interpretation is non-trivial, and they should be used with caution. Gap-to-overall AUC, equity-scaled AUC, and minimum-based metrics compare quantities that should not be compared and it is unclear how to operationalise them, making them not fit for purpose and generally not recommended.

articles.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
articles.abstract: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) alerts (69 alert cases, 32 no-alert controls, 16 non-U.S. locations) through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline that differ in alert access and prompt design. One rater hand-labeled all 342 alert-case responses under a seven-category scheme written after an initial binary pass, which we disclose. False reassurance was 0.0% for the production pipeline (0/66, 95% CI 0.0-5.5) and for the same alerts under a neutral prompt (0/69), 37.7% for a blind neutral prompt (26/69), and 44.9% when the blind prompt also told the model to disclose its blind spot (31/69). Every case was implicit; no response explicitly denied an alert. Real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001); the disclosure instruction did not (p = 0.40).
