Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
articles.abstract: High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH* deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol−1, and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm−2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm−2. These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

articles.title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
articles.abstract: Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM1‐O‐TM2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO4 (A2BO4) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

articles.title: Acoustic Levitation Engineered Au‐InSe Schottky Junctions for Single‐Molecule SERS Sensing
articles.abstract: Detecting single molecules with high sensitivity and specificity is of great scientific and practical interest. Surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is an ultrasensitive molecular detection technique for single‐molecule detection. However, the fabrication of ultrasensitive single‐molecule SERS substrates remains a key goal. Herein, we report an acoustic levitation assisted containerless strategy to construct InSe‐Au Schottky junctions with robust interfacial bonding, achieving single‐molecule detection of zeptomolar level and an EF of 1010. The controllable acoustic radiation pressure inside the levitated droplet induced robust interfacial coupling of InSe‐Au Schottky junctions, which was verified by HAADF‐STEM etc. The bianalyte Poisson‐binomial statistical model confirmed single molecule origin of Raman signals. Linear relationship between detection probability and ultralow Rhodamine B (RhB) concentration was established. Single molecule SERS mapping directly visualized molecular adsorption sites, identifying strongly bonded junction interface as critical signal enhancement region. The enhancement mechanism is primarily attributed to chemical enhancement, wherein the built‐in electric field facilitates multiple photoinduced charge‐transfer pathways, while the localized surface plasmon resonance of Au couples with out‐of‐plane dipole of InSe to enhance light harvesting. This strategy is material‐generalizable, as demonstrated by WSe2/GaSe‐Au systems with attomolar limits. This work provides new insights into engineering strongly bonded heterojunctions for single‐molecule sensing devices.

articles.title: Ag‐Se Synergistic Diffusion for Highly Homogeneous Elemental Distribution and Significantly Improved ACZTSSe Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The performance of Cu2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (CZTSSe) solar cells is primarily limited by an inability to control the selenization process, where non-uniform selenium distribution leads to profound Cu–Zn cation disorder and associated performance losses. Compositional engineering, such as in (AgxCu1−x)2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (ACZTSSe), can mitigate some defects; however, it fails to address the root cause: mastering the reaction kinetics to achieve elemental homogeneity. Herein, we introduce a self-sacrificing Ag2Se layer on Mo substrates that enables a bottom-up, cooperative Ag–Se diffusion pathway during grain growth. The rapid migration of Ag atoms modifies the local chemical environment, thereby acting as a kinetic driver that dramatically enhances the selenium diffusion flux. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm a 28.6% increase in the selenium diffusion coefficient (D Se), demonstrating that this kinetic enhancement activates the cooperative Ag–Se diffusion mechanism, thereby achieving a macroscopic improvement in material homogeneity. The resultant absorber exhibits an unprecedented, near-linear elemental distribution, which effectively suppresses Cu-related antisite defects (e.g., CuZn and CuSn). This superior homogeneity minimizes bulk recombination and facilitates efficient carrier transport, thereby providing a fundamental basis for the enhancement of photoelectric properties. Consequently, the champion device treated with 65 nm Ag2Se (ASe 65) achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.36% (certified as 13.91%), primarily due to a remarkable enhancement in short-circuit current density (J sc) and fill factor (FF). This work not only provides a foundational understanding of cooperative diffusion chemistry, but also establishes a novel paradigm for manipulating reaction kinetics in solid-state energy materials.

articles.title: Al3+/Ta5+ Co‐Doping Promotes Homogeneous Li+ Transport Enabling High Performance Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes with high energy density are regarded as one of the most promising cathode candidates for achieving next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, increasing the Ni content introduces critical challenges, including undesirable phase transitions, sluggish Li+ transport, and intergranular cracking, which hinder their large‐scale application. This work demonstrates an Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy, enabling homogeneous Li+ transport in a Ni‐rich cathode by forming LiNi0.94Ta0.01Al0.05O2 (LNTAO) with refined grains and suppressed Li/Ni cation mixing. The achieved homogenization suppresses high‐voltage phase transitions and facilitates Li+ intercalation/deintercalation during cycling. It also preserves the Ni valence state and Ni─O coordination environment, maintains grain‐boundary integrity, and suppresses interfacial side reactions during prolonged cycling. Enabled by these advantages, the cycle and rate performance of the Ni‐rich cathode are effectively enhanced. This Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy provides fundamental materials‐design insights into enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ni‐rich layered cathodes through the homogenization of Li+ transport.

articles.title: Amphoteric Cu‐Doping Leading to High Thermoelectric Performance in p‐Type Bismuth Antimony Telluride
articles.abstract: The role of copper in Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric materials is not well understood, and there are conflicting results regarding its impact on thermoelectric properties. Some reports claim Cu is an electron donor after intercalating into the van der Waals-like gap of (Bi,Sb)2Te3, while others show it acting as an acceptor. Here, we help clarify this discrepancy experimentally and theoretically by demonstrating that Cu behaves as an amphoteric dopant (acceptor or donor) governed by its processing pathway. While kinetic pathways allow for Cu intercalation into the van der Waals-like gaps and electron donor behavior, thermodynamic equilibrium favors the substitution of Cu for Bi or Sb cations and acceptor behavior, which provides stronger chemical bonding and stability compared to intercalated Cu. When prioritizing thermodynamic stability, p-type Cu x Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 exhibits high near-room-temperature zT values, with the best-performing composition among the investigated series reaching zT ≈1.36 ± 0.06 for four independently prepared x = 0.0025 samples. This arises from simultaneous improvements in both electronic properties (weighted mobility) and thermal properties (lattice thermal conductivity). Such improvements in zT for p-type (Bi,Sb)2Te3 in consistently manufactured materials would greatly benefit many applications for solid-state Peltier coolers and thermoelectric generators.

articles.title: An Ultramicroporous Ni‐Based MOF for Xe‐selective Capture and Ar/Kr/Xe Gas‐Phase Preparative Chromatography Separation in Liquid Fluoride Thorium Reactor Off‐Gases
articles.abstract: Efficient xenon separation is important for noble‐gas management in liquid fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR) off‐gas systems. Here, JUC‐86, an ultramicroporous Ni‐based metal‐organic framework, is investigated for Xe‐selective capture and Ar/Kr/Xe separation. JUC‐86 features a crystallographic aperture of approximately 5.2 Å and model‐derived pore widths of 4.1‐5.2 Å. At 298 K and 1 bar, the adsorption capacities of Xe, Kr, and Ar reach 75.6, 57.2, and 17.3 cm3 g−1, respectively. IAST calculations, isosteric heats of adsorption, and host–guest calculations consistently indicate a stronger affinity toward Xe. Under continuous‐flow conditions, JUC‐86 exhibits reproducible Xe/Kr breakthrough separation, with an average Xe capture capacity of 1.41 mmol g−1 and Kr productivity above 99.9% purity. The material also captures trace Xe from dilute Xe/Kr/Ar streams and enables effective preparative chromatographic separation of Ar, Kr, and Xe over varied operating conditions. Bonding‐based analysis further suggests a meaningful degree of intrinsic γ‐radiation tolerance. These results demonstrate the potential of JUC‐86 for Xe‐selective capture and chromatographic noble‐gas separation in advanced nuclear off‐gas management.

articles.title: BDNF‐Regulated Molecular‐to‐Material Transduction in an Ion–Electronic Memristive Biointerface for Modeling Addiction‐Related Neuroplasticity
articles.abstract: Addiction‐related memories are associated with dysregulated neurotrophic signaling and maladaptive synaptic plasticity. However, it still remains challenging in translating such disease‐relevant molecular regulation into history‐dependent and programmable material states. Herein, a brain‐derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)‐regulated ion–electronic memristive biointerface is developed by integrating a recognition module comprising a BDNF‐responsive aptamer and a tropomyosin receptor kinase B Fc chimera (TrkB‐Fc) with a photoactive sodium alginate (SA)/WO3 composite. Under 365 nm illumination, BDNF‐dependent interfacial regulation produces concentration‐ and history‐dependent conductance dynamics associated with W6+/W5+ mixed‐valence evolution. The device exhibits synaptic‐like responses, including paired‐pulse facilitation, learning–forgetting–relearning‐like dynamics, and reversible potentiation/depression‐like conductance modulation. These device‐state changes show functional correspondence with BDNF‐enhanced ΔFosB expression and morphine‐conditioned place preference, whereas ANA‐12 attenuates device‐state persistence and behavioral reinstatement in the respective experiments. Experimentally measured volatile responses are further used to construct reservoir states, while experimentally characterized nonvolatile conductance states provide a device‐informed basis for differential‐conductance readout‐weight representation in a software‐executed classification workflow, achieving a held‐out Fashion‐MNIST accuracy of 93.9%. Therefore, this work establishes a molecular‐to‐material transduction framework that converts neurotrophic regulation into programmable ion–electronic states and links biomolecular recognition, adaptive material dynamics, addiction‐related neuroplasticity, and proof‐of‐concept neuromorphic information processing.

articles.title: Back‐Contact Engineering via a MoO3/Ag Structure for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin‐Film Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The quality of the back contact critically determines the hole extraction efficiency and interfacial recombination losses in Sb2(S,Se)3 thin‐film solar cells. High‐efficiency devices typically use the Spiro‐OMeTAD/Au structure, but the reliance on Au electrodes increases material cost, creating an efficiency‐cost trade‐off. Here, we develop a cost‐effective Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact that enables the use of a low‐cost electrode while maintaining efficient carrier extraction. The Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact establishes a more favorable rear‐contact configuration, facilitating hole transfer while reducing carrier accumulation and interfacial recombination. Mild annealing further improves the back‐contact properties. Transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS), electrical, and photovoltaic measurements are interpreted together and consistently support improved interfacial carrier transfer with suppressed detrimental recombination. The optimized device achieves a PCE of 10.0%, approaching the performance level of reported Au‐based Sb2(S,Se)3 cells while using a low‐cost Ag‐based electrode. This work demonstrates an effective, economical back‐contact engineering strategy that delivers high performance with cost‐effectiveness.

articles.title: Bioinspired Hydrogels with Broadly Programmable Mechanics for Soft‐Tissue Interfaces
articles.abstract: Matching the mechanical properties of repair materials to tissue-specific demands remains a major challenge in soft-tissue repair. Here we report bioinspired anisotropic gelatin hydrogels formed by directional freezing and mechanically programmed through subsequent ionic treatment. By regulating intermolecular interactions while preserving the aligned, hierarchical porous architecture, this approach spans stiffnesses relevant to brain, kidney, tendon, and cartilage. Ion identity and treatment duration enable coordinated tuning of Young's modulus from 9.7 kPa to 3.59 MPa and tensile strength from 6 kPa to 14.25 MPa, together with broad regulation of viscoelasticity, extensibility, and fracture resistance. Multiscale SAXS/WAXS characterization, molecular simulations, and finite-element analysis reveal that ion-regulated chain association and hierarchical anisotropic organization collectively govern directional load transfer and mechanical reinforcement. Sodium citrate-treated AGE-SC 36H reaches a Young's modulus of 3.59 MPa, a tensile strength of 14.25 MPa, and a fracture energy of 413,305 J m− 2, while subsequent microbial transglutaminase (MTG) stabilization improves cyclic mechanical retention and resistance to swelling and enzymatic degradation under aqueous conditions. In a rat Achilles tendon model, AGE-SC 36H (MTG) promotes organized collagen remodeling and improves functional recovery over surgical repair alone. Overall, ionic regulation offers a general strategy for programming anisotropic hydrogel mechanics across material classes.

articles.title: Boosting Selective Ammonia Electrosynthesis from Nitrate Over Noble Metal Catalysts Via Surface Oxidation Engineering
articles.abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a sustainable pathway for closing the nitrogen cycle. However, the inherent activity-selectivity dilemma and fierce competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) severely restrict the practical application of noble-metal-based catalysts. Here, we report a universal low-temperature surface oxidation engineering strategy to reconstruct noble-metal (Ru, Ir, Pd, Pt) electrocatalysts. The resulting modification achieves simultaneous enhancement of NO3RR activity and efficient HER suppression, addressing a key challenge that is difficult to balance in conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. The optimized carbon-supported core-shell catalyst consisting of a Ru core and ultrathin RuO2 shell (Ru@RuO2/C) enables excellent ammonia Faradaic efficiency of over 90.0% from 0.05 to −0.2 V vs. RHE, with a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 99.91% and a yield rate of 2.18 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at 0 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the Ru@RuO2/C effectively optimizes the adsorption of *NO3 and suppresses the HER owing to interfacial charge transfer and electron density redistribution across the Ru and RuO2 interface. Applying the Ru@RuO2/C as the cathode catalyst, the assembled Zinc−nitrate battery exhibits a peak power density of 60.5 mW cm−2 and a specific capacity of 829 mAh g−1 at 100 mA cm−2.

articles.title: Broad‐Spectrum Multifunctional Optoelectronic Transistor Enabled by a Type‐II Organic p‐n Heterojunction for Advanced Secure Information Processing
articles.abstract: Secure information transmission faces mounting challenges amid increasingly complex data processing and intrinsic physical limitations of conventional electronic systems. Multifunctional optoelectronic information platforms offer a promising route to overcome these constraints. Herein, we report a broad‐spectrum multifunctional optoelectronic transistor based on a type‐II organic p‐n heterojunction comprising p‐type C10‐DNTT and n‐type indandione‐terminated quinoidal compound Q4T‐4F. The extended π‐conjugation and quinoidal skeleton of Q4T‐4F significantly broaden its absorption spectrum, enabling the integration of broad‐spectrum photodetection, electrical synaptic emulation, and non‐volatile memory in a single device. The p‐n heterojunction transistor exhibits a broad spectral response from 300 to 1100 nm with a reconfigurable photoresponse modulated by both gate voltage and light intensity. Interface charge trapping endows the device with essential synaptic characteristics and robust multilevel non‐volatile memory performance. Leveraging these integrated functions, we demonstrate advanced applications including optical/electrical encryption‐decryption and reconfigurable logic gates. This work establishes a versatile platform for advancing optoelectronic systems toward secure and efficient information processing.

articles.title: Charge Transport Dynamics in Doped Organic Polymer: Effect of New Split‐Functional Dopant on an Amorphous Organic Semiconductor
articles.abstract: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms governing charge transport in electronically doped conjugated polymers is important from both fundamental and device perspectives. Here, we investigate an amorphous semiconducting polymer, PTB7‐Th, as a suitable host to incorporate a specific organic salt system. The electronically disordered polymer, when doped with a split functional dopant that consists of organic cation 4‐(acetylamino)‐2,2,6,6‐tetramethyl‐1‐oxo‐piperidinium (ATOP) and the bulky anion tetrakis[3,5‐bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl] borate (BARF), undergoes a major enhancement in electrical transport. In addition to enhancing solubility, the BARF counterion effectively minimizes the coulombic interaction between the anion and the charge carrier on the polymer backbone, which facilitates efficient ion‐pair dissociation. A six‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in conductivity and a significant improvement in carrier mobility are observed in optimally doped samples. Temperature‐dependent DC conductivity measurements indicate variable‐range hopping transport, with improved hopping parameters upon doping. Additionally, AC measurements reveal faster carrier relaxation, systematic activation energy changes, and minimal ionic migration, highlighting improved electronic transport upon doping. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations capture ion–polaron and ion–ion correlations that rationalize the observed transport enhancement. The results highlight the connection from microscopic interactions to macroscopic enhancement in electrical performances while also identifying the origin of saturation beyond a critical dopant concentration.

articles.title: Correction to “Laser‐Controlled Ferrohydrodynamic Fluid Cavities for Modulation of Ultrasonic Waves”
Directional Electron Traction and Selective‐Sieving Effects Enabled by Biomimetic UIO‐66‐NH2‐Assisted Polyimide Electron Sponge for Ultra‐Durable Sodium‐Sulfur Battery
articles.abstract: Severe sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttling and sluggish reaction kinetics substantially hinder the development of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT/Na‐S) batteries. Herein, a biomimetic uio‐66‐NH2‐assisted polyimide with carbon‐nanotube (uio@PI/CNT) for separator‐modification is proposed. Selective‐sieving effects induced via the inherent PI‐pore segmentation by uio‐66‐NH2 efficiently inhibit NaPSs shuttling and maintain a uniform Na+ flux for homogeneous Na‐deposition. Particularly, imide‐carbonyl and triazine moieties in PI, regarded as “electron sponge” capable of successive electron uptake and supply, exert the directional electron‐traction between external circuit and NaPSs to enable prompt electron‐donation to and electron‐extraction from NaPSs during discharging and charging, thereby remarkably reducing the sulfur‐conversion energy barriers. Integrating with enhanced electron‐conduction via CNT, effective binding with NaPSs, and high‐speed Na+ transport mediated via sufficient groups synergistically provided by PI and uio‐66‐NH2 for retaining active‐specie and timely replenishing reactants to PI catalytic centers, the fast reaction kinetics and highly stable anode are achieved. Consequently, a high reversible capacity (1248 mAh g−1) at 1 A g−1 with 96.7% cycling‐retention and an ultralow fading (0.0055%) per cycle even at 2 A g−1 are presented. The catalytic mechanism involving “electron sponge”, with the selective‐sieving effects, imparts a novel direction for exploiting the ultra‐durable sodium‐sulfur batteries.

articles.title: Incorporating reef condition into conservation planning to meet place‐based biodiversity outcomes under the Global Biodiversity Framework
articles.abstract: To achieve Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Target 3, the selection of protected areas must consider the condition of ecosystems at sites in addition to the GBF 30% area target. Implementing this consideration for coral reef ecosystems is challenging because data describing condition are patchy and limited. Thus, there is uncertainty in how effective coral reef condition data are for informing conservation priorities. To address this uncertainty, we evaluated whether including ecosystem condition data changed conservation priorities when the objective was to protect reefs and implement Target 3. We tested multiple static and modeled temporal coral reef condition datasets for the Great Barrier Reef and found that including reef condition significantly altered spatial planning priorities (p < 0.001), with effects varying according to the condition indicator used. Almost half of the reefs prioritized for protection when condition metrics were included became low priority when they were excluded. Ignoring information about condition missed conservation targets for ∼22% of reef habitats once condition measures were included, highlighting how presence‐only approaches can overestimate conservation benefits by treating lower‐condition reefs as equal contributors to biodiversity protection. These differences in priority areas highlight the need to develop and use effective condition metrics for designing marine protected area systems for coral reefs globally. Making such data available and usable for managers and practitioners is a priority for coral reef conservation. Incorporación de la condición de los arrecifes a la planeación de la conservación para cumplir con los resultados de sitio bajo el Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad Resumen Para alcanzar la Meta 3 del Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad (GBF) de Kunming‐Montreal, la selección de áreas protegidas debe tener en cuenta el estado de los ecosistemas en los distintos emplazamientos, además del objetivo del GBF de cubrir el 30% de la superficie. Aplicar esta consideración a los ecosistemas de arrecifes de coral supone un reto, ya que los datos que describen su estado son pocos y están fragmentados. Por lo tanto, existe incertidumbre sobre la eficacia de los datos sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral a la hora de establecer prioridades de conservación. Para abordar esta incertidumbre, evaluamos si la inclusión de datos sobre el estado de los ecosistemas modificaba las prioridades de conservación cuando el objetivo era proteger los arrecifes y cumplir la Meta 3. Analizamos varios conjuntos de datos estáticos y temporales modelados sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral de la Gran Barrera de Coral y descubrimos que la inclusión del estado de los arrecifes alteraba significativamente las prioridades de planificación espacial (p <0.001), con efectos que variaban según el indicador de estado utilizado. Casi la mitad de los arrecifes que se consideraban prioritarios para su protección cuando se incluían los indicadores de estado pasaban a tener baja prioridad cuando se excluían dichos indicadores. Cuando ignoramos la información sobre el estado, no se alcanzaron los objetivos de conservación en aproximadamente el 22% de los hábitats de arrecifes una vez que se incluyeron las medidas de estado, lo que resalta cómo los enfoques basados únicamente en la presencia pueden sobreestimar los beneficios de conservación al considerar que los arrecifes en peor estado contribuyen en igual medida a la protección de la biodiversidad. Estas diferencias en las áreas prioritarias ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de desarrollar y utilizar métricas de estado eficaces para diseñar sistemas de áreas marinas protegidas para los arrecifes de coral a nivel mundial. Poner dichos datos a disposición de los gestores y profesionales, y garantizar que sean utilizables, es una prioridad para la conservación de los arrecifes de coral.

articles.title: Climate‐Driven Distribution Modeling of the Glacial Apollo Butterfly (Parnassius glacialis) for Biodiversity Conservation
articles.abstract: Understanding how climate change affects insect distribution is critical for biodiversity conservation, particularly in the case of range‐restricted and ecologically sensitive species. The glacial Apollo, Parnassius glacialis (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae), is a high‐altitude butterfly of notable scientific and esthetic value, yet its ecological response to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we model the current and future distribution of P. glacialis across China and identify key environmental drivers shaping its habitat. We developed an ensemble species distribution model using 45 occurrence records and 10 bioclimatic variables, integrating outputs from multiple algorithms to enhance predictive robustness. Temperature—particularly seasonal variation—emerged as the strongest determinant of habitat suitability, followed by precipitation. At present, suitable habitats are concentrated in northern, southwestern, and eastern China. However, projections under future climate scenarios reveal a marked reduction in suitable range, with the habitat centroid shifting to lower elevations in Hubei Province. The direction and extent of this shift vary among scenarios, highlighting the species' vulnerability to both climatic and socioeconomic trajectories. These findings raise urgent conservation concerns, suggesting that P. glacialis may face significant habitat loss and range contraction under projected climate conditions. We recommend the establishment of targeted protected areas, the integration of insect responses into climate adaptation policies, and the implementation of long‐term ecological monitoring. This study provides crucial insights into climate‐driven range shifts in high‐altitude butterflies and underscores the broader need for adaptive conservation strategies in a warming world.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Exonic SSR‐Containing Genes in Three Diving Duck Species Reveals Shared Functional Themes
articles.abstract: Simple sequence repeats (SSRs) are ubiquitous components of eukaryotic genomes that contribute to genome evolution, genetic variation, and gene regulation. Although genome‐wide SSR landscapes have been extensively characterized across vertebrates, the cross‐species distribution and functional associations of exonic SSR‐containing genes remain poorly understood, particularly in non‐model birds. To address this knowledge gap, we performed a comparative analysis of chromosome‐level genome assemblies from three diving duck species (Aythya ferina, Aythya marila, and Netta rufina) to investigate genome‐wide SSR patterns and the cross‐species sharing and functional characteristics of exonic SSR‐containing genes. Comparative analyses of genome‐wide SSRs revealed pronounced interspecific variation in SSR abundance and repeat composition, whereas exonic SSR abundance showed more similar values after normalization by total annotated exon sequence length. Cross‐species comparison identified 4336 exonic SSR‐containing genes shared among all three species, greatly outnumbering the species‐specific gene sets. Functional enrichment analyses identified four broad functional themes associated with these shared genes: (i) gene transcription and epigenetic regulation, (ii) protein homeostasis and the ubiquitin–proteasome system, (iii) development, differentiation and morphogenesis, and (iv) stress response and cellular maintenance. The most significantly enriched categories were associated with transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, RNA processing, and epigenetic regulation, whereas autophagy‐ and other cellular‐maintenance pathways indicated additional associations with stress‐response processes. These functional associations should be interpreted cautiously because they may be influenced by cross‐species annotation limitations and gene‐architecture differences. Collectively, our results reveal distinct patterns for genome‐wide and exonic SSRs distribution among the three diving duck species and identify shared functional associations of genes containing exonic SSRs. These findings provide a comparative genomic framework for future investigations of exonic SSRs in waterfowl and other non‐model vertebrates.

articles.title: Comparison of the Population Genetic Structures of Borrelia Virulence Gene ospC and a Putatively Neutral Intergenic Spacer
articles.abstract: Borrelia afzelii, a major causative agent of Lyme borreliosis in Europe, exhibits high polymorphism of the outer surface protein C (ospC) gene, which facilitates evasion of the vertebrate immune response. Its extensive polymorphism has been hypothesized to result from balancing selection imposed by host immunity, which predicts reduced population genetic structure at ospC relative to neutrally evolving genomic regions. To test this prediction, we genotyped ospC and the rrs–rrl intergenic spacer (IGS) in B. afzelii samples from questing Ixodes ricinus ticks and bank voles (Clethrionomys glareolus) sampled across nine populations in Poland between 2020 and 2024. Among‐population differentiation was consistently lower at ospC than at IGS, and while IGS exhibited a significant isolation‐by‐distance pattern, no such signal was detected for ospC. Collectively, these findings support the hypothesis that balancing selection maintains ospC polymorphism and counteracts geographic differentiation, with implications for the evolutionary epidemiology of Lyme borreliosis in Europe.

articles.title: Do Harbour Porpoise Mortality Records Reflect Living Population Structure? A Matrix Population Model Diagnostic
articles.abstract: Effective conservation of marine mammals depends on reliable demographic information, yet acquiring such data for highly mobile cetaceans is challenging. Harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena) are widely used as sentinel species, but much of what is known about their demography comes from stranding and bycatch records. While invaluable, these data may be filtered by drift, detection, reporting effort and age‐specific vulnerability. We developed a matrix population model (MPM)‐based diagnostic framework to quantify how observed stage compositions in mortality datasets deviate from asymptotic demographic expectations. Using a stage‐structured MPM parameterised from published vital rates, we derived the stable stage distribution (SSD) and compared it with age‐class distributions from 10,863 harbour porpoise strandings (of 16,181 total records) in Danish and North Sea waters, bycatch and mixed‐mortality records, and hunting captures from Greenland and Denmark. Deviations from SSD, and from the composition expected among deaths, were assessed using goodness‐of‐fit tests, distance metrics, and tests of the juvenile proportion. Strandings showed strong and consistent departures from SSD expectations, with juveniles markedly over‐represented across spatial and temporal scales. Juveniles remained over‐represented relative to the composition expected among deaths under baseline rates, and the departure from the living population was robust to variation in vital rates. Divergence from the asymptotic stage structure was moderate to strong, varied across space, and increased significantly over time in 2 of 6 regions. Bycatch, mixed‐mortality, and hunting captures showed comparable SSD divergence, indicating that juvenile‐heavy mortality composition is not an artefact of stranding sampling alone. Our results show that harbour porpoise stranding, bycatch, and even hunting data should not be assumed to be demographically representative of living populations. Separating sampling bias from higher juvenile mortality needs independent estimates of juvenile survival.

articles.title: Moult Timing as a Measure of Condition in a Northern Hemisphere Ungulate
articles.abstract: Many vertebrates that live in seasonal climates moult once or twice a year, with the effect of refreshing worn coat or plumage, increasing insulation or improving camouflage. The timing of moult may be in response to a variety of cues, but because it is costly, it is also likely to reflect the health and wellbeing of individuals, here referred to as their condition. Using the individually‐monitored red deer from the Isle of Rum, in which summer and winter coats are easily distinguished, we (a) test for traits that are predictive of moult timing, (b) explore traits that moult timing is predictive of and (c) analyse covariances between moult timings and calving dates at the individual, annual and residual level. We show that adult female moult timing in July and November is associated with age, reproductive status and parasite burden, and has been getting earlier over time in November. A female's moult timing also predicts the overwinter survival of herself and her current calf as well as her future fecundity. Moult timing varies among individuals and years. Covariances between calving dates and the timing of each moult shed light on the temporal patterns of condition within individuals and across years, for example, across years, winter moult covaries with the following calving date but not the summer moult that occurs shortly after. The timing of moult appears to be a non‐invasive measure of condition. Monitoring moult timing across years at the population level may shed light on year‐to‐year variation in population health and variation within populations is likely indicative of the relative conditions among individuals. Increased knowledge of population and individual condition may be of benefit for ungulate population management and conservation.

articles.title: Raptor Models Alter Rodent Behavior During Acorn Dispersal
articles.abstract: The relationship between rodents and oak trees has attracted considerable attention. The interaction spans a wide range of outcomes, from extreme predation, in which rodents consume acorns, to forms of collaboration that approach mutualism. Acorn characteristics and the behavior of rodent species within the oak habitats are among the factors shaping this interaction. This study examines the influence of third species on rodent–oak interaction by using raptor models. The main objective is to determine whether raptors in the treetops can deter rodents from feeding on acorns, thereby reducing acorn dispersal. To achieve this objective, we monitored acorns' dispersal by four rodent species, Algerian mouse, wood mouse, common vole, and garden dormouse, in 10 m × 10 m semi‐wild enclosures with oak trees in the four corners, two of them with raptor models. Beneath the 4 oaks, 60 acorns, 15 acorns per tree, were provided daily for 15 days, and the acorns in situ consumption and dispersal were tracked to determine whether the presence of raptor models altered the dispersal by any of the rodent species. The results show that species that are actively involved in acorn dispersion through transport (Algerian mouse, wood mouse) modify their behavior in response to the presence of raptor models in the treetops. The garden dormouse also modifies its behavior, although this species does not transport or bury acorns; however, it does move them around on the surface and consumes most of the acorns whole by preying on them. Therefore, it does not participate in the acorn dispersion process. The common vole typically occupies open habitats without oaks and does not modify its behavior, probably because raptor models are not perceived as a threat.

articles.title: Sex, Age, and Skull Morphology Effects on Eye Size and Refractive Errors in Reindeer
articles.abstract: Eye size influences captured light and visual resolution and is used as an indicator of the relative importance of vision. Although vision‐related sexual dimorphism is subtle among vertebrates, Cervids exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism in body size, antler development, and reproductive strategies. We tested the hypothesis that male reindeer (Rangifer tarandus tarandus) with larger skeletal dimensions would have larger eyes and narrower binocular overlap but similar refractive errors compared to females. We collected skull morphological, ocular biometric, and refractive error data from 69 semi‐domesticated reindeer (0.5–12.5‐year‐old; 27 females, 42 males) living year‐round under extreme high‐latitude seasonal variation in photoperiod in south‐central Norway. The relationships between eye size, mandible length, interorbital distance, and orbital diameter were analyzed, and binocular overlap and anterior blind zones were calculated. Eye size increased with measures of skull size, while refractive error remained minimal across all ages. Although male calves had significantly larger mandibles and interorbital distances, their orbital diameters were the same as in female calves. However, in adults, males also had larger orbital diameters. After controlling for differences in skeletal measures, males were found to have relatively smaller eyes than females, whereas binocular overlap and blind zones were similar. These findings demonstrate vision‐related sexual dimorphism in reindeer.

articles.title: Social Behaviour Drives Gut Microbiome Community Assembly Among Wild Long‐Tailed Macaques (Macaca fascicularis) in Thailand
articles.abstract: The ‘social microbiome’ conceptualises gut microbial communities as ‘islands’ of host social organisation. Yet, in comparison to broader aspects of social organisation such as animals' group membership and composition, the impact of inter‐individual differences in sociality on microbiome community ecology remains less well studied. Among a wild but human‐provisioned group of long‐tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis), we assessed the relative effects of individuals' sociality, compared to their demographic characteristics, anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors, and microbe‐microbe associations, on the relative abundance and co‐occurrence of bacterial taxa. Bipartite network analysis showed that bacterial communities among macaques were nested rather than segregated or modular structures. Several ‘core’ bacterial genera were found across all macaques, but other ‘non‐core’ bacteria were found only in a few macaques suggesting that their occurrence/abundance may be influenced by transient environmental factors. Joint Species Distributions Models showed that macaques' sociality, particularly their dominance rank and their connectedness or centrality within their social grooming network, had the strongest impact on taxa abundance, followed by their demographic characteristics, and finally their exposure to both anthropogenic and abiotic environmental factors. Phylogenetically distant taxa were more likely to co‐occur within the same macaque hosts than phylogenetically related taxa. These findings confirm that microbiome communities are strongly influenced by the social status and connectedness of individual hosts. Nevertheless, the finding that some taxa were more prevalent among high‐ranking or well‐connected macaques, while others were more prevalent among low‐ranking or socially peripheral macaques, warrants further investigation into how individual differences in social microbiomes might affect their health and fitness. Future studies, through the collection of behavioural and microbial data on additional macaque groups, may provide further insights into the relative effects of animals' social organisation and social behaviours on microbiomes.

articles.title: The Human‐Imprinted Regional Species Pool: Functional Trait Patterns of Commercial and Established Plants
articles.abstract: Urban plant communities assemble from a regional species pool shaped by both ecological processes and horticultural trade, yet how these two forces jointly structure its functional composition remains poorly understood. We characterized the potential regional species pool of Switzerland by compiling 5295 vascular plant species spanning herbs, shrubs, and trees and comparing established species (wild‐established only), commercial species (horticulturally available only), and overlapping species (both). Using a trait database covering life‐history strategies, morphology, environmental preferences, and human use, we examined functional trait space using principal component analysis and quantified functional richness, dispersion, and originality. We further tested which traits were associated with wild establishment among non‐native species and invasive status among overlapping species using Firth logistic regression. Commercial species were unevenly distributed across growth forms, dominating among trees (67.9%) and shrubs (59.7%) but less represented among herbs (17.9%). Functional differentiation was strongest along an environmental niche axis, with commercial herbs associated with drier conditions and commercial woody species with warmer conditions. Commercial species consistently had the lowest functional richness, dispersion, and originality across all growth forms. Wild establishment was associated with multiple environmental, reproductive, and ecological traits, whereas invasive status was associated with warmer temperature preference and anthropogenic tolerance, although the latter analysis was exploratory. These results indicate that commercial availability creates a functionally selective pool of species that may influence later urban community assembly. By shaping the functional possibilities available before local assembly occurs, horticultural trade may therefore leave an important human imprint on urban biodiversity, with potential downstream consequences for ecosystem functioning and trophic interactions.

articles.title: Unveiling the Ongoing Expansion of Bullheads of the Genus Ameiurus (Actinopteri: Siluriformes) in the Dnipro River Basin, Ukraine: New Distributional Records and Genetic Diversity
articles.abstract: Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. We employed an integrated framework combining laboratory molecular analysis (mtDNA COI barcoding) with field‐based morphological scoring via Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC). Sampling was conducted across multiple riverine networks within the catchment to evaluate whether range expansion is driven by natural downstream dispersal or human‐mediated pathways. A total of 66 specimens from six sampling localities were analysed, yielding 66 COI sequences. Phylogenetic reconstruction consistently recovered two discrete, high‐support clades corresponding to A. nebulosus and A. melas, a topology consistently supported across multiple distance‐based and phylogeny‐based delimitation methods. These results document the continued range expansion of both species in the Dnipro River basin, including the first molecularly confirmed occurrence record of A. melas in this basin, previously known only from the Southern Buh and Danube basins. Genetic analysis revealed five COI haplotypes per species, most of which are new to Ukraine, a pattern consistent with multiple independent introduction events or the retention of standing genetic variation from diverse source populations. DAPC profiling identified body colouration, pectoral spine serration, anal fin membrane pigmentation, and gill raker count as the most robust diagnostic traits for reliable field delimitation. The observed lack of isolation‐by‐distance and the allopatric establishment of both species in adjacent water bodies support a ‘jumpy’ colonisation pattern driven by unauthorised human‐mediated translocations rather than natural dispersal. This study provides a scalable, integrated framework to resolve taxonomic ambiguities in cryptic or plastic invasive fish populations. Our findings establish an ecological baseline for range forecasting and risk assessment of Ameiurus in European inland waters, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated molecular monitoring at the leading edges of freshwater biological invasions.
