articles.abstract: Despite its potential as an attractive alternative for renewable energy transport, catalytic ammonia decomposition faces several challenges before it can be established as a viable hydrogen (H 2 ) carrier technology.

articles.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction
articles.abstract: Floral rewards and signals must be coordinated to attract pollinators, but the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using melon as a model system, this study reveals how the developmental regulator YAB5 coordinates nectar production, flower opening, and floral signals to promote bee visitation.

articles.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication
articles.abstract: Single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary input of viral genomes, which varies with different viruses and cell types. We show that supra-unitary viral genome quantities, independently of viral protein synthesis, activate negative feedback regulators of RIG-I, MDA-5, and PKR, suppressing the innate immune response and allowing replication.

articles.title: Microbial products trigger chemosensory dialogues through intestinal G protein-coupled receptors
articles.abstract: Kadoki et al. developed GPCR-seq, a high-throughput platform to identify how the gut senses environmental chemicals. They discovered gut microbial products that activate intestinal receptors, triggering serotonin release or linking to inflammatory bowel disease. This work provides a scalable template for decoding how host-microbe communication influences human health.

articles.title: A stress-adapted fiber state promotes clonal expansion of deleted mitochondrial DNA
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion and multiple deletions frequently coexist in mitochondrial disease, neurodegeneration, and aging, yet how the two relate and why deletions accumulate focally remain unresolved. Here, longitudinal bulk and in situ analyses of Mpv17-/- murine muscle reveal that a compensatory rise in mitochondrial transcripts per mtDNA initially offsets severe, uniform mtDNA depletion, preserving the respiratory chain. However, this response carries a delayed cost: by six months transcripts decline, mtDNA deletions emerge, and respiratory-deficient fibers appear. Paradoxically, fibers harboring deletions accumulate supra-physiological amounts of mtDNA, despite prior depletion. This expansion is invariably accompanied by elevated Hsp60, and the same holds in human mitochondrial myopathy. We propose that depletion reprograms mitochondrial DNA and RNA metabolism, inadvertently promoting deletion formation and creating an Hsp60-high fiber state permissive for clonal expansion. Therefore, depletion and multiple deletions can be sequential phases of a common degenerative process, relevant also to aging and neurodegeneration.

articles.title: ALS-linked FUS mutation impairs GEMIN5-dependent mRNA recruitment to neuronal late endosomes
articles.abstract: Neurons depend on tightly regulated positioning of cellular components to maintain long-distance signaling, but the mechanisms guiding specific mRNAs to distant regions remain unclear. Here, we show that late endosomes function as selective RNA carriers in human motor neurons and uncover the molecular logic guiding their loading. Using APEX2-mediated proximity labeling, we identify the external transcriptome of RAB7A-positive endosomes and find a specific population of mRNAs enriched for endosomal, axonal, and synaptic functions. We find that mRNAs enriched in RAB7A endosomes contain evolutionarily conserved 5'UTRs that act as localization signals, and that the RNA-binding protein GEMIN5 interacts with these regions to promote endosomal RNA recruitment. Finally, we show that there is a conspicuous loss of endosome-associated transcripts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-associated conditions, accompanied by the mislocalization of GEMIN5 from endosomes. These findings uncover fundamental principles of RNA compartmentalization and highlight endosomal mRNA loading as a vulnerable axis in neuronal homeostasis.

articles.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome FXR/Sptlc2 signaling promotes alveolar macrophage mitophagy and limits lung inflammation
articles.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) undergo functional reprogramming that critically regulates lung inflammation. Although mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control, its role in macrophage functional reprogramming during acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Nr1h4 (FXR) as a transcriptional regulator of mitophagy in AMs. FXR activation transcriptionally upregulates serine palmitoyltransferase long chain base subunit 2 (Sptlc2), thereby enhancing mitophagy and promoting an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype under inflammatory conditions. The FXR/Sptlc2 axis reduces oxidative stress and inflammatory mediator production while increasing anti-inflammatory markers. Conversely, FXR deficiency impairs mitophagy, exacerbates pulmonary inflammation, and aggravates lung injury in vivo. These findings establish the FXR/Sptlc2 axis as a regulator of mitochondrial quality control and macrophage functional reprogramming and identify it as a potential therapeutic target in ARDS.

articles.title: Antibody 3CF5 neutralizes historical and emerging H5Nx influenza viruses by targeting a conserved non-receptor-binding hemagglutinin epitope
articles.abstract: Avian influenza viruses of the H5Nx subtype pose persistent pandemic threats. Here, we immunized rhesus macaques with an H5N6 vaccine and obtained 30 H5-reactive monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Three IgG mAbs, 3CF5, 3BG3, and 3BE7, demonstrated potent neutralizing activity against multiple H5Nx viruses and conferred protection in a lethal mouse challenge model. Notably, 3CF5 exhibited broad neutralization against H5Nx viruses spanning 1997-2024, including contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 strains associated with an ongoing outbreak in dairy cattle. Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) analysis revealed that 3CF5 targets a conserved non-receptor-binding epitope on the hemagglutinin (HA) head, spanning the vestigial esterase domain and an adjacent lateral surface. 3CF5 mediates neutralization primarily through inhibiting membrane fusion and also possesses antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Furthermore, isotype conversion of 3CF5-IgG to mucosal secretory IgA1 (sIgA1) enhanced neutralization potency against H5N1 viruses up to 128-fold, highlighting the advantage of sIgA1 as a nasally administered prophylactic agent.

articles.title: Ataxin-2 loss flips a metabolic switch for neuron health
articles.abstract: Gastaldo et al.1 report that lowering ataxin-2 protects neurons from TDP-43 toxicity in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis by activating neuronal glycolysis and astrocytic cholesterol synthesis, not by reversing TDP-43-dependent molecular pathology. The downstream effectors, IDH1 and HMGCS1, thus emerge as candidate therapeutic targets.

articles.title: CSE1L enrichment in pediatric and young adult acute myeloid leukemia reveals a ribosomal export dependency
articles.abstract: Proteins shuttle between the nucleus and cytoplasm through the nuclear pore and via nuclear transport receptors, termed importins and exportins. Although genetic alterations involving nucleoporins are enriched in pediatric, adolescent, and young adult (AYA) acute myeloid leukemia (AML), nucleocytoplasmic transport has not been extensively studied in this disease. We discover that genes encoding nucleocytoplasmic transport pathway components (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes [KEGG]: hsa03013) are enriched in AML cells from younger patients (≤40 years). Within this pathway, CSE1L is the highest expressed exportin in pediatric/AYA AML and shows minimal expression in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). CSE1L depletion reduces leukemic cell growth, proliferation, and clonogenic capacity, targeting leukemia stem cells while sparing normal HSCs. Mechanistically, we identify a novel Ran-GTP-dependent role for CSE1L in regulating pre-60S ribosomal subunit export in AML. Collectively, these data identify nucleocytoplasmic transport and ribosomal subunit export as enriched dependencies in pediatric/AYA AML and establish CSE1L-mediated export as a leukemic vulnerability.

articles.title: Dopamine turns mitochondrial stress into inflammation
articles.abstract: Daniali et al. show that dopamine drives mitochondrial stress, mtDNA release, and cGAS-STING-dependent IL-6 production in human macrophages. These findings suggest a mechanism linking dopaminergic signaling to mtDNA damage signatures increasingly detected in blood from patients with Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines induce astrocyte programs that support antigen-dependent CD4+ T cell restimulation
articles.abstract: Astrocyte contributions to CNS antigen presentation remain poorly defined. We show that interferon gamma (IFN-γ, the sole type II interferon), with proinflammatory cytokines, induces astrocytes to express components mediating attraction of and antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells. Re-analysis of astrocyte-enriched single-cell sequencing from bacterial mimetic-injected mice revealed a transcriptionally distinct, IFN-responsive astrocyte population enriched for antigen-presentation genes 24 h after peripheral immune challenge. In vivo, type II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II+)GFAP+ astrocytes localize to the brain surface across multiple mouse models of neuroinflammation and in human neurological disease tissue. In vitro, purified astrocytes stimulated with IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines expressed MHC-II, costimulatory molecules, and lymphocyte-recruiting chemokines, and in co-culture supported rapid antigen-dependent expansion of previously activated CD4+ T cells. Human iPSC-derived CNS cultures showed equivalent induction of antigen-presentation machinery in human astrocytes following inflammatory cytokine stimulation. These findings define a cytokine-induced astrocyte state expressing antigen-presentation machinery at neuroimmune interfaces that can support local CD4+ T cell responses.

articles.title: Locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons have diverse activity patterns across species and biological context
articles.abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) brainstem cell group is evolutionarily conserved across vertebrates and influences both mind (cognition) and body (cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and immune functions) via two-putatively distinct-spontaneous activity patterns. Yet, the degree to which spontaneous LC firing rates and patterns are homogeneous across species has never been assessed due to inherently limited sample sizes. To remedy this, we pooled cross-species data from 20 laboratories to show that firing rates differ across species and are modulated by sex, age, and type of in vitro or in vivo preparation. Contrary to the prevailing dual-mode firing pattern schema, we observed patterns spread across a low-dimensional manifold, with subregions enriched for specific biological factors and neurodegenerative disease models. Our findings show considerable diversity in an ancestral vertebrate neuromodulatory system.

articles.title: Molecular insights into the activation mechanism of the slow anion channel AtSLAH3
articles.abstract: The plant slow anion channel SLAH3 regulates essential physiological processes, including stomatal closure and stress responses, yet the structural mechanism underlying its activation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the activation mechanism of SLAH3 by determining cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the wild-type (WT) channel and gain-of-function mutants identified through a targeted mutagenesis screen of pore-lining residues. Notably, the L400A mutant was captured in a dilated, open-like conformation, in contrast to the auto-inhibited WT channel. Structural comparisons revealed concerted rearrangements of the pore-lining transmembrane helices and intracellular regulatory elements. The observations point to an activation model in which displacement of the intracellular auto-inhibitory module relieves pore occlusion, triggering conformational changes that propagate from the intracellular loop to pore-lining segments, ultimately widening the entrance for anion transport. Therefore, our study provides a structural framework for understanding SLAH3 regulation and advances our understanding of nitrate signaling and stress adaptation in plants.

articles.title: Sense-and-respond: Engineered bacteria drive epithelial repair during gut inflammation
articles.abstract: Zhao et al.1 engineer a reactive oxygen species-responsive probiotic strain of Escherichia coli that senses intestinal inflammation and responds by locally delivering IL-22-Fc to promote epithelial repair, establishing an integrated sense-and-respond platform for inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis and mucosal healing.

articles.title: The complexity of cerebral small vessel disease: In search of the ideal mouse model
articles.abstract: Currently, there are few animal models that reflect the physiological complexity of cerebral small vessel disease. Ruan et al.1 presented a pericyte-specific knockout of laminin-γ1 that exhibited several key disease-typical characteristic features at 11 months of age.

articles.title: Interpretable deep learning maps spatial morphological phenotypes to HCC and LUAD survival
articles.abstract: Liu et al. present MorphX, an interpretable deep learning framework that decodes cancer prognosis from whole-slide histological images and reveals morphological biomarkers. Across independent cohorts, MorphX identifies eight morphology-based biomarkers, supporting trustworthy, transparent, AI-driven precision oncology.

Niche-reprogramming CAR T therapy improves skeletal muscle regeneration and function in preclinical murine models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
articles.abstract: Diao and colleagues identify uPAR as a shared marker of pathogenic macrophage and fibro-adipogenic progenitor subsets in DMD. Selective depletion of these cells by uPAR CAR T cells remodels the dystrophic muscle niche, restores muscle regeneration, and improves limb and respiratory muscle function in preclinical murine models of DMD.

articles.title: Frontier Orbital Engineering of the Oxide Photocatalyst K2Zn2Nb4O13 by Coupling Crystal Structure, Electronic Structure, and Chemical Bonding
articles.abstract: Rational design of oxide photocatalysts with intrinsically efficient bulk carrier transport remains a major challenge because carrier migration is strongly governed by the complex interplay among crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding. Here, we propose a Frontier orbital engineering strategy to regulate intrinsic carrier transport by reconstructing the Frontier orbital composition within a structurally robust oxide framework. Based on the tunnel-type Na2Ti6O13 structure, the oxide semiconductor K2Zn2Nb4O13 was designed and synthesized through the cooperative substitution of Ti4+ by Zn2+/Nb5+. Combined high-resolution PXRD and NPD refinements confirm the successful realization of the designed tunnel framework with complete Zn/Nb ordering. Orbital-resolved electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) and conduction band minimum (CBM) are mainly derived from Zn 3d−O 2p and Nb1 4d−O 2p antibonding orbitals, respectively. Such orbital decoupling of Frontier orbital contributing units and the continuous covalent networks along the b-axis provide favorable pathways for bulk carrier migration and establish the structural and electronic basis for the proposed Frontier orbital engineering strategy. Experimentally, Pd-loaded K2Zn2Nb4O13 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic H2 generation activity, achieving a rate of 119(3) μmol/h. This work provides Frontier orbital engineering as a design paradigm for functional materials, enabling the rational manipulation of intrinsic charge transport properties through the synergistic regulation of crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding.

articles.title: High Temperature Stable Pt Nanoclusters Formation in Alumina-Encapsulated Pt Catalysts
articles.abstract: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics. Within the alumina-encapsulated system, a sub-2 nm Pt cluster population formed under all oxidizing atmospheres tested but not under inert atmosphere, and this population persisted for at least 12 h at 800 °C under propene complete combustion (PCC) conditions. Unencapsulated Pt/Al2O3 controls, by contrast, developed only a transient sub-2 nm population, detected within 1 min of aging in air at 800 °C and no longer present afterward, consistent with the rapid disappearance of small particles predicted by Ostwald ripening theory. CO-DRIFTS confirmed the presence of undercoordinated Pt surface sites in all oxidatively aged samples, with no detectable signal when the sample was aged under inert atmosphere. Propene combustion rates measured after aging for an alumina-encapsulated catalyst were approximately two and five times higher than the fresh encapsulated catalyst for catalysts aged under inert atmosphere and under oxygen and steam, respectively. DFT calculations of Pt diffusion through defective Al2O3 identified kinetically accessible diffusion pathways at 800 °C, with activation barriers as low as 0.76 eV. Furthermore, Pt surface binding was calculated to be favored in the presence of O2. These results identify oxygen-driven surface segregation, mediated by defect-assisted diffusion through the ALD overcoat, as a possible mechanism responsible for nanocluster formation in this system. The persistence of the sub-2 nm cluster population for at least 12 h at 800 °C under PCC conditions demonstrates the thermal stability of these sites within the encapsulated architecture.

articles.title: Switching the Ordering Pattern of Bi2Rh4 Breathing Distortion by Isovalent Chalcogen Substitution in Bi2Rh3 X 2 ( X = Se, S)
articles.abstract: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume. The resulting primitive lattice contains inequivalent Rh4 quadrilaterals formed by alternating expansion and contraction, establishing a C-centering-breaking breathing order. Although previous spectroscopic studies have reported CDW-like signatures in Bi2Rh3Se2, the calculated Fermi surfaces of the high-temperature phase do not reveal an obvious nesting vector expected for a simple nesting-driven Peierls-type CDW scenario. Instead, the Rh 4d-derived electronic states at the Fermi level are naturally sensitive to the observed Rh4 breathing distortion, indicating that the transition is best described as a breathing-order transition accompanied by electronic reconstruction. In Bi2Rh3S2, a comparable Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion appears, but its ordering pattern is switched: when described in the high-temperature-cell setting, the Bi2Rh4 units form a large−small−small sequence along the aHT-direction, accompanied by an antiphase relation between neighboring chains, producing a commensurate 3× superstructure consistent with the first-order character of the transition. Calculations based on the experimentally refined structures further reveal a reduction of the density of states near EF and an anisotropic redistribution of occupied low-energy states in the breathing-distorted phases, supporting the coupling between the Bi2Rh4 motif and electronic reconstruction. These results show that isovalent chalcogen substitution selects the in-plane ordering pattern of an intrinsic Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion, thereby switching the collective symmetry-breaking pathway and associated electronic response.

articles.title: Synthesis of fcc/2H and f cc /4H Copper Nanodisks Towards Carbon Dioxide Reduction
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional Cu nanostructures containing noncanonical face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed (fcc/hcp) heterophase boundaries are attractive for CO2 electroreduction but remain difficult to prepare by wet-chemical methods. Here, we report a high-temperature solution reduction route to Cu nanodisks with a thickness of 26.5 ± 2.3 nm and a diameter of 85.6 ± 3.7 nm. Transmission electron microscopy reveals abundant fcc/2H and fcc/4H interfaces on the nanodisk side surfaces, where the 2H and 4H polytypes exhibit AB and ABCB stacking, respectively. In CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3, the nanodisks achieve a methane Faradaic efficiency of 60.4% at −1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode and outperform fcc Cu nanoparticle and microsheet controls tested at the same catalyst loading. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the free-energy penalty for forming the *CHO intermediate is smaller on the fcc/2H and fcc/4H models than on fcc Cu. These results support a thermodynamic contribution of heterophase interfaces to the observed methane selectivity; the calculations do not establish a reduction in kinetic activation barriers. This solution-phase route therefore provides access to phase-engineered Cu nanodisks and enables structure−property relationships relevant to CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Reducing whale–vessel strikes through multiobjective vessel traffic routing
articles.abstract: Vessel strikes threaten many large whale species. Managers employ several mitigation measures to reduce vessel strike risk, including establishing or modifying vessel routing measures, such as shipping lanes. However, most studies utilized to inform the configuration of shipping lanes only consider a limited number of potential lanes, and in many cases, the criteria used to generate the lanes are unclear. We developed an approach to design, modify, or evaluate shipping lanes that involves clearly defining the objectives of the lanes and using the k least‐cost path (KLCP) algorithm, which identifies the KLCPs between two points on a cost surface, to identify all lanes that meet the objectives. We applied our approach to evaluate recommended shipping lanes in Cape Cod Bay, Massachusetts (United States), and off the Atlantic Coast of the southeastern United States with respect to the risk of vessel strikes to North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) and the time it takes vessels to travel the lanes. We identified all lanes with a risk of right whale strikes and a travel time less than or equal to that of the recommended lanes using the KLCP algorithm. In most cases, the lanes identified had similar spatial configurations to the recommended lanes and reduced the risk of strikes by <15%, which indicates that the existing recommended lanes are adequately, but not optimally, designed to reduce strike risk and travel time relative to potential alternative lanes. Our approach applying the KLCP algorithm provides a thorough, objective, and transparent way to identify vessel routing configurations that minimize whale–vessel strikes and meet other objectives. Reducción de las colisiones entre ballenas y embarcaciones mediante la planificación de rutas de tráfico marítimo con múltiples objetivos Resumen Las colisiones con embarcaciones suponen una amenaza para muchas especies de ballenas de gran tamaño. Los responsables aplican diversas medidas de mitigación para reducir el riesgo de la colisión, entre ellas el establecimiento o la modificación de medidas de trazado de rutas marítimas, como las rutas de navegación. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios utilizados para definir la configuración de las rutas de navegación solo tienen en cuenta un número limitado de rutas potenciales y, en muchos casos, los criterios empleados para generarlas no están claros. Desarrollamos un enfoque para diseñar, modificar o evaluar rutas marítimas que consiste en definir claramente los objetivos de las mismas y utilizar el algoritmo k de las rutas de menor coste (KLCP), que identifica las KLCP entre dos puntos en una superficie de costos, con el fin de determinar todas las rutas que cumplen dichos objetivos. Aplicamos nuestro enfoque para evaluar las rutas marítimas recomendadas en la bahía de Cape Cod, en Massachusetts (Estados Unidos), y frente a la costa atlántica del sureste de Estados Unidos, con la consideración del riesgo de colisiones de buques con las ballenas francas del Atlántico Norte (Eubaleana glacialis) y el tiempo que tardan los buques en recorrer dichas rutas. Identificamos todas las rutas con riesgo de colisiones con ballenas francas y un tiempo de travesía inferior o igual al de las rutas recomendadas utilizando el algoritmo KLCP. En la mayoría de los casos, las rutas identificadas presentaban configuraciones espaciales similares a las de las rutas recomendadas y reducían el riesgo de colisiones en menos del 15%, lo que indica que las rutas recomendadas existentes están diseñadas de forma adecuada, aunque no óptima, para reducir el riesgo de colisiones y el tiempo de travesía en comparación con posibles rutas alternativas. Nuestro enfoque, basado en la aplicación del algoritmo KLCP, ofrece una forma exhaustiva, objetiva y transparente de identificar configuraciones de rutas para buques que minimicen las colisiones entre ballenas y buques y cumplan otros objetivos.

articles.title: Climate and Other Human Causes of Spatial Variation in Mallard Mortality and Population Dynamics
articles.abstract: Wildlife population dynamics change across time and space, but few studies use formal spatiotemporal statistical models to understand these patterns. The population distribution of mallards (Anas platyrhyncos) in the Prairie Pothole Region of central North America (PPR) has shifted dramatically over the past several decades as agricultural intensity and climate have changed. We examined spatiotemporal variation in survival, natural mortality, and harvest mortality rates for mallards in the PPR from 1974 to 2023 using intrinsic conditional autoregressive models in a Bayesian framework. There was substantial variation over time and space for all demographic rates, and relationships between mortality and habitat variables varied by age and sex cohort. Specifically, environmental relationships indicate that habitats with less agricultural activity and more wetlands decrease survival via increased natural mortality driven by reproductive risks. We also found a worrying trend: females exhibited declining survival probabilities since the late 1980s and early 1990s. Our analyses demonstrate major variation in survival rates of a well‐studied organism across an environmental gradient, reveal subtle but critical differences relative to inference obtained from pooled data, and provide a clear roadmap to future research that can inform spatially explicit conservation and management goals.

articles.title: Flash Behaviour Does Not Help Rabbits Evade Human Predators
articles.abstract: A number of otherwise cryptic species have areas on their body of conspicuous colour that are hidden while stationary but displayed when moving. A suggested function of this conspicuous colouration is for flash behaviour, in which an otherwise cryptic prey exposes obvious colours during escape to disrupt the predators' ability to locate the prey when it stops moving and hides the colour. Experimental studies of artificial prey with human and avian predators have found that flash behaviour can increase ‘prey’ survival, but this has not been comprehensively tested using real prey. European rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus) display their white tail when running but are otherwise cryptic when resting or foraging. We experimentally tested whether flash behaviour inhibits detection by presenting videos of wild rabbits fleeing to human participants and manipulated the tail colour of the rabbits. We found that rabbits with unmanipulated white tails were neither more likely nor faster to be located than rabbits with tails digitally manipulated to be cryptic. This does not support the hypothesis that flash behaviour helps rabbits evade predators.

articles.title: Population‐Level Assimilated Dietary Responses of Black Bears to Baiting
articles.abstract: Wildlife feeding through intentional or unintentional practices can result in increased human‐wildlife conflict, disease transmission, population growth, and altered behavior. We quantified how spatial and temporal variation in black bear (Ursus americanus) bait availability within home ranges influenced black bear diet composition as mediated by sex and age. We tested carbon (δ13C) and nitrogen (δ15N) isotopes in hair samples from hunter‐harvested bears during pre‐baiting (about 1 May–9 August) and baiting (about 10 August–26 October) periods in Michigan, USA, 2017–2021 and used isotopic mixing models to estimate how diet varied between sexes and with spatially‐varying bait distribution. We used linear models to determine whether intrinsic (i.e., sex, age) and extrinsic (i.e., region, bait quantity and distribution) factors were correlated with δ13C and δ15N enrichment of black bear hair during pre‐baiting and baiting periods while controlling for corn agriculture, distance from waste accumulation sites, and human population density. Proportion of anthropogenic food in black bear diet was greater during the baiting period, especially for female black bears, but bait density did not influence black bear diet composition. Black bear hair from the Northern Lower Peninsula was more enriched in δ13C as compared to the Upper Peninsula and had the greatest δ13C and δ15N enrichment at about 10 years of age. Bait density and distribution did not influence δ13C or δ15N enrichment in black bear hair, potentially due to bait availability. Our results demonstrate that anthropogenic food from intentional and non‐intentional sources contributes substantially to black bear diet in Michigan, which may affect body condition, behavior, reproduction, and abundance.

articles.title: RTMB: An R Package for Fitting Latent Variable Models With Template Model Builder
articles.abstract: Hierarchical and latent variable models are fundamental in ecology, fisheries science, and epidemiology, but fitting them efficiently relies on automatic differentiation (AD) combined with approximations such as the Laplace approximation. Template Model Builder (TMB) has become a standard tool for this kind of inference in R, but it requires users to write the objective function in C++, which is a potential obstacle for those unfamiliar with it, slows model iteration through compilation, and complicates debugging and simulation. We present RTMB, an R package that exposes the full power of TMB's AD machinery directly from plain R. Users write the joint negative log‐likelihood as an ordinary R function; RTMB traces it onto an AD tape and hands the result to TMB's existing optimization, Laplace approximation, and reporting routines. We describe the design of the package, illustrate its use through a worked example, and provide a side‐by‐side comparison with the equivalent TMB implementation of a theta‐logistic state‐space population model. The result is a transparent, debuggable, and pedagogically accessible interface to state‐of‐the‐art latent variable inference, with runtime performance comparable to native TMB.

articles.title: Seabird Prey in Space and Time: Combining Multiple Datasets to Model the Distribution of Sandeel (Ammodytes marinus) and Sprat (Sprattus sprattus) in the North Sea
articles.abstract: Many seabird populations along the UK's East Coast have declined over the past three decades. A key concern is reduced availability of their primary breeding season prey, sandeel (Ammodytes marinus). While some seabirds have partially switched to sprat (Sprattus sprattus), this is not universal. Studying these predator–prey dynamics requires fine‐scale estimates of prey distributions that are both spatially and temporally resolved—yet such data are limited, especially for sandeel due to sampling challenges. We evaluate the utility of large‐scale ICES bottom trawl surveys to model sandeel distribution, combining them with winter dredge surveys designed specifically for this species. For sprat, we combine bottom trawl data with the Herring Acoustic Survey. Using hierarchical Bayesian spatiotemporal models (R‐INLA), we estimate the biomass of small and medium sandeel (≤ 16 cm) and sprat across the entire North Sea from 2000 to 2020, accounting for spatial and temporal dependencies. We validate our sandeel models by comparison with other modelling approaches and ICES stock assessments. Results reveal marked regional variation: sandeel increased in Area 3 (Norwegian EEZ), declined in Areas 1 and 2 and fluctuated in Area 4. Sprat biomass increased over time, with a modest northward expansion. This study provides the first North Sea‐wide, fine‐scale, multi‐decadal distribution models for these two key seabird prey species and identifies important regional drivers of their populations.

articles.title: Stable Reference Genes for RT‐qPCR in House Dust Mite Dermatophagoides farinae (Acari: Pyroglyphidae) at Different Developmental Stages
articles.abstract: To investigate the growth and development mechanisms in Dermatophagoides farinae, it is essential to understand its gene expression profiles across different life stages, which are typically assessed by transcriptional profiling based on RT‐qPCR. Suitable reference genes are vital for ensuring reliable and accurate results; however, none have been established for this species across different developmental stages. Here, we analyzed expression profiles of ten frequently used reference genes (RPL18, RPS18, RPS9, EF1A, RPS28, Actin, V‐ATPaseB, GAPDH, RPL32, and α‐tubulin) to determine their stability across different developmental stages of D. farinae. Four algorithms (GeNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, and ΔCt) were employed to examine gene stability, and their results were subsequently integrated by RefFinder to yield a comprehensive assessment. The results indicated that RPL18 and RPS28 were the two top‐ranked stable reference genes, whereas α‐tubulin and RPL32 showed the lowest stability. To confirm the robustness of the chosen reference genes, we assessed cytochrome P450 3A8 expression at developmental stages of D. farinae using three independent biological replicates and three technical replicates per stage. Normalization against RPL18 and RPS28, individually or combined, produced expression patterns consistent with previously reported developmental trends of cytochrome P450 genes in mites and insects, namely higher expression in larvae and protonymphs, lower expression in later stages, and minimal expression observed in eggs. In contrast, unstable reference genes yielded inconsistent results, thereby confirming our findings. In conclusion, this study identifies two highly stable reference genes that will provide a robust foundation for precise gene expression normalization and functional studies in D. farinae.

Prevalence, severity and factors exposing urban rock pigeons (Columba livia) to foot deformities in katima Mulilo, Namibia
articles.abstract: Urban environments expose wildlife to anthropogenic hazards, including materials capable of causing physical injuries. Among urban birds, the rock pigeon (Columba livia) is highly adapted to urban environments. However, frequent reports of digit entanglement and foot deformities in these environments suggest that urban conditions expose birds to foot injuries. Despite widespread observations of “string foot”, quantitative assessments of deformity prevalence and severity across urban land-use types remain limited, particularly within African cities. This study assessed the prevalence and severity of foot deformities in rock pigeons across three land-use zones in Katima Mulilo, Namibia: the Central Business District (CBD), market areas, and residential areas. A total of 300 pigeons were visually inspected during systematic field surveys. Foot deformities were recorded as present or absent and classified into three severity levels (mild, moderate, severe). Forty-six (15.3%) pigeons exhibited foot deformities. The prevalence of foot deformities varied significantly among land-use categories, with the highest recorded in the residential areas (22.5%), followed by the CBD (12.4%) and least in the market areas (10.4%). Moderate deformities were the most prevalent injury category (60.9%), followed by severe (23.9%) and mild deformities (15.2%). Pigeons observed in residential areas had significantly higher odds of deformities compared with those in the CBD (OR = 2.05, p = 0.044). Fibrous wastes, which constitute the important potential sources of entanglement hazard, were prevalent in the environment of pigeons. Results of this study suggest that foot injury in urban rock pigeons varied across land-use types and highlight the potential role of human-derived materials on pigeon health in urban areas. Targeted management of fibrous wastes in the CBD and residential areas is recommended to reduce entanglement-related foot deformities, with emphasis on improved local waste handling and disposal behavior.

articles.title: Global Change Is Reshaping Coral Communities and Threatening Reef Physical Functionality
articles.abstract: Coral reefs are undergoing profound compositional changes driven by climate change, disease, and chronic human disturbance. Coral cover is the primary metric used to track reef condition, but it often fails to capture the contributions of different coral species to reef carbonate production, structural complexity, and associated biodiversity. Here, I review evidence showing that global change disproportionately removes competitively dominant and architecturally complex corals, driving non‐random changes and coral community homogenisation. These changes erode reef functionality, even when overall cover is maintained. Species‐specific contributions to calcification and structural complexity span orders of magnitude, such that targeted losses of framework‐building taxa collapse carbonate budgets and habitat architecture in ways not predictable from cover trends. These structural changes cascade through associated communities, undermining functional diversity and the ecosystem processes on which reef resilience depends. Critically, rebounds in coral cover frequently reflect the colonisation by fast‐growing opportunistic species, which yield slow or absent recovery of physical functionality, while reassembly and the re‐establishment of large, structurally complex colonies (and the physical functionality they provide) might lag by decades. Furthermore, as mass disturbance events occur at ever‐shorter intervals, recovery windows close before reef‐building potential and complexity can be fully restored. Monitoring, management, and restoration should therefore focus on trait‐ and species‐explicit assessments that prioritise protection and restoration of keystone reef‐builders, target sites with high functional potential, and reduce stressors at appropriate scales. Integrating functional metrics into policy and restoration planning is essential to safeguard reef geomorphic and ecological services under continued global change.

articles.title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity
articles.abstract: Zhou et al. show VEGFR-1 signaling in intestinal Tfh cells is essential for immune surveillance. Its loss impairs IgA immunity, allowing a gut bacterium to deplete taurine, impair fat burning, and drive obesity. Restoring this axis offers an immune-based strategy for metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Reporting guidelines of stretchable solar cells toward standardized evaluation
articles.abstract: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

An intrinsically stretchable thin-film organic rechargeable sodium-ion battery enabled for wearable devices
articles.abstract: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.

articles.title: Fracture-mediated percolation governs electrical activation in liquid metal composite conductors
articles.abstract: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.

articles.title: Linking Population Genomics and Movement Ecology for Shark Conservation
articles.abstract: Climate change and overexploitation are increasingly threatening sharks, with pelagic species among the most affected. The complex ecology and life histories of these species, however, pose major challenges for conservation planning. Here, we examine how integrating genomics and movement ecology can better inform the conservation of highly migratory sharks. The growing availability of reference genomes and expanding population genomic datasets in sharks, coupled with advances in biologging, creates unprecedented opportunities to integrate these approaches and link long‐term, population‐level evolutionary processes with short‐term individual, behavioural patterns. This mini review explores research applications that integrate both fields to overcome their individual limitations and strengthen the evidence and conclusions used to inform conservation. Then we discuss, based on previous studies, how this framework can address specific conservation objectives and lead to decision‐ready outcomes, including the delineation of management units, the design of spatial and stock‐specific fisheries management measures, and the assessment of species' vulnerability to climate change. We conclude by highlighting that the translation of this knowledge into practice requires engagement with the scientific and management bodies responsible for evaluating the evidence, advising decision‐makers, and implementing shark conservation measures.

articles.title: A defined energy threshold in tribovoltaic catalysis for mechanical-to-chemical energy conversion
An Injectable Wet-Adhesive Hydrogel for Wireless Ultrasound-Driven Physico-Chemical Synergistic Repair of Cavernous Nerve Injury via Piezoelectricity and Nitric Oxide Release
Self-powered acoustic sensing based on triboelectric nanogenerators: Principle, fabrication, architecture, and intelligent applications
Sub-percolation engineering enables simultaneous mechanical reinforcement and triboelectric enhancement in coaxial chitosan/CNT fibers for wearable sensing
ZIF-8 derived polarity-engineered N-doped carbon/PAN nanofibers based triboelectric tactile sensors for AIoT applications
Balancing Fast Li-Ion Transport Kinetics and Mechanical Strength in PEO-Based Composite Solid Electrolytes through Minimal Dinitrile Incorporation
articles.abstract: Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) suffer from poor ionic conductivity because strong Li+–ether oxygen coordination restricts Li+ transport. Herein, we develop a competitive coordination strategy by introducing a minimal amount of hexanedinitrile (HDN; 2.30 wt %) into PEO CSEs. Its flexible tetramethylene spacer allows nitrile groups to compete with PEO for Li+, forming mobile Li(HDN)x+ species while largely preserving the polymer backbone. This design accelerates local Li+ migration and promotes interfacial Li+ exchange, mitigating the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized CSE-HDN achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.87 × 10–4 S cm–1 (60 °C) and a tensile strength of 1.08 MPa. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm–2, while Li||LiFePO4 cells retain 94.8% capacity after 250 cycles at 3C. These results identify competitive Li+–nitrile coordination as a strategy for designing high-performance PEO-based CSEs.

articles.title: Band-Engineering W18O49 with Cu Single Atoms Enables Efficient Photo-Induction of Oxygen Radicals for Highly Sensitive Room-Temperature NO2 Detection
articles.abstract: Metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors suffer from insufficient sensitivity and slow response/recovery due to inefficient charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics at room temperature. Herein, we demonstrated that single-atom Cu doping enabled precise band structure engineering of W18O49, thereby enabling photoassisted room-temperature NO2 detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. Single-atom Cu induced abundant oxygen vacancies and regulated the electronic configuration, facilitating oxygen radical generation and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the Cu1–W18O49 sensor exhibited a high response (RNO2/Rair = 572.3) toward 10 ppm of NO2 and excellent selectivity under light. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the formation of multiple nitrogen oxide species on the Cu1–W18O49 surface and revealed that the Cu doping induces a transformation of the NO3 adsorption configuration from a weak monodentate to a bidentate binding mode, highlighting the enhanced surface reactivity by Cu doping. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of high-performance photoactivated gas sensors.

articles.title: Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.

articles.title: Efficient Carrier Multiplication Beyond Mo- and W-Based Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Multilayer HfSe2 and ReSe2
articles.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are layered van der Waals semiconductors that can convert a single high-energy photon into multiple electron–hole pairs through carrier multiplication (CM). However, the factors governing CM efficiency within the TMDC family remain unclear, with studies limited to Mo- and W-based compositions. Here, we address this question by investigating HfSe2 and ReSe2, two less-explored TMDCs with markedly different electronic densities of states. Combining first-principles calculations with ultrafast optical spectroscopy, we establish the occurrence of efficient CM in both materials, with quantum yields 20–30% higher than those of previously studied multilayer TMDCs. Our analysis reveals that CM outcompetes phonon-mediated cooling. Furthermore, we observe similarly high CM efficiencies in HfSe2 and ReSe2 despite their vastly different number of possible CM pathways. This comparison reveals that the CM efficiency is mainly determined by the presence of at least a single CM decay pathway rather than the total number.

articles.title: High Refractive Index Silver Nanoparticle Metamaterials Approaching Fundamental Bounds
articles.abstract: Dense assemblies of metal nanoparticles offer a scalable route to high-index optical metamaterials, yet their collective response and loss mechanisms remain poorly understood. We synthesize quasi-spherical Ag nanoparticles with diameters ranging from 17 to 66 nm and assemble them into closely-packed monolayers. These films exhibit size-dependent refractive indices reaching a maximum of 10.3 with a low loss region emerging on the red shoulder of the resonance. We introduce a compact analytical model that quantitatively reproduces the measured optical constants and identifies the interparticle gap as the lever controlling the achievable index and loss. We compute Bergman-Milton fundamental limits, finding that our best assemblies reach two-thirds of the high-index–low-loss Pareto frontier for silver/polystyrene composites of arbitrary microstructure with the remaining samples approaching within a factor of 1.7–4. Together, experiment and theory establish silver nanoparticle assemblies as a tunable platform approaching fundamental bounds and define pathways for further performance gains.

articles.title: Mesoporosity Regulates Microbubble Emergence and Interfacial Bubble Accumulation during Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Gas bubbles generated during water electrolysis alter electrolyte access, ionic conduction, and local mass transport, thereby influencing electrochemical performance. Directly resolving this process is often challenging because numerous bubbles evolve and interact simultaneously on conventional gas-evolving electrodes. Here, we establish mesoporous Pt microelectrodes as a simplified model system to examine how the nanoscale porous architecture affects H2 bubble evolution relative to nonporous Pt electrodes with the same macroscopic disk geometry at matched nominal H2 generation rates. The mesoporous Pt electrode exhibited smaller detachment diameters and shorter detachment periods during single H2 bubble evolution in H2SO4. During multiple H2 bubble evolution in HClO4, the mesoporous electrode concentrated microbubble emergence into fewer locations and developed a less crowded near interface bubble population, with a smaller current-induced resistance increment. These results show how the nanoscale porous architecture can reorganize collective bubble evolution and thereby modify the associated ohmic penalty during electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution.

articles.title: Molecularly Addressable Nanoparticle-on-Mirror Cavity Arrays via DNA Origami-Mediated Template Assembly
articles.abstract: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities confine light within molecular gaps, but conventional drop casting does not register cavities at predefined coordinates. We integrate electron-beam lithography, face-selective DNA origami placement, and DNA-mediated gold-nanosphere docking to position molecularly programmable NPoMs on flat gold mirrors. Across six patches containing 2538 sites in total, the estimated mean single-particle occupation was approximately 84.7%. Dark-field spectra of cavities programmed with cyanine 5 (Cy5) show a split response centered near the Cy5 transition. Comparison with bare-cavity sweeps of facet width, gap thickness, and spacer index supports a molecularly anchored, Rabi-like interpretation of this response within a damped coupled-oscillator model. Photoluminescence controls reveal substantial gold luminescence, so dark-field scattering is used as the primary coupling observable. The platform therefore combines deterministic cavity registration with sequence-programmable molecular optical functionality.

articles.title: ROS-Responsive Selenocysteine-Releasing Nanozyme for Targeted Ferroptosis Suppression and Pancreatic β-Cell Protection in Type 2 Diabetes
articles.abstract: Pancreatic β-cell ferroptosis, driven by oxidative stress and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, has emerged as an important contributor to the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and insufficient selenocysteine (Sec) availability limit GPX4-dependent antioxidant defense, making effective ferroptosis intervention challenging. Here, we engineered a ROS-responsive Sec-loaded copper-based single-atom nanozyme (Se@CuSAzyme) that combines catalytic ROS scavenging with Sec supplementation. Benefiting from its intrinsic superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities, Se@CuSAzyme efficiently eliminated excessive ROS, while oxidative stress-triggered Sec release enhanced GPX4 expression. As a result, Se@CuSAzyme markedly suppressed high glucose and erastin-induced ferroptosis, reduced lipid peroxidation, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in pancreatic β-cells. In high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, Se@CuSAzyme demonstrated therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of metformin in ameliorating hyperglycemia, alleviating insulin resistance, and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, Se@CuSAzyme outperformed metformin in protecting against hepatic steatosis and glycolipid metabolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Single-Layer Diverse Chiral Metasurfaces Driven by Generative AI
articles.abstract: Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.

articles.title: Stereochemical Optimization Boosts the Chemotherapeutic Efficacy of Isomeric Bile Salt-Aquated Cisplatin Nanocomplexes
articles.abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP) requires a rate-limiting intracellular aquation to generate aquated cisplatin (aqCDDP) for DNA binding and exertion of oncostatic effects. On this basis, three isomeric bile salt-aqCDDP nanocomplexes (12α-SDC@CDDP, 7α-SCDC@CDDP, and 7β-SUDC@CDDP) were constructed to directly deliver aqCDDP. Although 7β-SUDC@CDDP exhibited the optimal pharmacokinetics, poor cellular uptake resulted in limited tumor accumulation and insufficient antitumor activity. For 7α-SCDC@CDDP, the nonspecific distribution in the liver and lung resulted in suboptimal antitumor activity. Notably, 12α-SDC@CDDP demonstrated 3-fold higher tumor accumulation than CDDP solution and the best antitumor activity owing to its highest cellular uptake. These results revealed that the stereochemical configuration of the hydroxyl group on bile salts regulated the trade-off between systemic circulation and cellular internalization, with 12α-hydroxylation favoring uptake and 7β-hydroxylation favoring circulation. These findings provided guiding implications for future bile salt–platinum nanomedicine design, particularly through stereochemical regulation to improve therapeutic performance.

articles.title: Super-Toughness Self-Healing MOF-Based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Reaction-Transport Coupling Regulates Transportation of Ions and Polysulfides in High-Performance Solid-State Li–S Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium–sulfur batteries have emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems due to high theoretical energy density and low cost. However, the practical application is severely hindered by issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish ion transport, and lithium dendrite growth. Here, we proposed a synergistic strategy based on nanoconfinement polymerization and self-healing dynamic cross-linking to successfully fabricate a self-healing composite solid electrolyte, composed of PVDF-HFP, graphene oxide, UiO-66, linear polydopamine chains, and a boronic ester cross-linked network. The electrolyte demonstrates high ionic conductivity (1.7 × 10–4 S cm–1), good puncture resistance (9.7 N), high elongation at break (335%), and superior capacity retention (a capacity decay rate of 0.0276% per cycle over 500 cycles). Even under a high sulfur loading of 4 mg cm–2, the capacity retention remained as high as 94.8%, which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. This strategy offers a new pathway to designing advanced solid electrolytes for high-energy batteries.

articles.title: A genome‑wide screen in E. coli reveals metabolic adaptations that enhance intratumoral fitness and bacterial cancer therapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. Here, through a genome‑wide functional screen, we identify the bacterial genes and pathways that govern intratumoral fitness. Targeted deletion of nonglucose phosphotransferase systems to align bacterial metabolic preference with tumor metabolite availability promotes bacterial intratumoral fitness. Integrating multiple metabolic adaptations into a single tumor‑avid Escherichia coli strain (Ec‑TA) results in increased tumor colonization, not only after intratumoral delivery but also after intravenous delivery, leading to increased anti‑tumor efficacy when using Ec‑TA engineered to deliver an encoded immunostimulatory payload. Furthermore, Ec‑TA displaces wild‑type bacteria from pre‑colonized tumors when administered systemically, underscoring its potential for locally delivering therapeutics in the presence of resident tumor microbes. These data demonstrate that adapting bacteria to the unique characteristics of the tumor metabolic microenvironment can drive the development of safer and more effective chassis for next‑generation bacterial cancer therapies.

articles.title: AI for detection of adverse events in the real world
articles.abstract: Immune-related adverse events are common in cancer immunotherapy and can be difficult to recognize in clinical routine. Work now shows that an agentic AI system built around a large language model can identify such events in prospectively collected clinical notes and can make human review of such notes faster and more consistent.

articles.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study
articles.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F 1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F 1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F 1 was 0.72–0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min ( P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01–2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).

articles.title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
articles.abstract: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.

articles.title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

articles.title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
articles.abstract: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

articles.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections
articles.abstract: Wang and colleagues show that autophagy deficiency in alveolar macrophages upregulates the expression of IL-1α and increases resistance to respiratory infections.

articles.title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
articles.abstract: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.

articles.title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
articles.abstract: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.

articles.abstract: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.

articles.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial
articles.abstract: A 5-year secondary analysis of the phase 2 PHERGain trial supports the clinical utility of a PET-guided adaptive strategy for treatment de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and provides circulating tumor DNA insights that could inform further treatment approaches.

articles.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
articles.abstract: A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.

articles.title: A small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Preclinical analysis and a phase 1 trial support VG-3927 as a promising drug candidate for Alzheimer’s disease, demonstrating successful penetration of the central nervous system, target engagement and tolerability.

articles.title: Applying digital twins to prevent preterm births
articles.abstract: Researchers developed a digital twin framework to safely evaluate the effects of drugs on the immune system and time to labor, which could enable personalized interventions to prevent preterm births.

articles.title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum
articles.abstract: A high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas of 189 colorectal tumors from patients aged 20–90+ years uncovers age-associated features of colorectal cancer.

articles.abstract: This Article presents a large-scale analysis of self-supervised learning methods for high-content morphological profiling.

articles.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends
articles.abstract: The computational tool JEEPERS detects and corrects jagged-end-induced errors in cell-free DNA methylation analysis, demonstrating improved performance in multiple applications, such as cancer detection and monitoring.
