articles.title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
articles.abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

articles.title: When AI takes away the thrill of discovery
articles.abstract: “Pure math is being devastated or revolutionized, depending on your point of view.” So said Cornell professor Steven Strogatz after the artificial intelligence (AI) company OpenAI announced in early September a potential solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems that represent the highest goals for mathematical proofs. OpenAI’s solution involved unleashing an army of AI agents at a cost of millions of dollars in computing power, and it also certainly drew on decades of human effort in mathematics before it. Then a few weeks later, OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts describing progress on 372 mathematical problem families, and Google DeepMind published (in Science ) solutions from their own AI math system. These events are potentially exciting for those who long to know the answers to these problems as soon as possible, but they have also sent the world of mathematics reeling, and pose an even bigger question for all fields: Can the satisfaction of understanding ever replace the thrill of discovery?

articles.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
articles.abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

articles.title: Wind turbines kill ‘shocking’ number of bats each year
articles.abstract: Deaths can be prevented by adjusting when wind turbines operate

articles.title: Budget 2026: NHS gets AI productivity review and winter pressure fund—but little else for health and social care
articles.abstract: An independent review of NHS productivity and future ringfenced spending on prevention have been announced in the government’s 2026 budget, the first under prime minister Andy Burnham.An additional £190m was announced to support the NHS response to winter pressures. But no direct share of this pot has been set aside to support general practices.Unveiled by chancellor John Healey on 28 October, the budget had, overall, much less on the NHS and adult social care than in previous years, with the main focus instead on household bills.The BMA’s chair of council, Tom Dolphin, said, “For a government that claims to put the NHS at the heart of its priorities, this budget falls worryingly short.“The failure to set out meaningful action to tackle crumbling buildings or ensure we have enough doctors to meet future demand raises serious questions about the government’s commitment to the health service’s long term future.”David Williams, deputy director...

articles.title: Endometriosis: earlier diagnosis without meaningful access to treatment is only half the solution
articles.abstract: Busby and Uppal highlight the unacceptable diagnostic delays faced by women with suspected endometriosis.1 A delay of almost a decade is indefensible. But this discussion risks creating the impression that earlier diagnosis alone will transform outcomes. For many patients, it will not.As someone who has had severe pelvic pain for years, I find myself asking a more uncomfortable question: what happens after diagnosis?Laparoscopy is invasive, costly to health systems, and carries surgical risks. Understandably, patients welcome the possibility of non-invasive biomarkers. But obtaining a diagnosis is only the beginning of the journey. Many women, despite finally receiving confirmation, are offered hormonal treatments that have already failed or prolonged analgesia, or they are placed onto waiting lists for surgery, where they can stay for years. Even expert excision surgery is not universally curative, recurrence remains common, and many people continue to live with chronic pain despite “successful” treatment.The consequence is that...

articles.title: Hundreds of GP websites crash after online provider enters administration
articles.abstract: “Questions must be asked” about the lack of warning before hundreds of practice websites went offline after an online provider entered administration, GP leaders say.They have also questioned why there doesn’t seem to be a coordinated national contingency plan for the failure of a provider delivering critical NHS infrastructure.Hundreds of general practice websites in England and Wales suddenly went offline on 28 October after their online provider—Silicon Practice—entered administration.The software company claimed on its website to provide services for more than 1000 general practices.NHS England said that less than 500 practices had been affected—under 10% of the total number of practices in England and Wales.Reacting, Sarah Jacques, GP co-lead of the Doctors’ Association UK. said: “The sudden loss of websites and online consultation services across hundreds of [general] practices is deeply concerning.”“These are no longer optional extras; they are essential routes through which patients access care.”A notice of administration was...

articles.title: India caps mark-ups on 137 cancer drugs after court highlights 900% price difference
articles.abstract: India has ordered a cap on the marked up prices of 137 cancer drugs amid increasing concern that high prices are pushing households into debt or putting treatment out of reach.The nation’s drug price regulator, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), said trade margins on the drugs would be capped at 30% of their maximum retail price (MRP), excluding tax, from 9 November.1The measure aims to lower prices charged to patients by limiting the margins added by distributors and retailers but does not directly cap the prices initially charged by manufacturers.Previously, only 20% of India’s estimated Rs125bn ($1.3bn; £986m; €1.2bn) cancer drug market was under NPPA price control. An NPPA analysis of market data, published in October, found that non-scheduled cancer drugs had an average trade mark-up of around 170%, reaching 700% or more in some cases.2The 137 drugs covered by the order include abemaciclib, bevacizumab, cetuximab, pemetrexed, palbociclib, pembrolizumab,...

articles.title: RCGP does U turn on policy that put assisted dying on par with arms dealers
articles.abstract: An “ethical policy” that prevented assisted dying campaign groups from hosting events at the Royal College of General Practitioners will be “reviewed and amended,” the college pledged today.This reversal comes after the campaign group Dignity in Dying was prevented from hosting a GP led event at the college’s London headquarters, prompting outrage among RCGP members and terminally ill patients.Dignity in Dying said that terminally and incurably ill people had hoped to share their experiences with clinicians, parliamentarians, and policy makers at the event.Until Thursday the RCGP website listed assisted dying alongside various groups and industries, including those involved in arms manufacturing, adult entertainment, and fossil fuel exploration, that are banned from holding events at the college’s 30 Euston Square headquarters.1“30 Euston Square is not permitted to accommodate meetings, events, or corporate membership from any organisation engaged with assisted dying or any event where its purpose is to promote and lobby...

articles.title: Strongman politics, women’s health according to Trump, and how to save the world
articles.abstract: For the optimists among us, two election results this week portend hope for two more next week. Serbia’s student led movement defeated the country’s former president, strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic, in its 24 October prime ministerial election, six months after Hungary rejected its long serving populist prime minister, Viktor Orban. On 26 October, Brazilians delivered a surprise re-election of President Luiz Inacio “Lula” da Silva, defeating the far right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro. By 1 November a final result should be known of how Israelis voted in what’s seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, ahead of the US midterm elections on 3 November, where tough guy Donald Trump’s supporters and his stranglehold on Congress will be tested by the growing discontent of American voters. A rebound of liberal or progressive values is being read into these election trends—but they are, in truth, accompanied by stark divisiveness and contestation.The broader...

articles.title: [Articles] Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.abstract: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

articles.title: [Comment] Beyond poverty eradication: what China's health and poverty alleviation experience means for global health
articles.abstract: The Lancet Commission on the Health and Poverty Alleviation Initiative in China1 arrives at an important moment for global health. Progress towards universal health coverage (UHC) has slowed in many countries,2 with catastrophic health expenditure continuing to push households into poverty. Geopolitical conflict, faltering multilateralism, and economic factors such as inflation have made it more challenging to address global poverty eradication and health goals. The relationship between health and poverty has long been recognised, yet policy responses often remain fragmented.

articles.title: [Comment] Faster troponin, same time in the emergency department: what is next for acute coronary syndrome assessment?
articles.abstract: Emergency department overcrowding and access block are now among the most consequential patient-safety problems facing acute hospitals globally.1 The associated harm is measurable, dose-dependent, and has no clearly safe threshold beyond approximately 5 h.2 Patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction constitute a large and possibly modifiable share of the emergency department burden. Chest pain is the second most common reason for adult emergency department attendance in the USA, accounting for approximately 8 million encounters annually and around 5·5% of all emergency department visits.

articles.title: [Editorial] Health and poverty: lessons from China
articles.abstract: The world has never been wealthier. Yet in 2025, an estimated 831 million people lived on less than US$3 per day. This stark disparity exposes a systemic failure to translate global prosperity into basic security and opportunity for all. As slowing economic growth and multiple crises, such as conflict and climate change, undermine the momentum of global poverty reduction, governments now face a pressing test: whether they will still find, reach, and protect those already furthest behind, or allow them to fall deeper into poverty.

articles.title: [Review] Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut–brain interaction
articles.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut–brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut–brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity.

articles.title: [The Lancet Commissions] A Lancet Commission on the Health and Poverty Alleviation Initiative in China
articles.abstract: Poverty alleviation is a pressing global challenge that is intricately linked with health, as emphasised by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In 2019, out-of-pocket health expenditure—health-care costs paid directly by individuals or households rather than covered by insurance or other third-party payers—pushed an additional 344 million people into poverty globally. In 2020, 724 million people were living in extreme poverty, defined as living on less than US$2·15 per person per day at 2017 purchasing power parity, 90 million more than the pre-COVID-19 pandemic UN projection.

articles.title: Accelerated aging and early-onset colorectal cancer
articles.abstract: The rising incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) challenges existing paradigms of tumorigenesis. Classical models based on cumulative mutational burden, environmental exposure, and hereditary predisposition fail to explain the emergence of malignancy in individuals under 50 years of age. In this review, we propose that EOCRC may be driven by accelerated biological aging and review how core aging processes are prematurely activated in EOCRC. Importantly, these alterations extend beyond the tumor microenvironment and are present in circulating immune cells and inflammatory mediators. We propose that EOCRC develops prematurely in response to environmental, metabolic, genetic, and related factors that systemically accelerate biological aging. This approach reconciles the origin of EOCRC with traditional models of tumorigenesis, while highlighting novel opportunities for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Peripersonal space: a neural system mapping self–environment interaction ‘here and now’
articles.abstract: The space surrounding the body where physical interactions with external stimuli occur is referred to as peripersonal space (PPS). Traditionally conceived as a spatial construct, PPS is better understood as a neural representation that integrates bodily inputs with external cues to predict body–object interactions. After summarizing its multisensory, motor, and plastic properties, this review draws on computational models to examine how PPS captures statistical regularities of body–object interactions. This predictive function may position PPS as an interface between self and environment, contributing to minimal self-consciousness and its alterations across states of consciousness and neuropsychiatric conditions. Recent findings extend this framework to the inner body, suggesting that interoceptive signals shape PPS and that PPS-related processing may influence immune responses.

articles.title: A Geometry-Induced Finite Warburg element for Reversible Diffusion Impedance at Microdisk Electrodes
articles.abstract: A compact analytical representation is developed for the diffusion impedance of a disk electrode under reversible conditions, obtained by transforming the chronoamperometric relaxation function into the frequency domain. A Padé approximant is constructed for the uniform-concentration boundary condition, preserving the finite low-frequency diffusion resistance of the steady-state disk current and the high-frequency Cottrell regime. It is extended to reactions in which both oxidized and reduced species contribute, with unequal diffusion coefficients and surface concentrations. Its accuracy is quantified against converged numerical solutions, including an exact solution of the coupled problem with finite-rate kinetics. The approximant reproduces the Saito resistance and the $45^{\circ}$ Warburg phase exactly; its modulus is within 0.6\% of the converged solution for $ωa^2/D\le12$ and 7\% below the Cottrell amplitude at high frequency. The uniform-concentration and uniform-flux boundary conditions both give a diffusion impedance of geometric origin, but differ by up to 11\% in modulus because each couples differently to the spreading diffusion field; a criterion based on the rate constant and the disk radius delineates where each applies. The exact solution shows that this crossover is broad and that the decomposition into a charge-transfer resistance and a diffusion impedance is accurate to about 5\% for $1\le2k^0a/D\le100$. Fitted to a published spectrum of a platinum microdisk, it reproduces the reported diffusion coefficient within 1\%, while the two limiting elements lie 4.8\% below and 4.1\% above it. The element is a practical tool for microdisk impedance analysis.

articles.title: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities
articles.abstract: Polaritonic chemistry holds the promise of controlling chemical reactivity through confined light-matter interactions, yet how reactions respond inside optical cavities remains debated. Here, we take a more zoomed-out view, inspired by electrostatic catalysis. We extend nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to cavity-modified reactions and show that their behavior falls into four distinct reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions can follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior regardless of cavity tuning, or switch between the two as the cavity frequency is varied. We establish this picture analytically and demonstrate it in the Shin Metiu model and in four molecular reactions treated with ab initio electronic-structure methods. Even at this deliberately coarse-grained level, cavity-modified reactivity already shows qualitatively different and strongly counterintuitive behavior, including reactions that switch character with cavity frequency. Yet this complexity can still be reduced to a simple competition between permanent-dipole and polarizability responses. This reaction-type classification therefore provides a new route to organize and anticipate cavity-modified reactivity.

articles.title: Development of a Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Transition State Search in Molecular Systems: A Transferable Model Across Structural and Dimensional Variations
articles.abstract: We developed a DRL approach for TS searches combining the deep Q-network and the bidirectional long short-term memory architectures to handle variable-sized molecular systems. We applied our method to 1,3,5-hexatriene (Triene), alanine dipeptide (Ala2), and 1,3,5,7-octatetraene (Tetraene) as target systems with the search space limited to backbone dihedral angles. Our model successfully learned the TS search tasks for all examined systems. More importantly, we demonstrate that our model pre-trained on Triene exhibits distinct transfer-learning capabilities across both backbone modifications (Triene to Ala2) and chain extensions (Triene to Tetraene). Such transferability is highly promising for future applications to molecules in general, as it allows an agent trained on simple systems to accelerate TS searches in larger or more complex ones. We expect that these findings on cross-system transferability represent an important step forward in developing DRL-based approaches for TS searches.

articles.title: Differentiable Electronic Grand Canonical Learning for Electrochemistry
articles.abstract: Electronic grand-canonical density functional theory captures how structure and electronic charge respond to electrode potential and, together with statistical mechanics, how these responses give rise to emergent phenomena. However, its computational cost limits the system sizes and sampling times accessible to first- principles simulations. Here, we introduce a differentiable architecture that represents the grand potential and obtains forces and electronic charge as its derivatives, exactly satisfying the mixed-derivative constraints required for thermodynamic consistency, and implement it within the equivariant MACE framework as GC- MACE. We demonstrate more accurate joint learning across multiple electrochemical interfaces and improved transferability to thicker water films relative to previous models, while enabling constant-potential simulations at substantially larger length and time scales than accessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. With broad training data, the framework offers a route to thermodynamically consistent foundation interatomic potentials for the electronic grand canonical ensemble

articles.title: Distilling Large-Scale Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials to Predict Long-Timescale Electrolyte Transport Properties
articles.abstract: Accurately predicting the transport properties of liquid electrolytes is critical for next-generation battery design and requires force fields that are both quantum-mechanically accurate and fast enough for long-timescale simulation. Recent large-scale pretrained machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approach density-functional-theory accuracy, but remain too slow to access the necessary timescales to converge transport properties. We provide a knowledge distillation procedure to transfer the accuracy of a large-scale "teacher" MLIP into fast, system-specific "students", without any additional ab initio data. Our distilled models run ~40x faster, reproduce teacher-predicted structural observables, and produce stable 20 ns trajectories in days, rather than the months the teacher would require. Across a diverse set of sodium- and lithium-ion electrolytes, student-predicted self-diffusivities, ionic conductivities, and shear viscosities track experiment and outperform classical force-field predictions, establishing distillation as a practical route to accurate, long-timescale simulations necessary for high-throughput electrolyte screening.

articles.title: Lateral opening site of human oligopeptide transporter 2 plays a key role in the interaction with polymyxins
articles.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria pose a critical global health threat, while polymyxins remain a last-line therapy. However, their clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity. Human oligopeptide transporter 2 (hPepT2) is a membrane transporter mediating the reabsorption of polymyxins in renal cells and contributes to their nephrotoxicity, but the molecular basis of their interaction remains unclear. Here, we investigated the structure-interaction relationship (SIR) of polymyxins with hPepT2 by integrating computational, chemical, and cell biology approaches. Bioinformatic modeling predicted an outward-facing hPepT2 structure and a potential transport pathway, with polymyxins interacting at the lateral opening, particularly E214, D215, D317, D342, and E622. Transporter mutagenesis and molecular analyses confirmed that D215 is critical for polymyxin binding, while other residues influence transporter turnover and/or expression. We subsequently synthesized polymyxin analogs with modifications at Dab1, Dab3, Dab5, and Dab9 of polymyxins, which reduced interactions with hPepT2. Notably, alanine substitution at Dab3 reduced nephrotoxicity in mice while retaining antibacterial activity. Overall, this proof-of-concept study demonstrates that the hPepT2-polymyxin SIR model provides a viable strategy for developing novel, safer lipopeptide antibiotics.

articles.title: Lymphatic vessels under pressure
articles.abstract: Lymphatic vessels beat faster as they fill with fluid through a chain of calcium signaling, though the first pressure sensor remains a mystery.

articles.title: Molecular and functional analysis of calcium binding by a cancer-linked calreticulin mutant
articles.abstract: Calreticulin (CRT) is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone with low-affinity calcium-binding sites in its C-terminal domain. This region is altered by somatic mutations in the CRT gene (CALR), which drive a subset of myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). Perturbations in ER calcium storage and signaling are reported for the MPN type I mutant, CRTDel52, and are linked to disease pathogenesis. Using recombinant CRT proteins, we found similar low-affinity calcium-binding characteristics for wild-type CRT and CRTDel52, as determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Residues 340–349, conserved in both wild-type CRT and CRTDel52, contribute to binding. Furthermore, ER and cytosolic calcium levels, and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE), were comparable in CRT knockout (CRT-KO) cells reconstituted with wild-type CRT or CRTDel52. Notably, the CRT-KO induces expression of multiple ER proteins known to contain low-affinity calcium-binding sites or regulate ER calcium levels. Overall, these findings indicate that CRTDel52 retains at least some low-affinity calcium-binding capacity and that CRT deficiency induces compensatory cellular changes that maintain ER calcium homeostasis.

articles.title: Revealing the benefit of eye motion for acuity under emulated cone loss
articles.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases progressively erode the cone photoreceptor mosaic, reducing the retina’s spatial sampling power, yet visual acuity is remarkably resilient to cone loss. Prior work has shown that clinically normal visual acuity (20/25 or better) can persist despite up to 50% of cone cells being lost (Ratnam et al., 2013; Foote et al., 2018). However, studies on individuals with retinal degeneration cannot control for patients’ stage of disease progression, creating the need for an experimental paradigm that can mimic these diseases in healthy subjects. The Oz Vision system creates visual percepts through programmable, per-cell stimulation of thousands of cone cells. We reprogram this system to emulate cone loss in healthy eyes by withholding stimulation from a subset of randomly selected cones, rendering them inactive, in a method we term ‘cone dropout’. Using this approach, we characterize the visual system’s robustness to cone loss, showing that visual acuity declines nonlinearly with increasing cone dropout. Importantly, we uncover the compensatory benefit that eye motion provides under cone-deprived conditions, finding that at the highest level of dropout, a visual system with eye motion has an equivalent acuity to a static dropout condition with nearly twice as many sampling elements. Through analysis of eye motion and stimulation data, we find that this benefit arises from the additional information accumulated by ‘surviving’ cones as they sample more of the letter through fixational eye motion.

articles.title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling
articles.abstract: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis – a major metabolic use of this amino acid – was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Gls, the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into mouse B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired. Otherwise, it was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, that is, the conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival, involved supporting progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

articles.title: Whole-brain mapping of spinal-projecting neurons in larval zebrafish
articles.abstract: To elicit voluntary movements and integrative reflexes underlying behavior, the brain sends command signals to the spinal cord via specialized long-range descending neurons, known as spinal-projecting neurons (SPNs). The vast and widespread distribution of SPNs, combined with their complex long-distance connectivity, poses a significant challenge for mapping their anatomical organization and associating specific populations with distinct functions. Here, we took advantage of the transparency and genetic accessibility of larval zebrafish to uncover the fundamental principles of SPN anatomical organization in a teleost. Using an optical backfilling method relying on photoactivable GFP, we generate a whole-brain map of all neurons sending axons toward the spinal cord. This approach reveals far more SPNs than previously described through conventional strategies, offering an unparalleled opportunity to revisit distinct spinal-projecting nuclei distributed across the hindbrain, midbrain, and diencephalic structures. Combining information on cell location, morphology, and projection patterns, we propose tentative homological designations for zebrafish of SPN nuclei based on established descriptions in mammals and other vertebrates.

articles.title: Competitive Interactions between Propylene Combustion Products Regulate Catalyst Durability over Facet-Tuned Pt/TiO2
articles.abstract: While product-induced inhibition is widely recognized in heterogeneous catalysis, the joint influence of co-generated products on time-dependent catalytic deactivation remains underexplored. Herein, uniform colloidal Pt nanoparticles were deposited on anatase TiO2 supports selectively exposing (101) or (001) facets to fabricate two facet-controlled model Pt/TiO2 catalysts. We uncovered the intrinsic deactivation mechanism for low-temperature lean propylene combustion via stability tests, alternating feed kinetics, in situ DRIFTS, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-on-stream reaction tests recorded persistent activity decay for both catalysts, with far more serious decay observed on Pt/TiO2(101). Multiple characterization results excluded Pt sintering/encapsulation, C3H6/O2 poisoning, and partial Pt oxidation as dominant degradation factors. Instead, CO2 adsorption and subsequent carbonate accumulation on TiO2 surfaces were identified as the primary deactivation sources, which cut off supplementary oxygen delivery at metal–support interfaces. DFT adsorption energy data proved that H2O possessed a stronger surface affinity than CO2 on both facet types, and in situ generated H2O competed for adsorption sites to curb carbonate accumulation. Apart from this competitive effect, reaction-derived H2O alleviated excessive coverage of Pt sites by C3H6 and facilitated the adsorption and activation of gas-phase O2. Thanks to the relatively high water-binding capacity of TiO2(001), the corresponding Pt/TiO2(001) catalyst maintained abundant interfacial water during operation and exhibited much milder carbonate-triggered decay. These findings clarified the competitive co-adsorption interplay between CO2 and H2O across Pt–TiO2 interfaces and offered general kinetic guidance for developing durable catalysts toward industrial hydrocarbon lean combustion.

articles.title: Electrolyte Cation Engineering Selectively Regulates Competing Urea Oxidation Pathways
articles.abstract: The electrochemical urea oxidation reaction (UOR) has emerged as an attractive anodic reaction for various energy conversion systems. Recently, increasing attention has been directed toward controlling UOR selectivity on Ni-based electrocatalysts following the recognition that the UOR can produce over-oxidized products. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on catalyst design to regulate surface-bound intermediates, whereas whether electrolyte-mediated noncovalent interactions can selectively control competing UOR pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we show that rational electrolyte engineering using alkali-metal cations selectively regulates the UOR pathway by modulating the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. Electrochemical rate deconvolution and product analysis reveal that weakly hydrated cations selectively accelerate the direct oxidation pathway, promoting the formation of the over-oxidized NO2– and NCO– products, while leaving the indirect pathway essentially unaffected. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measurements, together with molecular dynamics simulations of cation hydration dynamics, indicate that weakly hydrated cations create a more dynamic interfacial water environment with faster water exchange, thereby facilitating interfacial OH–-mediated successive dehydrogenation during direct urea oxidation. Leveraging this mechanistic understanding, the electrolyte-engineering strategy was applied to a cascade urea-to-ammonia conversion system, achieving a urea-to-ammonia conversion efficiency of 77.5% and approximately threefold higher ammonia productivity in CsOH than in LiOH. These findings establish electrolyte engineering as a complementary strategy to catalyst design and highlight noncovalent electrolyte–electrode interactions as an effective handle for controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity in an integrated UOR-based nitrogen conversion system.

articles.title: Hydrogen-Ion-Mediated Ni/Ni(OH)2 Dual Sites to Synergistically Accelerate *OH/Organics Adsorption for Highly Efficient Electrochemical 5-Amino-1 H -tetrazole Electrooxidation within a Wide Potential Range
articles.abstract: Nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole compounds are essential structural scaffolds for energetic materials, dyes, and agrochemicals, owing to their favorable energetic and physicochemical properties. Potassium 5,5′-azotetrazolate (PZT), as a representative and efficient nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole material, is conventionally synthesized via thermochemical oxidative coupling, which suffers from safety hazards and environmental pollution. Electrochemical synthesis offers a compelling alternative, but the severe competitive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) impedes achieving highly-efficient N–N coupling activity and Faradaic efficiency (FE). Herein, a core–shell CF@CuO@Ni/Ni(OH)2 electrode is fabricated through controlled H+-mediated electrodeposition. The CF@CuO core provides a three-dimensional (3D) conductive scaffold and suppresses the competing OER, while the Ni0/Ni(OH)2 shell undergoes electrochemical reconstruction into coexisting NiO/NiOOH working phases. The catalyst reaches 10 mA·cm–2 at 1.16 V vs RHE and maintains a Faradaic efficiency above 94% over a broad potential range of 1.2–1.6 V. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational analyses prove that surface-adsorbed *OH initiates 5-AT dehydrogenative coupling via a PCET pathway on the reconstructed NiO/NiOOH surface. NiO triggers synergistic *OH/5-AT adsorption, while NiOOH facilitates dehydrogenation. In a continuous-flow AEM electrolyzer, the system operates at 500 mA cm–2 over 300 h while sustaining PZT production (purity ≥99%) and H2 evolution. Extension to DAT and DAF further demonstrates the transferability of the catalyst toward related amino-functionalized N-heterocycles undergoing oxidative N–N coupling. This work establishes that reconstructed NiO/NiOOH dual sites, supported on an OER-suppressing CuO scaffold, enable selective and energy-efficient N–N oxidative coupling of amino heterocycles.

articles.title: Simultaneous Stabilization of Copper Species and Regulation of the Cu+/Cu0 Balance on SiO2 for Selective Ethanol Dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Selective ethanol dehydrogenation is a promising route for acetaldehyde production; however, achieving stable copper catalysts on inert supports with a well-balanced Cu+/Cu0 ratio remains challenging. Herein, we report a urea-assisted strategy to simultaneously stabilize copper species and regulate the Cu+/Cu0 balance on a silica support. The gradual release of ammonia promotes the formation of interfacial Cu–O–Si linkages and basic copper nitrate species, which serve as precursors for Cu+ and Cu0, respectively. The resulting catalyst exhibits highly dispersed copper species with a balanced Cu+/Cu0 distribution, delivering high activity, >95% acetaldehyde selectivity, and stable performance in ethanol dehydrogenation. Mechanistic studies reveal that Cu+ sites facilitate ethanol activation, while Cu0 sites promote C–H bond cleavage. However, excessive Cu+ species lead to the formation of strongly adsorbed enolic intermediates, which trigger C–C coupling and byproduct formation. This work highlights the importance of Cu+/Cu0 synergy and provides a general strategy for designing stable and selective copper-based catalysts on inert supports.

articles.title: A 2.2 V Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Enabled by Passive pH Decoupling
articles.abstract: Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.

articles.title: Current Density as a Critical Factor Governing the Cycle Life of Polysulfide-Based Redox Flow Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.

articles.title: Operando Raman Spectroscopy-Guided 24-Hour Aging Assessment of Activated Carbon Positive Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Capacitors
articles.abstract: While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.

articles.title: Heterogeneity enabled unexpected hexagonal-to-face-centered cubic phase transformation and twinning for strength-ductility synergy in harmonic-structured titanium
Fluxes and Functions of the Sphingolipid Cycle Within the Tumor Microenvironment
articles.abstract: Sphingolipids are a bioactive family of lipids essential for maintaining the physical and chemical properties of membranes and acting as signaling messenger molecules. Recent studies have illuminated the cell biological roles that these lipids play in cancer contexts. These lipids are implicated across cancer types, playing roles in cell death, proliferative signaling, and therapeutic responses. Here, we review findings describing the roles of ceramide, sphingomyelin, glycosphingolipids, and sphingosine-1-phosphate in the cell-intrinsic mechanistic functions in malignancy and in the cross talk that occurs between diverse cell types within the tumor microenvironment. We describe how these diverse lipids operate in a sphingolipid cycle with numerous inputs and outputs spanning organelles and cells across the tumor microenvironment. We also discuss the contributions of this pathway to the metastatic cascade. Finally, we summarize previous therapeutic shortcomings and the current outlook of targeted therapeutic strategies, contextualizing our existing knowledge within their respective clinical applications.

articles.title: Chemical Ecology and Management of Imported Fire Ants
articles.abstract: Imported fire ants ( Solenopsis invicta and S. richteri ) are invasive pests that were introduced into the United States via Mobile, Alabama, in the early twentieth century. As these species spread, interbreeding led to the emergence of hybrid populations. Their rapid expansion and ecological dominance prompted extensive control efforts, including chemical eradication campaigns and biologically informed strategies. Today, fire ants infest over 140 million hectares across the southern United States, affecting public health, agriculture, and ecosystems. Despite decades of research, many fire ant semiochemicals remain unidentified because of the ants’ complex social behavior and because multicomponent chemical signals occur in trace amounts and are difficult to isolate, especially those involved in aerial mating. Additionally, components often lack activity unless presented in specific combinations. These challenges limit traditional bioassay-guided structure elucidation. This review summarizes advances in fire ant chemical ecology, highlights persistent knowledge gaps, and proposes innovative strategies to accelerate pheromone discovery and improve management.

articles.title: The Regulatory Landscape of Insecticide Resistance Evolution in Arthropod Pests
articles.abstract: Insecticide resistance threatens global agriculture and public health, highlighting the need to understand its underlying molecular mechanisms. Transcriptional regulation is a major component of resistance evolution, shaping the temporal, spatial, and quantitative expression of resistance-associated genes. Accumulating evidence indicates that cis -regulatory variation and trans -acting factors frequently underpin this transcriptional reprogramming, while gene duplication provides additional dosage effects. Emerging studies further implicate RNA-mediated mechanisms as additional regulatory layers. These processes often operate through defined signaling pathways, particularly MAPK-mediated networks, that coordinate the expression of detoxification enzymes and transporters, enabling rapid adaptation while shaping associated fitness trade-offs. Dissecting these complex networks through multi-omics and functional genomics can help clarify the evolutionary architecture of metabolic resistance and provide a basis for improved resistance monitoring and management.

articles.title: X-Ray Imaging in Entomology
articles.abstract: X-ray imaging provides fascinating insights into insect morphology, physiology, behavior, and evolution. In recent years, microcomputed tomography, in particular, has emerged as an indispensable tool for studying insects in three dimensions, ushering in a new digital era for insect morphological research. Thanks to the increasing accessibility of X-ray imaging systems along with innovations such as dose-efficient and high-throughput imaging, the technique is thriving. This review surveys the current landscape of X-ray imaging in entomology, outlining key techniques and analysis workflows and highlighting the diverse ways in which X-ray imaging is used to address fundamental and applied questions in insect science. Furthermore, it discusses emerging trends, such as AI-driven analysis and large-scale digitization, as well as the challenges and opportunities these developments pose for the future of integrative entomology.

articles.title: Conservative Management of Kidney Failure
articles.abstract: The default therapy for end-stage kidney disease is often dialysis, but for those with advanced age and multimorbidity, it may not provide significant benefit to longevity or quality of life. Conservative management (CM) is a holistic care pathway for those whose care preferences do not align with dialysis. CM aims to optimize quality of life over the disease course as patient priorities evolve and their disease progresses. Components of CM include customized chronic kidney disease care, symptom management, and navigation of transitions of care, including end-of-life care. Nephrology clinicians are the central providers of CM and ideally collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to provide medical, psychosocial, and spiritual care.

articles.title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins
articles.abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

articles.title: Communicating Climate-Related Risks via Storytelling and Statistics
articles.abstract: Strategies are needed to effectively communicate the public health effects associated with climate change–amplified events, e.g., floods, wildfires, and heat waves. This review explores ways to translate complex statistics and present other critical aspects of climate change using storytelling (through narratives, exemplars, and images) to engage people and maximize comprehension and healthy behaviors. We also examine how to shape the strategy or strategies used based on audience characteristics such as adult age, numeracy, literacy, and ideology. We delineate the key psychological levers through which these strategies work—effort reduction, emotions, psychological distance, efficacy, and presence of relevant numbers—and propose a barrier-matched framework to choose communication approaches. We also illustrate key concepts with case studies. Developing long-term capacity to deliver effective messages is one step toward empowering people to act safely in response to threats, build a more resilient society, enhance quality of life, and save money and lives.

articles.title: The Noisy Work of Uncertainty Visualization
articles.journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application
articles.abstract: Better representation of the uncertainty in a data visualization is a focus of recent research activity. A problem with the current literature is that there is a lack of clarity about the definition of uncertainty and what it means to represent it in a plot. This confusion has led to conflicting results in the literature, especially in experiments that assess the effectiveness of different uncertainty representations. In this review, we summarize the current literature, provide workable definitions, and illustrate these definitions with examples. In doing so, we ask what it really takes to achieve transparency in statistical graphics. We hope that it will be useful for guiding new graphics methodology and experimental research.
