articles.title: Cryptic Diversity and Patterns of Structure in Nine Species of North Pacific Rockfishes (Sebastes spp. and Sebastolobus spp.)
articles.abstract: Understanding how habitat and life history traits contribute to population genetic structure is critical for evaluating conservation risks and identifying optimal management of wild populations. Species derived from adaptive radiations can provide a useful model for studying such patterns because the presence of some consistent traits allows for closer examination of attributes which differ. Here, we examine population structure in rockfishes (genera Sebastes and Sebastolobus), a group of speciose, recently diverged marine fishes that exhibit a continuum of genetic structure, from cryptic species to putative genetic panmixia. In this study, we analyse low‐coverage whole genome resequencing data from nine rockfish species and identify four major types of genetic differentiation: cryptic diversity, isolation‐by‐distance (IBD), no detectable structure (putative panmixia) and no detectable structure with a single genomic region putatively underlying local adaptation. Two species, Dark (Sebastes ciliatus) and Northern (S. polyspinis) rockfishes, each exhibited cryptic diversity consisting of two sympatric groups differentiated at every chromosome throughout the genome. Black rockfish in Southeast Alaska also had two genetic groups, despite an overall signal of IBD from the West Coast of North America through the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). Five species showed evidence of genetic panmixia throughout the sampled range, while Yelloweye Rockfish exhibited high gene flow across ~4000 km, from southern California to the GOA, but had strong differentiation between the Salish Sea and the outer coast. Of the species in which no structure was detected, only Blackspotted Rockfish had one outlier region exhibiting signatures of potential local adaptation. Our results highlight how multiple mechanisms likely promote genetic structure in rockfishes, hinting at tentative links to depth distributions and offshore habitats that might influence patterns of differentiation in rockfishes more broadly. Further, this study provides genetic data for some of the most abundant rockfishes in commercial fisheries in the Northeast Pacific, enhancing the scientific information available for informing fisheries management.

articles.title: Temporal Community Assembly of Bacteria and Protists in Different Habitats of a Mountain Lake
articles.abstract: Whether microbial community assembly is primarily deterministic (selection‐driven) or stochastic (dispersal‐driven) remains a central debate in microbial ecology. We investigated community assembly of bacteria and protists and their driving ecological processes in mountain Lake Tovel using a 5‐year 16S and 18S rRNA metabarcoding dataset. The frequencies of assembly mechanisms and their processes depend on the considered temporal scale. We assessed the influence of temporal scale (years, seasons, temporal distances from 1 to 48 months across all years) and year‐pooling (a common strategy in the assessment of assembly patterns) on the inference of community assembly in the upper euphotic (0–3 m), lower euphotic (3–25 m) and deep hypolimnetic (30–35 m) layers. Focusing on single years, bacteria showed more often different assembly mechanisms (both deterministic and stochastic) across layers and years than protists. Year‐pooling hid the inter‐year differences and preserved the signal of the most frequent single‐year process. A lagged effect of water temperature on bacterial community assembly was found, while an immediate effect on protist assembly. Bacterial and protists' niche width was generally independent of year‐pooling and increased with depth. Our study showed that different temporal scales and depth layers should be considered to gain a comprehensive overview on community assembly.

articles.title: Transposable Element Activity Is Associated With the Rise of Termite Diversity
articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) have long been hypothesized as a driver of lineage diversification due to their mutagenic ability. However, the correlation between rates of TE activity and diversification has rarely been tested, since it is challenging to measure the rate of TE activity in the deep past. Here, we investigated TE activity during the last ~150 million years of termite evolution. First, we determined the timing of TE amplification events using the sequence divergence of TE copies and identified two waves of TE bursts that took place synchronously across termite lineages, coinciding with the two major phases of termite diversification. Furthermore, we built phylogenetic trees using the presence/absence of orthologous TE insertions in the flanking regions of Ultraconserved Elements (UCEs), in which the branch length provided a measure of the rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs along the termite phylogenetic tree. The rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs predicted up to 34.8% of the variation in the termite net diversification rate. Overall, these results supported TEs as an important contributor to species diversification. More broadly, this study provided a phylogenomic approach to quantify TE activity in the deep past.

Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy — Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy — Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

articles.title: Microbial volatile humulene orchestrates plant–microbe alliance to establish disease‐suppressive rhizosphere
articles.abstract: Proposed working model of humulene‐mediated suppression of tomato bacterial wilt. Summary Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) suppress growth and virulence traits of soil‐borne pathogens, yet their ecological roles in disease suppression remain unclear. Here, we show that the sesquiterpene humulene from Streptomyces acts as a multifunctional regulator that suppresses bacterial wilt through coordinated inhibition of Ralstonia solanacearum, plant metabolic reprogramming, and rhizosphere microbiome modulation. We combined in vitro pathogen assays, pot experiments, microbiota transplantation, rhizosphere 16S rRNA profiling, root‐exudate metabolomics, and plant and pathogen transcriptomics to investigate the direct and microbiome‐mediated effects of humulene. Humulene reduced disease severity and pathogen abundance via a microbiome‐dependent mechanism. Microbiota transplantation confirmed that the humulene‐conditioned microbiome retains transferable disease‐suppressiveness. Humulene also selectively enriched antagonistic Streptomyces, not by direct growth promotion, but by reprogramming tomato root exudation to produce lipid‐derived petroselinic acid, which promoted Streptomyces growth, humulene production, and pathogen suppression. Root transcriptomics further revealed activation of lipid metabolic pathways involving alternative fatty acid desaturation and oxylipin signaling. Together, humulene functions as an ecological signal that integrates pathogen suppression, host lipid metabolism, and microbiome assembly to establish a disease‐suppressive rhizosphere, enabling microbiome‐informed control of bacterial wilt.

articles.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
articles.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

articles.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
articles.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
articles.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

articles.title: New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
articles.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

articles.title: Selection-for-prediction: rethinking early cognitive development
articles.abstract: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants’ behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors—evolutionarily shaped selection biases—interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error—rather than conceptual contradiction—may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.

articles.title: Cesium-Triiodide-Mediated Crystallization Regulation of Pure-Iodide Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells Exceeding 30% Efficiency
articles.abstract: Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: Electrically Enabled Isothermal CeO2 Thermochemical Water Splitting below 900 °C
articles.abstract: Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.

articles.title: Rational Ionomer Design Directs Hydrogenation Pathways and Reactant Accessibility in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
articles.abstract: Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

articles.title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression
articles.abstract: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.

articles.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula
articles.abstract: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.

articles.title: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons
articles.abstract: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.

articles.title: Promoter of lncRNA Gene PVT1 Is a Tumor-Suppressor DNA Boundary Element
Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
articles.abstract: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.

articles.title: Root microbiota regulates tiller number in rice
Proteasome inhibition bidirectionally regulates ferroptosis sensitivity
articles.abstract: How proteasome function shapes ferroptosis sensitivity is poorly understood. Murray et al. demonstrate that proteasome inhibition enhances sensitivity to ferroptosis induced by direct inhibition of GPX4, while protecting against system xc− inhibitors. Sensitization to GPX4 inhibitors requires protein synthesis and is opposed by activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4).

articles.title: A phage-encoded small RNA that mimics chimeric guide to inhibit CRISPR-Cas9
articles.abstract: Chen et al. identify rAcrIIA1, a phage-encoded chimeric crRNA-tracrRNA mimic that competitively blocks Cas9 guide loading and DNA interference. This reprogrammable RNA guide enables efficient genome editing, gene silencing, and diagnostics, with enhanced trans-cleavage activity.

articles.title: CNS targeted AAV gene therapies: Recent advances and clinical insights
articles.abstract: Brown and colleagues review recent approaches to overcome limitations to AAV brain gene therapies from vector design through clinical implementation, highlighting how success and patient safety must consider routes of administration, target engagement, and dosing.

articles.title: Inhibition of the CTP synthase 1 prevents GVHD and delays skin graft rejection revealing distinct alloreactive T cell responses
articles.abstract: Allogeneic transplants can trigger graft-versus-host disease and graft rejection. Lopes Souza et al. demonstrate that deletion of Ctps1 in T cells prevents GVHD and reduces skin rejection. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of CTPS1 improves survival in acute GVHD, highlighting CTPS1 as a promising therapeutic target for alloreactive T cell responses.

Surface acoustic waves drive interfacial fragmentation in porous fibrous solids
A self-organized tri-lineage bone model in liquefied microcapsules captures matrix dynamics in early remodeling
articles.abstract: Mano and colleagues have developed a self-organized bone-like model by co-encapsulating stromal and monocytic cells in liquefied gelatin microcapsules. Their direct interaction effectively supports the emergence of osteoblast-, osteocyte-, and osteoclast-like phenotypes, facilitating cellular crosstalk and promoting mineralized matrix formation and turnover without the need for lineage-specific induction.

articles.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function
articles.abstract: Yu and colleagues reveal that hematopoietic stem cells employ Rbpms condensates to spatially restrict the translation elongation machinery. By slowing protein synthesis and ensuring proper protein folding, this mechanism preserves proteostasis, quiescence, and LT stem cell function.

articles.title: Programming hot-carrier dynamics in gold nanoclusters for high-gain photodetectors
articles.abstract: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.

articles.title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
articles.abstract: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

articles.title: Recent applications of asymmetric hydrogenation in total synthesis of natural products and drugs
articles.abstract: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.

articles.title: Solar vapor generation technologies: fundamentals, innovations and applications
articles.abstract: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.

articles.title: An Interpretable and Transferable Physics-Aware Machine-Learning Framework for Stability Prediction of Dual-Atom Alloys
articles.abstract: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.

articles.title: Eco‐Evolutionary Feedback to a Pesticide Worsens the Impact of a Pesticide Switch in a Pivotal Freshwater Non‐Target Species
articles.abstract: Pest management often requires the rotation of insecticides, sequentially exposing non‐target populations to different compounds. In a two‐phased experiment, we assessed whether exposure to the pesticide chlorpyrifos induces rapid evolution in the non‐target species Daphnia magna and quantified the response of control and pre‐exposed populations to a second exposure to the same pesticide, another pesticide with the same mode of action (malathion), or a pesticide with another mode of action (deltamethrin). Chlorpyrifos selection induced rapid shifts in genotype composition and reduced genotype richness and strongly influenced population development following the second exposure. Chlorpyrifos‐selected populations outperformed control populations when subsequently exposed to chlorpyrifos and malathion but underperformed when exposed to deltamethrin. Our results highlight an eco‐evolutionary feedback in which rapid adaptive responses to a pesticide worsen the response when exposed to a different type of pesticide in non‐target species, increasing vulnerability to common agricultural practices.

articles.title: Facet-directed hydroxyl-rich surface environments stabilize iridium single atoms for efficient acidic water oxidation
articles.abstract: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

articles.title: Triboelectric DC generation via dielectric polarization coupling for self-powered IoT systems
articles.abstract: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.

articles.title: High functional redundancy and stable diversity of phylogenetically distant arthropods across a tropical university campus urbanization gradient
articles.abstract: Rapid and unplanned urbanization significantly disrupts natural ecosystems and often leads to biotic homogenization across all climatic regions, including the tropics. The conservation potential of urban green spaces, including university campuses, remains relatively understudied, particularly regarding the divergent responses of different trophic groups within these ecosystems. University campuses are different from other urban environments in that their structures are primarily designed to support education and scientific research while conserving natural habitats. Here, we investigated the possibilities of taxonomic and functional homogenization within the tropical suburban environment of a university campus in Nadia, West Bengal, India, by studying the presence and functional characteristics of two phylogenetically distant arthropod groups, butterflies (primary consumers and pollinators) and spiders (top predators). Butterflies are often used as bioindicators, whereas spiders, which function as apex predators in urban ecosystems, serve to monitor habitat alterations. We performed systematic point counts for butterflies and visual searches for spiders across ten sampling plots categorized into three distinct habitat types based on anthropogenic disturbance (highly urbanized roadside, highly managed, and unmanaged natural zones). Taxonomic diversity was assessed using standard alpha diversity indices. Community composition and beta diversity were analyzed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA). To evaluate functional diversity (FRic, FEve, and FDiv), species were categorized according to key functional traits. We found high species richness at the suburban site, which remained consistent across all habitats. Our analysis showed a lack of significant community divergence, and functional diversity remained stable across different habitat categories in both groups (ANOVA: p > 0.05). Our results also indicated high functional redundancy for each land use. PERMANOVA test indicated that habitat type reflects a non-significant amount of variation in community composition for both butterflies (p = 0.413) and spiders (p = 0.886). These results demonstrate that different areas within a single university campus may not act as environmental filters for different species; instead, they support species assemblages based upon the available microhabitats. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of university campuses as functional refuges within urban biodiversity networks, emphasizing the need to maintain local botanical heterogeneity to conserve biodiversity.

articles.title: Intra- and interspecific variation in growth and heat tolerance traits of saprotrophic fungi isolated from pyrogenic carbon in a frequent fire ecosystem
articles.abstract: Fire is an important disturbance in many terrestrial ecosystems across the globe. A byproduct of fire is partially combusted organic matter, or pyrogenic carbon (PyC), which can be difficult for most microbes to decompose. Pyrophilic fungi are fungi that can break down and use PyC, survive through extreme heat, and/or have adaptations to rapidly colonize under postfire conditions. However, only a few fungal taxa have been characterized for their pyrophilic traits. Understanding the growth strategies and pyrophilic traits of fungi found in post-fire environments can help us understand mechanisms of ecosystem recovery from fire and their contributions to carbon cycling. Here, we characterized the pyrophilic traits of seven fungal isolates (Trichoderma and Mucor species) by testing their ability to grow on different carbon substrates (media containing PyC, sucrose, or water agar). Isolates were also incubated across a range of temperatures to determine if carbon source impacts thermotolerance and if the ability to catabolize PyC co-occurs with higher thermotolerance. We found that PyC-associated fungi exhibited a wide range of growth strategies, and many were able to grow on PyC. However, we found weak evidence for thermotolerance and growth on PyC as coordinated pyrophilic traits. Finally, we also found high intraspecific variation in growth strategies and weak tradeoffs along the fungal economics spectrum growth traits. These results were additionally supported by FT-IR analysis of substrates and fungal tissues, which showed different tissue chemistry based on substrate. Our results highlight the importance of intraspecific variation in carbon use ability and growth strategy as a key area of future research for pyrophilic fungi.

articles.title: Macroinvertebrate diversity patterns in floodplain wetlands under fragmentation, northwest China
articles.abstract: Wetlands are among the most diverse and dynamic ecosystems on Earth. Meanwhile, they have experienced habitat loss and degradation worldwide, leading to biodiversity declines. As a primary driver of wetland loss and degradation, fragmentation can pose profound impacts on natural environmental regimes of floodplain wetlands. Here, we investigated the composition of macroinvertebrate assemblages in the Heihe Floodplain, Northwest China comparing wetlands with connection to rivers (i.e., riverine wetlands) and those isolated from rivers (i.e., lacustrine wetlands), with the wetland type used as a proxy for hydrological connectivity. We observed evident differences in species composition and community structure of macroinvertebrates between riverine and lacustrine wetlands. Three indicator species (Palaemon sp., Radix sp., Gyraulus sp.) were identified for lacustrine wetlands, whereas none were detected for riverine wetlands. Compared to lacustrine wetlands, riverine wetlands had significantly lower taxonomic and functional richness, but they had significantly higher mean local contributions to taxonomic and functional beta diversity, as well as more heterogeneous communities at regional scale. Our study highlights the need for a balanced wetland conservation strategy that protects lacustrine wetlands with high local diversity while also maintaining or restoring appropriate hydrological connectivity to promote regional biodiversity recovery and enhance ecosystem service functions. It also underscores the importance of incorporating functional traits and beta diversity into environmental monitoring and conservation planning to safeguard wetland biodiversity and associated ecosystem functions and services.

articles.title: Multi-scenario responses of ecological security networks in the Yangtze River Delta under a multi-model framework
articles.abstract: Rapid urbanization and land-use change are reshaping ecological spaces in urban agglomerations, underscoring the need to identify conservation and restoration priorities under alternative development pathways. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, this study integrates landscape ecological risk assessment, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and circuit theory to evaluate ecological security network responses under business-as-usual, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios for 2035. To better capture the spatial heterogeneity of ecological resistance, landscape ecological risk was incorporated into the composite resistance surface together with land use, elevation, and slope, allowing resistance values to reflect differences among areas of the same land-use type under different landscape configurations and disturbance conditions. Multi-period validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.87 and 0.90 and Kappa coefficients of 0.81 and 0.85 for the 2018 and 2020 land-use simulations, respectively. Built-up land expanded most strongly under the urban development scenario, increasing by 6, 866.91 km2, whereas the increase was limited to only 54.37 km2 under the ecological protection scenario. Ecological risk exhibited a persistent spatial gradient of higher risk in the northeast and lower risk in the southwest, with high-risk areas concentrated primarily in highly urbanized regions. Ecological pinch points and barrier points were mainly concentrated along urban fringes and intercity connection zones. Comparison of the three development scenarios showed that the ecological protection scenario was more effective in constraining uncontrolled urban expansion and maintaining ecological connectivity. However, barrier points inherited from historically developed areas persisted under the ecological protection scenario, and their number did not decline markedly. This trade-off indicates that ecological protection alone cannot fully resolve regional connectivity constraints. Improving regional ecological connectivity therefore requires targeted restoration of persistent barrier points together with coordinated protection of ecological source areas and corridors.

articles.title: Herbivory enhances cadmium foraging in the invasive hyperaccumulating plant Phytolacca americana
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Biological invasions and heavy metal pollution are two pervasive environmental challenges threatening global ecosystems. While the elemental defence hypothesis posits that certain plants accumulate heavy metals to deter herbivores, it remains unclear whether invasive hyperaccumulators actively forage for these toxic elements and whether such below‐ground behaviour is dynamically induced by above‐ground biotic stress. Here, we investigated the foraging behaviour of the invasive hyperaccumulator Phytolacca americana in a rhizobox experiment simulating a dual‐stress environment of heterogeneous cadmium (Cd) distribution and Spodoptera litura herbivory. We considered root morphological responses and employed integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We found that P. americana preferentially allocated root biomass to Cd‐enriched soil patches when exposed to cadmium. Notably, above‐ground insect herbivory significantly amplified this below‐ground Cd foraging response. The interaction between Cd stress and herbivory markedly altered root morphology. Cd accumulated primarily in fine roots, where plants optimized their specific root length and tissue density to efficiently exploit Cd‐rich zones. Integrated molecular analyses revealed that Cd treatment significantly suppressed cytokinin levels in the roots. This hormonal shift likely promotes lateral root formation and accelerates heavy metal sequestration. Our results demonstrate that above‐ground biotic interactions can actively drive below‐ground heavy metal foraging strategies in invasive plants, manifesting as a complex morphological plasticity mediated by cytokinin signalling. More broadly, our study highlights how synergistic responses to multiple environmental stressors can enhance the adaptive capacity and ecological success of invasive species in contaminated habitats. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 生物入侵与重金属污染是威胁全球生态系统的两类普遍环境问题。元素防御假说认为，某些植物可通过积累重金属抵御植食性动物，但入侵性超富集植物是否会主动觅取这些有毒元素，以及这种地下行为是否受到地上生物胁迫的诱导，目前尚不清楚。 本研究通过根箱实验模拟镉(Cd)异质分布与斜纹夜蛾(Spodoptera litura)取食的双重胁迫环境，探究了入侵性超富集植物美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana)的觅食行为，解析其根系形态响应，并结合转录组学与代谢组学分析揭示其内在机制。 结果表明，在镉处理条件下，美洲商陆优先将根系生物量分配至镉富集土壤斑块，而地上昆虫取食会进一步增强这一地下镉觅食响应；镉胁迫与植食作用的交互显著改变了根系形态。镉主要积累于细根，植株通过优化比根长与组织密度高效利用富镉区域。转录‐代谢联合分析结果显示，镉处理显著降低了根系细胞分裂素水平，这一激素变化可能促进侧根形成并提高重金属觅食效应。 上述结果表明，地上生物互作可主动驱动入侵植物的地下重金属觅食策略，该策略表现为由细胞分裂素信号介导的复杂形态可塑性。本研究揭示了对多重环境胁迫的协同响应如何提升入侵物种在污染生境中的适应性与生态优势。

articles.title: Climate Change Experienced by Life on Earth—Drivers and Mechanisms of Future Trends in Microclimates
articles.abstract: Microclimate, the climate directly experienced by organisms, is crucial for understanding ecological responses to climate change, yet its long‐term dynamics and the drivers of decadal microclimate changes remain underexplored in ecology and global change biology. Microclimate changes do not necessarily track macroclimate trends. Changes in meteorological conditions (e.g., cloud cover, wind patterns) and vegetation dynamics (e.g., canopy opening, desertification in drylands, shrub encroachment in the tundra) associated with climate change can lead to locally divergent microclimate trends, thereby altering spatial variability. Understanding and quantifying how macroclimate change translates to fine‐scale microclimate change experienced by organisms, populations and communities is therefore essential for predicting ecological responses to global environmental change. This review examines how macroclimate change drives microclimate changes as experienced by life on Earth—and how these micro‐scale changes may, in turn, feed back into the regional and global climate system. Our primary focus is on near‐surface air and soil temperature—due to their relevance to most terrestrial organisms and ecosystem processes. The review is structured around three pathways of microclimate changes: (I) direct effects of changes in meteorological conditions, (II) indirect effects via vegetation changes, and (III) feedbacks between microclimate and climate change. Using three mechanistic model simulations in real‐world landscapes, we illustrate and quantify the key mechanisms that lead to divergent warming trends. We show that microclimate change emerges from interacting atmospheric, land‐surface, and biophysical processes, which can differ substantially across space and time. Predicting future microclimates therefore requires accounting for these processes and their temporal dynamics. By providing an accessible synthesis of these processes, this review aims to strengthen links between ecology and atmospheric science and improve our understanding of how climate change translates into microclimatic conditions relevant to life on Earth.

articles.title: The Importance, Challenges and Solutions of a Changing Climate for Conserving Migratory Animals and the Ecosystem Services They Provide
articles.abstract: Each year, billions of animals undertake migratory journeys, resulting in large transfers of energy across the globe. Population declines in many migratory species have affected these, reducing ecosystem resilience. We quantify the value lost and show how conserving migratory species can contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation, and deliver socio‐economic benefits.

articles.title: Chloride-mediated SAM locking via ligand-exchange reaction enables 18.8% active-area efficiency and stable organic solar modules
articles.abstract: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.

articles.title: Singlet fission and triplet transfer to a metal halide perovskite absorber
articles.abstract: Singlet fission in tetracene generates triplet excitons that are harvested by a metal halide perovskite through a ZnPc-mediated interface with energetics consistent with an interfacial hybrid charge-transfer (IHCT) pathway, enabling triplet sensitization and their contribution to photocurrent generation in perovskite photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant‐ and fungal‐derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems
articles.abstract: Using amino acid isotope fingerprinting, Sagi et al. show how Arctic wolf spiders shift between plant‐ and microbe‐based energy sources with changes in body size and plant productivity. This reveals how environmental conditions and consumer traits jointly shape carbon flow and link green and brown food webs in rapidly changing ecosystems. Abstract Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. Spatiotemporal variation in the transfer of plant‐ versus microbial‐derived energy to higher trophic levels is poorly understood but can affect bottom‐up and top‐down processes. For example, seasonal shifts in herbivore versus microbivore availability (bottom‐up) may alter prey choice by generalist‐feeding predators and lead to changes in top‐down predator control on primary production and decomposition. We tested how spatiotemporal variation in primary production influences the use of different energy channels by a widely distributed generalist invertebrate predator in the Arctic tundra. We sampled wolf spiders across four sites spanning a productivity gradient in the Alaskan Arctic during peak summer and on a weekly basis at one focal site throughout the growing season. Using essential amino acid (EAA) carbon isotope (δ13C) fingerprinting, we traced the flow of plant‐, bacterial‐ and fungal‐derived EAAs to spiders and quantified the use of plant‐ versus microbe‐based energy channels between sites and across summer. Wolf spiders were associated with more plant‐ and less fungal‐derived carbon assimilation when larger or collected from sites with higher normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Across the growing season, spiders shifted from primarily assimilating fungal‐based resources in early summer to plant‐derived resources in late summer, aligning with seasonal increases in NDVI. These patterns demonstrate spatiotemporal variation in carbon flow through different energy channels and suggest subsequent top‐down predator effects may also vary with basal resource availability. Our findings also suggest wolf spider body size may predict whether predation indirectly influences primary production or decomposition. As climate change alters seasonality, resource dynamics and invertebrate body sizes, these insights provide a basis for predicting spatiotemporal variation in predator impacts on ecosystem processes. Finally, our work demonstrates the utility of compound‐specific stable isotope analysis for integrating ecological and biogeochemical theory through the conceptual lens of zoogeochemistry.

articles.title: Breaking the density-stability trade-off of isolated gallium sites for propane dehydrogenation
Correction to “Plant species responses to nutrient addition, but not to herbivore exclusion, strengthen over time in global grasslands”
Monolayer photonic-crystal manganese halide gel scintillator for full-vision imaging
articles.abstract: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.

articles.title: The camtrapR R package: From data management to interactive ecological analysis of camera trap data
articles.abstract: Camera trapping has become an indispensable tool in wildlife ecology, generating vast datasets that require efficient and robust analytical workflows. The R package camtrapR was originally developed for preparing camera trap data for analysis in external packages and has since become a standard tool for this purpose. The analyses themselves, however, still had to be conducted elsewhere. Here, we present a major update that transforms camtrapR into an end‐to‐end analytical platform that unifies data import, exploration, covariate preparation, activity pattern estimation, occupancy modelling and spatial prediction. All new functionality is available as R functions and through surveyDashboard(), a new code‐free graphical user interface that guides users through the entire analytical pipeline. Data import supports widely used formats, including exports from the Wildlife Insights platform and datasets conforming to the Camtrap DP data standard. Exploratory tools generate species accumulation curves, maps of species detections and activity patterns for up to two species. Covariates can be extracted at camera trap sites from user‐supplied rasters or online sources, providing inputs for model fitting and, as raster layers, for spatial predictions. Users can fit single‐species and community occupancy models, some of the most widely adopted analytical frameworks in wildlife ecology, and map predicted occupancy across space. Community occupancy models are fitted in a Bayesian framework using JAGS or NIMBLE. These hierarchical models estimate species‐ and community‐level responses to environmental predictors and improve inference for rare species. The workflow includes convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for model assessment and produces spatial predictions of species occupancy and species richness. The workflow can be implemented both in code and within the dashboard. By combining a code‐free interface with advanced modelling capabilities, camtrapR now makes robust camera trap data analysis accessible to a wider audience of ecologists, wildlife managers and students. This paper accompanies camtrapR version 3 and serves as the reference for its expanded functionality.

articles.title: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3′UTR shortening in proliferating cells
articles.abstract: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.

articles.title: Independent Major‐Effect Loci and Limited Trait Associations Characterize Warning Colour Variation Across Sexes and Life Stages in the Wood Tiger Moth (Arctia plantaginis)
articles.abstract: Variation in warning colouration is common, despite strong positive frequency‐dependent selection favouring the most common morph and may arise from spatially or temporally variable selection or associations with other traits. We investigated the maintenance of warning colour variation in the wood tiger moth, Arctia plantaginis, which shows sexual dimorphism in colouration: two distinct male morphs controlled by a single locus, and continuous variation in female hindwing colour and larval warning signal size. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 657 individuals from a laboratory stock derived from a wild polymorphic population, we examined the genetic basis of multiple life‐history traits, chemical defence, pheromones and male activity. We specifically tested for associations with male colour and aimed to identify the genetic basis of female and larval colour variation. We detected separate major‐effect loci for female colour and larval signal size, which were different from the male colour locus. Hindwing melanism was the only trait associated with male colour, mapping to a nearby major‐effect locus and showing a link to reduced activity at higher temperatures. Female colour was phenotypically correlated with pheromone amount. However, apart from melanism, none of the traits measured showed an association with any of the loci controlling warning colours and we found no evidence that male colour is part of a ‘supergene’ or complex co‐adapted phenotype. Instead, our results indicate largely independent genetic architectures for warning colours, suggesting that variable selection rather than genetic associations may contribute to the maintenance of colour polymorphisms in this species.

articles.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
articles.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

articles.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

articles.title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease
articles.abstract: Khatri and colleagues assembled a single-cell atlas of 1 million human neutrophils based on the integration of 43 independent single-cell transcriptome datasets to define multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and disease states.

articles.title: A tolerogenic function for gut TFH cells
articles.abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells maintain immunological tolerance, but the cellular niches sustaining them across tissues are poorly defined. Work now identifies T follicular helper cells as a source of IL-2 that supports Treg cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue and promotes intestinal immune homeostasis.

articles.title: IL-2-producing TFH cells sustain Treg cell homeostasis and immune tolerance in the gut
articles.abstract: Ballesteros-Tato and colleagues identify a spatially restricted follicular helper T cell-dependent interleukin-2 niche critical for regulatory T cell stability in gut-associated lymphoid tissues.

articles.title: Spatial confinement promotes germinal center diversity and tempers immunodominance
articles.abstract: Chen et al. examine why germinal centers (GCs) are confined to isolated islands in reactive lymph nodes during an immune response. They find that spatial confinement of GC B cells leads to greater antibody diversity by limiting the exchange and expansion of dominant B cell clones.

articles.title: Global, regional and national burden of pertussis in 1990–2023: a Global Burden of Disease study
articles.abstract: Updates to the Global Burden of Disease study showed that while global trends in pertussis (whooping cough) declined from 1990 to 2023, the rebound in incidence and mortality since 2020, particularly in high-income regions, reflects stalled vaccination progress worldwide.

articles.title: The need for resilience in global vaccination programs
articles.abstract: New studies of trends in the global burden of measles and pertussis offer a reminder of how much vaccination has achieved and a warning of the need to build more resilient and sustainable vaccination programs.

articles.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
articles.abstract: Tang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

articles.title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
articles.abstract: SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

articles.title: Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
articles.abstract: The breakdown of Hooke’s law marks the onset of nonlinear behaviour: when displacements become large, restoring forces weaken and Hookean proportionality fails. In quantum materials, intense optical excitation can drive the crystal lattice into a similar regime, where established linear relations between light, electrons and phonons no longer hold. Displacive excitation of coherent phonons, the principal mechanism for launching structural motion, typically assumes that lattice-driving forces scale linearly with the photo-excited carrier density. At high excitation, however, this linearity can break down, which fundamentally limits accessible lattice displacements. Here we show that such nonlinear limitations can be surpassed in a sliding ferroelectric by timing, rather than strengthening the optical drive. Time-resolved second-harmonic generation reveals that the interlayer-sliding phonon governing ferroelectricity saturates and even diminishes under single-pulse excitation. By means of first-principles calculations, we attribute this nonlinearity to band-specific electron–phonon coupling that induces competing forces on the lattice. By splitting the optical energy into two well-timed pulses that avoid populating counteracting states, we achieve markedly larger phonon amplitudes at fixed total fluence. The resulting enhanced sliding motion exposes a regime of anharmonic phonon coupling that emerges only far from equilibrium.

articles.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
articles.abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

Helicobacter pylori Infection — Advances, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
articles.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren’s Disease
articles.abstract: BackgroundSjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.MethodsWe conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.ResultsOverall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.ConclusionsIn these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

An AGC kinase cascade regulates ROP signaling for the correct timing of pollen germination
articles.abstract: Model for PDK1‐AGC1.5/7 kinase cascade function in controlling pollen germination. Summary In flowering plants, the timing of pollen germination is crucial for successful fertilization and an important trait for seed and fruit crops. Environmental factors tightly regulate pollen germination, with germination‐suppressing conditions on the pollen‐producing anther and germination‐promoting conditions on the receiving stigma. Using genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods, we show that this environmental sensitivity of pollen germination in Arabidopsis thaliana is regulated by a 3‐PHOSPHOINOSITIDE‐DEPENDENT KINASE 1 (PDK1)‐AGC1.5/AGC1.7 kinase cascade. We show that PDK1 hyperphosphorylates downstream AGC1.5/7 kinases to enhance their activity. Pollen‐specific phosphoproteomics identified multiple proteins involved in pollen growth whose phosphorylation is controlled by AGC1.5/7. Two germination‐promoting RHO OF PLANTS GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTORS (ROPGEFs) are phosphorylated by AGC1.5/7 at a novel site, reducing ROPGEF plasma membrane polarization. Loss of PDK1‐AGC kinase signaling resulted in precocious pollen germination on the anther, which was rescued by high AGC1.5 kinase activity. Conversely, AGC1.5/7 overexpression or a phosphomimic ROPGEF version inhibited precocious pollen germination. Distinct subcellular localization of PDK1 and AGC1 kinases upon pollen germination is likely to alleviate their inhibitory effect. Our data indicate that the correct timing of pollen germination requires the fine‐tuned activity of a PDK1‐AGC1 kinase cascade inhibiting ROPGEFs on the anther, preventing precocious pollen germination.

articles.title: B‐BOX DOMAIN PROTEIN 19 shapes tea quality by modulating the ratio of catechins and theanine and confers cold tolerance in tea plants
articles.abstract: A working model of the core regulator CsBBX19 which fine‐tunes tea quality and cold tolerance in tea plants. Summary Early spring cold spells threaten tea plant (Camellia sinensis) yield and disrupt the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio that determines the desirable balance of umami and astringency taste of tea. However, the molecular mechanism coordinating cold tolerance with this key quality trait remains unclear. Here, we identified a light‐responsive B‐BOX DOMAIN PROTEIN CsBBX19 as a core regulator simultaneously shaping tea quality and cold tolerance. Results demonstrated that silencing CsBBX19 relieves the transcriptional repression of theanine‐biosynthetic genes (CsTSI and CsAlaDC) to elevate theanine levels, yet weakens the activation of catechins‐biosynthetic genes (CsANS1, CsANR1, CsLAR1, and CsSCPL1/2/5) to reduce catechins content. The CsBBX19‐modulated theanine accumulation also enhanced the cold tolerance of tea plants by suppressing cell‐wall‐loosening EXPANSIN (CsEXPA10/20/21) and activating the CsCBF3‐mediated cold response pathway. Furthermore, the expression of CsBBX19 significantly reduced by light via a feedback loop involving CsHY5, which directly binds to the promoter of CsBBX19 to repress its transcription, while CsBBX19 conversely interacts with CsHY5 to reinforce its autoactivation, thereby fine‐tuning the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio and cold resilience in tea plants. Our findings underscore the central roles of CsBBX19 in light‐mediated cold response and tea quality formation, providing valuable targets for synchronously improving cold resilience and quality in tea plants.

articles.title: Duplication and functional divergence of TCP4 genes in turnip
articles.abstract: Target genes of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Summary Gene duplication is widely recognized as a significant catalyst for plant adaptive evolution. The retained duplicated genes usually undergo functional divergence to govern plant growth and stress resistance. Turnip (Brassica rapa var. rapa) shows a broad capacity for environmental adaptation. Here, we investigate how duplicated TCP4 genes modulate turnip growth and development. We identify three TCP4 paralogs, BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b in turnip, characterize their expression patterns and analyze sequence variation in their conserved domains. We further model their three‐dimensional structures and compare their protein–protein interactions and downstream regulatory networks. We show that BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b exhibit distinct expression profiles. A single mutation within the conserved TCP domain leads to differences in protein–protein interactions among BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Combined with DAP‐Seq, ChIP‐qPCR and luciferase assays, our results demonstrate that BrrTCP4 and BrrTCP4a activate BrrCOs and BrrFTs to regulate turnip flowering, while BrrTCP4b preferentially participates in the trehalose synthesis pathway by targeting TPP and TPS genes. Our research findings indicate the functional divergence of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b to balance growth and stress responses in turnip, thereby advancing our understanding of how gene duplication drives functional specialization and contributes to plant evolutionary adaptation. 概括 重复基因是植物适应性进化的重要催化剂。保留下来的重复基因会发生功能分化，进而调控植物的生长发育和抗逆性。蔓菁(Brassica rapa var. rapa)隶属于十字花科芸薹属，该属经历了一次特有的全基因组三倍化事件，是研究重复基因的理想材料。因此，本文我们研究了蔓菁TCP4重复基因如何调控蔓菁的生长发育。 共线性分析发现蔓菁BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b是基因组复制产生的三个重复基因。我们分析了它们的表达模式和其保守结构域中的序列变异。并进一步模拟了它们的三维结构，比较了它们的互作蛋白及下游调控网络的差异。 研究结果显示BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b具有不同的表达模式。保守TCP结构域内的单个氨基酸突变导致了BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a与BrrTCP4b互作蛋白的差异。结合DAP‐Seq、ChIP‐qPCR和荧光素酶实验发现，BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a直接激活BrrCOs和BrrFTs以调控蔓菁开花，而BrrTCP4b则通过靶向TPP和TPS基因优先参与海藻糖合成途径。 我们的研究结果揭示了BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b重复基因发生了功能分化，这种分化平衡了蔓菁的生长发育与胁迫响应。相关研究结果加深了我们对基因重复如何驱动功能分化并促进植物适应性进化的理解。

articles.title: Elevated CO2 drives nonlinear trait responses and reshapes growth‐virulence trade‐offs in a plant pathogen
articles.abstract: Temporal variation in carbon dioxide concentration within the crop canopy and in the atmosphere. Summary Atmospheric CO2 is rising at unprecedented rates. While its physiological effects on plants are well‐documented, the direct evolutionary impact on plant pathogens remains unknown. We investigated how CO2 interacts with other abiotic factors to shape the evolutionary potential of pathogens. We combined controlled CO2 gradient experiments with quantitative genetics to assess the interactive effects of CO2, temperature and geography on Phytophthora infestans. We measured intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness, the two key pathogen traits, across seven geographically distinct populations and partitioned their phenotypic variance into heritability and plasticity components. Both intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness showed a shared quadratic response to CO2, peaking c. 2000 ppm before declining. Elevated CO2 reduced phenotypic variance in aggressiveness under extreme concentrations. CO2 also reconfigured the life‐history correlation between growth and aggressiveness, shifting it from positive under ambient CO2 to negative near the optimum. Heritability exceeded plasticity for aggressiveness in most populations, indicating that virulence responds primarily through selection. Trait responses were modulated by local climate and geography, with the strongest CO2‐driven increases occurring under thermal and geographic extremes. Our results demonstrate that rising CO2 acts as a direct agent of selection, nonlinearly reshaping pathogen phenotypic architecture and life‐history strategies in a geographically heterogeneous manner.

articles.title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy for Near-Integrable Dynamics
articles.abstract: The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.
